The median sale price across Apollo Beach in late 2025 was approximately $525,000, up roughly 8 percent year over year. That median is significantly influenced by the volume of waterfront transactions -- deep-water canal properties, bay-front estates, and lagoon-adjacent homes that trade in the $700,000 to $2 million range. Non-waterfront homes in Waterset and the eastern Apollo Beach subdivisions bring the median down when volume is high in those segments. A buyer using the median as a baseline without understanding the waterfront premium will consistently misread individual property valuations.

Market segmentation by property type:

  • Deep-water canal front: Properties with direct bay access, private docks, and no bridge or depth restrictions for larger vessels. MiraBay deep-water canals, Symphony Isles, Golf and Sea Village canal front, and Andalucia bayfront. Price range: $700,000 to $3.5 million-plus depending on location, home size, and dock infrastructure.
  • Lagoon and restricted canal front: MiraBay lagoon properties and shallower canal homes that offer water views and some boating access but with more limitations. Price range: $500,000 to $900,000 for the waterfront premium.
  • Non-waterfront single family: MiraBay interior, Waterset, and other subdivisions without direct water access. Price range: $350,000 to $650,000 depending on community, size, and builder or age.
  • Townhomes and entry-level new construction: Waterset townhomes and smaller new-construction product. Price range: mid-$200,000s to $350,000 -- the lowest price points in the Apollo Beach market for new product.

Days on market in Apollo Beach vary significantly by segment. Entry-level non-waterfront homes and newer construction in Waterset tend to move faster -- 30 to 60 days when priced correctly. Waterfront properties, particularly higher-priced bay-front and deep-water canal homes, can sit 60 to 150 days as the buyer pool narrows at higher price points. The general trajectory of the Apollo Beach market has been upward, supported by the continuing growth of the South Shore corridor, ongoing employer expansion in Tampa Bay, and the persistent appeal of waterfront access at prices that barrier island markets cannot approach.

New construction is an active part of the Apollo Beach market, with multiple builders delivering homes across Waterset, the newer MiraBay sections, and emerging subdivisions. Buyers considering new construction in Apollo Beach should understand the CDD (Community Development District) fee structures that apply to most new communities, as these fees -- which fund community infrastructure and amenities -- add meaningfully to the annual carrying cost of ownership beyond the HOA fee and property taxes.

Waterfront Living in Apollo Beach

The waterfront access that Apollo Beach offers is not generic near-water proximity. The canal systems in MiraBay, Symphony Isles, Golf and Sea Village, and Andalucia connect directly to Tampa Bay -- one of the largest open-water bodies on Florida's Gulf Coast, with access to the Gulf of Mexico through Tampa Bay's mouth between Egmont Key and the Pinellas County coast. For boating purposes, Apollo Beach is not a backwater. It is a legitimate Tampa Bay waterfront address.

The practical meaning of that access varies by canal. Deep-water canals in MiraBay and Andalucia accommodate vessels of meaningful size -- center consoles, cruisers, pontoons -- without depth or bridge restrictions. Shallower canals in older Apollo Beach subdivisions may restrict vessel size and draft, which is why the distinction between deep-water and restricted-water access matters so much to the boating buyer. Before purchasing any canal-front property in Apollo Beach, a boat-owning buyer should verify the canal depth at low tide, the bridge clearance if applicable, and the distance to open bay -- these factors determine whether a specific property can actually serve the boating lifestyle the buyer envisions.

Fishing from Apollo Beach-area waters is a legitimate activity, not just a marketing claim. The grass flats of Tampa Bay off Apollo Beach support spotted sea trout, redfish, and flounder year-round, with snook in the warmer months along the mangrove edges. Tarpon move through the bay in late spring and early summer. Cobia are a spring target off the shipping channel markers. For the buyer whose priority is inshore saltwater fishing from a home dock, Apollo Beach is one of the best addresses in Hillsborough County -- the grass flat access, the channel proximity, and the bay's nutrient-rich water all contribute to fishing quality that many South Shore residents underutilize.

The kayaking and paddleboarding environment in Apollo Beach is excellent, particularly for wildlife-oriented paddling. The mangrove shorelines around Tampa Bay's edge support great blue herons, roseate spoonbills, ospreys, and wading birds in numbers that regularly surprise visitors. The warm water discharge from the Big Bend Power Station creates a year-round warm-water zone that attracts manatees from November through April -- paddlers and kayakers who position themselves near the outflow during these months are virtually guaranteed manatee encounters at extremely close range.

TECO Manatee Viewing Center

The Tampa Electric Manatee Viewing Center on Dickman Road is one of the most visited free attractions in the Tampa Bay region and the single experience most closely associated with Apollo Beach in the minds of people who have never visited the community. The center is open annually from November 1 through April 15, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily, with no admission fee and free parking. The warm water discharge from the Big Bend Power Station creates a thermal refuge for manatees seeking relief from cooler Tampa Bay temperatures during the winter months, and the concentrations that result are extraordinary.

During peak viewing days in January and February, manatee concentrations at the viewing center can reach hundreds of animals visible from the elevated boardwalks and observation platforms. The center's design -- multiple viewing decks at different elevations, with clear sightlines to the warm water discharge area -- allows visitors to observe manatees at close range without disturbing them. The facility also includes an education center, nature trails through the surrounding preserve, and during the Tampa Bay Rays offseason, a stingray touch tank exhibit.

For Apollo Beach residents, the Manatee Viewing Center is not a tourist destination -- it is a neighborhood amenity. The winter ritual of watching manatee gatherings from the boardwalk, taking visiting family members to see the animals, and observing the seasonal rhythm of the manatee population is part of what makes Apollo Beach different from every other South Shore community. The center's presence also has a practical real estate effect: it reinforces the community's identity as a waterfront, wildlife-connected place, which supports property values across the Apollo Beach market.

Beyond the manatee center, the broader Apollo Beach waterfront supports manatee sightings year-round for residents with bay access. Canal-front homeowners in MiraBay and the established Apollo Beach neighborhoods regularly encounter manatees in the canals -- particularly in spring and early summer when the animals disperse from the warm-water discharge zone into the surrounding bay and canal network. For many buyers, this resident wildlife presence is a meaningful quality-of-life factor that is difficult to quantify but impossible to ignore.

Outdoor Recreation Beyond the Manatees

Apollo Beach's outdoor recreation extends well beyond the manatee viewing center, though that center tends to dominate any description of the community's natural assets. The full picture of outdoor access in Apollo Beach includes fishing, boating, kayaking, paddleboarding, trail use, and park access across a variety of environments.

Apollo Beach Nature Preserve: A protected mangrove and bay shoreline preserve adjacent to the Apollo Beach residential area. The preserve provides shore fishing access, wildlife viewing, and a natural counterpoint to the developed canal communities. The mangrove habitat here supports the same wading bird populations and juvenile fish nursery function that makes the Apollo Beach bay shoreline so productive for inshore fishing.

E.G. Simmons Regional Park: Located in nearby Ruskin, within easy reach of Apollo Beach, E.G. Simmons provides boat launch access to Tampa Bay's southern reach, camping facilities, picnic areas, and fishing from the shore and from the bayfront. For Apollo Beach residents who want Tampa Bay access without a private canal, E.G. Simmons is the most accessible public launch point in the area.

Waterset Trails: The 12-mile trail network within Waterset is the most developed land-based recreational infrastructure in the Apollo Beach area. The trails connect through the community's park and pond system, providing a genuine recreational walking and biking environment that does not require leaving the community. For residents of Waterset and the surrounding neighborhoods, the trail system is a daily-use amenity rather than a weekend destination.

Little Manatee River State Park: Less than 15 miles from Apollo Beach, this state park provides kayaking and canoeing on the Little Manatee River -- a designated Florida Paddling Trail -- along with hiking, horseback riding, and camping in an environment that contrasts significantly with the bay-front and canal landscape of Apollo Beach proper. For residents who want freshwater paddling and woodland hiking alongside their saltwater bay access, the park is a meaningful nearby option.

Schools in Apollo Beach

Apollo Beach is served by the Hillsborough County Public School District -- one of the 10 largest school districts in the United States, covering the full range from highly rated suburban schools to underperforming urban campuses. The Apollo Beach-area schools occupy the district's middle tier, with specific standouts that drive residential decisions for families with school-age children.

Waterset Charter School (K-8): The standout educational institution in the Apollo Beach market. Waterset Charter is a public charter school located within the Waterset community, serving grades K through 8 with enrollment through a Hillsborough County lottery system. The school's within-community location makes it walkable for Waterset residents, an amenity that is genuinely unusual in suburban South Shore. The charter format allows for a structured curriculum approach, and the school's performance ratings have been consistently positive. Waitlists are common, and families prioritizing Waterset Charter enrollment should plan accordingly.

Apollo Beach Elementary School: The established elementary school serving the core Apollo Beach community, including MiraBay, Andalucia, and the older Apollo Beach neighborhoods. Apollo Beach Elementary has received generally strong ratings and serves the established waterfront community population effectively.

Inez Doby Elementary School: Serving portions of the Apollo Beach and South Shore area, Inez Doby provides additional elementary capacity in a growing market where school boundaries shift as population increases.

Eisenhower Middle School: The primary middle school serving Apollo Beach area students. Eisenhower has generally performed at or above district averages and serves the transition from elementary education for the community's student population.

East Bay High School: The district high school serving Apollo Beach, Gibsonton, and the surrounding South Shore area. East Bay High has a competitive athletic program and the full range of AP coursework that the Hillsborough County district provides across its high schools. Families coming from the highest-performing school districts in the metro -- Steinbrenner, Newsome, or the magnet programs centered in Tampa -- should evaluate East Bay relative to their specific expectations.

Dorothy C. York Innovation Academy: A specialized learning option within the Apollo Beach area, offering a technology and STEM-focused curriculum for families seeking an alternative to the traditional school structure.

Private school options in the South Shore area are more limited than in the northern Hillsborough County suburbs. Families with strong private school requirements should factor in the drive to established private institutions in Brandon, Riverview, or South Tampa, which adds commute time to the school decision calculus.

Getting Around: The Apollo Beach Commute

Apollo Beach's location at the southern edge of Hillsborough County places it in a specific relationship with Tampa's employment centers that every buyer should understand before committing to a purchase. The community is not an easy commute from downtown Tampa on a typical weekday -- the distances and the road infrastructure between Apollo Beach and the urban core create meaningful drive times that are part of the lifestyle trade-off buyers make when they choose Apollo Beach over closer-in suburban communities.

To downtown Tampa: Approximately 25 to 35 miles depending on the specific Apollo Beach address, via I-75 North or US 41/Tamiami Trail. In off-peak conditions, the drive is 30 to 40 minutes. In morning rush hour northbound and afternoon southbound, the drive routinely extends to 50 to 70 minutes or more, particularly during school months and major events.

To MacDill Air Force Base: Approximately 15 to 20 miles via US 41 North or the Selmon Expressway. MacDill's position on the Interbay Peninsula south of downtown Tampa places it closer to Apollo Beach than to many northern Hillsborough County communities, and the base's proximity is a significant driver of Apollo Beach's military family population. Commute times from Apollo Beach to MacDill gate run approximately 25 to 40 minutes depending on conditions and the specific gate used.

To Brandon and Riverview: 10 to 20 miles east via US 301 or SR 60. Brandon's employment and retail centers are accessible in 20 to 30 minutes from most Apollo Beach addresses, making the Brandon corridor's commercial infrastructure functionally part of Apollo Beach's daily life.

To Tampa International Airport: Approximately 25 to 35 miles via I-75 North and SR 60 West, or via the Selmon Expressway. Non-peak drive times run 35 to 50 minutes. Airport proximity is a meaningful consideration for buyers who travel frequently for business.

Restaurants, Shopping, and Daily Life

Apollo Beach's commercial infrastructure has grown significantly as the community's population has expanded, but it remains a suburban area where most meaningful retail, dining, and service activity requires leaving the immediate community for nearby Riverview, Brandon, or the US 41 corridor. Understanding this reality -- and whether it is a trade-off the specific buyer is comfortable making -- is part of the honest assessment of Apollo Beach as a place to live.

Waterfront dining: Apollo Beach's dining identity is built around its waterfront restaurants. Finn's Dockside Bar and Grill on Golf and Sea Boulevard is a local institution -- an open-air waterfront bar and restaurant on the water with dock access, cold beer, fresh seafood, and the unpretentious waterfront Florida atmosphere that defines what Apollo Beach dining is at its best. Circles Waterfront Restaurant is the area's established sit-down waterfront option, offering a more complete menu alongside the water views. Both represent the core of Apollo Beach's dining culture: casual, water-adjacent, and built around the community's bay identity.

Everyday dining: Apollo Beach and the surrounding South Shore corridor support most of the chain and regional casual dining options that daily life requires. First Watch for breakfast, Maple Street Biscuit Company for brunch, and the Apollo Beach Diner for classic American fare serve the community's everyday dining needs. The Riverview and Brandon commercial corridors, 10 to 20 minutes away, expand the dining options substantially.

Grocery and retail: A Publix serves the community within the Apollo Beach retail center, with additional options in Riverview and Brandon for buyers who want more grocery variety. Major retail destinations -- Target, larger shopping centers, and specialty retail -- are concentrated in Brandon and Riverview, a 15 to 25 minute drive.

Healthcare in Apollo Beach

The immediate Apollo Beach area does not have a major hospital. The nearest full-service hospital facilities are in the Brandon and Riverview area to the northeast and in South Tampa to the north. Advent Health Riverview is the closest full-service hospital to Apollo Beach, approximately 15 to 20 minutes north. The Advent Health Brandon campus provides additional capacity and specialty care approximately 20 to 25 minutes northeast. Tampa General Hospital -- one of the Tampa Bay region's leading academic medical centers -- is approximately 30 to 40 minutes north and serves as the regional referral center for complex and specialized care.

Medical offices, urgent care facilities, and outpatient specialty clinics have expanded significantly in the South Shore corridor over the past decade, driven by the population growth in the Apollo Beach, Riverview, and Wimauma areas. For routine and non-emergency healthcare needs, Apollo Beach residents have reasonable access to primary care, specialist offices, and urgent care without driving to Tampa. The gap is in emergency and complex inpatient care, where the nearest facilities require a drive of 15 to 20 minutes minimum.

Who Buys in Apollo Beach

The Apollo Beach buyer pool is more diverse than any single community profile captures. The community attracts buyers across a wide range of demographics, price points, and lifestyle priorities -- but several distinct buyer profiles dominate the market.

The waterfront lifestyle buyer: The buyer who has decided that direct bay or canal access is a non-negotiable lifestyle requirement. This person likely owns or plans to own a boat, has fishing or water recreation as a central leisure activity, and is willing to make the South Shore commute trade-off to live on the water. They are looking at MiraBay deep-water canals, Andalucia, Symphony Isles, and the older Apollo Beach canal neighborhoods. Price range is typically $600,000 to $2 million-plus. This is Apollo Beach's core buyer identity -- the person the community was built to serve.

The MacDill military family: Active duty and retired military families connected to MacDill Air Force Base make up a meaningful segment of the Apollo Beach buyer pool. The base's proximity -- 15 to 20 miles north -- combined with the community's family-friendly infrastructure, Waterset Charter School access, and the general South Shore value proposition relative to the Tampa coastal markets creates a strong draw. This buyer is often relocating quickly, needs schools decided before a move date, and prioritizes value and community infrastructure over waterfront premium.

The Waterset new construction family: Buyers entering the Apollo Beach market through Waterset are typically younger families drawn by the master-planned community's schools, amenities, and new construction availability at accessible price points. These buyers are often first-time homeowners or buyers moving up from smaller starter homes, and they are choosing Waterset's $350,000 to $550,000 range over comparable-priced options in Riverview or Wesley Chapel because of the specific Waterset value package: charter school access, resort amenities, trail connectivity, and a strong community identity.

The wildlife and nature-oriented buyer: Buyers who specifically identify the Manatee Viewing Center, the bay access, the wading bird populations, and the general natural environment of Apollo Beach as primary decision factors. This buyer may not be a boater -- they are kayakers, birdwatchers, and naturalists who want the waterfront environment without necessarily requiring a private dock. They end up in a range of Apollo Beach communities, sometimes in Waterset for the trails, sometimes in waterfront-adjacent properties without private dock access, and sometimes at the entry-level price points that give them proximity to the bay environment without the waterfront premium.

The relocation buyer from out of state: Apollo Beach's waterfront identity and its position on the Tampa Bay metro's southern edge make it a consistent target for out-of-state buyers relocating to the Tampa Bay area. These buyers often begin their search with barrier island or South Tampa targets and discover Apollo Beach when waterfront access at coastal prices proves unavailable in their preferred range. The I did not know this existed reaction is common among buyers who tour MiraBay or Andalucia for the first time -- the combination of bay access, resort infrastructure, and price points significantly below comparable barrier island product consistently surprises buyers whose research started with Clearwater or St. Pete Beach.

Apollo Beach vs. the South Shore Alternatives

Understanding Apollo Beach's position in the South Shore real estate landscape requires comparing it honestly to its nearest neighbors, because the right community for a specific buyer depends on what they are actually optimizing for.

Apollo Beach vs. Riverview: Riverview is larger, more commercially developed, and generally less expensive for non-waterfront product. Riverview has better highway access to Tampa and more retail infrastructure embedded in the community. Riverview does not have Tampa Bay waterfront access. The choice between Apollo Beach and Riverview is a straightforward water-versus-convenience trade-off at most price points.

Apollo Beach vs. Ruskin: Ruskin is immediately west of Apollo Beach and shares the South Shore bay shoreline. Ruskin has more agricultural character, less community infrastructure, and generally lower prices. E.G. Simmons Regional Park provides bay access in Ruskin, but the waterfront community development that characterizes Apollo Beach is less extensive in Ruskin. The buyer who wants South Shore waterfront access at the most accessible price points sometimes ends up in Ruskin -- the buyer who wants the full Apollo Beach community infrastructure chooses Apollo Beach.

Apollo Beach vs. the barrier islands: The comparison buyers most frequently make when entering the Apollo Beach market from outside the Tampa Bay area. Clearwater Beach, St. Pete Beach, Treasure Island, and the Anna Maria Island coast offer Gulf of Mexico-front access and beach walkability but at prices that have generally removed them from the consideration set for most buyers who want a primary residence rather than a vacation investment. Apollo Beach offers bay access, boating, fishing, and waterfront lifestyle at a fraction of the barrier island price point, with no surge pricing, no seasonal rental overlay, and a genuine year-round residential community. For the buyer who cares about boats more than beaches, Apollo Beach is not a compromise -- it is a better answer.

Working With Barrett Henry in Apollo Beach

Barrett Henry has worked the Apollo Beach and South Shore markets as a licensed Florida Realtor, based in the Tampa Bay area and representing buyers and sellers across the full range of Apollo Beach's communities -- from entry-level new construction in Waterset to deep-water canal estates in MiraBay and bayfront properties in Andalucia. The Apollo Beach market rewards local knowledge: understanding which canals are deep-water and which restrict vessel access, which MiraBay sections have the strongest community identity, which Waterset phases have the best school access, and where the value pockets are in the older Apollo Beach subdivisions for the waterfront buyer willing to look past dated finishes.

For buyers relocating to Apollo Beach from outside Florida, the market can be disorienting -- the community structure, the waterfront access hierarchy, the CDD fee landscape, and the school choice complexity all require local context to navigate effectively. For sellers in Apollo Beach, positioning a property accurately within the market's segmented structure -- waterfront tier, community identity, school access -- is the difference between a listing that sells in 30 days and one that sits for 150.

The Apollo Beach guides, community profiles, and market analysis on this site are written with the goal of giving buyers and sellers the honest, specific information that generic real estate portals do not provide. If the information here has been useful and you are ready to take the next step, Barrett Henry can be reached directly at (813) 733-7907 or barrett@nowtb.com. The Apollo Beach market moves quickly at the right price points, and the right property sold correctly does not wait long for the right buyer.

title: Apollo Beach 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ homes in Apollo Beach typically range from $280,000-$500,000. Top active adult communities in the area include Waterset active adult sections and nearby Sun City Center, offering resort-style amenities, low-maintenance living, and an active social calendar.

Why Active Adults Choose Apollo Beach

Apollo Beach has become an increasingly popular destination for active adults and retirees seeking the Florida lifestyle without sacrificing access to quality healthcare, cultural amenities, and everyday convenience. Apollo Beach is a waterfront community on Tampa Bay's eastern shore, offering canal-front homes, bay access, and a resort-style lifestyle. The MiraBay and Waterset master-planned communities are among the most sought-after addresses in southern Hillsborough County.

The appeal of 55+ living in Apollo Beach extends far beyond the weather. Active adult communities in this area provide a turnkey lifestyle that includes exterior home maintenance, landscaping, and community amenities - freeing residents to focus on the activities, travel, and social connections that make retirement fulfilling. With no state income tax, Florida remains one of the most tax-friendly states for retirees, and Apollo Beach's cost of living compares favorably to many other retirement destinations along the Gulf Coast.

Whether you are planning a full-time relocation, seeking a seasonal winter residence, or downsizing from a larger home in the area, Apollo Beach's 55+ market offers a range of options from maintenance-free villas to single-family homes with full resort amenities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping active adult buyers find the right community and home to match their lifestyle and budget.

Top 55+ Communities in and Near Apollo Beach

The following communities represent the best options for 55+ buyers in the Apollo Beach area. Each offers a distinct lifestyle, amenity package, and price point.

Waterset active adult sections

Waterset active adult sections is among the most established and well-regarded active adult communities serving Apollo Beach residents. This community offers a comprehensive lifestyle package that includes maintained exteriors, community pools, fitness facilities, and an extensive calendar of social events, clubs, and organized activities. Homes range from attached villas with two bedrooms and two bathrooms to larger single-family residences with three bedrooms, dens, and two-car garages. Floor plans are designed specifically for active adult living, with single-story layouts, wide doorways, step-free entries, and owners suites positioned for privacy. The community atmosphere is welcoming and social, with residents forming lasting friendships through shared activities that range from golf and tennis to card games, art classes, and group travel.

nearby Sun City Center

nearby Sun City Center provides another excellent option for 55+ buyers in the Apollo Beach area. This community appeals to active adults who want a maintenance-free lifestyle without sacrificing home quality or community amenities. Properties here feature modern finishes, energy-efficient construction, and thoughtful floor plans that accommodate both daily living and entertaining. The amenity package typically includes a community clubhouse, pool, walking trails, and organized social programming. Residents appreciate the sense of community that develops naturally when neighbors share similar life stages and interests. The location provides convenient access to healthcare facilities, shopping, dining, and the cultural attractions that make Apollo Beach such an appealing retirement destination.

Price & Monthly Cost Overview for Apollo Beach 55+ Homes

Understanding the full cost of 55+ living - including purchase price, HOA fees, and additional community charges - is essential for retirement planning. The table below outlines typical costs for active adult properties in the Apollo Beach area.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Includes
2-Bed / 2-Bath Villa$280,000-$500,000$200-$500Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2-Bath Single Family$280,000-$500,000$250-$550Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Premium$280,000-$500,000$300-$600Full maintenance, lawn, amenities, cable
Condo / Attached Villa$280,000-$500,000$350-$700Exterior, roof, insurance, amenities

Monthly HOA fees in 55+ communities cover a wide range of services. Some communities include exterior painting, roof maintenance, lawn care, pest control, cable TV, and community amenities in a single monthly fee. Others charge separately for certain services. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a complete cost breakdown for any community you are considering. Contact Barrett for current pricing and availability.

Amenities & Lifestyle in Apollo Beach 55+ Communities

The amenity package is what truly sets 55+ communities apart from traditional neighborhoods. Active adult communities in the Apollo Beach area offer lifestyle amenities that rival upscale resorts.

Fitness and Wellness

Most 55+ communities in Apollo Beach include fitness centers equipped with cardio machines, strength training equipment, and stretching areas designed for active adults. Many offer group fitness classes such as water aerobics, yoga, tai chi, and low-impact cardio that cater specifically to the 55+ demographic. Walking trails, swimming pools, and spa facilities provide additional wellness options that encourage daily physical activity in a comfortable, age-appropriate setting.

Social Clubs and Activities

The social calendar in a well-run 55+ community is remarkably full. Residents in Apollo Beach area communities can typically choose from dozens of clubs and interest groups covering everything from bridge and mahjong to woodworking, photography, gardening, and performing arts. Organized activities such as day trips, dinner outings, holiday celebrations, and educational seminars keep the community engaged and connected. For many residents, this built-in social network is the single greatest benefit of 55+ living.

Golf, Tennis, and Recreation

Golf remains a cornerstone of the 55+ lifestyle in Hillsborough County, and many active adult communities near Apollo Beach offer on-site or nearby golf courses. Tennis and pickleball courts have become increasingly popular, with organized leagues and social play available most days. Bocce ball, shuffleboard, and horseshoes are additional recreational options that provide both exercise and social interaction in a relaxed, friendly setting.

Pools and Outdoor Living

Community pools in Apollo Beach 55+ neighborhoods are designed for both exercise and relaxation. Heated pools extend the swimming season year-round, while separate spa and soaking pools provide therapeutic benefits. Many communities feature poolside pavilions, outdoor grills, and covered seating areas where residents gather for impromptu socializing and organized pool parties throughout the year.

Healthcare Access Near Apollo Beach

Access to quality healthcare is a top priority for 55+ buyers, and Apollo Beach delivers excellent options. The greater Tampa Bay area is home to some of Florida's finest medical facilities, ensuring that active adult residents are never far from the care they need.

Major healthcare providers serving the Apollo Beach area include BayCare Health System, AdventHealth (formerly Florida Hospital), HCA Healthcare facilities, and Tampa General Hospital - consistently ranked among the top hospitals in Florida. Specialty care, including cardiology, orthopedics, oncology, and rehabilitation, is readily available at multiple facilities within a short drive of most Apollo Beach neighborhoods.

Many 55+ communities in the area also provide on-site or nearby primary care offices, pharmacy services, and wellness programs that make routine healthcare convenient and accessible. The combination of world-class medical facilities and community-level wellness resources gives Apollo Beach 55+ residents confidence that their healthcare needs will be met at every stage of retirement.

What 55+ Buyers Should Know

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations beyond a traditional home purchase. Barrett Henry advises every active adult buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Age verification requirements: Under the Housing for Older Persons Act, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one resident who is 55 or older. Communities enforce this through age verification at purchase. Some communities also restrict the age of permanent residents under 55, though policies vary.
  • Deed restrictions: 55+ communities typically have deed restrictions that govern modifications, rentals, pets, and use of common areas. Read these documents carefully to ensure they align with your lifestyle. Some communities restrict pet sizes, limit the number of overnight guests, or require owner-occupancy for a minimum period before renting.
  • HOA governance: Understand how the HOA is structured, who serves on the board, and how decisions are made. Attend an HOA meeting before purchasing if possible. A well-governed HOA with transparent finances and responsive management is essential to a positive 55+ living experience.
  • Reserve fund health: Review the reserve study and financial statements to ensure the community has adequate funds for future repairs and replacements. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments that create unexpected financial burdens for residents on fixed incomes.
  • Resale considerations: Consider the community's historical resale performance and current market dynamics. Some 55+ communities experience higher inventory levels due to natural turnover, which can affect resale timing and pricing. Barrett Henry can provide comparable sales data to help you evaluate resale potential.
  • Insurance requirements: Verify what insurance is covered by the HOA and what you need to carry individually. Some communities include master insurance policies that cover exterior structures and common areas, while individual unit owners are responsible for interior coverage and personal property.

Why Apollo Beach?

Waterfront living with canal-front homes, Tampa Bay access, the TECO Manatee Viewing Center, and a 25-minute commute to downtown Tampa via US-41 or I-75.

With a population of approximately 25,000 and a median home price around $430,000, Apollo Beach provides an accessible entry point to the Tampa Bay lifestyle. The local economy is supported by Tampa Electric (TECO), nearby MacDill AFB, medical and retail employers along the US-41 corridor, and the broader region offers cultural attractions including performing arts, museums, professional sports, and waterfront dining that keep active adults engaged and entertained.

For 55+ buyers exploring Apollo Beach real estate, the combination of Florida's tax advantages, the area's healthcare infrastructure, and the quality of available active adult communities makes Apollo Beach a compelling retirement destination. Whether you are relocating from out of state or downsizing from a larger home in Hillsborough County, Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can guide you through every step of the process. Learn more about selling your current home or contact Barrett to begin your search.

Frequently Asked Questions About Apollo Beach 55+ Homes

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community?

Federal law requires that at least 80 percent of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Most communities in the Apollo Beach area allow younger spouses or partners to reside with a qualifying 55+ owner. However, policies regarding other household members under 55 vary by community. Some restrict younger residents entirely, while others allow exceptions with board approval. Barrett Henry can clarify the age policies for any community you are considering.

What do HOA fees cover in Apollo Beach 55+ communities?

HOA fees in Apollo Beach 55+ communities typically cover exterior home maintenance, roof reserves, lawn care, common area landscaping, community amenity operations, security, and sometimes cable TV, internet, and pest control. The scope of coverage varies significantly between communities, so it is important to get a detailed breakdown before comparing fees between different neighborhoods. Higher fees are not necessarily a negative - they often reflect a more comprehensive maintenance and amenity package.

Are 55+ homes a good investment?

55+ homes in the Apollo Beach area have generally appreciated in line with or slightly below the broader market, depending on the specific community and its management quality. The primary value proposition of 55+ homes is lifestyle rather than investment return - the maintenance-free living, social amenities, and community atmosphere provide a quality of life that is difficult to quantify financially. That said, well-managed communities with strong HOAs and desirable locations have shown solid appreciation over time.

Can I rent out my 55+ home in Apollo Beach?

Rental policies vary by community. Some 55+ communities in the Apollo Beach area permit rentals with restrictions such as minimum lease terms (often 6-12 months), annual rental limits, and tenant age requirements. Others prohibit rentals entirely or restrict them to hardship cases with board approval. If future rental flexibility is important to you, verify the community's rental policy before purchasing.

What is the social atmosphere like in Apollo Beach 55+ communities?

Most 55+ communities near Apollo Beach foster a warm, welcoming social atmosphere with organized activities, clubs, and events that make it easy for newcomers to connect with neighbors. From card groups and book clubs to organized outings and holiday celebrations, the social calendar provides ample opportunities to build friendships and stay engaged. Many residents describe the social aspect of 55+ living as the most unexpected and rewarding benefit of their purchase decision.

title: Apollo Beach Condos & Townhomes
content:
Quick Answer

Condos and townhomes in Apollo Beach range from $230,000-$420,000, offering low-maintenance living with community amenities. Popular options include MiraBay townhomes and Waterset townhomes. Buyers should carefully review association finances, insurance, and warrantability before purchasing.

Why Condos & Townhomes Are Popular in Apollo Beach

Condos and townhomes represent one of the fastest-growing segments of the Apollo Beach real estate market. Buyers are drawn to the lower price points, reduced maintenance responsibilities, and community amenities that attached and multi-family housing provides. Apollo Beach is a waterfront community on Tampa Bay's eastern shore, offering canal-front homes, bay access, and a resort-style lifestyle. The MiraBay and Waterset master-planned communities are among the most sought-after addresses in southern Hillsborough County.

For first-time buyers, condos and townhomes in Apollo Beach offer an affordable entry point into homeownership. For downsizers, they provide a lock-and-leave lifestyle that eliminates the burden of yard maintenance, exterior upkeep, and roof repairs. And for investors, the strong rental demand in the Apollo Beach area makes condos and townhomes an attractive addition to a real estate portfolio - provided the association allows rentals.

The Apollo Beach market offers a wide range of condo and townhome options, from garden-style condos with ground-floor access to multi-story townhomes with private garages and rooftop terraces. Whether you prioritize walkability, commute convenience, or community amenities, there is a condo or townhome community in Apollo Beach that fits your needs. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping buyers navigate the unique considerations of condo and townhome purchases.

Popular Condo & Townhome Communities in Apollo Beach

The following communities represent some of the best options for condo and townhome buyers in the Apollo Beach area.

MiraBay townhomes

The community offers a range of floor plans from compact two-bedroom units to spacious three-bedroom residences with modern finishes. Residents enjoy community amenities including a pool, fitness area, and well-maintained common spaces. The location provides convenient access to major employers, shopping centers, and transportation corridors, making MiraBay townhomes particularly popular with working professionals and young families who want an affordable home in a desirable location.

Waterset townhomes

Waterset townhomes appeals to buyers who value a well-managed community with consistent standards and solid finances. Units here feature updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and open floor plans that maximize living space. The community amenity package includes pool access, covered parking, and professionally maintained grounds. Waterset townhomes has maintained a strong resale track record, with properties typically selling within a reasonable timeframe and at competitive prices relative to the broader Apollo Beach market.

Andalucia villas

Andalucia villas offers another excellent option for condo and townhome buyers in Apollo Beach. This community provides a mix of unit types that accommodate different household sizes and budgets. Common amenities include a pool, playground or recreation area, and visitor parking. The HOA is well-managed with adequate reserves, and the community has a track record of stable fees and minimal special assessments. For buyers prioritizing value and long-term stability, Andalucia villas deserves serious consideration.

Andalucia villas

Andalucia villas rounds out the top condo and townhome options in Apollo Beach with units that balance affordability and quality. This community attracts a diverse mix of first-time buyers, downsizers, and investors who appreciate the combination of reasonable pricing, solid HOA management, and a convenient location. Depending on the specific unit, buyers may find updated interiors with granite countertops, stainless appliances, and luxury vinyl flooring that give the home a fresh, modern feel.

Price & HOA Overview for Apollo Beach Condos & Townhomes

The following table provides general pricing guidance for condos and townhomes in the Apollo Beach market. HOA fees vary by community and the services included.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Typical Features
1-Bed / 1-Bath Condo$230,000-$420,000$200-$400Pool, basic maintenance

2-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$230,000-$420,000$150-$350Garage, exterior maintenance
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$230,000-$420,000$175-$400Garage, pool, exterior maintenance

HOA fees for condos are generally higher than for townhomes because condo associations typically cover more services including exterior insurance, roof maintenance, painting, and sometimes water, sewer, and trash. Townhome HOAs tend to cover less, with owners responsible for their own exterior maintenance and insurance in some communities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed HOA fee breakdown and financial review for any community. Contact Barrett for current listings and pricing.

Condo vs. Townhome: Understanding the Differences

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they have important legal and practical differences that affect ownership, financing, and daily life.

Ownership Structure

In a condo, you own the interior space of your unit and share ownership of common areas (building exterior, roof, grounds, amenities) with other unit owners through the association. In a townhome, you typically own the structure and the land beneath it, with shared ownership limited to common areas like pools, parks, and private roads. This distinction affects insurance requirements, maintenance responsibilities, and how future improvements are funded.

Maintenance Responsibility

Condo associations in Apollo Beach generally handle all exterior maintenance, including the roof, building envelope, painting, landscaping, and common areas. Townhome owners often retain responsibility for their own roof, driveway, and limited exterior maintenance, though the HOA may handle landscaping and common area upkeep. This difference is reflected in HOA fees - condo fees tend to be higher because they cover more services.

Privacy and Space

Townhomes typically offer more interior space, multiple floors, a private garage, and sometimes a small yard or pation. Condos tend to be single-level units that may share walls on multiple sides. For buyers who prioritize privacy and the feel of a traditional home, townhomes are often the better choice. For buyers who prefer single-level living and minimal maintenance, condos may be more appropriate.

What Condo & Townhome Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome in Apollo Beach requires due diligence beyond what a traditional single-family home purchase demands. Barrett Henry advises every buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Association financial health: Request the most recent financial statements, budget, and reserve study. Look for adequate reserves (ideally 20 percent or more of the annual budget), stable fee history, and no pending special assessments. Florida law now requires reserve studies and adequate funding for structural components following legislative changes in recent years.
  • Reserve fund compliance: Florida statutes now require condo associations to maintain funded reserves for structural components, including the roof, foundation, and load-bearing walls. Verify that the association is in compliance, as underfunded reserves can trigger special assessments and affect property values.
  • Insurance coverage: Understand the difference between the association's master policy and your individual HO-6 policy. The master policy typically covers the building exterior and common areas, while your HO-6 covers your interior, personal property, and liability. Verify coverage limits and deductibles for both policies.
  • Rules and restrictions: Review the association's governing documents, including CC&Rs, bylaws, and rules and regulations. Common restrictions cover pets, rentals, parking, noise, renovations, and use of common areas. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the unit in the future, verify the association's rental policy. Many Apollo Beach associations limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously, impose minimum lease terms, or require tenant approval by the board. Some associations prohibit rentals entirely.
  • Pending litigation and violations: Ask whether the association is involved in any lawsuits and whether the building has any outstanding code violations. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Financing Condos: Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable

Financing a condo purchase in Apollo Beach requires understanding the distinction between warrantable and non-warrantable condominiums, as this classification directly affects your mortgage options.

A warrantable condo meets the guidelines set by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which means it qualifies for conventional financing with competitive interest rates and standard down payment requirements. To be warrantable, a condo association generally must have adequate reserves, no more than 15 percent of units delinquent on fees, no single entity owning more than 20 percent of units, and at least 50 percent of units owner-occupied.

A non-warrantable condo fails to meet one or more of these guidelines, which limits financing options to portfolio loans, credit unions, or cash purchases. Non-warrantable condos often carry higher interest rates, larger down payment requirements, and fewer lender options. Common reasons a Apollo Beach condo might be non-warrantable include high investor concentration, pending litigation, inadequate reserves, or a single entity owning too many units.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can help you determine the warrantability status of any condo you are considering and connect you with lenders who specialize in both warrantable and non-warrantable financing. Contact Barrett to discuss your financing options.

Lifestyle Benefits of Condo & Townhome Living

Beyond the financial considerations, condos and townhomes in Apollo Beach offer lifestyle advantages that appeal to a wide range of buyers.

  • Low maintenance: Say goodbye to weekend yard work, exterior painting, and roof repairs. Condo and townhome living frees up time for the activities you actually enjoy.
  • Community amenities: Many Apollo Beach communities include pools, fitness centers, and social spaces that would cost thousands to replicate in a single-family home setting.
  • Affordability: Condos and townhomes typically offer a lower entry price than comparable single-family homes, making homeownership accessible to first-time buyers and those on a budget.
  • Location: Attached housing communities are often situated in prime locations near employment centers, shopping, dining, and entertainment - areas where single-family homes may be priced significantly higher.
  • Security: Many condo communities in Apollo Beach feature controlled access, security cameras, and well-lit common areas that provide an added layer of safety.
  • Lock and leave: For frequent travelers, seasonal residents, and busy professionals, the ability to lock the door and leave without worrying about yard maintenance or home security is invaluable.

Why Apollo Beach?

Waterfront living with canal-front homes, Tampa Bay access, the TECO Manatee Viewing Center, and a 25-minute commute to downtown Tampa via US-41 or I-75.

Apollo Beach has a population of approximately 25,000 and a median home price of $430,000. The local economy benefits from Tampa Electric (TECO), nearby MacDill AFB, medical and retail employers along the US-41 corridor, creating consistent demand for housing at all price points. For buyers exploring Apollo Beach real estate, condos and townhomes offer an affordable, low-maintenance path to homeownership in one of Florida's most dynamic markets.

Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an affordable entry point, a downsizer seeking a simpler lifestyle, or an investor building a rental portfolio, Apollo Beach's condo and townhome market has options to match your goals. Frequently Asked Questions About Apollo Beach Condos & Townhomes

How much are HOA fees for condos in Apollo Beach?

Monthly HOA fees for condos in Apollo Beach typically range from $200 to $500, depending on the community's amenity package, age, and services included. Fees that cover exterior insurance, roof reserves, water, sewer, and trash tend to be higher but reduce the owner's out-of-pocket costs for those items. Barrett Henry can provide exact fee information and a breakdown of included services for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my condo or townhome in Apollo Beach?

Rental policies vary by association. Some Apollo Beach communities allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on total rental units. Others prohibit rentals or require board approval for each tenant. If rental flexibility is important to you, verify the association's policy before purchasing and confirm that the current rental cap has not been reached.

What is a special assessment and should I be worried?

A special assessment is a one-time charge levied by the association to cover unexpected expenses or projects that exceed reserve fund capacity. Common triggers include roof replacement, elevator modernization, structural repairs, and insurance premium increases. While special assessments are a normal part of condo ownership, frequent or large assessments may indicate poor financial planning. Reviewing the reserve study and financial statements before purchasing helps assess this risk.

Do I need separate insurance for my condo?

Yes. While the association's master policy covers the building exterior and common areas, individual condo owners in Apollo Beach need an HO-6 policy that covers interior finishes, personal property, liability, and loss assessment coverage. Loss assessment coverage is particularly important, as it protects you if the association levies a special assessment for a covered loss that exceeds the master policy's coverage.

What is the difference between a condo and a townhome for financing purposes?

Condos face additional financing scrutiny because lenders evaluate the entire association - not just the individual unit. Townhomes, which typically convey land with the structure, are often financed more like single-family homes with fewer association-level requirements. However, some townhome communities are structured as condominiums from a legal standpoint, which triggers condo financing requirements.   • Rules and restrictions: Read the CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions) thoroughly. Common restrictions cover exterior paint colors, landscaping, parking, rentals, pets, and home-based businesses. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the property in the future, verify the community's rental policies. Many gated communities in Apollo Beach limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously or impose minimum lease terms.

  • Pending litigation: Ask the HOA whether any lawsuits are pending against the association. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

title: Apollo Beach Homes with Pool
content:
Quick Answer

Apollo Beach pool homes typically range from $370,000-$900,000+, with screened enclosures being standard across Hillsborough County. Buyers should budget for pool inspection, resurfacing timelines, and updated equipment when evaluating resale pool properties.

Why Pool Homes Are So Popular in Apollo Beach

In Apollo Beach, a swimming pool is not a luxury - it is a way of life. With average temperatures above 70 degrees for nine months of the year and summer highs regularly reaching the mid-90s, residents rely on their backyard pools for daily relief, weekend entertaining, and year-round outdoor living. Apollo Beach is a waterfront community on Tampa Bay's eastern shore, offering canal-front homes, bay access, and a resort-style lifestyle. The MiraBay and Waterset master-planned communities are among the most sought-after addresses in southern Hillsborough County.

Pool homes in Apollo Beach consistently command higher resale values than comparable non-pool properties. According to recent market data, homes with pools sell for approximately 5-8 percent more than similar homes without one. For families, retirees, and remote workers who spend significant time at home, a pool transforms the backyard into a private retreat that rivals any resort.

The popularity of pool homes has only increased since 2020, when more buyers began prioritizing outdoor living space, home offices with views, and personal recreation areas. In Apollo Beach, that trend shows no signs of slowing, with pool-equipped listings often receiving multiple offers within days of hitting the market.

Best Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Apollo Beach

Choosing the right neighborhood is just as important as finding the right pool. Here are the top areas in Apollo Beach where pool homes are most prevalent and desirable.

MiraBay

MiraBay is widely regarded as one of the premier neighborhoods in Apollo Beach for pool homes. Properties here tend to feature larger lots, established landscaping, and pools that have been well-maintained over the years. Many homes in MiraBay include screened pool enclosures with extended lanais, outdoor kitchens, and tropical plantings that create a true backyard oasis. The neighborhood offers convenient access to shopping, dining, and major roadways, making it ideal for families and professionals alike.

Waterset

Waterset attracts buyers who want pool homes with a community feel. Many properties in this neighborhood include pools with newer equipment, updated decking, and spacious screen enclosures. The area is known for its well-kept streetscapes, neighborhood parks, and family-friendly atmosphere. Pool homes in Waterset tend to offer excellent value, with price points that appeal to first-time pool home buyers and move-up buyers.

Andalucia

For buyers seeking pool homes with larger lots and more privacy, Andalucia delivers. This area features properties with expansive backyards, mature trees, and pools that serve as the centerpiece of outdoor entertainment areas. Many pool homes in Andalucia include covered patios, summer kitchens, and fire pit areas that extend the usable outdoor space well beyond the pool deck itself.

Southshore Falls

Southshore Falls rounds out the top pool home neighborhoods in Apollo Beach with a mix of newer construction and updated resale homes. Pools here range from classic rectangular designs to freeform tropical layouts with water features. The neighborhood benefits from newer infrastructure, well-maintained HOA standards, and proximity to parks and recreation areas that complement the backyard pool lifestyle.

Pool Home Price Overview in Apollo Beach

The following table provides a general overview of pool home pricing across Apollo Beach by property type and size. Prices vary by neighborhood, pool condition, lot size, and home features.

Property TypePool Home Price RangeTypical Lot Size
3-Bedroom / 2-Bath$370,000-$900,000+0.15-0.25 acres
4-Bedroom / 2.5-Bath$370,000-$900,000+0.20-0.35 acres
4-Bedroom / 3-Bath (Premium)$370,000-$900,000+0.25-0.50+ acres
5+ Bedroom Estate$370,000-$900,000+0.50+ acres

The median home price in Apollo Beach is approximately $430,000, with pool homes generally commanding a premium above that figure. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed market analysis for your specific neighborhood and price range. Contact Barrett for current pool home inventory.

Types of Pools You Will Find in Apollo Beach

Not all pools are created equal, and understanding the types available in Apollo Beach will help you narrow your search and budget accordingly.

Screened Pool Enclosures

The vast majority of residential pools in Apollo Beach - and across Florida - feature aluminum-framed screen enclosures, commonly called pool cages. These enclosures keep out insects, reduce debris, and provide a measure of safety for children and pets. A standard pool cage in good condition adds significant value to a home and is considered essential by most buyers in Hillsborough County. Replacement costs for a full pool cage can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on size, so cage condition is a key inspection item.

Saltwater Pools

Saltwater pool systems have surged in popularity across Apollo Beach due to lower maintenance costs and a more comfortable swimming experience. Saltwater generators produce chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, reducing the need for chemical handling and producing water that is gentler on skin, hair, and swimwear. Many resale homes have been converted from traditional chlorine to saltwater systems, and most new construction pools include saltwater as standard.

Heated Pools

While Apollo Beach enjoys a warm climate, winter mornings can bring pool water temperatures down into the 60s. Gas heaters, heat pumps, and solar heating systems extend the swimming season to a full twelve months. Gas heaters provide the fastest heat-up time, while heat pumps offer better energy efficiency for day-to-day use. Solar heating is the most economical long-term option and works well with the abundant Florida sunshine.

Freeform and Custom Pools

Many homes in Apollo Beach feature custom-designed freeform pools with rock waterfalls, grottos, tanning ledges, and infinity edges. These resort-style pools are most common in upscale neighborhoods and estate properties, where the pool and outdoor living area serve as the architectural focal point of the home. Buyers should note that custom pools may cost more to maintain and insure than standard designs.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist

Purchasing a pool home requires additional due diligence beyond a standard home inspection. Barrett Henry recommends every pool home buyer evaluate the following items before making an offer.

  • Pool inspection: Hire a certified pool inspector separate from the general home inspector. They will evaluate the shell, plumbing, equipment, deck, and screen enclosure for defects, leaks, and code compliance.
  • Resurfacing timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or quartz) typically last 8-15 years. Determine when the pool was last resurfaced and budget accordingly if resurfacing is due within the next few years. Costs range from $5,000 to $12,000.
  • Equipment age: Pool pumps, filters, heaters, and salt systems have a lifespan of 5-10 years. Aging equipment may work today but represent a near-term replacement cost. Ask the seller for maintenance records and equipment installation dates.
  • Screen enclosure condition: Inspect the cage for corrosion, torn screens, sagging frames, and signs of storm damage. A full cage replacement can cost $8,000-$15,000, so factor this into your offer if damage is present.
  • Insurance impact: Pool ownership affects homeowners insurance premiums and liability coverage. Discuss pool-specific coverage with your insurance agent before closing. A pool fence or cage is typically required for compliance with local safety codes.
  • Deck and drainage: Pool decks should be level, free of large cracks, and properly graded to direct water away from the home. Settling, trip hazards, and poor drainage are common issues in older pool homes.

Outdoor Living Features Beyond the Pool

In Apollo Beach, the pool is often just one element of a comprehensive outdoor living area. The best pool homes pair the swimming pool with features that extend the home's livable square footage into the backyard.

Lanais and Covered Patios

A screened lanai adjacent to the pool provides shaded seating, outdoor dining, and protection from afternoon rain showers. Many Apollo Beach homes feature extended lanais with ceiling fans, recessed lighting, and tile or travertine flooring that create a seamless indoor-outdoor transition.

Summer Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens - called summer kitchens in Florida - have become a must-have amenity in Apollo Beach pool homes. A typical summer kitchen includes a built-in grill, countertop space, a mini-refrigerator, and a sink. Upscale versions add pizza ovens, smokers, kegerators, and bar seating that turn the pool area into an entertainment destination.

Landscape and Lighting

Tropical landscaping, LED pool lighting, and landscape lighting create a resort atmosphere that enhances both daytime and evening enjoyment. Mature palms, birds of paradise, and jasmine hedges are popular plantings that thrive in Apollo Beach's climate and complement the pool setting.

Why Apollo Beach?

Waterfront living with canal-front homes, Tampa Bay access, the TECO Manatee Viewing Center, and a 25-minute commute to downtown Tampa via US-41 or I-75.

With a population of approximately 25,000, Apollo Beach offers a strong and diverse economy anchored by Tampa Electric (TECO), nearby MacDill AFB, medical and retail employers along the US-41 corridor. The combination of employment opportunities, lifestyle amenities, and a growing real estate market makes Apollo Beach one of the most compelling places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region.

For buyers exploring Apollo Beach real estate, pool homes represent an outstanding investment in both quality of life and long-term property value. Whether you are relocating from out of state, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for your retirement oasis, Apollo Beach delivers the Florida lifestyle at a price point that competes favorably with other Gulf Coast markets.

Frequently Asked Questions About Apollo Beach Pool Homes

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Apollo Beach?

Monthly pool maintenance in Apollo Beach typically runs between $100 and $200 for weekly professional service, which includes chemical balancing, skimming, brushing, and equipment checks. Homeowners who maintain their own pools can reduce costs to $40-$80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual costs for electricity to run the pump average $600-$1,200 depending on the pump type and run time.

Do pool homes cost more to insure in Apollo Beach?

Yes, pool homes generally carry higher homeowners insurance premiums due to increased liability exposure. The additional cost is typically $100-$300 per year, though rates vary by insurer, pool type, and whether the pool has a safety fence or enclosure. Screen enclosures can help reduce premiums by meeting safety barrier requirements.

What is the best time to buy a pool home in Apollo Beach?

The best time to buy a pool home in Apollo Beach is typically during the late fall and winter months (November through February), when buyer competition decreases and sellers may be more willing to negotiate. However, inventory for pool homes tends to be limited year-round, so working with an experienced agent like Barrett Henry ensures you see new listings the moment they hit the market.

Should I buy a home with an existing pool or build one?

Both options have merits. Buying an existing pool home avoids the 3-6 month construction timeline and the hassle of managing a pool build project. However, building a new pool lets you customize the design, equipment, and features to your exact specifications. New pool construction in Apollo Beach typically costs $35,000-$80,000 depending on size, features, and site conditions. Barrett Henry can help you evaluate both options based on available inventory and your budget.

Are there HOA restrictions on pools in Apollo Beach?

Many neighborhoods in Apollo Beach have HOA guidelines that govern pool construction, including setback requirements, fence or enclosure standards, and equipment placement. Some HOAs require architectural review board approval before a pool can be built. Barrett Henry can review HOA documents and identify any restrictions before you make an offer on a property where you plan to add a pool.

title: Apollo Beach Housing Market
content:
Apollo Beach is one of Tampa Bay's most sought-after waterfront communities, and heading into 2026 the market reflects that demand. Median home prices sit around $425,000, supported by the area's direct Gulf access, canal-front lots, and proximity to both Tampa and Sarasota. If you're tracking the broader Florida housing market in 2026, Apollo Beach is consistently outperforming suburban averages thanks to its unique waterfront inventory.

What's Happening in the Apollo Beach Market Right Now?

Waterfront demand continues to outpace supply. Canal-front and bay-access properties are selling in under three weeks when priced correctly, sometimes with multiple offers. Non-waterfront single-family homes sit slightly longer (30-35 days) but are still moving. New construction in MiraBay and Waterset is adding inventory, which is giving buyers a little more breathing room than in 2022-2023. Interest rates holding at 6 to 6.5% have cooled the frenzy, but serious buyers are still active.

Across Tampa Bay, interest rates holding in the 6 to 6.5% range have recalibrated buyer expectations. Monthly payment sensitivity is real: a $420,000 home at 6.25% runs roughly $2,585/month (principal and interest, 20% down), meaningful to most buyers. This has pushed some demand toward rate-buydown incentives, adjustable-rate products, and smaller-footprint homes. Apollo Beach buyers are no different.

Inventory overall remains below pre-2020 levels even as it has improved from the historic lows of 2021-2022. That structural undersupply continues to put a floor under prices across Tampa Bay, Apollo Beach included.

Is It a Buyer's or Seller's Market in Apollo Beach?

Apollo Beach sits in slight seller-advantage territory in early 2026, but it's nuanced. Waterfront and canal homes favor sellers. Standard subdivision homes are more balanced, and buyers can often negotiate closing costs or a rate buydown. If you're targeting a waterfront property under $600K, expect competition. Over $800K, the pool of buyers shrinks and negotiating room opens up.

As a general benchmark: under 3 months of inventory favors sellers; 3-4 months is balanced; above 4 months favors buyers. Apollo Beach's 2.4 months of supply tells the story. Conditions can shift quickly, especially if mortgage rates drop or a large employer announces a relocation. Check with a local agent for current week-over-week trends.

Price Trends by Property Type in Apollo Beach

Not all property types appreciate at the same rate. Here's a breakdown of where values sat in 2025 versus early 2026 across major categories in Apollo Beach:

Data reflects Stellar MLS sales data and active listing trends for the Apollo Beach area. Individual property values vary by condition, location within the market, and upgrade level.

Should You Buy in Apollo Beach in 2026?

The short answer: yes, if your finances support it and you're planning to hold for at least 3-5 years.

If waterfront living is your goal, 2026 may be one of the better windows in recent memory. Prices have appreciated modestly rather than spiking, and rates, while higher than pandemic lows, are steady. Waiting could mean paying more as inventory tightens again. Explore Apollo Beach listings and neighborhood info to get a feel for what's available right now.

Trying to time the market is a losing game in a market like Apollo Beach. Buyers who waited in 2023 for prices to drop are now buying at higher prices and higher rates. The fundamentals that drive Apollo Beach's demand, location, schools, employment access, lifestyle, haven't changed. Every month you wait is another month of rent you're paying toward someone else's equity.

If you're weighing Apollo Beach against neighboring communities, it's worth a conversation with a local agent who knows the micro-level differences. Small neighborhood details, flood zone designations, HOA restrictions, school district lines, commute times at peak hours, can make a significant difference in both lifestyle and resale value.

Should You Sell in Apollo Beach in 2026?

The short answer: yes, if you price it right and present it well.

Sellers are in a solid position, especially with updated kitchens, new roofs, or waterfront features. The days of zero-days-on-market are largely gone, but a well-priced, well-presented home in Apollo Beach is still moving in 3-4 weeks. Overpricing by even 5% can add 60+ days to your timeline in today's rate-sensitive market.

The sellers who struggle in 2026 are the ones anchoring to 2022 peak pricing. The market has normalized. That's not bad news, it's a functional, sustainable market. Properly priced, well-maintained homes in Apollo Beach are still closing in 25-40 days and sellers are netting strong proceeds relative to their purchase basis.

Key preparation steps before listing in Apollo Beach: pull comparable sales from the last 90 days (not 6 months), get a pre-listing inspection if your home is 15+ years old, invest in professional photography, and have a conversation about timing, certain months outperform others even in a steady market.

How Apollo Beach Compares to the Broader Tampa Bay Market

Tampa Bay as a region continues to perform above national averages in 2026. Population growth, job creation in finance, healthcare, and tech, and a relative affordability advantage over coastal metros (Miami, Naples, Sarasota) are driving sustained in-migration. Apollo Beach benefits from all of those macro tailwinds while having its own neighborhood-specific demand drivers.

For buyers or sellers comparing multiple Tampa Bay communities, understanding where Apollo Beach sits in the regional pricing ladder is essential. At $425,000 median, Apollo Beach is positioned as a distinct community with its own value proposition not just a suburb of Tampa.

Nestled in the heart of Tampa Bay, Apollo Beach offers a unique blend of community charm, convenient amenities, and Florida lifestyle that attracts homebuyers from across the country. Why Buy New Construction in Apollo Beach?

Buying new construction in Apollo Beach means moving into a home designed with today's lifestyle in mind. Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Apollo Beach also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Apollo Beach area, including GL Homes, Lennar, Homes by WestBay. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Apollo Beach typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Apollo Beach
Entry-Level / Starter$380K-$450K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s
Premium / Luxury$550K+

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Apollo Beach?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.
