Why Buy New Construction in Lakewood Ranch?

Buying new construction in Lakewood Ranch means moving into a home designed with today's lifestyle in mind. Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Lakewood Ranch also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Lakewood Ranch area, including Neal Communities, Lennar, Toll Brothers, Taylor Morrison, Stock Development. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Lakewood Ranch typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Lakewood Ranch
Entry-Level / Starter$450K-$600K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s
Premium / Luxury$700K+

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Lakewood Ranch?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Lakewood Ranch require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Lakewood Ranch?

Flood insurance costs in Lakewood Ranch vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Lakewood Ranch?

Most waterfront properties in Lakewood Ranch allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Lakewood Ranch generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.

Why Land O Lakes is One of Tampa Bay's Best Places to Live

Land O Lakes occupies a sweet spot in the Tampa Bay area real estate landscape: close enough to Tampa for an easy commute, far enough away for larger lots, newer construction, and a quieter suburban lifestyle. Located in southern Pasco County along the Suncoast Parkway (SR-589), Land O Lakes has attracted families and professionals who want the best of both worlds. The community has grown dramatically over the past two decades, with planned neighborhoods, excellent schools, and expanding retail and dining options making it increasingly self-sufficient.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Land O Lakes Homes

The character of Land O Lakes is defined by its blend of newer master-planned communities and older, more established neighborhoods set among the area's natural lakes and wooded corridors. Communities like Connerton, Bexley, and Lakeshore Ranch have elevated the area's profile, offering resort-style amenities and modern home designs that rival more expensive Tampa Bay submarkets. Meanwhile, the area's proximity to thousands of acres of conservation land, including Conner Preserve and the Jay B. Starkey Wilderness Park, gives residents access to outdoor recreation that is increasingly rare in the region.

Land O Lakes appeals strongly to families prioritizing school quality, as Sunlake High School is among the top-rated high schools in Pasco County. Commuters appreciate the Suncoast Parkway's direct, toll-road access to Tampa International Airport and the Veterans Expressway, making northbound and southbound travel efficient. If you are researching a move to the Tampa Bay area, Land O Lakes offers a compelling package that many buyers overlook in favor of more heavily marketed Wesley Chapel to the east.

Where is Land O Lakes? Location and Getting Around

Land O Lakes is located in southern Pasco County, bordered to the south by Hillsborough County (specifically the Lutz area) and to the west by the Suncoast Parkway. The community extends roughly from the SR-52 corridor in the north down to the Pasco-Hillsborough county line. The Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) is the primary artery connecting Land O Lakes to Tampa, running south to connect with the Veterans Expressway and ultimately to Tampa International Airport and downtown Tampa.

The drive from Land O Lakes to downtown Tampa typically takes 30 to 45 minutes via the Suncoast Parkway and Veterans Expressway under normal traffic conditions. Tampa International Airport is approximately 25 to 35 minutes south. The community also has access to US-41 on its eastern side, which connects south into Lutz and north toward Zephyrhills. For residents who work in the Odessa or Trinity corridors to the west, SR-54 provides an east-west connection without requiring a trip into Tampa.

Land O Lakes itself has developed a growing commercial base along SR-54, Collier Parkway, and the US-41 corridor, making daily errands convenient without leaving the area. The community is car-dependent, as public transit options are minimal. Pasco County Public Transportation provides limited bus routes, but the vast majority of residents commute and travel by personal vehicle. As the area continues to grow, road capacity improvements are ongoing.

Land O Lakes Real Estate Market Overview

Land O Lakes offers a diverse real estate market with a median list price of approximately $450,000, though the range extends from the high $200s for older homes in established neighborhoods to $700,000 and above in communities like Bexley and Lakeshore Ranch. The market has moderated from the peak prices of 2022, providing buyers with more negotiating leverage and more time to conduct due diligence. New construction remains active, with multiple builders offering move-in-ready and to-be-built options across the area's planned communities.

Connerton, one of Land O Lakes' most established planned communities, has a median list price of approximately $439,000, making it an accessible entry point for buyers who want community amenities at a reasonable price. Lakeshore Ranch, a gated community with a 12,000-square-foot clubhouse and three resort-style pools, carries an average home price near $549,000. Del Webb Bexley, the active adult section of the Bexley community, appeals to the 55-plus buyer at price points near $580,000 and above.

Buyers can explore available listings in Land O Lakes now, or request a home valuation if you are considering selling. First-time buyers will find options in Land O Lakes' older neighborhoods and some newer townhome developments that offer an affordable entry into homeownership in a desirable community. Sellers can connect with Barrett Henry through the sell your home page to discuss current market conditions and positioning strategy.

Neighborhoods and Subdivisions in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes offers a wide variety of neighborhood styles and price points. Below are the major communities that buyers should evaluate.

Connerton: Built on approximately 8,000 acres of a former cattle ranch, Connerton is one of Pasco County's largest master-planned communities, with roughly 3,000 acres set aside as a nature preserve managed by the State of Florida. The community features a town center, resort-style amenities, walking trails, and a mix of single-family homes and townhomes from multiple builders. Prices generally run from the mid-$300s to the low-$500s. Connerton's commitment to preserving natural land gives it a character that many newer communities lack.

Lakeshore Ranch: A gated, amenity-rich community featuring a 12,000-square-foot clubhouse, three pools (including a resort pool, lap pool, and splash pad), a fitness center, basketball courts, tennis courts, a boat dock, and a business center. Lakeshore Ranch homes average near $549,000 and offer a resort lifestyle in a private, gated setting. The community is particularly popular with families and move-up buyers.

Bexley: Straddling the Land O Lakes and Wesley Chapel areas along the Suncoast Parkway, Bexley sits on 1,200 acres with significant conservation land and over 10 miles of trails connecting to the Suncoast Trail. Multiple builders offer homes from the $400s to the $700s and above. Del Webb Bexley provides an age-restricted 55-plus section within the broader Bexley community. The community's programming, hub buildings, and trail connectivity make it one of the most complete planned communities in the region.

Concord Station: A mid-sized planned community offering single-family homes in the $350,000 to $500,000 range. Concord Station features a community pool, clubhouse, tennis courts, and playground. Its position near SR-54 and the Suncoast Parkway makes commuting straightforward.

Suncoast Crossing: A newer community offering a mix of townhomes and single-family options along the Suncoast Parkway corridor. Entry-level pricing makes Suncoast Crossing accessible to a wide range of buyers, with townhomes starting in the low-to-mid $300s. The community appeals to commuters who prioritize Suncoast Parkway access.

Stonegate: An established community featuring larger single-family homes on generous lots, with prices from the $400,000s to the $600,000s. Stonegate's mature landscaping and established character appeal to buyers seeking a neighborhood that has grown into itself rather than a brand-new subdivision still finding its identity.

Whispering Oaks: An older, established community offering larger lots and more mature tree canopy than newer subdivisions. Homes here are generally priced in the $350,000 to $500,000 range and offer more square footage per dollar than many newer communities.

Lake Padgett Estates: A lakefront community featuring a private ski lake, a beach area, tennis courts, and a community boat ramp. Lake Padgett homes vary widely in price depending on lot size and water access, from the $300,000s to the $700,000s. The community's lakefront character gives it a distinctive appeal among outdoor enthusiasts.

Pine Glen and Plantation Palms: Two established communities offering single-family homes in the $300,000 to $450,000 range. Plantation Palms includes access to the Plantation Palms Golf Course, a public course that serves as a community amenity for golf-oriented buyers.

Schools in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes is served by the Pasco County School District, and school quality is one of the community's strongest selling points. The area's rapid population growth over the past decade has been accompanied by the opening of several new schools designed to serve the newer communities, giving families excellent local options at every grade level.

Sunlake High School is the standout performer in the area, ranking third among all ranked high schools in the Pasco County School District. Sunlake earns an A-minus rating on Niche and a 7 out of 10 from GreatSchools, which places it well above average compared to public schools statewide. The school serves approximately 2,192 students in grades 9 through 12, maintains a 94% graduation rate, and posts average SAT scores of approximately 1200 and ACT scores near 25. These figures are meaningfully above both county and state averages.

Land O Lakes High School serves the community's longer-established neighborhoods and is the area's more historic high school. The school offers a broad range of academic and extracurricular programs. Middle schools serving the area include Charles S. Rushe Middle School and Pine View Middle School. Elementary schools include Connerton Elementary, Bexley Elementary (newer, serving the Bexley community), and Oakstead Elementary, among others. As always, buyers should verify current attendance boundaries with the Pasco County School District before purchasing based on school assignments.

Private school options in the broader area include Imagine School at Land O Lakes and several faith-based private schools accessible from the community. The overall school quality in Land O Lakes is a primary driver of the area's appeal to families relocating from higher-cost markets in Florida and from out of state.

Things to Do in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes may not have the flashy resort amenities of some Wesley Chapel communities, but it more than compensates with access to outstanding natural areas and a growing local activity scene. Conner Preserve is the area's premier outdoor destination, encompassing approximately 2,980 acres of preserved Florida wilderness with well-marked hiking trails, mountain biking tracks, and equestrian paths. The preserve is one of the largest publicly accessible natural areas in Pasco County and provides residents a genuine outdoor retreat within minutes of their homes.

The Suncoast Parkway Trail is a multi-use paved path running along the SR-589 corridor, ideal for cyclists, walkers, and runners. The trail connects into the broader Suncoast Trail system, ultimately linking to major trail networks throughout Hillsborough and Pasco counties. Lake Padgett's private ski lake is a beloved community amenity for water sports enthusiasts, while numerous other natural lakes throughout the community offer fishing, kayaking, and scenic recreation.

Plantation Palms Golf Course provides a public golf option within the community. The SR-54 corridor and the growing commercial areas near Collier Parkway offer movie theaters, fitness centers, bowling, escape rooms, and other entertainment options that have expanded significantly with Land O Lakes' population growth. For more entertainment and retail, Wesley Chapel's Shops at Wiregrass and Tampa Premium Outlets are less than 20 minutes east on SR-54.

Dining and Restaurants in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes' restaurant scene has grown considerably over the past decade, reflecting the community's expanding and increasingly diverse population. Hungry Harry's Famous Bar-B-Que is a standout local favorite, drawing consistent praise for its large portions and classic southern barbecue preparations. Ukulele Brand's, a lakeside seafood restaurant with waterfront views and live music, has established itself as the go-to choice for a memorable date night or special occasion in the area.

The SR-54 corridor hosts a growing collection of dining options, from casual family restaurants to sports bars and international cuisine. National chains like Texas de Brazil, First Watch, and various major casual dining brands have followed the residential growth and now serve the community. The area along Collier Parkway and US-41 has also developed a concentration of restaurants and quick-service options that make daily dining convenient.

For expanded dining options, Land O Lakes residents frequently venture south to Lutz, east to Wesley Chapel, or south into Tampa for special occasions. The relative proximity of the Suncoast Parkway makes Tampa dining accessible within 30 to 40 minutes, providing the dining variety of a major city without requiring a permanent urban address.

Thinking About Land O Lakes? Let's Talk.

Barrett Henry has helped buyers and sellers across the Tampa Bay area navigate real estate decisions with confidence. Whether you're exploring Land O Lakes for the first time or ready to make a move, a quick conversation can save you time and money.

Commute and Transportation from Land O Lakes

The Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) is Land O Lakes' defining transportation asset, providing a direct toll road connection south into Tampa. The commute from southern Land O Lakes to Tampa International Airport typically runs 25 to 35 minutes. Downtown Tampa is roughly 30 to 45 minutes via the Suncoast Parkway and Veterans Expressway. MacDill Air Force Base, via the same route plus the Selmon Expressway east, is approximately 45 to 55 minutes.

Residents in northern Land O Lakes near SR-52 have longer commutes into Tampa, typically 45 to 55 minutes, but benefit from lower home prices and newer construction that often more than compensates for the additional drive time. The SR-54 corridor provides an east-west connection to Wesley Chapel, Zephyrhills, and I-75 eastbound. For residents working in the Trinity or New Port Richey areas to the west, SR-54 provides a direct connection via the Suncoast Parkway interchange.

Orlando is accessible in approximately 90 minutes via I-75 south to I-4 east, making Land O Lakes a viable option for dual-city commuters or those with occasional Orlando business. St. Petersburg is approximately 50 to 60 minutes via the Suncoast Parkway and the Howard Frankland Bridge. As with most Pasco County communities, public transit options are limited and a personal vehicle is essentially required for daily life.

Cost of Living in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes represents solid value in the Tampa Bay market: home prices are meaningful but more modest than in closer-in suburbs like South Tampa or Carrollwood, and the newer construction stock means lower maintenance costs and better energy efficiency than older communities. Pasco County property taxes run approximately 1.0% to 1.3% of assessed value annually. Many Land O Lakes communities, particularly the planned communities like Connerton, Bexley, and Lakeshore Ranch, carry Community Development District (CDD) fees that can range from a few hundred dollars to over $2,500 annually. Understanding these fees before purchase is essential, and the CDD fee guide at nowtb.com explains exactly how they work.

HOA fees in Land O Lakes communities vary from around $50 per month in simpler communities to $300 or more in amenity-rich gated communities like Lakeshore Ranch. Flood risk in Land O Lakes is generally lower than in coastal communities, though some properties near lakes and low-lying areas carry flood zone designations. Buyers should always verify flood zone status before purchase. The Florida flood zones guide provides helpful context for this evaluation. The HOA rules guide is also worth reviewing for anyone considering a community governed by a homeowners association.

Utility costs in Land O Lakes are typical for the region, with Pasco County Utilities providing water and sewer services to most communities. Electric costs from Duke Energy or TECO average $150 to $250 monthly for a typical single-family home, depending on square footage and energy efficiency. Overall, Land O Lakes delivers a competitive cost-of-living profile for the school quality and community amenities provided. For a full accounting of purchase transaction costs, the Florida closing costs guide is a valuable reference.

New Construction in Land O Lakes

New construction remains active in Land O Lakes, particularly in the expanding phases of Connerton and Bexley. Builders active in the area include Lennar, D.R. Horton, Taylor Morrison, Pulte Homes, and David Weekley Homes, among others. Entry-level new construction starts in the high $300s for townhomes and smaller single-family options, while mid-range new homes in communities like Connerton and Concord Station run from the $400,000s to the $550,000s. Move-up and luxury new construction in Bexley and Lakeshore Ranch can reach $700,000 and above.

Builders are actively offering incentives in 2026's more balanced market, including mortgage rate buy-downs, closing cost contributions, and design center upgrades. Buyers interested in new construction should always work with their own buyer's agent to ensure their interests are properly represented, as builder sales representatives work for the builder. Barrett Henry has extensive experience helping buyers navigate new construction transactions in Land O Lakes and throughout Pasco County.

Pros and Cons of Living in Land O Lakes

Pros of Living in Land O Lakes:

Top-rated schools: Sunlake High School ranks among the best public high schools in Pasco County, and the broader school district serves the community well. School quality is consistently cited as one of the top reasons families choose Land O Lakes over other Pasco County communities.

Suncoast Parkway access: The toll road connection directly to Tampa International Airport and the Veterans Expressway gives Land O Lakes commuters a genuine advantage over Pasco communities that rely solely on I-75. Many residents find the Suncoast Parkway commute faster and less stressful than the I-75 corridor during peak hours.

Nature access: Conner Preserve, Jay B. Starkey Wilderness Park, and the Suncoast Trail system give Land O Lakes residents exceptional access to outdoor recreation. For families and outdoor enthusiasts, this proximity to protected natural land is a lasting quality-of-life asset.

Value relative to Tampa: Land O Lakes offers comparable schools and newer construction at meaningfully lower price points than Carrollwood, Westchase, or Lutz in Hillsborough County. The price-per-square-foot advantage for new construction is particularly compelling for families who need space.

Diverse community options: From the nature-focused Connerton to the gated luxury of Lakeshore Ranch to the 55-plus active adult lifestyle at Del Webb Bexley, Land O Lakes offers something for buyers at virtually every life stage and budget.

Cons of Living in Land O Lakes:

Car dependency: Like most of Pasco County, Land O Lakes is entirely car-dependent. No meaningful public transit serves the community, and even basic errands require a vehicle. This is a significant consideration for households with limited transportation options.

CDD fees and HOA costs: Most of Land O Lakes' desirable planned communities carry some combination of CDD fees and HOA dues that add meaningfully to total monthly housing costs. Buyers need to fully account for these in their budget calculations.

Growing pains: Ongoing construction throughout the community means traffic, noise, and incomplete road infrastructure in some areas. SR-54 in particular can experience significant congestion as development along the corridor continues to intensify.

Limited urban entertainment: While Land O Lakes' dining and entertainment options are growing, residents seeking a full urban experience will need to travel to Tampa or Wesley Chapel. The community's suburban character is a strength for many buyers but a limitation for those who want walkability and urban amenities close to home.

Land O Lakes for Real Estate Investors

Land O Lakes presents solid investment fundamentals for long-term rental investors. Gross rental rates for single-family homes typically range from $1,900 to $2,900 per month depending on size, community, and condition. Demand from working families and young professionals who are not yet ready to purchase keeps vacancy rates low, and the area's continued population growth supports long-term rental demand. Investors should focus on communities that allow rentals, as some gated or HOA communities have restrictions on tenant occupancy periods.

Short-term rental investing is generally not viable in Land O Lakes' HOA communities, as most governing documents prohibit rentals of less than six months or one year. Long-term rental investors should evaluate total cost of ownership carefully, factoring CDD fees, HOA dues, property management (typically 8% to 10% of gross rent), and maintenance reserves into their analysis. Comparing Land O Lakes to nearby Zephyrhills or New Port Richey can reveal better cap rates in exchange for slower appreciation. For a comprehensive look at investment properties in the Tampa Bay area, Barrett Henry can provide market-specific analysis.

Frequently Asked Questions About Land O Lakes

Is Land O Lakes a good place to live?

Yes, Land O Lakes is widely considered one of the better family-friendly communities in Pasco County and the broader Tampa Bay area. Excellent schools, nature access, new construction quality, and reasonable commute times via the Suncoast Parkway make it consistently attractive to families and professionals relocating from out of state. The primary trade-offs are car dependency and HOA or CDD costs in the planned communities.

What are home prices in Land O Lakes in 2026?

The median list price in Land O Lakes is approximately $450,000 overall, though prices range considerably by community. Connerton's median is near $439,000. Lakeshore Ranch averages near $549,000. Del Webb Bexley runs approximately $580,000 and above. Older and more established neighborhoods offer options in the $300,000 range for buyers on tighter budgets.

What school district is Land O Lakes in?

Land O Lakes is served by the Pasco County School District. The top-rated high school in the area is Sunlake High School, which ranks third among all Pasco County high schools on Niche's rankings and has an A-minus rating. Land O Lakes High School serves the area's more established neighborhoods. Elementary schools include Connerton Elementary, Bexley Elementary, and Oakstead Elementary, among others.

Is Land O Lakes in Pasco County or Hillsborough County?

Land O Lakes is in Pasco County, though it borders Hillsborough County to the south. The community shares the Lutz area with southern Pasco, and the county line runs through what feels like a continuous suburban zone. For tax, school, and regulatory purposes, Land O Lakes falls under Pasco County jurisdiction.

How far is Land O Lakes from Tampa?

From southern Land O Lakes, downtown Tampa is approximately 30 to 45 minutes via the Suncoast Parkway and Veterans Expressway. Tampa International Airport is typically 25 to 35 minutes. From northern portions of Land O Lakes near SR-52, add another 10 to 15 minutes to all estimates. The Suncoast Parkway makes the commute significantly more direct than going through surface streets.

Are there 55-plus communities in Land O Lakes?

Yes. Del Webb Bexley is an active adult 55-plus community located within the broader Bexley development. Del Webb Bexley offers resort-style amenities, a clubhouse, fitness center, and a full activity calendar designed for active adult residents. Pricing at Del Webb Bexley runs approximately $580,000 and above. For more information on 55-plus communities throughout Tampa Bay, see the Tampa Bay 55-plus communities guide.

What are the best neighborhoods in Land O Lakes?

Top neighborhoods depend on your priorities. Connerton is ideal for buyers who want a large community with natural surroundings and reasonable pricing. Lakeshore Ranch suits buyers who want resort amenities in a gated setting. Bexley appeals to trail enthusiasts and those who want access to the Suncoast Trail system. Lake Padgett Estates is excellent for water sports enthusiasts. Older communities like Whispering Oaks and Stonegate offer established character and often more square footage per dollar.

Is Land O Lakes a good place to invest in real estate?

Land O Lakes offers solid fundamentals for long-term rental investors, with single-family gross rents typically ranging from $1,900 to $2,900 per month. Strong rental demand from families who are not yet ready to buy, combined with the area's continued population growth, supports consistent occupancy. Investors should carefully review HOA and CDD obligations, and verify that the community allows rental properties before purchasing.

How does Land O Lakes compare to Wesley Chapel?

Land O Lakes and Wesley Chapel are both excellent family-friendly Pasco County communities, but they have distinct characters. Wesley Chapel has more new construction activity, larger commercial development, and resort-style communities like Epperson with its Crystal Lagoon. Land O Lakes has better Suncoast Parkway access to Tampa, more access to natural areas like Conner Preserve, and slightly more moderate prices in some communities. School quality is strong in both areas.

What parks and outdoor areas are near Land O Lakes?

Conner Preserve (2,980 acres) is the flagship outdoor destination, offering hiking, mountain biking, and equestrian trails through preserved Florida wilderness. Jay B. Starkey Wilderness Park lies to the west and provides additional trail systems. The Suncoast Parkway Trail offers paved multi-use recreation accessible directly from many community neighborhoods. Lake Padgett's private ski lake serves residents of that community for water sports.

55+ Homes for Sale in Land O' Lakes, Florida

Active adult living in Land O' Lakes offers the perfect blend of Florida sunshine, community connection, and maintenance-ease. Whether you are retiring to the Sunshine State, downsizing from a larger home, or simply seeking a vibrant 55+ community, Land O' Lakes in Pasco County has options that cater to every lifestyle and budget.

Homes in Land O' Lakes's 55+ communities generally range from $225,000 to $450,000. Popular active adult neighborhoods include Connerton 55+ Villas, and Lake Padgett Estates. These communities are designed for residents aged 55 and older and offer amenities, social programming, and low-maintenance living that make every day feel like a vacation.

What Makes 55+ Communities in Land O' Lakes Special

Age-restricted communities in Land O' Lakes go far beyond simply being neighborhoods for older adults. They are purpose-built lifestyle communities that offer:

Resort-Style Amenities

Most 55+ communities in Land O' Lakes feature impressive clubhouses that serve as the social hub of the neighborhood. You can expect to find heated swimming pools, fitness centers with modern equipment, card rooms, billiards, arts and crafts studios, and multi-purpose event spaces. Many communities also offer pickleball courts, bocce ball, shuffleboard, and walking trails - all designed to keep residents active and engaged.

Low-Maintenance Living

One of the biggest draws of 55+ living is the reduced maintenance burden. Many communities in Land O' Lakes include lawn care, exterior maintenance, and sometimes even roof and exterior painting in the HOA fees. This means less time on a ladder and more time on the golf course, at the pool, or pursuing hobbies. Some communities offer villa-style homes or attached homes that further minimize maintenance responsibilities.

Active Social Calendar

Loneliness is a real concern for retirees, and 55+ communities address this head-on with robust social programming. From book clubs and card games to organized day trips and holiday celebrations, there is always something happening. Many Land O' Lakes communities have dedicated lifestyle directors who organize events and activities throughout the year.

Safety and Security

Many 55+ communities in Land O' Lakes are gated, providing an extra layer of security. The age restriction itself creates a quieter, more predictable neighborhood environment. Low speed limits, well-lit streets, and neighborhood watch programs contribute to a safe living environment.

Top 55+ Communities in Land O' Lakes

Connerton 55+ Villas

Connerton 55+ Villas stands out as one of Land O' Lakes's premier active adult communities. Residents enjoy a well-appointed clubhouse, resort-style pool, fitness center, and a calendar packed with social events and activities. What Buyers Should Know About 55+ Communities

If you are considering a 55+ community in Land O' Lakes, here are some important factors to evaluate:

Age Requirements

Federal Housing for Older Persons Act (HOPA) requires that at least 80% of units have one resident aged 55 or older. Some communities are stricter. Understand the specific age rules of any community you are considering, especially if you have a younger spouse or plan to have younger family members visit or stay.

HOA Fees and What They Cover

55+ community HOA fees in Land O' Lakes typically range from $150 to $500+ per month. These fees often cover amenities, common area maintenance, landscaping, and sometimes exterior maintenance of your home. Carefully review what is included and compare it to the cost of maintaining a traditional home. Many buyers find that the convenience more than justifies the fee.

Healthcare Access

Proximity to healthcare is a priority for many 55+ buyers. Land O' Lakes offers access to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton, ensuring that quality medical care is never far away. Many 55+ communities are also conveniently located near pharmacies, urgent care centers, and specialist offices.

As Florida continues to attract retirees from across the country, demand for quality active adult communities remains strong. This makes purchasing in a Land O' Lakes 55+ community a sound investment.

Condos and Townhomes for Sale in Land O' Lakes, Florida

Condos and townhomes in Land O' Lakes offer a smart alternative to traditional single-family homes. Whether you are a first-time buyer, a downsizer looking to simplify, or an investor seeking rental income, the Land O' Lakes condo and townhome market in Pasco County provides excellent options across a range of price points and styles.

Condos and townhomes in Land O' Lakes generally range from $180,000 to $350,000. Popular areas include Land O' Lakes town center area, Connerton, and Lake Padgett. From modern townhome communities with attached garages to condo complexes with resort-style amenities, Land O' Lakes has a diverse inventory to explore.

Why Choose a Condo or Townhome in Land O' Lakes?

Lower Entry Price

Condos and townhomes in Land O' Lakes typically cost less than comparable single-family homes, making them an excellent entry point into the real estate market. First-time buyers can build equity while enjoying community amenities that would be expensive to replicate in a standalone home. The lower price point also means lower property taxes and insurance costs in many cases.

Low-Maintenance Lifestyle

One of the greatest advantages of condo and townhome living is the reduced maintenance responsibility. Depending on the community, your association fees may cover exterior maintenance, roofing, landscaping, and even pest control. This frees up your time for the things you enjoy - and it is a major reason why downsizers and busy professionals gravitate toward this type of property.

Community Amenities

Many condo and townhome communities in Land O' Lakes offer amenities that rival single-family neighborhoods:

  • Community swimming pools and spas
  • Fitness centers and yoga rooms
  • Clubhouses with event spaces
  • Gated access and security features
  • Walking trails and green spaces
  • Dog parks and pet-friendly areas
  • Covered parking and guest parking

Investment Potential

Condos and townhomes in Land O' Lakes can be excellent investment properties. The lower purchase price combined with strong rental demand in Pasco County makes them attractive for investors seeking cash flow. Before purchasing as an investment, verify the community's rental policies - some associations restrict short-term rentals or have minimum lease terms.

Condos vs. Townhomes - What is the Difference?

While the terms are sometimes used interchangeably, there are important distinctions between condos and townhomes in Land O' Lakes:

Condominiums

When you buy a condo, you own the interior of your unit and share ownership of common areas (hallways, grounds, amenities) with other owners. Condos can be in mid-rise buildings, garden-style complexes, or converted apartments. HOA fees tend to cover more items including exterior maintenance, roofing, and building insurance. Condos are ideal for buyers who want maximum convenience with minimum maintenance.

Townhomes

Townhome buyers own both the interior and the land beneath the unit (in most cases). Townhomes are multi-story attached homes that share one or two walls with neighbors. They typically offer more square footage than condos, include private garages, and sometimes have small fenced yards. HOA fees for townhomes may cover less than condo fees - often just common area maintenance and exterior building maintenance.

What Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome involves some unique considerations compared to buying a single-family home:

  • Review the association documents: Carefully read the CC&Rs, bylaws, rules and regulations, and recent meeting minutes. These documents govern everything from pet policies to rental restrictions to exterior modification rules.
  • Evaluate the financials: Request the association's budget, reserve study, and any pending special assessments. A well-funded reserve means the association can handle major repairs without levying surprise assessments.
  • Understand the fees: Monthly association fees in Land O' Lakes typically range from $150 to $400+ depending on the community and its amenities. Know exactly what is included and factor this into your monthly budget.
  • Check insurance requirements: Condo insurance (HO-6 policy) is different from traditional homeowners insurance. Your lender will require adequate coverage, and you should understand what the association's master policy covers versus what your individual policy needs to cover.
  • Financing considerations: Some lenders have stricter requirements for condo loans, including minimum owner-occupancy ratios and reserve requirements. FHA and VA loans have additional condo approval requirements. Work with a lender experienced in condo financing.

Why Land O' Lakes?

Land O' Lakes is a nature-rich community known for its lakes, preserves, and family-friendly master-planned developments. Residents enjoy Conner Preserve, Wilderness Park, and the Suncoast Trail. The Suncoast Parkway provides quick access to Tampa and Gulf beaches.

With access to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton, condo and townhome residents enjoy both convenience and community. The growing Land O' Lakes market means strong appreciation potential for buyers who get in now.

Gated Community Homes for Sale in Land O' Lakes, Florida

Gated communities in Land O' Lakes offer the best of Florida living - security, privacy, resort-style amenities, and well-maintained neighborhoods. If you value a controlled-access environment with a strong sense of community, Land O' Lakes's gated neighborhoods deliver on every front. From guard-gated enclaves to electronic-access communities, there are options for every budget and lifestyle in Pasco County.

Homes in Land O' Lakes's gated communities generally range from $375,000 to $800,000. Popular gated neighborhoods include Connerton, Oakstead, Suncoast Crossing, and Lakeshore Ranch. These communities typically feature amenities like clubhouses, fitness centers, pools, tennis and pickleball courts, walking trails, and professionally maintained common areas.

Benefits of Living in a Gated Community in Land O' Lakes

Gated communities continue to grow in popularity across Pasco County, and Land O' Lakes is no exception. Here are the key benefits that attract buyers to gated living:

Security and Peace of Mind

The primary draw of a gated community is security. Controlled access points limit entry to residents, their guests, and authorized service providers. Many gated communities in Land O' Lakes feature manned guard gates, security cameras, roving patrols, and well-lit streets. This creates a safer environment for families, retirees, and anyone who values privacy.

Community Amenities

Gated communities in Land O' Lakes often rival resort destinations when it comes to amenities. Expect to find:

  • Resort-style swimming pools and splash pads
  • State-of-the-art fitness centers
  • Tennis, pickleball, and basketball courts
  • Walking and biking trails
  • Playgrounds and tot lots
  • Clubhouses with event spaces
  • Lakes, ponds, and nature preserves
  • Dog parks and pet-friendly areas

Property Value Protection

HOA-enforced deed restrictions in gated communities help protect your investment. Standards for home maintenance, landscaping, and exterior appearance keep the neighborhood looking its best. This consistency supports strong property values and makes gated communities a sound long-term investment in Land O' Lakes.

Lower Traffic and Quieter Streets

Because through-traffic is eliminated, gated community streets are quieter and safer. Children can ride bikes, families can walk the dog, and residents can enjoy their front yards without the noise and hazards of public road traffic.

Top Gated Communities in Land O' Lakes

Connerton

Connerton is one of Land O' Lakes's most desirable gated communities. The neighborhood features well-built homes with modern floor plans, generous lot sizes, and premium finishes. Community amenities often include a resort-style pool, fitness facility, and miles of walking trails. The HOA maintains common areas to a high standard, creating a polished, welcoming environment throughout the community.

Homes in Connerton appeal to families, professionals, and retirees alike. You will find a range of home sizes, from three-bedroom starter homes to spacious five-bedroom estates with expansive owners suites, gourmet kitchens, and outdoor living areas.

Oakstead

Oakstead offers another excellent gated living option in Land O' Lakes. This community is known for its well-designed homes, tree-lined streets, and strong neighborhood identity. Residents enjoy access to community amenities while benefiting from the security and privacy that gated access provides.

The location of Oakstead provides convenient access to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton. Whether you are commuting to work, running errands, or heading out for recreation, everything you need is close by.

Understanding HOA Fees in Land O' Lakes Gated Communities

Homeowners association fees are part of gated community living. In Land O' Lakes, monthly HOA fees typically range from $150 to $500 or more, depending on the community and its amenities. Here is what your HOA fees generally cover:

  • Gate and security infrastructure maintenance
  • Common area landscaping and irrigation
  • Community pool, fitness center, and clubhouse upkeep
  • Street lighting and road maintenance within the community
  • Reserve funds for major repairs and improvements
  • Management company fees

When evaluating a gated community, review the HOA's financial statements and reserve study. A well-managed HOA with healthy reserves is a sign of a community that takes care of its properties and infrastructure. Your REALTOR® can help you evaluate HOA documents as part of the purchase process.

Why Land O' Lakes?

Land O' Lakes is a nature-rich community known for its lakes, preserves, and family-friendly master-planned developments. Residents enjoy Conner Preserve, Wilderness Park, and the Suncoast Trail. The Suncoast Parkway provides quick access to Tampa and Gulf beaches.

The area is served by Land O' Lakes High, Sunlake High, and Pine View Elementary. Families and retirees alike are drawn to Land O' Lakes's combination of safety, community, and Florida lifestyle. With easy access to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton, gated community residents enjoy both suburban tranquility and urban convenience.

Buying a Gated Community Home - What to Know

Before purchasing in a gated community in Land O' Lakes, here are some important considerations:

  • Review the CC&Rs: Covenants, Conditions, and Restrictions govern what you can and cannot do with your property. Understand rules about exterior modifications, parking, pets, and rentals before you buy.
  • Evaluate the HOA: Request the HOA budget, reserves, and meeting minutes. A well-run HOA is essential to maintaining property values.
  • Consider CDD fees: Some newer communities in Land O' Lakes have Community Development District fees in addition to HOA fees. These are typically used to pay for infrastructure and appear on your property tax bill.
  • Visit at different times: Drive through the community during the day, evening, and weekend to get a true sense of the neighborhood's activity and atmosphere.
  • Understand guest access: Know how guests, delivery drivers, and service providers will access the community. Some gated communities require advance notification or gate codes.

Why Land O Lakes Is One of Tampa Bay's Best-Kept Secrets

Land O Lakes occupies a genuinely strategic position in the greater Tampa Bay residential market, close enough to Tampa's employment and amenity base to be practical for daily life, yet far enough removed to offer the spacious lots, natural lake scenery, and relative tranquility that suburban and exurban buyers increasingly demand. Situated in southern Pasco County along the Suncoast Parkway (Veterans Expressway) corridor, Land O Lakes provides direct, traffic-light-free expressway access to Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, and downtown Tampa in under 35 minutes from most community entrances. This combination of rural character and urban access is rare in a metro area that has grown as quickly as Tampa Bay, and it explains why Land O Lakes has seen consistent demand growth as buyers priced out of Hillsborough County look north for comparable value.

One of Land O Lakes' defining characteristics is the sheer diversity of its real estate product. Unlike Wesley Chapel, which is dominated by recent master-planned CDD communities, Land O Lakes offers a genuinely varied landscape: older established neighborhoods with large lots and no HOA, lakefront properties on the area's numerous natural lakes, master-planned communities with resort amenities, golf-course living, and newer developments with modern construction standards. This diversity means the area serves a much broader buyer spectrum than its smaller neighbor communities. A retired couple seeking a lakefront property with no HOA restrictions can find it on Lake Padgett or Lake Saxon. A young family prioritizing the Sunlake High School IB program can find it in Connerton or Lakeshore Ranch. An executive wanting a gated golf community can find it in Oakstead. The community's ability to serve multiple buyer profiles simultaneously is a key competitive advantage.

Pasco County's historically lower tax burden compared to Hillsborough County is a meaningful financial consideration for Land O Lakes buyers. While the difference in millage rates varies year to year, Land O Lakes property owners generally pay less in annual property taxes on comparable assessed values than they would on equivalent homes in New Tampa or other Hillsborough County communities. For buyers financing with a mortgage, this tax differential is reflected in their monthly payment and can meaningfully affect affordability calculations. It is also worth noting that many of Land O Lakes' established communities, particularly Lake Padgett Estates, carry no HOA fees and no CDD assessments, making them some of the lowest total-cost-of-ownership options in the entire Tampa Bay market for buyers who value that flexibility.

The commercial and infrastructure landscape along Land O Lakes' SR-54 corridor has evolved dramatically in recent years, transforming what was once a largely underdeveloped stretch into a rapidly filling commercial district. New grocery anchors, major retail tenants, medical facilities, and restaurant chains have arrived along SR-54 between US-41 and the Suncoast Parkway, reducing residents' need to travel south into Hillsborough for everyday needs. The area's proximity to the Tampa Bay area's growing healthcare system, including Florida Medical Clinic's multiple Land O Lakes locations and convenient access to BayCare and AdventHealth facilities to the east in Wesley Chapel, rounds out the lifestyle picture. For buyers who discovered Tampa Bay through Wesley Chapel's marketing machine but find the price point challenging, Land O Lakes routinely offers comparable amenity levels at 10 to 15% lower median prices, making it a compelling alternative that more buyers are discovering each year.

Land O Lakes Communities & Neighborhoods

Connerton

One of Land O Lakes' most successful master-planned communities, Connerton is notable for offering resort-style amenities, multiple pools, fitness center, tennis and pickleball courts, walking trails, and a full-service clubhouse, without CDD fees in many of its sections, a rare combination in the Tampa Bay market. The community sits along the SR-41 corridor north of SR-54 and features well-maintained streetscapes, dedicated conservation greenways, and a variety of home sizes and price points from the low $300s to the mid-$500s. Connerton's community events calendar and active HOA make it a genuinely cohesive neighborhood rather than just a collection of houses.

Oakstead

A gated golf-course community centered around the Oakstead Golf Club's 18-hole course, Oakstead offers a refined lifestyle in a well-established setting. The community features multiple gated sections with varying levels of privacy and price points, a clubhouse with dining, resort-style pool, tennis courts, and fitness facilities. Homes range from attached villas in the mid-$300s to large single-family estates exceeding $700,000 on premium golf-course lots. Oakstead's guard-gated entry and golf-course orientation attract buyers seeking an active adult or executive lifestyle.

Lake Padgett Estates

Lake Padgett Estates is a beloved established community that occupies a unique niche in the Land O Lakes market: lakefront and lake-access properties with no HOA and minimal deed restrictions. Homes here sit on and around a chain of natural lakes including Lake Padgett, Lake Saxon, and others, offering genuine waterfront living at price points significantly below what comparable lakefront would cost in Hillsborough County. The neighborhood attracts buyers who value individual freedom, boat docks, RV parking, workshops, alongside the natural beauty of Florida lake living. Homes range broadly from the mid-$200s for interior lots to $1 million-plus for premium lakefront estates.

Lakeshore Ranch

A newer master-planned community developed in the 2010s, Lakeshore Ranch features exceptional amenity levels including three community pools, a fishing dock, fitness center, tennis courts, basketball courts, and a large clubhouse. The community's lakeside setting creates a resort-like atmosphere that rivals communities in Wesley Chapel at a typically more competitive price point. Newer construction with modern floor plans, energy-efficient systems, and contemporary finishes make Lakeshore Ranch a strong choice for buyers seeking move-in-ready homes in Land O Lakes.

Ballantrae

Ballantrae is a well-regarded community along the SR-54 corridor offering newer construction, a community pool and park, and competitive pricing in the mid-to-upper $300s. The community's location provides convenient access to both the SR-54 commercial corridor and the Suncoast Parkway. Ballantrae tends to attract young families and first-time move-up buyers who want modern construction and community amenities without the full CDD cost structure of some neighboring communities.

Suncoast Lakes & Other Communities

Suncoast Lakes is a community positioned directly along the Suncoast Parkway corridor, offering a clubhouse, pool, and walking trails with excellent expressway access. Land O Lakes also contains numerous other established and emerging communities including Plantation Palms (golf), Lake Thomas Pointe, Dupree Lakes, and a variety of smaller subdivisions and rural residential areas. The breadth of options across price points, lot sizes, and lifestyle orientations makes Land O Lakes one of the most versatile markets in the greater Tampa Bay area.

Land O Lakes Schools

Pasco County Schools has invested heavily in Land O Lakes' educational infrastructure, and the area's flagship high school now offers one of the most distinctive academic programs in the region.

Sunlake High School

Sunlake High School is Land O Lakes' flagship public high school and is home to a fully accredited International Baccalaureate (IB) programme, one of only a handful of Pasco County schools to offer this rigorous globally recognized curriculum. Sunlake has earned strong state school grades and offers robust AP course offerings, competitive athletics, performing arts, and dual-enrollment partnerships. The IB program is a significant draw for academically motivated families choosing between Land O Lakes and other north Tampa Bay communities.

Land O Lakes High School

Land O Lakes High School serves portions of the community and offers a comprehensive curriculum with AP courses, vocational and career-technical programs, strong athletics, and fine arts. The school has a long history in the community and continues to develop new programs to serve Land O Lakes' growing and increasingly diverse student population.

Middle & Elementary Schools

Land O Lakes is served by multiple well-regarded middle schools including Pine View Middle and Charles S. Rushe Middle School. Elementary schools in the area include Connerton Elementary, Sunlake Academy, and several others with strong track records of academic achievement. Pasco County continues to open new schools in the Land O Lakes area to keep pace with residential growth, meaning many facilities are relatively new and well-equipped.

Private & Charter Options

Several private school options operate in the Land O Lakes area, supplemented by access to established Tampa-area private schools via the Suncoast Parkway. Charter school options within Pasco County add additional flexibility. Always verify current school zone assignments with Pasco County Schools before purchasing, as rapid growth in the area regularly prompts boundary adjustments.

Amenities, Employment & Lifestyle

Healthcare Access

  • Florida Medical Clinic (Land O Lakes locations)
  • AdventHealth Wesley Chapel (nearby east)
  • BayCare Wesley Chapel Hospital
  • Pasco County Health Department
  • Growing network of specialty practices on SR-54

Shopping & Dining

  • SR-54 commercial corridor (rapidly developing)
  • US-41 (Land O Lakes Blvd) retail strip
  • Publix, Walmart, major grocers
  • Quick access to Tampa Premium Outlets
  • Growing restaurant selection along SR-54
  • Bealls, TJ Maxx, Home Depot, Target

Lakes & Outdoor Recreation

  • Lake Padgett, Lake Saxon, Lake Thomas
  • Fishing, boating, kayaking, swimming
  • Connerton Nature Preserve trails
  • Oakstead Golf Club (18-hole public/semi-private)
  • Plantation Palms Golf Club
  • Pasco County parks and sports fields

Commute & Transportation

  • Suncoast Parkway to Tampa (35 min)
  • Direct to Tampa International Airport
  • Westshore business district access
  • SR-54 east connection to Wesley Chapel & I-75
  • US-41 south to Lutz & Tampa
  • PCPT bus service available

Buyer's Note: HOA & CDD Landscape in Land O Lakes

Land O Lakes is unique in the north Tampa Bay market because it contains a mix of communities with HOAs and CDDs, communities with HOA only (and no CDD), and older established neighborhoods with neither. This creates a wide range of total cost-of-ownership scenarios. Lake Padgett Estates, for example, has no HOA fees and no CDD, but also no community amenities. Connerton offers amenities with HOA fees but some sections carry no CDD. Always request a full fee disclosure from any community before making an offer. Barrett Henry will help you understand the complete financial picture of any specific property.

Frequently Asked Questions, Land O Lakes Homes

What is the median home price in Land O Lakes in 2026?

The median sale price in Land O Lakes across zip codes 34637, 34638, and 34639 is approximately $395,000 as of early 2026. Prices range from the low-to-mid $200s for smaller homes in older non-HOA neighborhoods to over $1 million for premium lakefront properties in Lake Padgett Estates or luxury estates in Oakstead. The median price point is notably lower than comparable communities in Wesley Chapel and significantly lower than New Tampa, making Land O Lakes an attractive value proposition for buyers seeking the north Tampa Bay lifestyle at a lower entry price.

Is Land O Lakes a city or unincorporated area?

Land O Lakes is an unincorporated community within Pasco County, it does not have its own city government, mayor, or city council. This means land use decisions, zoning, and public services are managed at the county level by Pasco County government. For homeowners, this typically means property taxes go to the county rather than a city, and there is no separate city income or utility tax. The unincorporated status also means slightly different development rules than incorporated cities, which has historically allowed for a mix of rural and suburban character that buyers find appealing.

Does Land O Lakes have lakefront homes available?

Yes, this is one of Land O Lakes' most distinctive features. The area is dotted with natural lakes, and Lake Padgett Estates in particular offers a significant inventory of lakefront and lake-access homes at price points well below what comparable lakefront costs in Hillsborough County or coastal Pasco communities. Lakes in the area support boating, fishing, swimming, and kayaking. Lakefront inventory turns over regularly but tends to sell quickly when priced correctly. Barrett Henry monitors lakefront inventory closely and can alert you when new lake-access properties hit the market.

What are the property taxes like in Land O Lakes compared to Tampa?

Pasco County's millage rate has historically been modestly lower than Hillsborough County's, resulting in somewhat lower base property taxes on equivalent assessed values. On a $400,000 home, the annual tax savings compared to an equivalent Hillsborough property can range from a few hundred to over a thousand dollars depending on the specific millage rates in effect that year and applicable exemptions. Florida's homestead exemption applies equally in both counties. Buyers should request current millage rates from both counties and calculate the specific tax impact on any property they are considering.

How is the Suncoast Parkway for commuting?

The Suncoast Parkway (SR-589) is a tolled limited-access expressway that runs north-south through western Pasco County, connecting Land O Lakes directly to the Veterans Expressway and onward to Tampa's Westshore business district and Tampa International Airport. Under normal traffic conditions, Land O Lakes residents can reach the airport in approximately 30 to 35 minutes and Westshore in about 30 minutes. The expressway is generally less congested than I-75 or I-275 during peak hours, making it a relatively stress-free commute corridor. SunPass transponders are recommended for frequent users to avoid toll plazas.

What are the best communities in Land O Lakes for families with children?

Families with children consistently favor Connerton (excellent amenities, no CDD sections, Sunlake HS pyramid), Lakeshore Ranch (resort amenities, newer construction, strong schools), and communities within the Sunlake High School attendance zone for IB program access. Ballantrae and communities near SR-54 are also popular for their newer construction, proximity to schools, and competitive pricing. The school assignment for any specific address should be verified with Pasco County Schools before purchasing, as the IB program at Sunlake is a zoned-school program with some magnet pathways.

Is there new construction available in Land O Lakes?

Yes, Land O Lakes has active new construction in several communities. Connerton continues to have new phases and occasional infill lots. New communities along the SR-54 and Suncoast Parkway corridors are being developed as Pasco County's growth extends westward. Compared to Wesley Chapel, the new construction pipeline in Land O Lakes is smaller, but it is growing as developers recognize the market's strength. National and regional builders including Lennar, D.R. Horton, and M/I Homes have been active in the area. Barrett Henry works with buyers on new construction purchases and provides guidance on builder contracts and upgrades.

What is Connerton's unique selling point in Land O Lakes?

Connerton is often cited as the best value master-planned community in the Land O Lakes market because it delivers resort-level amenities, multiple pools, a large fitness center, tennis and pickleball courts, miles of trails, a clubhouse with event facilities, while many sections carry no CDD (Community Development District) assessments. In Wesley Chapel, comparable amenity levels typically come with CDD fees of $1,000 to $3,000+ per year on top of HOA dues. Connerton's ability to offer a similar amenity experience without the CDD burden makes it uniquely attractive for cost-conscious buyers who still want the master-planned lifestyle.

Is Land O Lakes at risk from hurricanes or flooding?

Land O Lakes' inland location in Pasco County places it well outside the coastal storm surge zones that threaten waterfront Tampa Bay communities. It is not subject to the evacuation orders that affect coastal zones during hurricane events. That said, Florida's flat terrain means any area can experience localized flooding during extreme rainfall. Most Land O Lakes subdivisions are in FEMA Flood Zone X (minimal hazard), though properties adjacent to retention ponds, wetlands, or natural lakes should have their specific zone verified. The natural lakes in Lake Padgett Estates can see elevated water levels during wet seasons and wet years.

Pool Homes for Sale in Land O' Lakes, Florida

If you are searching for a home with a pool in Land O' Lakes, you have come to the right place. Land O' Lakes is a nature-rich community known for its lakes, preserves, and family-friendly master-planned developments, and pool homes here are among the most sought-after properties in Pasco County. With Florida's year-round sunshine and warm climate, a private pool is not just a luxury - it is a lifestyle upgrade that allows you to enjoy outdoor living every single day.

Pool homes in Land O' Lakes generally range from $350,000 to $700,000, depending on the neighborhood, lot size, pool type, and home features. Popular neighborhoods for pool homes include Connerton, Oakstead, Lakeshore Ranch, Dupree Lakes, and Lake Padgett. Whether you are looking for a screened-in lanai with a heated pool or a resort-style backyard with a spa and outdoor kitchen, Land O' Lakes has options to match your vision.

Why Buy a Pool Home in Land O' Lakes?

Florida homeowners use their pools nearly year-round, and Land O' Lakes is no exception. The warm Pasco County climate means you can swim from March through November without heating, and many homeowners enjoy their pools even during the milder winter months with an affordable pool heater. Here is why buyers love pool homes in Land O' Lakes:

  • Year-round outdoor living: Florida's climate makes a pool home a daily amenity, not a seasonal luxury. Screened enclosures keep bugs out while letting the sunshine in.
  • Increased property value: Pool homes in Land O' Lakes consistently command a premium over comparable homes without pools. When it comes time to resell, a well-maintained pool is a strong selling point.
  • Family and entertainment: A backyard pool is the centerpiece of family life - from weekend barbecues to daily exercise to quiet evenings by the water.
  • Health and wellness: Swimming is one of the best low-impact exercises available. Having a pool at home makes it easy to stay active every day.
  • Florida lifestyle: There is a reason people move to Florida - the outdoor lifestyle. A pool home in Land O' Lakes lets you live it fully.

Top Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Land O' Lakes

Connerton

Connerton is one of the most popular neighborhoods in Land O' Lakes for pool homes. Homes here typically feature spacious lots, modern construction, and well-designed outdoor living spaces. Many properties include screened pools, covered lanais, and fenced backyards - ideal for families and those who enjoy entertaining. The community offers convenient access to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton.

Oakstead

Oakstead attracts buyers seeking quality pool homes with strong community amenities. You will find a range of architectural styles here, from single-story ranch homes to two-story residences with expansive floor plans. Many pool homes in Oakstead include upgraded features like saltwater pools, travertine decking, and summer kitchens.

Lakeshore Ranch

Lakeshore Ranch offers pool homes that appeal to a variety of budgets and preferences. Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an entry-level pool home or a move-up buyer seeking a luxury retreat, this neighborhood has options worth exploring. Many homes feature open floor plans that flow seamlessly to the pool area, creating a true indoor-outdoor living experience.

What to Look for When Buying a Pool Home in Land O' Lakes

Purchasing a pool home involves some additional considerations beyond a standard home purchase. Here is what savvy buyers should know when shopping for pool properties in Land O' Lakes:

Pool Condition and Age

Have the pool inspected separately from the home inspection. A qualified pool inspector will check the pump, filter, heater, surface condition, plumbing, and equipment pad. Resurfacing a pool can cost $5,000 to $15,000, so knowing the pool's condition before you buy is essential. Ask the seller for maintenance records and the age of key equipment.

Screen Enclosure

Most pool homes in Land O' Lakes feature screened enclosures (also called pool cages or lanai screens). These are essential in Florida to keep out insects, reduce debris in the pool, and provide a comfortable outdoor living space. Inspect the screen enclosure carefully - replacement can cost $5,000 to $20,000 depending on size. Hurricane damage to screens is common in Florida, so check for any patches or structural issues.

Insurance and Costs

Pools do affect homeowners insurance premiums in Florida. Make sure to get insurance quotes before closing so you understand the full cost of ownership. Monthly pool maintenance typically runs $100 to $200, and electricity for the pool pump adds to your utility bill. Many Land O' Lakes homeowners find that these costs are well worth the lifestyle benefits.

Pool Type and Features

Common pool types in Land O' Lakes include concrete (gunite), fiberglass, and vinyl liner. Concrete pools are the most common in Florida and offer the most customization. Look for features like:

  • Saltwater vs. chlorine systems (saltwater is gentler on skin and lower maintenance)
  • Pool heating - heat pumps are energy-efficient and extend your swim season
  • Spa or hot tub integration
  • LED pool lighting for evening ambiance
  • Sun shelf or tanning ledge for lounging
  • Outdoor kitchen or summer kitchen near the pool

Why Land O' Lakes?

Land O' Lakes offers a compelling combination of lifestyle, location, and value that makes it one of the best places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region. Residents enjoy Conner Preserve, Wilderness Park, and the Suncoast Trail. The Suncoast Parkway provides quick access to Tampa and Gulf beaches.

The Land O' Lakes area is served by Land O' Lakes High, Sunlake High, and Pine View Elementary, making it attractive to families. Commuters appreciate the proximity to Tampa (25 minutes south), Suncoast Parkway access, Advent Health Connerton.

Whether you are relocating to the Tampa Bay area, upgrading to a larger home, or looking for your dream pool property, Land O' Lakes deserves a place on your shortlist.

The 2026 median home price is around $400,000, with 2-3% annual appreciation keeping it in line with broader Tampa Bay trends. Wesley Chapel's explosive growth has had a halo effect on Land O Lakes, rising values and increased retail development have made this area one of Pasco's most desirable. What's Happening in the Land O Lakes Market Right Now?

The Land O Lakes market is powered by new construction demand. Communities like Connerton, Bexley (at its northern edge), and Wilderness Lake Preserve continue to draw buyers who want square footage and newer builds. Resale inventory is limited, 2.5 months, which keeps sellers competitive. The biggest shift in 2026 is that buyers are more rate-aware than ever; many are opting for builder rate buydowns to get into the low-to-mid 5s rather than accepting the market rate.

Across Tampa Bay, interest rates holding in the 6 to 6.5% range have recalibrated buyer expectations. Monthly payment sensitivity is real: a $420,000 home at 6.25% runs roughly $2,585/month (principal and interest, 20% down), meaningful to most buyers. This has pushed some demand toward rate-buydown incentives, adjustable-rate products, and smaller-footprint homes. Land O Lakes buyers are no different.

Inventory overall remains below pre-2020 levels even as it has improved from the historic lows of 2021-2022. That structural undersupply continues to put a floor under prices across Tampa Bay, Land O Lakes included.

Is It a Buyer's or Seller's Market in Land O Lakes?

Land O Lakes is a slight seller's market in 2026. New construction is giving buyers more choices than in peak 2022, but resale inventory is still tight. Buyers willing to consider quick-move-in or spec homes have the most leverage. On resales, well-maintained homes priced at market are moving in 3-4 weeks.

As a general benchmark: under 3 months of inventory favors sellers; 3-4 months is balanced; above 4 months favors buyers. Land O Lakes's 2.5 months of supply tells the story. Conditions can shift quickly, especially if mortgage rates drop or a large employer announces a relocation. Check with a local agent for current week-over-week trends.

Price Trends by Property Type in Land O Lakes

Data reflects Stellar MLS sales data and active listing trends for the Land O Lakes area. Individual property values vary by condition, location within the market, and upgrade level.

Should You Buy in Land O Lakes in 2026?

The short answer: yes, if your finances support it and you're planning to hold for at least 3-5 years.

Land O Lakes is a quality long-term hold, schools, amenities, and proximity to the Suncoast Parkway support continued demand. If you're considering new construction, compare builder incentives carefully; rate buydowns are worth more than most upgrade packages. Explore Land O Lakes listings and community details.

Trying to time the market is a losing game in a market like Land O Lakes. Buyers who waited in 2023 for prices to drop are now buying at higher prices and higher rates. The fundamentals that drive Land O Lakes's demand, location, schools, employment access, lifestyle, haven't changed. Every month you wait is another month of rent you're paying toward someone else's equity.

If you're weighing Land O Lakes against neighboring communities, it's worth a conversation with a local agent who knows the micro-level differences. Small neighborhood details, flood zone designations, HOA restrictions, school district lines, commute times at peak hours, can make a significant difference in both lifestyle and resale value.

Should You Sell in Land O Lakes in 2026?

The short answer: yes, if you price it right and present it well.

Sellers competing against nearby new construction need to be strategic. Price at or slightly below comparable new builds to attract buyers who want established landscaping, no build wait time, and negotiating room. Updated kitchens and bathrooms are strong differentiators.

The sellers who struggle in 2026 are the ones anchoring to 2022 peak pricing. The market has normalized. That's not bad news, it's a functional, sustainable market. Properly priced, well-maintained homes in Land O Lakes are still closing in 25-40 days and sellers are netting strong proceeds relative to their purchase basis.

Key preparation steps before listing in Land O Lakes: pull comparable sales from the last 90 days (not 6 months), get a pre-listing inspection if your home is 15+ years old, invest in professional photography, and have a conversation about timing, certain months outperform others even in a steady market.

How Land O Lakes Compares to the Broader Tampa Bay Market

Tampa Bay as a region continues to perform above national averages in 2026. Population growth, job creation in finance, healthcare, and tech, and a relative affordability advantage over coastal metros (Miami, Naples, Sarasota) are driving sustained in-migration. Land O Lakes benefits from all of those macro tailwinds while having its own neighborhood-specific demand drivers.

For buyers or sellers comparing multiple Tampa Bay communities, understanding where Land O Lakes sits in the regional pricing ladder is essential. At $400,000 median, Land O Lakes is positioned as a distinct community with its own value proposition not just a suburb of Tampa.
