title: Sun City Center Real Estate | Barrett Henry
content:
Sun City Center, Florida is one of the largest and most celebrated 55+ retirement communities in the United States. Located in south Hillsborough County along I-75, this golf-cart community offers a resort-style lifestyle with hundreds of clubs, multiple pools, sports facilities, and the kind of social calendar most people only dream about in retirement. If you or someone in your family is exploring 55+ living in the Tampa Bay area, Sun City Center deserves a serious look.

Founded in 1961 by Del Webb, the same developer who built the original Sun City in Arizona, Sun City Center grew into a self-sufficient retirement town over the following decades. Today it encompasses multiple distinct communities, each with its own character, HOA structure, and amenity package, all sharing the same golf cart roads, medical facilities, and commercial corridor that make daily life here genuinely convenient. With a combined population estimated at over 20,000 residents across all sections, it is a real community, not just a subdivision.

This guide covers everything you need to know: the communities, home prices, amenities, pros and cons, and the real estate market as it stands heading into 2026. Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has helped buyers navigate the Tampa Bay and Nature Coast markets for over two decades and knows this corner of south Hillsborough County well.

Why Sun City Center is One of Tampa Bay's Best Kept Secrets

Most people outside of Florida have heard of The Villages in central Florida, but serious retirement researchers quickly discover Sun City Center. It offers comparable amenities at a fraction of the price, with proximity to Tampa's world-class medical facilities, international airport, professional sports teams, and Gulf beaches. It has been consistently recognized by national retirement publications as one of the top places to retire in America.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Sun City Center Homes

What sets Sun City Center apart is the golf cart culture. Residents drive their carts on dedicated community roads to reach clubhouses, restaurants, shopping, medical offices, and neighbors' homes. The freedom that comes with that lifestyle is something visitors consistently say they didn't fully appreciate until they experienced it firsthand. It is a real town built around active adult living, not a gated resort that happens to allow older residents.

The community also benefits from its location midway between Tampa and Sarasota. Residents are roughly 30 minutes from Tampa, 30 minutes from Sarasota, and about 30 to 45 minutes from the Gulf beaches. That kind of central positioning is hard to replicate elsewhere in Florida at this price point. For families who have loved ones considering retirement communities, explore our full Tampa Bay 55+ Communities Guide to compare options across the region.

Sun City Center also benefits from strong community identity and infrastructure that has developed over more than 60 years. The roads, commercial corridor, medical facilities, and community organizations have all matured to a degree that gives new residents an immediate support structure. Unlike newer 55+ developments that may have amenities under construction or commercial development still years away, Sun City Center is complete. The restaurants, doctors, grocery stores, banks, and social organizations are all there, ready to be used from day one. That maturity is a significant practical advantage, particularly for buyers who are making a permanent move rather than a seasonal arrangement.

Where is Sun City Center? Location, Geography, and Getting Around

Sun City Center sits in southern Hillsborough County, roughly 25 to 30 miles south of downtown Tampa. The community centers around Sun City Center Boulevard (SR-674), which runs east-west through the heart of the area. Interstate 75 forms the eastern boundary, with Exit 240 providing the primary access point. US-41 (Tamiami Trail) runs along the western edge.

The geography is flat and well-suited to year-round outdoor living. The community is surrounded by wetlands and nature preserves, including Little Manatee River State Park to the north and the Apollo Beach Nature Preserve to the west. Nearby communities include Ruskin to the north and Apollo Beach to the northwest. Both offer additional dining, waterfront access, and services that Sun City Center residents use regularly.

Within the community, golf carts are the primary mode of transportation for many residents. Carts can be driven on internal roads during all hours and on certain community roads during daylight hours. Kings Point operates a tram service that circulates within the gated section and also shuttles residents to nearby grocery stores, pharmacies, and medical offices. For travel outside the immediate area, residents rely on personal vehicles or rideshare services, as public transit options are limited.

Tampa International Airport is approximately 35 to 40 minutes north via I-75. Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport is roughly 35 minutes south, offering another option for those who travel frequently. For everyday needs, Sun City Center Boulevard has grocery stores, pharmacies, medical offices, banks, and restaurants within golf-cart distance.

Sun City Center Real Estate Market Overview

The Sun City Center real estate market has shifted toward buyers heading into 2026. As of late 2026, median home prices were in the range of $279,000 to $295,000, representing a notable pullback from the post-pandemic peaks. Inventory has increased significantly, with the number of available homes up roughly 30% compared to the prior year. Homes are taking longer to sell, averaging around 80 to 90 days on market, which gives buyers more time and more leverage than they had in 2022 or 2023.

Price ranges vary considerably by property type and community. Condos and villas in Kings Point can start below $150,000 for smaller attached units, while larger single-family homes in the original Sun City Center community or newer sections can reach into the $400,000s to $500,000s. The typical home value across the broader area hovers around $320,000, which is substantially below Tampa's metro median and well below the national average.

The buyer's market conditions reflect both the increased inventory and some specific dynamics of the 55+ market. Many sellers are aging-in-place residents transitioning to assisted living, estates, or residents who purchased during the peak and need to right-size. For buyers, this creates real opportunity. For sellers, pricing correctly and presenting homes well is more important than it has been in recent years.

If you're weighing a purchase or thinking about selling, a free home valuation is the right starting point. Barrett works with buyers exploring their options and sellers who need a clear-eyed market strategy. The Florida closing costs guide is also worth reviewing before you begin the process.

Neighborhoods and Subdivisions in Sun City Center

Sun City Center is not a single development. It is a collection of distinct communities sharing a common geographic footprint and lifestyle. Understanding the differences matters, because HOA fees, amenities, age restrictions, and property types vary significantly from one section to the next.

The Original Sun City Center Community: This is the neighborhood built by Del Webb beginning in 1961. It contains approximately 6,200 homes and is home to roughly 11,000 residents. It is managed by the Sun City Center Community Association (SCC CA), which governs amenities across three campuses (Central, South, and West). Each campus has its own clubhouse, fitness center, pools, sports courts, and activity spaces. The community association fee is modest compared to Kings Point, making this section more affordable from an HOA perspective. Single-family homes here range widely in size and vintage.

Kings Point: Kings Point is a large gated community within Sun City Center, built between 1973 and 2015, with approximately 5,277 attached villas and single-family homes housing around 9,500 residents. It is arguably the most amenity-rich section. The 90,000-square-foot Kings Point Clubhouse includes indoor and outdoor pools, a fitness center, hobby rooms, billiards, a cafe, and the Borini Theater. A second South Clubhouse adds a resort-style pool, craft studios, and a cyber cafe. HOA fees in Kings Point vary by sub-association and can range from a few hundred to over $500 per month. The tram service within Kings Point and to surrounding areas is a major quality-of-life feature. Kings Point is often compared to other gated retirement communities, and it typically comes out favorably on value.

Renaissance: Renaissance is a newer gated section within Sun City Center, offering more contemporary home designs and a slightly different vibe from the older sections. It has its own amenities and HOA structure. Homes here tend to be newer construction and can command a premium over comparable properties in the original community.

Cypress Creek and Surrounding Areas: Just outside the core 55+ areas, Cypress Creek and similar communities offer townhomes and single-family homes that are not age-restricted. These are popular with younger families, investors, and those who want proximity to Sun City Center's services without the age requirement. The CDD fee guide is helpful here, as some of these communities carry community development district fees.

For a broader comparison of retirement living options across the Tampa Bay area, visit our Tampa Bay 55+ Communities Guide. If golf is part of your retirement vision, our Tampa Bay Golf Communities Guide is worth bookmarking as well.

Schools in Sun City Center: Ratings, Zoning, and Options

Sun City Center is primarily a retirement community, and school quality is not the primary driver for most buyers here. However, some residents have grandchildren who visit regularly or family members in the area, and it is worth understanding the local school landscape. The community falls within Hillsborough County Public Schools, which is the eighth-largest school district in the United States.

Eisenhower Middle School and Lennard High School serve much of the south Hillsborough area surrounding Sun City Center. Performance ratings for schools in this part of the county have historically been below the district's northern suburban averages. Buyers who have school-aged children in their household and are considering the non-age-restricted sections near Sun City Center should consult Hillsborough County's school finder to confirm current zoning, as boundaries can change.

For buyers focused primarily on retirement living in the age-restricted sections, schools are a secondary consideration. The proximity to USF, Hillsborough Community College, and other higher education institutions in the broader Tampa Bay area does give residents access to continuing education programs, which are popular among active retirees.

Lifelong learning is a significant part of the culture in Sun City Center. Many residents take advantage of Hillsborough Community College's continuing education programs, OLLI (Osher Lifelong Learning Institute) at the University of South Florida, and lecture series hosted within the community's own clubhouses. Educational travel programs, book clubs, and computer literacy classes organized through community clubs keep residents engaged well beyond their formal working years. This kind of intellectual engagement is often cited by long-term residents as one of the underrated benefits of life in Sun City Center.

Things to Do in Sun City Center

Activity is the defining feature of life in Sun City Center. The greater community supports nearly 200 clubs and interest groups across its various neighborhoods. Whether your interests run toward pickleball, woodworking, oil painting, genealogy research, Tai Chi, model railroading, or line dancing, there is almost certainly a club for it. The breadth and depth of organized activity is genuinely remarkable for a community of this size.

Sports and fitness options are extensive. Residents have access to indoor and outdoor swimming pools, tennis courts, pickleball courts, shuffleboard, lawn bowling, volleyball, basketball, and a softball field. There are eight golf courses within and immediately around the Sun City Center area, offering more than 160 holes of golf. The courses include both 18-hole and executive-length options and are open to the public as well as residents.

The Borini Theater in Kings Point hosts performances and live entertainment throughout the year. There are multiple fitness centers, a computer lab, art studios, ceramics, woodworking, and more across the three campuses. The community also has a dog park, walking trails, and a movie screening room.

Beyond the gates, residents enjoy day trips to the Gulf beaches (roughly 40 to 45 minutes), the cultural offerings of Tampa and Sarasota, and nature activities at Little Manatee River State Park and the Apollo Beach Nature Preserve, where manatees gather in the warm waters near the TECO power plant from fall through spring. The Tampa Bay Beaches Guide has the details on the best coastal spots within range.

Volunteering is also a major part of life in Sun City Center. The community's Emergency Squad, staffed entirely by volunteers, is a nationally recognized organization that provides non-emergency medical transport and assistance to residents. It is the kind of grassroots civic institution that defines Sun City Center as a genuine community rather than just a residential development. For residents who come from careers where they had meaningful social roles, the opportunity to continue contributing in retirement through volunteering is a significant quality-of-life factor that the community supports in abundance.

For golf enthusiasts, the situation in Sun City Center is exceptional. Eight courses within and around the community offer more than 160 holes of golf accessible to residents. Courses range from executive-length layouts suited for quick rounds to full 18-hole courses offering a complete game. Residents who play frequently find that having so many options nearby virtually eliminates tee time conflicts and keeps the game fresh. Our Tampa Bay Golf Communities Guide has more on golfing communities across the region if you want to compare.

Best Restaurants and Dining in Sun City Center

Sun City Center Boulevard serves as the main commercial corridor, and dining options within the community have expanded over the years. Residents frequently mention that restaurants in and around Sun City Center have improved considerably, with a growing variety of cuisines and casual dining options accessible by golf cart. The community has multiple cafes within the clubhouse facilities as well, making it easy to grab a meal between activities.

For more varied dining, residents regularly head to nearby Ruskin and Apollo Beach, both of which have grown their restaurant scenes significantly in recent years. Apollo Beach in particular has a number of waterfront dining options that residents enjoy for weekend outings. The Ruskin area also has a well-regarded farmers market and a variety of local eateries. For fine dining and upscale cuisine, Tampa and Sarasota are both within a reasonable drive.

The grocery and market situation within Sun City Center is solid, with major grocery stores, pharmacies, and specialty food shops accessible on or near the main corridor. Residents with dietary restrictions or specialty food needs generally supplement local shopping with occasional trips to the larger store selections in Brandon or Tampa.

Thinking About Sun City Center? Let's Talk.

Barrett Henry has helped buyers and sellers across the Tampa Bay area navigate real estate decisions with confidence. Whether you're exploring Sun City Center for the first time or ready to make a move, a quick conversation can save you time and money.

Call or text: (813) 733-7907 | Email: barrett@nowtb.com

Commute and Transportation from Sun City Center

Most Sun City Center residents are retired and do not commute in the traditional sense. That said, transportation access is still a meaningful consideration, particularly for snowbirds, part-time residents, and those who have family in the Tampa metro area.

Interstate 75 is the primary arterial connection, accessible via Exit 240 at SR-674 (Sun City Center Boulevard). From that interchange, Tampa is approximately 25 to 30 minutes north in normal traffic conditions. Sarasota is roughly 30 to 35 minutes south. Brandon and the broader eastern Hillsborough County area are accessible via US-301 or I-75 north to I-4. The Brandon area is roughly 20 to 25 minutes by interstate.

Tampa International Airport is about 35 to 40 minutes from Sun City Center. Sarasota-Bradenton International Airport is a comparable distance to the south and often easier for residents who prefer a smaller airport experience. Both airports provide solid regional and national connectivity.

Within the community, residents depend on golf carts, personal vehicles, and the Kings Point tram service. There is no meaningful public transit serving Sun City Center proper. Rideshare services (Uber and Lyft) operate in the area and residents use them for medical appointments and other errands when driving is not preferred. Some communities also have volunteer driver programs organized through local churches and civic groups.

Cost of Living in Sun City Center

Sun City Center has earned a reputation as one of the most affordable large 55+ retirement communities in Florida, and that reputation is largely deserved. Home prices are well below the Tampa metro median and significantly below the national average. The community's cost-of-living profile is one of its strongest selling points for retirees on fixed incomes or those looking to stretch their retirement dollars.

HOA and amenity fees vary significantly depending on the section. In the original Sun City Center community, the HOA fees tend to be lower, with a master association fee in the range of a few hundred dollars per year plus per-person amenity access fees. Kings Point has more varied fee structures depending on the specific sub-association, with monthly HOA fees that can range from roughly $200 to over $500. These fees typically cover lawn maintenance, exterior upkeep (for villas and attached homes), building insurance (for condos), and access to amenities. Individual unit owners still pay for interior insurance, property taxes, and utilities separately.

Florida has no state income tax, which is a material benefit for retirees drawing Social Security, pensions, or retirement account distributions. Property taxes in Hillsborough County are moderate. Residents over 65 may qualify for additional homestead exemption benefits that can reduce assessed value further. The Florida HOA rules guide is a useful resource for understanding what to expect before purchasing in any HOA community here.

Day-to-day costs for groceries, healthcare, and services in the Sun City Center area are generally in line with or below Tampa-area averages. The concentration of medical providers in and around the community, including primary care, specialty practices, and an emergency facility, reduces the need for long drives to access healthcare, which can be a hidden cost savings for retirees.

New Construction in Sun City Center

New construction is available in Sun City Center, though the majority of the market here involves resale properties in established communities. The original Del Webb sections and Kings Point were largely built out decades ago, with newer sections added over subsequent years. Renaissance is one of the newer areas of development within the broader Sun City Center footprint.

There are several builders active in the broader south Hillsborough area around Sun City Center offering new 55+ product, and some national builders have listings accessible via the community. Prices for new construction in the area start around $300,000 and move upward depending on the builder, floor plan, and lot. New construction inventory and builder offerings change frequently, so current availability is best confirmed through a real estate professional with active market access.

Buyers considering new construction in a 55+ community should pay close attention to the HOA structure, amenity fees, and CDD charges that accompany new developments. These recurring costs can add hundreds of dollars per month to total housing expense and should be clearly understood before signing a purchase contract. Builder incentives are common in the current market, including mortgage rate buydowns, closing cost contributions, and design center credits. Working with a buyer's agent who is not employed by the builder gives you representation and negotiating leverage that purchasing directly from a builder's sales office does not provide.

For those considering new construction, the surrounding Cypress Creek and Ruskin areas also have active new home developments that are not age-restricted, which may appeal to buyers with younger family members nearby or those who prefer not to be in a 55+ environment. Our Moving to Tampa Bay guide covers new construction options across the broader region. If you are also exploring new luxury options, the luxury properties section of this site has additional resources.

Healthcare in Sun City Center

For retirees, access to quality healthcare is often the deciding factor in choosing where to live. Sun City Center excels here in ways that many comparable communities do not. South Bay Hospital, operated by HCA Florida Healthcare, is located directly in Sun City Center and provides emergency services, inpatient care, surgical suites, and diagnostic imaging. The ability to reach a hospital by golf cart or a very short car ride is something that matters enormously to older adults and their families.

Beyond the hospital, the community has an impressive concentration of medical offices within or immediately adjacent to the commercial corridor. Primary care physicians, cardiologists, orthopedic surgeons, dermatologists, ophthalmologists, and other specialists maintain offices in Sun City Center, reducing the need to travel to Tampa for routine and specialty care. Several urgent care facilities are also within easy reach. For major procedures or specialized treatment not available locally, Tampa General Hospital, Moffitt Cancer Center, and the AdventHealth and BayCare hospital systems in Tampa are all within 30 to 40 minutes.

Assisted living, memory care, and rehabilitation facilities are also well-represented in and around Sun City Center. This matters to residents who are thinking about aging in place and want to know that options exist nearby if needs change. It also matters to adult children who are researching communities for parents and want to understand the full continuum of care available without requiring a move to another city. Sun City Center's healthcare infrastructure is one of its most significant competitive advantages over retirement communities in more rural parts of Florida.

Pros and Cons of Living in Sun City Center

Pros:

  • One of the most amenity-rich 55+ communities in the country at a relatively affordable price point
  • Golf cart lifestyle provides a unique sense of freedom and community connection
  • Nearly 200 clubs and social organizations mean it is very difficult to be bored or isolated
  • Strong proximity to Tampa's medical systems, airport, and cultural amenities
  • Eight golf courses within and around the community
  • Internal tram service (Kings Point) reduces driving burden for residents
  • No Florida state income tax benefits retirees significantly
  • Buyer's market conditions in 2026-2026 create favorable purchase opportunities
  • Active, engaged community culture that consistently ranks among top retirement destinations nationally

Cons:

  • Age restrictions (55+) mean it is not suitable for families or younger buyers
  • HOA and amenity fees can be substantial, particularly in Kings Point, and should be carefully reviewed before purchase
  • Car dependence for travel beyond the community is real; public transit is not a meaningful option
  • Florida's heat and humidity from roughly May through October can be challenging for those accustomed to cooler climates
  • The resale market currently has more supply than demand, which benefits buyers but can challenge sellers who need top dollar
  • Hurricane preparedness is a reality in Florida; buyers should understand flood zone status and insurance costs before purchasing
  • Dining and retail options within golf-cart range, while expanding, are more limited than what a full urban area provides

For guidance on flood zones and insurance considerations, our Florida Flood Zones Guide is a helpful starting point.

Sun City Center Real Estate for Investors

Sun City Center presents an interesting investment profile that differs from typical residential markets. Because the communities are age-restricted, investment properties are purchased for long-term rental income rather than short-term or vacation rental strategies. The renter pool consists of active retirees who prefer to rent before buying, snowbirds who want a seasonal base, or residents transitioning between living situations.

Demand for rental units in 55+ communities tends to be stable, supported by demographics. The population of Americans aged 65 and older is growing rapidly, and Sun City Center is well-positioned to benefit from that trend for years to come. Investors should understand, however, that HOA rules in these communities can restrict rental activity, including minimum lease terms and tenant approval requirements. Reviewing HOA documents carefully before purchasing any investment property here is essential. Our Florida HOA rules guide covers what to look for.

Seasonal rental demand from snowbirds is a meaningful component of the market. Many northern residents spend three to six months in Sun City Center each winter without purchasing a home, preferring the flexibility of renting. This creates a recurring annual demand for furnished units available from October or November through March or April. Investors who can furnish and rent a villa or condo on a seasonal basis have historically found this a productive strategy, though HOA minimum lease periods must be carefully checked before pursuing it.

The non-age-restricted sections near Sun City Center, including Cypress Creek and parts of Ruskin, may offer more flexibility for investors who want broader rental options. These areas have seen population and infrastructure growth that supports rental demand from workers in the south Hillsborough County area. For broader investment strategy across multiple markets, visit the investing section of this site.

One consideration for investors entering this market now: the current buyer's market conditions mean there are opportunities to acquire properties at prices below the peak. Buyers who understand the long-term demographic tailwinds and are patient on appreciation may find this an attractive entry point. As always, consult with a local expert before making any investment decision. Commercial real estate inquiries are also welcome. Those interested in the full property search can browse all current listings across multiple markets.

Making the Transition: Moving to Sun City Center

Moving to a 55+ retirement community is a different kind of real estate decision than buying a typical family home. For many buyers, it involves selling a larger home they have lived in for decades, downsizing their possessions, and relocating to an entirely new geographic area. Sun City Center's real estate market sees this pattern constantly, and the community has developed informal networks to help new residents navigate the transition smoothly.

One practical consideration: the timing of buying in Sun City Center relative to selling your previous home matters. Many buyers choose to rent temporarily in Sun City Center first, spending a winter season to confirm the community is the right fit before committing to a purchase. Others prefer to buy before selling their primary residence and carry both properties briefly. Both strategies have tradeoffs in terms of carrying costs, logistical complexity, and market timing. A conversation with a knowledgeable agent before making either decision can save considerable time and money.

For buyers coming from out of state, it is worth understanding Florida's homestead exemption rules. To claim the full homestead exemption benefit, you must be a permanent Florida resident with the property as your primary domicile as of January 1 of the tax year. Snowbirds who maintain a primary residence in another state do not qualify. Planning the timing of your permanent move around this calendar is a simple step that can save several hundred to a few thousand dollars in annual property taxes. Florida also does not have a state estate tax, which is a meaningful planning consideration for retirees with significant assets.

Families helping parents make the move to Sun City Center should know that Barrett works with adult children who are handling the research and logistics on behalf of a parent or loved one. The real estate process, including reviewing HOA documents, understanding the different communities, and evaluating specific properties for accessibility and functionality, can be navigated with someone who knows the market. Whether you are the buyer or the adult child helping a parent find the right home, the contact page is the best place to start. Nearby Bradenton, Lakeland, and St. Petersburg are worth reviewing if you are comparing multiple communities in the broader region before deciding.

Frequently Asked Questions About Sun City Center

Is Sun City Center strictly age-restricted?
The core communities of Sun City Center and Kings Point require at least one resident to be 55 or older, and no permanent residents under 18 are permitted. Guests and visitors, including grandchildren, can typically stay for extended periods according to HOA rules, but the specific policies vary by sub-association.

Can you really drive golf carts everywhere?
Within the community, yes. Golf carts can be driven on internal roads at any hour. On certain Sun City Center Boulevard roads during daylight hours, carts can access local shopping and services. They cannot be driven on I-75 or other state roads.

What is the difference between Sun City Center and Kings Point?
Kings Point is a gated community within the broader Sun City Center area. It has its own HOA, gate access, separate amenities (including the large Kings Point Clubhouse), and a tram service. The original Sun City Center community is not gated in the same way and is managed by its own community association. Both share proximity to the same shops, restaurants, and medical services along Sun City Center Boulevard.

What are the HOA fees in Sun City Center?
Fees vary considerably. In the original community, the master HOA fee is modest, with additional per-person amenity fees in the range of a few hundred dollars annually. In Kings Point, monthly HOA fees range from roughly $200 to over $500 depending on the specific sub-association and what is included. Always request the HOA disclosure package before making an offer.

How far is Sun City Center from Tampa?
Approximately 25 to 30 miles south of downtown Tampa via I-75. In typical traffic conditions, the drive is around 30 minutes. Tampa International Airport is about 35 to 40 minutes north.

Are there beaches near Sun City Center?
The Gulf beaches are roughly 40 to 45 minutes west. Tampa Bay's eastern shore is closer but does not have the white-sand beach experience of the Gulf Coast. St. Pete Beach, Siesta Key, and other popular beaches are within a manageable drive.

Is Sun City Center a good place to retire?
It consistently ranks among the top retirement destinations in national surveys. The combination of affordability, amenities, social activity, medical access, and central location within Florida's Gulf Coast corridor is hard to beat. Like any community, it suits some lifestyles better than others. Those who embrace social activity and the golf-cart culture tend to love it. Those who prefer quiet privacy and urban amenities may find it less suitable.

What is the Sun City Center climate like?
Subtropical. Winters are mild with temperatures generally in the 60s and 70s. Summers are hot and humid, with daily highs in the 90s from roughly June through September. The community sees its peak population and social activity during the winter months, when snowbirds arrive from northern states and Canada.

Is Sun City Center in a flood zone?
Parts of the Sun City Center area are in FEMA-designated flood zones, and others are not. Flood zone status varies by specific property, so it is critical to look up any property you are considering individually. Our Florida Flood Zones Guide explains how to do this and what the implications are for insurance costs.

What types of homes are available in Sun City Center?
The community has a broad mix of property types, including attached villas (the most common in Kings Point), single-family detached homes, condominiums, and some patio homes. Sizes range from one-bedroom condos to spacious three-bedroom-plus single-family homes with garages and lanais.

Is the Sun City Center real estate market a buyer's market right now?
As of late 2026 and into 2026, yes. Inventory has increased significantly, homes are taking longer to sell, and median prices have pulled back from the 2022-2023 peaks. Buyers have more negotiating room than they have had in several years. This can change, and market conditions should always be verified with a current market analysis.

Does Sun City Center have medical facilities?
Yes. South Bay Hospital is located in Sun City Center and provides emergency and inpatient services. The community has numerous medical offices for primary care and specialty medicine within or immediately adjacent to the community, accessible by golf cart for many residents. Major hospitals in the Tampa Bay system are within about 30 minutes.

Can non-residents buy investment properties in Sun City Center?
Yes, non-residents can purchase properties as investments. However, HOA rules govern rental policies, including minimum lease durations and tenant approval processes. Most communities require leases of at least six months or one year and restrict short-term vacation rentals. Review HOA documents carefully before purchasing for investment.

How does Sun City Center compare to other 55+ communities in Tampa Bay?
Sun City Center is generally larger and more amenity-rich than most 55+ options in the area, and it tends to be more affordable than comparable communities in communities like Sarasota or Lakewood Ranch. Our Tampa Bay 55+ Communities Guide provides a side-by-side look at the options across the region.

What are the nearby communities to Sun City Center?
The immediate neighbors are Ruskin to the north and Apollo Beach to the northwest. Brandon and Riverview are farther north and provide expanded shopping, dining, and services. Bradenton is to the south and offers a full range of urban amenities along with Gulf beach access.

title: Sun City Center 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ homes in Sun City Center typically range from $180,000-$450,000. Top active adult communities in the area include Kings Point and Freedom Plaza, offering resort-style amenities, low-maintenance living, and an active social calendar.

Explore 55+ CommunitiesBrowse Active Adult Homes

Why Active Adults Choose Sun City Center

Sun City Center has become an increasingly popular destination for active adults and retirees seeking the Florida lifestyle without sacrificing access to quality healthcare, cultural amenities, and everyday convenience. Sun City Center is Florida's premier 55+ retirement destination in Hillsborough County. This master-planned active adult community offers golf courses, hundreds of clubs and activities, on-site healthcare, and an unbeatable sense of community. Golf carts are a primary mode of transportation.

The appeal of 55+ living in Sun City Center extends far beyond the weather. Active adult communities in this area provide a turnkey lifestyle that includes exterior home maintenance, landscaping, and community amenities - freeing residents to focus on the activities, travel, and social connections that make retirement fulfilling. With no state income tax, Florida remains one of the most tax-friendly states for retirees, and Sun City Center's cost of living compares favorably to many other retirement destinations along the Gulf Coast.

Whether you are planning a full-time relocation, seeking a seasonal winter residence, or downsizing from a larger home in the area, Sun City Center's 55+ market offers a range of options from maintenance-free villas to single-family homes with full resort amenities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping active adult buyers find the right community and home to match their lifestyle and budget.

Top 55+ Communities in and Near Sun City Center

The following communities represent the best options for 55+ buyers in the Sun City Center area. Each offers a distinct lifestyle, amenity package, and price point.

Kings Point

Kings Point is among the most established and well-regarded active adult communities serving Sun City Center residents. This community offers a comprehensive lifestyle package that includes maintained exteriors, community pools, fitness facilities, and an extensive calendar of social events, clubs, and organized activities. Homes range from attached villas with two bedrooms and two bathrooms to larger single-family residences with three bedrooms, dens, and two-car garages. Floor plans are designed specifically for active adult living, with single-story layouts, wide doorways, step-free entries, and owners suites positioned for privacy. The community atmosphere is welcoming and social, with residents forming lasting friendships through shared activities that range from golf and tennis to card games, art classes, and group travel.

Freedom Plaza

Freedom Plaza provides another excellent option for 55+ buyers in the Sun City Center area. This community appeals to active adults who want a maintenance-free lifestyle without sacrificing home quality or community amenities. Properties here feature modern finishes, energy-efficient construction, and thoughtful floor plans that accommodate both daily living and entertaining. The amenity package typically includes a community clubhouse, pool, walking trails, and organized social programming. Residents appreciate the sense of community that develops naturally when neighbors share similar life stages and interests. The location provides convenient access to healthcare facilities, shopping, dining, and the cultural attractions that make Sun City Center such an appealing retirement destination.

Price & Monthly Cost Overview for Sun City Center 55+ Homes

Understanding the full cost of 55+ living - including purchase price, HOA fees, and additional community charges - is essential for retirement planning. The table below outlines typical costs for active adult properties in the Sun City Center area.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Includes
2-Bed / 2-Bath Villa$180,000-$450,000$200-$500Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2-Bath Single Family$180,000-$450,000$250-$550Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Premium$180,000-$450,000$300-$600Full maintenance, lawn, amenities, cable
Condo / Attached Villa$180,000-$450,000$350-$700Exterior, roof, insurance, amenities

Monthly HOA fees in 55+ communities cover a wide range of services. Some communities include exterior painting, roof maintenance, lawn care, pest control, cable TV, and community amenities in a single monthly fee. Others charge separately for certain services. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a complete cost breakdown for any community you are considering. Contact Barrett for current pricing and availability.

Amenities & Lifestyle in Sun City Center 55+ Communities

The amenity package is what truly sets 55+ communities apart from traditional neighborhoods. Active adult communities in the Sun City Center area offer lifestyle amenities that rival upscale resorts.

Fitness and Wellness

Most 55+ communities in Sun City Center include fitness centers equipped with cardio machines, strength training equipment, and stretching areas designed for active adults. Many offer group fitness classes such as water aerobics, yoga, tai chi, and low-impact cardio that cater specifically to the 55+ demographic. Walking trails, swimming pools, and spa facilities provide additional wellness options that encourage daily physical activity in a comfortable, age-appropriate setting.

Social Clubs and Activities

The social calendar in a well-run 55+ community is remarkably full. Residents in Sun City Center area communities can typically choose from dozens of clubs and interest groups covering everything from bridge and mahjong to woodworking, photography, gardening, and performing arts. Organized activities such as day trips, dinner outings, holiday celebrations, and educational seminars keep the community engaged and connected. For many residents, this built-in social network is the single greatest benefit of 55+ living.

Golf, Tennis, and Recreation

Golf remains a cornerstone of the 55+ lifestyle in Hillsborough County, and many active adult communities near Sun City Center offer on-site or nearby golf courses. Tennis and pickleball courts have become increasingly popular, with organized leagues and social play available most days. Bocce ball, shuffleboard, and horseshoes are additional recreational options that provide both exercise and social interaction in a relaxed, friendly setting.

Pools and Outdoor Living

Community pools in Sun City Center 55+ neighborhoods are designed for both exercise and relaxation. Heated pools extend the swimming season year-round, while separate spa and soaking pools provide therapeutic benefits. Many communities feature poolside pavilions, outdoor grills, and covered seating areas where residents gather for impromptu socializing and organized pool parties throughout the year.

Healthcare Access Near Sun City Center

Access to quality healthcare is a top priority for 55+ buyers, and Sun City Center delivers excellent options. The greater Tampa Bay area is home to some of Florida's finest medical facilities, ensuring that active adult residents are never far from the care they need.

Major healthcare providers serving the Sun City Center area include BayCare Health System, AdventHealth (formerly Florida Hospital), HCA Healthcare facilities, and Tampa General Hospital - consistently ranked among the top hospitals in Florida. Specialty care, including cardiology, orthopedics, oncology, and rehabilitation, is readily available at multiple facilities within a short drive of most Sun City Center neighborhoods.

Many 55+ communities in the area also provide on-site or nearby primary care offices, pharmacy services, and wellness programs that make routine healthcare convenient and accessible. The combination of world-class medical facilities and community-level wellness resources gives Sun City Center 55+ residents confidence that their healthcare needs will be met at every stage of retirement.

What 55+ Buyers Should Know

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations beyond a traditional home purchase. Barrett Henry advises every active adult buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Age verification requirements: Under the Housing for Older Persons Act, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one resident who is 55 or older. Communities enforce this through age verification at purchase. Some communities also restrict the age of permanent residents under 55, though policies vary.
  • Deed restrictions: 55+ communities typically have deed restrictions that govern modifications, rentals, pets, and use of common areas. Read these documents carefully to ensure they align with your lifestyle. Some communities restrict pet sizes, limit the number of overnight guests, or require owner-occupancy for a minimum period before renting.
  • HOA governance: Understand how the HOA is structured, who serves on the board, and how decisions are made. Attend an HOA meeting before purchasing if possible. A well-governed HOA with transparent finances and responsive management is essential to a positive 55+ living experience.
  • Reserve fund health: Review the reserve study and financial statements to ensure the community has adequate funds for future repairs and replacements. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments that create unexpected financial burdens for residents on fixed incomes.
  • Resale considerations: Consider the community's historical resale performance and current market dynamics. Some 55+ communities experience higher inventory levels due to natural turnover, which can affect resale timing and pricing. Barrett Henry can provide comparable sales data to help you evaluate resale potential.
  • Insurance requirements: Verify what insurance is covered by the HOA and what you need to carry individually. Some communities include master insurance policies that cover exterior structures and common areas, while individual unit owners are responsible for interior coverage and personal property.

Why Sun City Center?

The ultimate active adult lifestyle with three golf courses, 200+ clubs and activities, on-site medical facilities, and a golf-cart-friendly community.

With a population of approximately 22,000 and a median home price around $295,000, Sun City Center provides an accessible entry point to the Tampa Bay lifestyle. The local economy is supported by South Bay Hospital, Sun City Center community services, nearby Tampa and Brandon medical campuses, and the broader region offers cultural attractions including performing arts, museums, professional sports, and waterfront dining that keep active adults engaged and entertained.

For 55+ buyers exploring Sun City Center real estate, the combination of Florida's tax advantages, the area's healthcare infrastructure, and the quality of available active adult communities makes Sun City Center a compelling retirement destination. Whether you are relocating from out of state or downsizing from a larger home in Hillsborough County, Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can guide you through every step of the process. Learn more about selling your current home or contact Barrett to begin your search.

Frequently Asked Questions About Sun City Center 55+ Homes

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community?

Federal law requires that at least 80 percent of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Most communities in the Sun City Center area allow younger spouses or partners to reside with a qualifying 55+ owner. However, policies regarding other household members under 55 vary by community. Some restrict younger residents entirely, while others allow exceptions with board approval. Barrett Henry can clarify the age policies for any community you are considering.

What do HOA fees cover in Sun City Center 55+ communities?

HOA fees in Sun City Center 55+ communities typically cover exterior home maintenance, roof reserves, lawn care, common area landscaping, community amenity operations, security, and sometimes cable TV, internet, and pest control. The scope of coverage varies significantly between communities, so it is important to get a detailed breakdown before comparing fees between different neighborhoods. Higher fees are not necessarily a negative - they often reflect a more comprehensive maintenance and amenity package.

Are 55+ homes a good investment?

55+ homes in the Sun City Center area have generally appreciated in line with or slightly below the broader market, depending on the specific community and its management quality. The primary value proposition of 55+ homes is lifestyle rather than investment return - the maintenance-free living, social amenities, and community atmosphere provide a quality of life that is difficult to quantify financially. That said, well-managed communities with strong HOAs and desirable locations have shown solid appreciation over time.

Can I rent out my 55+ home in Sun City Center?

Rental policies vary by community. Some 55+ communities in the Sun City Center area permit rentals with restrictions such as minimum lease terms (often 6-12 months), annual rental limits, and tenant age requirements. Others prohibit rentals entirely or restrict them to hardship cases with board approval. If future rental flexibility is important to you, verify the community's rental policy before purchasing.

What is the social atmosphere like in Sun City Center 55+ communities?

Most 55+ communities near Sun City Center foster a warm, welcoming social atmosphere with organized activities, clubs, and events that make it easy for newcomers to connect with neighbors. From card groups and book clubs to organized outings and holiday celebrations, the social calendar provides ample opportunities to build friendships and stay engaged. Many residents describe the social aspect of 55+ living as the most unexpected and rewarding benefit of their purchase decision.

title: Sun City Center Condos & Townhomes
content:
Quick Answer

Condos and townhomes in Sun City Center range from $150,000-$320,000, offering low-maintenance living with community amenities. Popular options include Kings Point condos and Sun City Center villas. Buyers should carefully review association finances, insurance, and warrantability before purchasing.

Schedule a ShowingSearch Homes

Why Condos & Townhomes Are Popular in Sun City Center

Condos and townhomes represent one of the fastest-growing segments of the Sun City Center real estate market. Buyers are drawn to the lower price points, reduced maintenance responsibilities, and community amenities that attached and multi-family housing provides. Sun City Center is Florida's premier 55+ retirement destination in Hillsborough County. This master-planned active adult community offers golf courses, hundreds of clubs and activities, on-site healthcare, and an unbeatable sense of community. Golf carts are a primary mode of transportation.

For first-time buyers, condos and townhomes in Sun City Center offer an affordable entry point into homeownership. For downsizers, they provide a lock-and-leave lifestyle that eliminates the burden of yard maintenance, exterior upkeep, and roof repairs. And for investors, the strong rental demand in the Sun City Center area makes condos and townhomes an attractive addition to a real estate portfolio - provided the association allows rentals.

The Sun City Center market offers a wide range of condo and townhome options, from garden-style condos with ground-floor access to multi-story townhomes with private garages and rooftop terraces. Whether you prioritize walkability, commute convenience, or community amenities, there is a condo or townhome community in Sun City Center that fits your needs. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping buyers navigate the unique considerations of condo and townhome purchases.

Popular Condo & Townhome Communities in Sun City Center

The following communities represent some of the best options for condo and townhome buyers in the Sun City Center area.

Kings Point condos

Kings Point condos is one of the most sought-after condo and townhome communities in Sun City Center. The community offers a range of floor plans from compact two-bedroom units to spacious three-bedroom residences with modern finishes. Residents enjoy community amenities including a pool, fitness area, and well-maintained common spaces. The location provides convenient access to major employers, shopping centers, and transportation corridors, making Kings Point condos particularly popular with working professionals and young families who want an affordable home in a desirable location.

Sun City Center villas

Sun City Center villas appeals to buyers who value a well-managed community with consistent standards and solid finances. Units here feature updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and open floor plans that maximize living space. The community amenity package includes pool access, covered parking, and professionally maintained grounds. Sun City Center villas has maintained a strong resale track record, with properties typically selling within a reasonable timeframe and at competitive prices relative to the broader Sun City Center market.

Freedom Plaza residences

Freedom Plaza residences offers another excellent option for condo and townhome buyers in Sun City Center. This community provides a mix of unit types that accommodate different household sizes and budgets. Common amenities include a pool, playground or recreation area, and visitor parking. The HOA is well-managed with adequate reserves, and the community has a track record of stable fees and minimal special assessments. For buyers prioritizing value and long-term stability, Freedom Plaza residences deserves serious consideration.

Freedom Plaza residences

Freedom Plaza residences rounds out the top condo and townhome options in Sun City Center with units that balance affordability and quality. This community attracts a diverse mix of first-time buyers, downsizers, and investors who appreciate the combination of reasonable pricing, solid HOA management, and a convenient location. Depending on the specific unit, buyers may find updated interiors with granite countertops, stainless appliances, and luxury vinyl flooring that give the home a fresh, modern feel.

Price & HOA Overview for Sun City Center Condos & Townhomes

The following table provides general pricing guidance for condos and townhomes in the Sun City Center market. HOA fees vary by community and the services included.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Typical Features
1-Bed / 1-Bath Condo$150,000-$320,000$200-$400Pool, basic maintenance
2-Bed / 2-Bath Condo$150,000-$320,000$250-$500Pool, fitness, parking
2-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$150,000-$320,000$150-$350Garage, exterior maintenance
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$150,000-$320,000$175-$400Garage, pool, exterior maintenance

HOA fees for condos are generally higher than for townhomes because condo associations typically cover more services including exterior insurance, roof maintenance, painting, and sometimes water, sewer, and trash. Townhome HOAs tend to cover less, with owners responsible for their own exterior maintenance and insurance in some communities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed HOA fee breakdown and financial review for any community. Contact Barrett for current listings and pricing.

Condo vs. Townhome: Understanding the Differences

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they have important legal and practical differences that affect ownership, financing, and daily life.

Ownership Structure

In a condo, you own the interior space of your unit and share ownership of common areas (building exterior, roof, grounds, amenities) with other unit owners through the association. In a townhome, you typically own the structure and the land beneath it, with shared ownership limited to common areas like pools, parks, and private roads. This distinction affects insurance requirements, maintenance responsibilities, and how future improvements are funded.

Maintenance Responsibility

Condo associations in Sun City Center generally handle all exterior maintenance, including the roof, building envelope, painting, landscaping, and common areas. Townhome owners often retain responsibility for their own roof, driveway, and limited exterior maintenance, though the HOA may handle landscaping and common area upkeep. This difference is reflected in HOA fees - condo fees tend to be higher because they cover more services.

Privacy and Space

Townhomes typically offer more interior space, multiple floors, a private garage, and sometimes a small yard or pation. Condos tend to be single-level units that may share walls on multiple sides. For buyers who prioritize privacy and the feel of a traditional home, townhomes are often the better choice. For buyers who prefer single-level living and minimal maintenance, condos may be more appropriate.

What Condo & Townhome Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome in Sun City Center requires due diligence beyond what a traditional single-family home purchase demands. Barrett Henry advises every buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Association financial health: Request the most recent financial statements, budget, and reserve study. Look for adequate reserves (ideally 20 percent or more of the annual budget), stable fee history, and no pending special assessments. Florida law now requires reserve studies and adequate funding for structural components following legislative changes in recent years.
  • Reserve fund compliance: Florida statutes now require condo associations to maintain funded reserves for structural components, including the roof, foundation, and load-bearing walls. Verify that the association is in compliance, as underfunded reserves can trigger special assessments and affect property values.
  • Insurance coverage: Understand the difference between the association's master policy and your individual HO-6 policy. The master policy typically covers the building exterior and common areas, while your HO-6 covers your interior, personal property, and liability. Verify coverage limits and deductibles for both policies.
  • Rules and restrictions: Review the association's governing documents, including CC&Rs, bylaws, and rules and regulations. Common restrictions cover pets, rentals, parking, noise, renovations, and use of common areas. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the unit in the future, verify the association's rental policy. Many Sun City Center associations limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously, impose minimum lease terms, or require tenant approval by the board. Some associations prohibit rentals entirely.
  • Pending litigation and violations: Ask whether the association is involved in any lawsuits and whether the building has any outstanding code violations. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Financing Condos: Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable

Financing a condo purchase in Sun City Center requires understanding the distinction between warrantable and non-warrantable condominiums, as this classification directly affects your mortgage options.

A warrantable condo meets the guidelines set by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which means it qualifies for conventional financing with competitive interest rates and standard down payment requirements. To be warrantable, a condo association generally must have adequate reserves, no more than 15 percent of units delinquent on fees, no single entity owning more than 20 percent of units, and at least 50 percent of units owner-occupied.

A non-warrantable condo fails to meet one or more of these guidelines, which limits financing options to portfolio loans, credit unions, or cash purchases. Non-warrantable condos often carry higher interest rates, larger down payment requirements, and fewer lender options. Common reasons a Sun City Center condo might be non-warrantable include high investor concentration, pending litigation, inadequate reserves, or a single entity owning too many units.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can help you determine the warrantability status of any condo you are considering and connect you with lenders who specialize in both warrantable and non-warrantable financing. Contact Barrett to discuss your financing options.

Lifestyle Benefits of Condo & Townhome Living

Beyond the financial considerations, condos and townhomes in Sun City Center offer lifestyle advantages that appeal to a wide range of buyers.

  • Low maintenance: Say goodbye to weekend yard work, exterior painting, and roof repairs. Condo and townhome living frees up time for the activities you actually enjoy.
  • Community amenities: Many Sun City Center communities include pools, fitness centers, and social spaces that would cost thousands to replicate in a single-family home setting.
  • Affordability: Condos and townhomes typically offer a lower entry price than comparable single-family homes, making homeownership accessible to first-time buyers and those on a budget.
  • Location: Attached housing communities are often situated in prime locations near employment centers, shopping, dining, and entertainment - areas where single-family homes may be priced significantly higher.
  • Security: Many condo communities in Sun City Center feature controlled access, security cameras, and well-lit common areas that provide an added layer of safety.
  • Lock and leave: For frequent travelers, seasonal residents, and busy professionals, the ability to lock the door and leave without worrying about yard maintenance or home security is invaluable.

Why Sun City Center?

The ultimate active adult lifestyle with three golf courses, 200+ clubs and activities, on-site medical facilities, and a golf-cart-friendly community.

Sun City Center has a population of approximately 22,000 and a median home price of $295,000. The local economy benefits from South Bay Hospital, Sun City Center community services, nearby Tampa and Brandon medical campuses, creating consistent demand for housing at all price points. For buyers exploring Sun City Center real estate, condos and townhomes offer an affordable, low-maintenance path to homeownership in one of Florida's most dynamic markets.

Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an affordable entry point, a downsizer seeking a simpler lifestyle, or an investor building a rental portfolio, Sun City Center's condo and townhome market has options to match your goals. Frequently Asked Questions About Sun City Center Condos & Townhomes

How much are HOA fees for condos in Sun City Center?

Monthly HOA fees for condos in Sun City Center typically range from $200 to $500, depending on the community's amenity package, age, and services included. Fees that cover exterior insurance, roof reserves, water, sewer, and trash tend to be higher but reduce the owner's out-of-pocket costs for those items. Barrett Henry can provide exact fee information and a breakdown of included services for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my condo or townhome in Sun City Center?

Rental policies vary by association. Some Sun City Center communities allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on total rental units. Others prohibit rentals or require board approval for each tenant. If rental flexibility is important to you, verify the association's policy before purchasing and confirm that the current rental cap has not been reached.

What is a special assessment and should I be worried?

A special assessment is a one-time charge levied by the association to cover unexpected expenses or projects that exceed reserve fund capacity. Common triggers include roof replacement, elevator modernization, structural repairs, and insurance premium increases. While special assessments are a normal part of condo ownership, frequent or large assessments may indicate poor financial planning. Reviewing the reserve study and financial statements before purchasing helps assess this risk.

Do I need separate insurance for my condo?

Yes. While the association's master policy covers the building exterior and common areas, individual condo owners in Sun City Center need an HO-6 policy that covers interior finishes, personal property, liability, and loss assessment coverage. Loss assessment coverage is particularly important, as it protects you if the association levies a special assessment for a covered loss that exceeds the master policy's coverage.

What is the difference between a condo and a townhome for financing purposes?

Condos face additional financing scrutiny because lenders evaluate the entire association - not just the individual unit. Townhomes, which typically convey land with the structure, are often financed more like single-family homes with fewer association-level requirements. However, some townhome communities are structured as condominiums from a legal standpoint, which triggers condo financing requirements. Why Gated Communities Appeal to Sun City Center Buyers

Gated communities have become one of the most sought-after property types in Sun City Center and across Hillsborough County. The appeal goes well beyond the security gate - buyers are drawn to the maintained streetscapes, community amenities, architectural consistency, and lifestyle that gated living provides. Sun City Center is Florida's premier 55+ retirement destination in Hillsborough County. This master-planned active adult community offers golf courses, hundreds of clubs and activities, on-site healthcare, and an unbeatable sense of community. Golf carts are a primary mode of transportation.

For families, the controlled access and lower-traffic streets create a safer environment for children to play outdoors, ride bikes, and walk to neighborhood amenities. For professionals and retirees, gated communities offer a lock-and-leave convenience that is difficult to replicate in traditional neighborhoods. And for all buyers, the HOA-maintained common areas, landscaping, and amenities add significant value to daily life.

The demand for gated community homes in Sun City Center has grown steadily, particularly among out-of-state buyers relocating from the Northeast and Midwest who prioritize security, community standards, and resort-style amenities. Top Gated Communities in Sun City Center

The following communities represent the best of gated living in and around Sun City Center. Each offers a distinct combination of home styles, amenities, price points, and lifestyle.

Kings Point

Kings Point stands out as one of the premier gated communities in the Sun City Center area. Residents enjoy a controlled-access entry staffed by security personnel, meticulously maintained common areas, and a full suite of community amenities. Homes in Kings Point range from well-appointed single-family residences to larger estate-style properties, many featuring private pools, upgraded landscaping, and three-car garages. The community typically includes amenities such as a community pool, fitness center, tennis or pickleball courts, and walking trails that wind through preserved natural areas. The HOA ensures architectural standards are maintained, preserving property values and neighborhood aesthetics for all residents.

Renaissance

Renaissance offers a compelling combination of value, amenities, and location within the Sun City Center market. The gated entry provides controlled access while the interior streetscapes feature mature landscaping, sidewalks, and well-maintained common areas. Homes in Renaissance appeal to both families and professionals, with floor plans that typically include open-concept living areas, owners suites with spa-style bathrooms, and covered lanais overlooking private backyards. The community amenity package often includes a resort-style pool, playground, and community gathering spaces that foster a strong sense of neighborhood connection.

Sun City Center proper

This community attracts buyers who value a well-managed HOA, consistent architectural standards, and proximity to Sun City Center's best shopping, dining, and employment centers. The community amenities typically include pool facilities, common-area landscaping, and recreational spaces that make everyday living feel like a permanent vacation.

Security Features in Sun City Center Gated Communities

Security is often the primary motivation for buying in a gated community, and Sun City Center communities offer various levels of access control and monitoring.

  • Guard-gated entry: The highest level of security, with a staffed gatehouse that verifies every visitor. Guard-gated communities such as Kings Point typically have higher HOA fees but provide the strongest access control and residents report the greatest peace of mind.
  • Automated gate entry: Electronic gates with keypad, key fob, or remote access are the most common type in Sun City Center. These systems control vehicle access effectively while keeping HOA costs lower than guard-gated alternatives.
  • Perimeter fencing and walls: Most gated communities in Sun City Center feature continuous perimeter fencing or walls that define the community boundary and deter unauthorized access.
  • Security cameras and monitoring: Many communities supplement gate access with camera systems at entries, common areas, and perimeter points. Some HOAs contract with private security firms for regular patrols.
  • Guest management systems: Modern gated communities increasingly use smartphone-based guest management apps that allow residents to pre-authorize visitors, receive entry notifications, and manage access remotely.

Community Amenities That Define Gated Living

The amenity package is what transforms a gated neighborhood from a collection of homes into a true community. In Sun City Center, buyers can expect the following amenities in most gated communities.

Pool and Fitness Facilities

Nearly every gated community in Sun City Center includes at least one community pool, and many feature resort-style aquatic centers with lap lanes, children's splash areas, and poolside cabanas. Fitness centers range from basic equipment rooms to full-service gyms with cardio machines, free weights, and group fitness studios. These amenities eliminate the need for gym memberships and provide convenient, steps-from-home fitness options.

Tennis, Pickleball, and Recreation

Tennis and pickleball courts have become standard amenities in Sun City Center gated communities, reflecting the explosive growth of racket sports in Florida. Many communities also include basketball courts, playgrounds, dog parks, and multi-use athletic fields that serve residents of all ages.

Clubhouse and Social Spaces

Community clubhouses serve as gathering spots for HOA meetings, holiday parties, book clubs, and private events. Larger gated communities in Sun City Center may include event rooms with catering kitchens, covered outdoor pavilions, and dedicated meeting spaces that foster social connection among residents.

What to Ask Before Buying in a Sun City Center Gated Community

Barrett Henry advises every buyer considering a gated community in Sun City Center to evaluate the following factors before making an offer.

  • HOA financial health: Request the most recent budget, financial statements, and reserve study. A well-funded reserve (typically 30 percent or more of the annual budget) indicates the community can handle major repairs and replacements without special assessments.
  • Special assessments history: Ask whether the community has levied any special assessments in the past five years and what projects prompted them. Frequent special assessments may signal underfunded reserves or aging infrastructure.
  • Rules and restrictions: Read the CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions) thoroughly. Common restrictions cover exterior paint colors, landscaping, parking, rentals, pets, and home-based businesses. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the property in the future, verify the community's rental policies. Many gated communities in Sun City Center limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously or impose minimum lease terms.
  • Insurance requirements: Some gated communities require specific insurance coverage levels or types. Verify insurance requirements and obtain quotes before closing to avoid surprises.
  • Pending litigation: Ask the HOA whether any lawsuits are pending against the association. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Why Sun City Center?

The ultimate active adult lifestyle with three golf courses, 200+ clubs and activities, on-site medical facilities, and a golf-cart-friendly community.

Sun City Center has a population of approximately 22,000 and a median home price of $295,000. The local economy is supported by South Bay Hospital, Sun City Center community services, nearby Tampa and Brandon medical campuses, providing a stable employment base that drives consistent housing demand. For buyers exploring Sun City Center real estate, gated communities offer a compelling combination of security, amenities, and property value protection.

The broader Tampa Bay region continues to attract new residents from across the country, and gated communities in Sun City Center are among the first neighborhoods to feel the benefit of that growth. Whether you are relocating for work, retiring to Florida, or upgrading to a more amenity-rich lifestyle, Sun City Center's gated communities deliver a standard of living that is difficult to match. How much are HOA fees in Sun City Center gated communities?

Others prohibit rentals entirely or require HOA board approval for each tenant. Always review the CC&Rs before purchasing if you anticipate renting the property.

Are gated communities safer than non-gated neighborhoods?

Gated communities in Sun City Center generally experience lower rates of property crime compared to non-gated areas, though no security system is impervious. The controlled access, reduced through-traffic, and community awareness that gated living provides create an environment where residents feel more secure. Guard-gated communities with active patrol and camera systems offer the highest level of security.

Do gated community homes hold their value better?

Historically, homes in well-managed gated communities in Sun City Center have shown strong value retention and appreciation. The consistent maintenance standards, controlled development, and desirable amenities help protect property values even in softer markets. The key factor is HOA management quality - communities with strong financial reserves and proactive maintenance outperform those with deferred maintenance and underfunded reserves.

What happens if the HOA raises fees significantly?

HOA fee increases in Sun City Center gated communities typically require board approval and are communicated to homeowners in advance. Most communities limit annual increases to a set percentage unless a special vote authorizes a larger increase. Reviewing the HOA's budget trajectory and reserve study will give you insight into whether significant fee increases are likely in the near future.

Homes for Sale in Sun City Center, FL

Sun City Center is one of Florida's premier active adult communities, offering an affordable and vibrant retirement lifestyle in southern Hillsborough County. With multiple golf courses, clubhouses, fitness centers, and hundreds of social clubs, the community attracts buyers from across the country who are looking for their ideal Florida home. As of early 2026, median home prices in Sun City Center range from approximately $250,000 to $320,000, depending on the subdivision, home type, and proximity to amenities.

Overview of the Sun City Center Real Estate Market

Sun City Center is a 55+ age-restricted community, which means at least one resident in each household must be 55 or older. The community was originally developed in the 1960s and has grown to include thousands of homes across several distinct subdivisions. Property types range from single-family homes and villas to condominiums, giving buyers a wide selection at various price points.

The real estate market here tends to be more stable than conventional neighborhoods because of the consistent demand from retirees. Inventory fluctuates seasonally, with more listings typically appearing in late spring and summer as snowbirds return north. Buyers who are ready to act during these windows often find the best selection of available homes.

Popular Subdivisions and Neighborhoods

Kings Point is one of the most popular subdivisions within Sun City Center. It operates as a gated condominium community with its own clubhouse, pools, fitness facilities, and a veterans theater. Kings Point homes and condos tend to be among the most affordable options in the community, making it particularly attractive to buyers on a fixed income.

Freedom Plaza offers a continuing care retirement community (CCRC) model, providing independent living, assisted living, and skilled nursing all on one campus. This is a strong option for buyers who want long-term care planning built into their living arrangement.

The original Sun City Center neighborhoods include single-family homes with access to the main community association's amenities, including golf courses, the Atrium building, lawn bowling, softball fields, and dozens of activity rooms. Homes in these sections typically range from the mid-$200s to the low $400s.

What to Know Before You Buy

Purchasing in a 55+ community comes with additional considerations that buyers should understand before making an offer. Community association fees vary significantly between subdivisions and cover different amenities. Some associations include lawn care and exterior maintenance, while others do not.
