About Thonotosassa, FL

Thonotosassa is a small, unincorporated rural community tucked into the northeast corner of Hillsborough County, offering one of the few remaining opportunities in the greater Tampa Bay area to own genuine acreage without traveling far from the city. The community sits roughly 15 miles northeast of downtown Tampa, making it a realistic daily commute for buyers who want land, privacy, and a slower pace of life without sacrificing access to employment, entertainment, and services. The drive along US-92 or I-4 typically runs 30 to 40 minutes depending on traffic and destination.

The centerpiece of Thonotosassa is Lake Thonotosassa itself, the largest natural lake in Hillsborough County. The lake spans over 800 acres and supports boating, fishing, and wildlife watching. Lakefront properties command a premium and rarely stay on the market long. Away from the shoreline, the community is characterized by large lots, mature tree canopies, pasture land, and a quiet atmosphere that feels worlds away from suburban Tampa while still being in the same county.

The housing stock in Thonotosassa is genuinely diverse. You will find older mid-century homes on large lots, custom-built newer construction on multi-acre parcels, equestrian estates with stables and paddocks, and lakefront properties with docks. Most of the area is not subject to HOA restrictions, which attracts buyers who want to keep animals, operate small agricultural businesses, store recreational vehicles, or simply live without deed restrictions. This freedom is a major draw for horse owners, hobbyist farmers, and buyers who have felt constrained by suburban covenant communities.

Prices in Thonotosassa reflect the wide variety of property types. Entry-level homes on modest lots can be found below $250,000, while premium lakefront or equestrian estates on multiple acres can exceed $700,000 or more. The median sits near $350,000, but that figure is less meaningful here than in a uniform subdivision community. Every property should be evaluated on its own characteristics, lot size, water access, improvements, and condition all carry significant weight in pricing.

Neighborhood Highlights

  • Lake Thonotosassa: The largest lake in Hillsborough County offers boating, fishing, kayaking, and scenic waterfront living. Lakefront lots are a rare and sought-after commodity.
  • Acreage and Privacy: Multi-acre parcels are common and relatively affordable compared to similar rural properties in neighboring counties. Buyers regularly find 2- to 10-acre parcels in their searches.
  • Equestrian Community: Thonotosassa has one of the highest concentrations of horse-friendly properties in Hillsborough County. Many listings include stables, run-in sheds, fenced pastures, and trail access.
  • No HOA Freedom: The vast majority of the community operates without homeowner association oversight, giving residents broad latitude over how they use their property.
  • Established Character: Unlike master-planned communities built all at once, Thonotosassa has grown organically over decades, creating a genuine neighborhood feel with long-term residents and community identity.
  • Wildlife and Nature: Proximity to Hillsborough River State Park and the Hillsborough River corridor provides wildlife viewing, hiking, and canoe access within minutes of most homes.

Schools Serving Thonotosassa

Students in the area are generally zoned for schools including Thonotosassa Elementary School, which is located within the community itself. Middle and high school students typically attend Jennings Middle School and Armwood High School, which serve the broader northeast Hillsborough area. Private and charter school options in the surrounding Brandon and Temple Terrace corridors provide additional choices. Amenities and Lifestyle

Thonotosassa offers a lifestyle centered on outdoor recreation, rural quiet, and community self-sufficiency. Day-to-day conveniences are available in nearby communities. Brandon's retail corridor along Causeway Boulevard is approximately 15 to 20 minutes away and provides grocery stores, restaurants, medical facilities, and national retailers. Temple Terrace and the USF area are also within easy reach to the west. Within the community, you will find a smattering of local businesses, feed stores, and community gathering spots that reflect the area's agricultural roots. Hillsborough River State Park offers 16,000 acres of natural Florida wilderness with hiking trails, swimming areas, a historic Civilian Conservation Corps bridge, and extensive canoe launch facilities just minutes from many Thonotosassa addresses.

Frequently Asked Questions, Thonotosassa Homes for Sale

Q: Is Thonotosassa a good place to live if I work in Tampa?

Yes. The commute from Thonotosassa to most Tampa employment centers runs 30 to 40 minutes under normal traffic conditions. Access via US-92, I-4, and SR-574 connects the community to downtown Tampa, the USF corridor, and the I-75 employment spine efficiently. Many residents consider the trade-off of a modest commute entirely worthwhile for the land, privacy, and lower price per square foot they receive.

Q: Can I have horses in Thonotosassa?

Absolutely. Thonotosassa is one of the most horse-friendly communities in Hillsborough County. Because most properties are not subject to HOA restrictions and lots are typically large, keeping horses is common and generally permitted. Many listings already include fencing, stables, and pasture area. Buyers specifically seeking equestrian properties should work with an agent familiar with the area to identify listings with appropriate infrastructure and acreage minimums for the number of horses they intend to keep.

Q: What is the median home price in Thonotosassa?

The median home price in Thonotosassa is approximately $350,000, but the range is exceptionally wide. Modest homes on smaller lots can be found under $250,000, while premium lakefront properties and equestrian estates on multiple acres can exceed $700,000 or more. Because every property in Thonotosassa is somewhat unique, a comparative market analysis specific to your target property type is more useful than relying on the median figure alone.

Q: Are there HOA fees in Thonotosassa?

The overwhelming majority of properties in Thonotosassa are not subject to homeowner association fees or deed restrictions. This is one of the primary reasons buyers choose the area. There are a small number of subdivisions within the broader Thonotosassa ZIP code that do carry HOA rules, so your buyer's agent should confirm HOA status for any specific property before you make an offer.

Q: Is Lake Thonotosassa open to boating?

Yes. Lake Thonotosassa is the largest natural lake in Hillsborough County and supports motorized boating, fishing, and non-motorized watercraft. A public boat ramp provides access for residents and visitors. Many lakefront homes include private docks. The lake is known for bass fishing and is a popular destination for local anglers and recreational boaters.

Q: What ZIP code is Thonotosassa?

The ZIP code for Thonotosassa is 33592. This ZIP code covers the Thonotosassa community and some surrounding rural areas of northeast Hillsborough County. When searching for homes or services, this is the ZIP code to use for Thonotosassa addresses.

Q: Are there new construction homes in Thonotosassa?

Yes, though new construction in Thonotosassa typically takes the form of custom builds on existing lots rather than large subdivision developments. Buyers who purchase raw land or a teardown parcel can work with a custom builder to construct a home to their specifications. This is more common in Thonotosassa than buying a production home in a planned community, and it reflects the area's rural, non-HOA character.

Q: How far is Thonotosassa from Tampa International Airport?

Thonotosassa is approximately 20 to 25 miles from Tampa International Airport. The drive typically takes 30 to 40 minutes, with I-4 west to I-275 south being the most direct route. This is a reasonable distance for frequent travelers, particularly compared to more distant suburban communities in Pasco or Polk counties.

Q: Is flooding a concern in Thonotosassa?

Like many areas near lakes and the Hillsborough River, some portions of Thonotosassa carry flood zone designations. Properties near the lake or in low-lying areas may require flood insurance. Buyers should request a flood zone determination for any specific property and factor potential flood insurance costs into their budget. Your agent can help you identify properties in preferred flood zones where flood insurance is not mandatory.

Quick Answer

Thonotosassa pool homes typically range from $300,000-$600,000, with screened enclosures being standard across Hillsborough County. Buyers should budget for pool inspection, resurfacing timelines, and updated equipment when evaluating resale pool properties.

Why Pool Homes Are So Popular in Thonotosassa

In Thonotosassa, a swimming pool is not a luxury - it is a way of life. With average temperatures above 70 degrees for nine months of the year and summer highs regularly reaching the mid-90s, residents rely on their backyard pools for daily relief, weekend entertaining, and year-round outdoor living. Thonotosassa is a rural community northeast of Tampa, centered around Lake Thonotosassa and Hillsborough River State Park. It offers large lots, a country atmosphere, and increasing interest from buyers seeking acreage and privacy close to Tampa.

Pool homes in Thonotosassa consistently command higher resale values than comparable non-pool properties. According to recent market data, homes with pools sell for approximately 5-8 percent more than similar homes without one. For families, retirees, and remote workers who spend significant time at home, a pool transforms the backyard into a private retreat that rivals any resort.

The popularity of pool homes has only increased since 2020, when more buyers began prioritizing outdoor living space, home offices with views, and personal recreation areas. In Thonotosassa, that trend shows no signs of slowing, with pool-equipped listings often receiving multiple offers within days of hitting the market.

Best Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Thonotosassa

Choosing the right neighborhood is just as important as finding the right pool. Here are the top areas in Thonotosassa where pool homes are most prevalent and desirable.

Lake Thonotosassa

Lake Thonotosassa is widely regarded as one of the premier neighborhoods in Thonotosassa for pool homes. Properties here tend to feature larger lots, established landscaping, and pools that have been well-maintained over the years. Many homes in Lake Thonotosassa include screened pool enclosures with extended lanais, outdoor kitchens, and tropical plantings that create a true backyard oasis. The neighborhood offers convenient access to shopping, dining, and major roadways, making it ideal for families and professionals alike.

Morris Bridge area

Morris Bridge area attracts buyers who want pool homes with a community feel. Many properties in this neighborhood include pools with newer equipment, updated decking, and spacious screen enclosures. The area is known for its well-kept streetscapes, neighborhood parks, and family-friendly atmosphere. Pool homes in Morris Bridge area tend to offer excellent value, with price points that appeal to first-time pool home buyers and move-up buyers.

Hillsborough River corridor

For buyers seeking pool homes with larger lots and more privacy, Hillsborough River corridor delivers. This area features properties with expansive backyards, mature trees, and pools that serve as the centerpiece of outdoor entertainment areas. Many pool homes in Hillsborough River corridor include covered patios, summer kitchens, and fire pit areas that extend the usable outdoor space well beyond the pool deck itself.

Knights area

Knights area rounds out the top pool home neighborhoods in Thonotosassa with a mix of newer construction and updated resale homes. Pools here range from classic rectangular designs to freeform tropical layouts with water features. The neighborhood benefits from newer infrastructure, well-maintained HOA standards, and proximity to parks and recreation areas that complement the backyard pool lifestyle.

Pool Home Price Overview in Thonotosassa

The following table provides a general overview of pool home pricing across Thonotosassa by property type and size. Prices vary by neighborhood, pool condition, lot size, and home features.

Types of Pools You Will Find in Thonotosassa

Not all pools are created equal, and understanding the types available in Thonotosassa will help you narrow your search and budget accordingly.

Screened Pool Enclosures

The vast majority of residential pools in Thonotosassa - and across Florida - feature aluminum-framed screen enclosures, commonly called pool cages. These enclosures keep out insects, reduce debris, and provide a measure of safety for children and pets. A standard pool cage in good condition adds significant value to a home and is considered essential by most buyers in Hillsborough County. Replacement costs for a full pool cage can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on size, so cage condition is a key inspection item.

Saltwater Pools

Saltwater pool systems have surged in popularity across Thonotosassa due to lower maintenance costs and a more comfortable swimming experience. Saltwater generators produce chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, reducing the need for chemical handling and producing water that is gentler on skin, hair, and swimwear. Many resale homes have been converted from traditional chlorine to saltwater systems, and most new construction pools include saltwater as standard.

Heated Pools

While Thonotosassa enjoys a warm climate, winter mornings can bring pool water temperatures down into the 60s. Gas heaters, heat pumps, and solar heating systems extend the swimming season to a full twelve months. Gas heaters provide the fastest heat-up time, while heat pumps offer better energy efficiency for day-to-day use. Solar heating is the most economical long-term option and works well with the abundant Florida sunshine.

Freeform and Custom Pools

Many homes in Thonotosassa feature custom-designed freeform pools with rock waterfalls, grottos, tanning ledges, and infinity edges. These resort-style pools are most common in upscale neighborhoods and estate properties, where the pool and outdoor living area serve as the architectural focal point of the home. Buyers should note that custom pools may cost more to maintain and insure than standard designs.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist

Purchasing a pool home requires additional due diligence beyond a standard home inspection. Barrett Henry recommends every pool home buyer evaluate the following items before making an offer.

  • Pool inspection: Hire a certified pool inspector separate from the general home inspector. They will evaluate the shell, plumbing, equipment, deck, and screen enclosure for defects, leaks, and code compliance.
  • Resurfacing timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or quartz) typically last 8-15 years. Determine when the pool was last resurfaced and budget accordingly if resurfacing is due within the next few years. Costs range from $5,000 to $12,000.
  • Equipment age: Pool pumps, filters, heaters, and salt systems have a lifespan of 5-10 years. Aging equipment may work today but represent a near-term replacement cost. Ask the seller for maintenance records and equipment installation dates.
  • Screen enclosure condition: Inspect the cage for corrosion, torn screens, sagging frames, and signs of storm damage. A full cage replacement can cost $8,000-$15,000, so factor this into your offer if damage is present.
  • Insurance impact: Pool ownership affects homeowners insurance premiums and liability coverage. Discuss pool-specific coverage with your insurance agent before closing. A pool fence or cage is typically required for compliance with local safety codes.
  • Deck and drainage: Pool decks should be level, free of large cracks, and properly graded to direct water away from the home. Settling, trip hazards, and poor drainage are common issues in older pool homes.

Outdoor Living Features Beyond the Pool

In Thonotosassa, the pool is often just one element of a comprehensive outdoor living area. The best pool homes pair the swimming pool with features that extend the home's livable square footage into the backyard.

Lanais and Covered Patios

A screened lanai adjacent to the pool provides shaded seating, outdoor dining, and protection from afternoon rain showers. Many Thonotosassa homes feature extended lanais with ceiling fans, recessed lighting, and tile or travertine flooring that create a seamless indoor-outdoor transition.

Summer Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens - called summer kitchens in Florida - have become a must-have amenity in Thonotosassa pool homes. A typical summer kitchen includes a built-in grill, countertop space, a mini-refrigerator, and a sink. Upscale versions add pizza ovens, smokers, kegerators, and bar seating that turn the pool area into an entertainment destination.

Landscape and Lighting

Tropical landscaping, LED pool lighting, and landscape lighting create a resort atmosphere that enhances both daytime and evening enjoyment. Mature palms, birds of paradise, and jasmine hedges are popular plantings that thrive in Thonotosassa's climate and complement the pool setting.

Why Thonotosassa?

Rural living with Lake Thonotosassa recreation, Hillsborough River State Park, and large homesites while remaining just 20 minutes from USF and New Tampa.

With a population of approximately 14,000, Thonotosassa offers a strong and diverse economy anchored by Nearby USF and New Tampa employers, agriculture, Hillsborough County operations. The combination of employment opportunities, lifestyle amenities, and a growing real estate market makes Thonotosassa one of the most compelling places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region.

For buyers exploring Thonotosassa real estate, pool homes represent an outstanding investment in both quality of life and long-term property value. Whether you are relocating from out of state, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for your retirement oasis, Thonotosassa delivers the Florida lifestyle at a price point that competes favorably with other Gulf Coast markets.

Frequently Asked Questions About Thonotosassa Pool Homes

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Thonotosassa?

Monthly pool maintenance in Thonotosassa typically runs between $100 and $200 for weekly professional service, which includes chemical balancing, skimming, brushing, and equipment checks. Homeowners who maintain their own pools can reduce costs to $40-$80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual costs for electricity to run the pump average $600-$1,200 depending on the pump type and run time.

Do pool homes cost more to insure in Thonotosassa?

Yes, pool homes generally carry higher homeowners insurance premiums due to increased liability exposure. The additional cost is typically $100-$300 per year, though rates vary by insurer, pool type, and whether the pool has a safety fence or enclosure. Screen enclosures can help reduce premiums by meeting safety barrier requirements.

What is the best time to buy a pool home in Thonotosassa?

The best time to buy a pool home in Thonotosassa is typically during the late fall and winter months (November through February), when buyer competition decreases and sellers may be more willing to negotiate. However, inventory for pool homes tends to be limited year-round, so working with an experienced agent like Barrett Henry ensures you see new listings the moment they hit the market.

Should I buy a home with an existing pool or build one?

Both options have merits. Buying an existing pool home avoids the 3-6 month construction timeline and the hassle of managing a pool build project. However, building a new pool lets you customize the design, equipment, and features to your exact specifications. New pool construction in Thonotosassa typically costs $35,000-$80,000 depending on size, features, and site conditions. Why Buy New Construction in Thonotosassa?

Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Thonotosassa also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Thonotosassa area, including Custom builders, some new development. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Thonotosassa typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Thonotosassa
Entry-Level / Starter$300K-$400K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Thonotosassa?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

content:
Quick Answer

Waterfront homes in Thonotosassa include properties on Hillsborough River, Lake Thonotosassa. Pricing varies widely based on water type, lot size, and direct access. Flood insurance and seawall condition are key considerations.

Schedule a Waterfront TourSee Waterfront Homes

Types of Waterfront in Thonotosassa

Thonotosassa offers several types of waterfront living, each with its own character, pricing, and lifestyle:

  • Hillsborough River, Lake Thonotosassa - the primary waterfront options in Thonotosassa range from open-water properties with panoramic views to canal-front homes with private dock access and lake-front properties with peaceful settings.

The type of waterfront determines not just the lifestyle but also insurance costs, maintenance requirements, and resale value. Open-water properties with direct bay or Gulf access typically command the highest premiums.

Popular Waterfront Areas

The most sought-after waterfront neighborhoods in Thonotosassa include areas within Thonotosassa area, Lake Thonotosassa, Morris Bridge area. These neighborhoods offer a mix of water types, lot sizes, and price points.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Thonotosassa require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Thonotosassa?

Flood insurance costs in Thonotosassa vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Thonotosassa?

Most waterfront properties in Thonotosassa allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Thonotosassa generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.

Town N Country is one of Tampa Bay's most strategically located communities. Sitting just west of Tampa International Airport and anchored by the Veterans Expressway, this unincorporated Hillsborough County community of roughly 90,000 residents puts you within easy reach of downtown Tampa, the Westshore business district, the Gulf beaches, and some of the best dining and entertainment in the region. All of that, at home prices that remain more accessible than South Tampa or the coastal markets to the west.

Town N Country is not a planned suburban development with a single builder and a strict architectural code. It is an organically grown community that has developed over more than six decades, resulting in a genuine diversity of home styles, lot sizes, neighborhood characters, and price points. That organic character is part of what makes it interesting from a real estate perspective. You can find waterfront estate homes in Dana Shores, classic ranch-style bungalows in the core subdivisions, and modern townhomes in newer infill communities, all within the same community boundaries.

This guide covers the Town N Country real estate market, neighborhoods, schools, commute options, and what daily life actually looks like here. Whether you are a first-time buyer, a growing family, or someone relocating to the Tampa Bay area, this is a community that earns a serious look. Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, serves buyers and sellers throughout west Hillsborough County and knows this market well.

Why Town N Country is One of Tampa Bay's Best Kept Secrets

Town N Country has long played second fiddle in local real estate conversations to flashier addresses like South Tampa, Hyde Park, or Westchase. That is good news for buyers who do their homework. The community delivers most of the same geographic advantages at a meaningful price discount. You get direct Veterans Expressway access, proximity to Tampa International Airport, and connectivity to downtown Tampa in roughly 20 to 30 minutes, all without paying Westshore or South Tampa prices.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Town 'n' Country Homes

The community has genuine diversity in both its housing stock and its population. You will find older ranch-style homes on large lots, newer townhomes, established subdivisions with tree-lined streets, and waterfront properties along Old Tampa Bay. That range means buyers at multiple price points can find something here. It also means investors and entry-level buyers have options that simply do not exist in the pricier markets to the south and east.

Town N Country is also close to everything people move to the Tampa Bay area for. The airport is essentially next door. The Gulf beaches via the Courtney Campbell Causeway are 30 to 40 minutes west. Clearwater and St. Pete are accessible without ever touching I-275 if you know the right routes. And the Westshore business district, one of the largest employment centers in Tampa Bay, is just minutes away by car.

The community has also benefited from the broader Tampa Bay growth story of the past decade. As Tampa has grown into a nationally recognized city for business relocation, sports, culture, and quality of life, the communities adjacent to major employment and infrastructure nodes have seen sustained demand. Town N Country's proximity to Tampa International Airport gives it a durable advantage that newer outer-ring communities cannot replicate. You cannot move an airport, and that locational certainty gives Town N Country real staying power as a real estate market.

For buyers relocating from out of state, Town N Country is also a practical choice for a first home in the Tampa Bay area. Its central location means you can easily explore the broader metro during weekends to develop your sense of which neighborhoods and areas you most enjoy, while living in a community that provides ready access to the airport, employment, and services from day one. Many buyers who start their Tampa Bay search thinking they want Westchase or South Tampa ultimately discover that Town N Country's value and location make it the better fit for their actual lifestyle.

Where is Town N Country? Location, Geography, and Getting Around

Town N Country is an unincorporated community in western Hillsborough County, bounded roughly by Tampa International Airport to the east, Old Tampa Bay to the west, the Hillsborough-Pinellas County line area to the north, and the Westshore District to the southeast. It is not a municipality, meaning it falls under Hillsborough County jurisdiction rather than City of Tampa services.

The community took shape beginning in the late 1950s, when a 525-acre dairy farm was purchased and developed. Today it occupies a prime position in the metro, with major waterfront and highway infrastructure defining its edges. The Veterans Expressway (SR-589) is the primary north-south arterial, running through the heart of Town N Country and connecting the community to Northdale, Carrollwood, and Lutz to the north. Interstate 275 provides additional east-west and north-south connectivity, and the Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR-60) connects to Clearwater and the beaches to the west.

Getting around Town N Country almost always requires a car. The area has limited public transit, though HART bus routes serve portions of the community and the HARTFlex on-demand van service provides some additional coverage. Rideshare services operate throughout the area. For most residents, the convenience of the expressway system means that while you drive everywhere, you rarely have to drive far. The airport is one stoplight away for much of the community, a fact that frequent travelers appreciate enormously.

Nearby communities include Clearwater to the northwest, Tampa proper to the east and south, and the Westchase area to the north. The St. Petersburg area is accessible via the Gandy Bridge or Courtney Campbell and is roughly 30 to 40 minutes from Town N Country in normal traffic.

Town N Country Real Estate Market Overview

Town N Country has shown more pricing resilience than some other parts of the Tampa Bay market heading into 2026. Median home prices in the area were tracking in the range of $399,000 to $410,000 as of early 2026, which places Town N Country above the national median but below the broader Tampa metro average. That positioning reflects the community's genuine location advantages, particularly airport proximity and expressway access, which support sustained demand.

The market has softened from its post-pandemic peak, and homes are spending more time on market than in 2021 or 2022. Days on market have stretched to the 90-plus-day range for some properties, giving buyers more time and more leverage. However, well-priced homes in desirable pockets still attract competitive attention. The gap between listing and sale price has widened somewhat, meaning negotiation is back in play for buyers who engage strategically.

The price range within Town N Country is broad. Entry-level condos and townhomes can be found below $250,000. Single-family homes on standard lots range from the $300,000s to the $500,000s. Waterfront and water-view properties along Old Tampa Bay or canal frontage can reach the high $600,000s and above, with Dana Shores waterfront properties commanding premium prices. This range makes Town N Country appealing to a wide segment of buyers, from first-time buyers to move-up buyers and even some luxury-tier purchasers.

If you are thinking about buying or selling in Town N Country, start with a free home valuation to understand where your property or your target home fits in the current market. Reviewing our Florida closing costs guide before you start the process is also worthwhile, as many buyers underestimate what they will spend at the closing table.

Neighborhoods and Subdivisions in Town N Country

Town N Country encompasses a wide range of neighborhoods with distinct characters, price points, and property types. Here is a look at the areas that buyers most frequently explore.

Dana Shores: Dana Shores is a premium neighborhood within Town N Country, offering some of the most desirable addresses in the community. Located adjacent to Rocky Point and the Old Tampa Bay waterfront, Dana Shores features custom homes on deep water canals with direct access to Tampa Bay, as well as dry lots with proximity to the Rocky Point Golf Course and the Skyway Sports Complex. Homes here often feature two-car garages, private boat docks, pools, and upscale landscaping. The location one stoplight from Tampa International Airport is exceptional for frequent travelers. Waterfront properties in Dana Shores can reach well into the high $600,000s and above.

Town N Country Proper: The core of the community is made up of established single-family home subdivisions built from the late 1950s through the 1980s. These neighborhoods feature ranch-style homes on generous lots, mature tree canopy, and a character that newer planned communities often lack. The price range here is broad, with entry-level homes starting in the $300,000s. Many homes have been renovated and updated while retaining their original footprint and lot size. This is where buyers looking for value and character in a central location tend to focus.

Sweetwater Creek and Timberlane Woodlake: These are among the more popular family-oriented neighborhoods in Town N Country. Sweetwater Creek is convenient to the airport and Westshore and draws young professionals and families. Timberlane Woodlake is known for large yards, spacious streets, and its proximity to well-regarded schools. These neighborhoods tend to move relatively quickly when priced competitively.

Town N Country Townhome Communities: Several newer townhome communities provide low-maintenance options for buyers who want modern finishes without single-family-home upkeep. These communities are popular with first-time buyers and investors and typically carry HOA fees that cover exterior maintenance, landscaping, and common area amenities. Our Florida HOA guide is a good reference before committing to any HOA community.

Town N Country is well-positioned between several other communities worth exploring. If you need more space or want newer construction, the Land O Lakes and Wesley Chapel areas to the north offer newer planned communities. If walkability and urban character appeal to you, South Tampa is just east. And if waterfront is the priority, Clearwater and the barrier islands are 30 to 45 minutes west.

Schools in Town N Country: Ratings, Zoning, and Options

Town N Country schools fall within the Hillsborough County Public School District, the eighth-largest school district in the United States. School quality in Town N Country is mixed, as it is in most large unincorporated communities, with some schools performing well above district averages and others performing below. Buyers with school-aged children should verify zoning for any specific property using Hillsborough County's school finder tool, as boundaries can shift. Hillsborough County also maintains a robust school choice program, meaning students are not necessarily locked into their zoned campus if another school better meets their needs. Magnet school programs, specialized academies, and charter schools are additional options worth researching before assuming the zoned school is the only choice.

Town and Country Elementary, the school that shares the neighborhood's name, serves families in the core area. Middle school and high school options include Monroe Middle School and Alonso High School, which serves portions of Town N Country and has received positive community reviews in recent years. Some parts of the community are zoned for schools with stronger performance ratings, and the location near the airport means some families also have access to school choice programs or private school options in Westshore and South Tampa that are a short drive away.

Private school options near Town N Country include several Catholic schools, Lutheran schools, and independent academies in the broader west Tampa area. Families with specific school priorities should map those alongside property searches to ensure alignment before committing to a purchase. The Westchase area, just to the north, is known for stronger school ratings and may be worth including in your search if school performance is a primary driver. See our buyer's guide for more on evaluating schools during a home search.

Things to Do in Town N Country

Town N Country offers genuine recreational variety for a suburban community. The Upper Tampa Bay Trail is one of the area's signature amenities: a 7.25-mile multi-use trail running through a nature preserve with waterfront views of Old Tampa Bay. The trail is popular with cyclists, joggers, and walkers and connects to a broader trail network. It is the kind of outdoor asset that adds real quality-of-life value to the community.

The Town N Country Recreation Center provides community fitness and programming options, including a gymnasium, fitness center, and outdoor pool. Rocky Point Golf Course, adjacent to Dana Shores, is a well-regarded public course with scenic bay views. The Skyway Sports Complex in the same area hosts organized sporting events and recreational leagues.

For shopping, the area has solid coverage with major retailers and grocery stores along Sheldon Road and Veterans Expressway corridor. WestShore Plaza and International Plaza, two of Tampa's premier shopping destinations, are within 10 to 15 minutes. Citrus Park Town Center is accessible via the Veterans Expressway in about 15 minutes for additional retail options.

Beyond the immediate community, Town N Country's location unlocks the full Tampa Bay experience. The Tampa Riverwalk, Busch Gardens, the Florida Aquarium, Amalie Arena (home of the Lightning), and Raymond James Stadium (home of the Buccaneers) are all within 20 to 30 minutes. Clearwater Beach and St. Pete Beach, consistently ranked among the best beaches in the nation, are roughly 30 to 45 minutes west. The Tampa Bay Beaches Guide covers all the best coastal options in detail.

For boaters, Town N Country's Old Tampa Bay waterfront access is a genuine amenity. Several marinas and boat launch facilities are within or near the community. Rocky Point and the Courtney Campbell Causeway area provide popular spots for kayakers, paddleboarders, and anglers as well. The bay and its connected waterways offer access to Tampa Bay's fishing grounds, which are among the most productive inshore fisheries in the state. Residents who enjoy the water lifestyle often cite this proximity as one of the strongest arguments for choosing Town N Country over more inland Tampa Bay communities.

Best Restaurants and Dining in Town N Country

Town N Country's dining scene has grown and diversified along with the community's population. The area has a broad mix of independent restaurants and chain establishments serving a wide range of cuisines, from Latin American and Caribbean to Asian, seafood, and American comfort food. The community's population diversity is reflected in the restaurant options, which lean toward authentic ethnic cuisine more than many suburban Tampa neighborhoods.

Restaurants frequently mentioned by residents include a solid lineup of Cuban, Colombian, and Latin American spots reflecting the community's demographics. Foodys Restaurant and other local independent eateries have developed loyal followings. The Rusty Pelican, a waterfront dining landmark on Rocky Point with views of Tampa Bay, is a neighborhood gem and popular for special occasions. Grand Harvest and several other dining options along the Veterans Expressway and Sheldon Road corridor round out the local choices.

For fine dining and upscale options, the Westshore District and Hyde Park are just minutes east and offer a full range of Tampa's best restaurant scene. Cigar City Brewing, a Tampa institution, is within easy reach. The Courtney Campbell Causeway corridor also has several waterfront dining options popular with residents heading toward Clearwater. Town N Country is well-positioned to access all of it without a long drive from home.

The grocery and everyday shopping situation in Town N Country is strong. Multiple major grocery chains are well-represented along Sheldon Road, Gunn Highway, and the Veterans Expressway corridor. The area also has a solid concentration of ethnic grocery stores reflecting the community's diverse population, which is a genuine asset for residents who cook international cuisines or have specialty dietary needs. Proximity to WestShore Plaza and International Plaza, two of Tampa's premier retail centers, means that major retail shopping is genuinely convenient without requiring a long drive or trip into traffic-heavy downtown Tampa corridors.

Thinking About Town N Country? Let's Talk.

Barrett Henry has helped buyers and sellers across the Tampa Bay area navigate real estate decisions with confidence. Whether you're exploring Town N Country for the first time or ready to make a move, a quick conversation can save you time and money.

Commute and Transportation from Town N Country

Town N Country's commute story is one of its strongest selling points. The Veterans Expressway provides direct, high-speed access north toward Carrollwood, Northdale, Lutz, and the SR-54 corridor. I-275 connects residents to downtown Tampa in roughly 15 to 20 minutes in normal conditions and to St. Petersburg via the Howard Frankland Bridge. The Courtney Campbell Causeway (SR-60) heads west toward Clearwater and the beaches. Having three major highway options within the community gives residents real flexibility in managing traffic.

Commute times to major employment centers from Town N Country are generally strong by Tampa Bay standards. The Westshore business district, one of the region's largest employment clusters, is approximately 10 to 15 minutes by car. Downtown Tampa is 20 to 25 minutes. Tampa International Airport is essentially at the community's doorstep, making it ideal for frequent business travelers. Ybor City and the Channel District are 25 to 30 minutes east.

The Veterans Expressway is a toll road, and regular commuters should factor toll costs into their monthly budget, particularly if using it daily for north-south travel. The SunPass transponder system provides discounted rates for frequent users and makes tollway commuting more manageable. Traffic congestion near the airport interchanges can be significant during peak morning and evening commute windows, particularly on Westshore Boulevard and near the I-275 and Veterans Expressway interchange.

For those who travel by air frequently, the airport's immediate proximity is a genuine quality-of-life advantage. Tampa International Airport is consistently rated one of the best airports in the country for ease of use, and having it 10 minutes from home rather than 40 or 45 minutes makes a real difference over time. It is one of the reasons real estate in Dana Shores and adjacent waterfront neighborhoods commands a premium.

Cost of Living in Town N Country

Town N Country occupies a middle ground in the Tampa Bay cost-of-living landscape. Home prices are meaningfully lower than South Tampa, Hyde Park, and the barrier island markets, but higher than the outer suburban communities like Brandon, Riverview, or Valrico to the east. For buyers who place high value on location and connectivity, Town N Country often delivers the best value-per-dollar of any west Hillsborough community.

When comparing communities across the Tampa Bay area, it helps to think beyond the sticker price of the home and consider total cost of ownership. In Town N Country, many of the core single-family subdivisions have no HOA fees or very modest ones, which is a meaningful advantage over newer planned communities in Wesley Chapel, Riverview, or Apollo Beach where HOA and CDD fees can add $300 to $600 per month to total housing costs. That difference compounds significantly over the years of homeownership. A home in Town N Country at $410,000 with no HOA may represent better total value than a comparable home at $390,000 in a community with $500 per month in combined HOA and CDD fees.

Median home prices in the area were tracking around $399,000 to $410,000 as of early 2026. Rental costs are also elevated relative to the broader county, with average rents for apartments in the area around $1,750 per month. Dana Shores and other premium waterfront pockets run considerably higher. The area's proximity to the airport and employment centers supports strong rental demand, which benefits both owner-occupants and investors in terms of long-term property value stability.

Florida's lack of a state income tax benefits all residents and is particularly meaningful for workers in higher income brackets. Property taxes in Hillsborough County are moderate. Homestead exemption, available to primary residents, reduces the taxable assessed value and provides some protection against rapid assessment increases through the Save Our Homes benefit.

Day-to-day cost of living in Town N Country is broadly in line with the Tampa metro area. Groceries, utilities, and services are typical for the region. Toll costs on the Veterans Expressway should be factored into the monthly budget for regular users. Flood insurance is a consideration for waterfront and low-lying properties; check our Florida Flood Zones Guide and our closing costs guide for what to anticipate.

New Construction in Town N Country

New construction in Town N Country is primarily focused on infill townhome development and smaller planned communities rather than large-scale master-planned subdivisions. The community is largely built out in terms of land availability, so new product tends to be on smaller parcels or redevelopment sites rather than greenfield communities. This has a positive effect on the character of the broader community: there is no single builder's aesthetic dominating the neighborhood, and lot sizes and setbacks from older construction provide more generous spacing than many newer planned developments.

Townhome communities like Kingsport Townhomes represent the style of new construction most active in the area: modern, low-maintenance attached homes with 3 bedrooms, 2.5 baths, and 1 or 2-car garages at price points designed to attract first-time buyers and investors. New construction townhomes in Town N Country generally start in the $300,000s and move upward depending on the community and finishes. Several communities have been delivered without CDD fees, which is worth noting for buyers tracking total monthly housing costs. Our CDD fee guide explains how these fees work and what to look for.

For buyers seeking new construction with more variety of options, the broader west Hillsborough and north Hillsborough corridor has more active inventory. Communities in Land O Lakes, Wesley Chapel, and even the Lutz area off the Veterans Expressway north extension offer more traditional new single-family home communities with larger lot options. Our Moving to Tampa Bay guide covers new construction options across the region for buyers who want to compare.

Healthcare and Services in Town N Country

Town N Country benefits from its position within the Tampa Bay metro area's extensive healthcare network. Tampa General Hospital, one of Florida's premier academic medical centers, is approximately 20 to 25 minutes by car. St. Joseph's Hospital and BayCare's hospital system have facilities within a comparable distance. AdventHealth facilities serve various parts of the metro as well. For everyday healthcare needs, the community has numerous primary care offices, urgent care centers, dental practices, and specialty clinics along and near the major commercial corridors.

The proximity to Tampa International Airport also gives Town N Country residents a somewhat unexpected advantage: access to national medical facilities when needed. For residents who want to travel for specialty care or second opinions at centers outside Tampa, having a major international airport nearby is genuinely useful. The airport's national connectivity means that major medical centers in Houston, Boston, Cleveland, or elsewhere are reachable with minimal hassle compared to communities that require a long drive to the nearest airport first.

Veterans resources are also relevant for many Town N Country residents. The James A. Haley Veterans Hospital in Tampa serves veterans across the region and is roughly 25 to 30 minutes east via I-275. Several VA outpatient clinics and community-based outpatient clinics (CBOCs) serve the Hillsborough County area. Town N Country's diverse population includes a meaningful number of veterans who rely on these resources, and proximity matters when healthcare appointments are frequent.

Pros and Cons of Living in Town N Country

Pros:

  • Exceptional highway access: Veterans Expressway, I-275, and Courtney Campbell all within easy reach
  • Tampa International Airport is minutes away, ideal for frequent travelers
  • More affordable than South Tampa and Westshore for comparable metro access
  • Diverse housing stock from waterfront estates in Dana Shores to affordable townhomes
  • Upper Tampa Bay Trail provides high-quality outdoor recreation within the community
  • Strong rental demand supports property values for investors
  • Proximity to Westshore District, one of Tampa Bay's largest employment centers
  • Cultural and dining diversity reflects the community's varied population
  • Gulf beaches are 30 to 45 minutes west via the Courtney Campbell Causeway

Cons:

  • Car dependence is high; public transit is limited for most daily needs
  • Traffic near airport interchanges can be significant during peak commute hours
  • Toll costs on the Veterans Expressway add to monthly transportation budget
  • School ratings in parts of the community are below district averages
  • Airport proximity means aircraft noise in some neighborhoods, particularly near flight paths
  • Limited new construction options compared to outer suburban markets
  • Some older housing stock requires renovation investment to bring to current standards
  • Flood insurance is a factor for waterfront and low-lying properties

The airport noise factor is worth discussing directly: some parts of Town N Country sit near active flight paths, and depending on the wind direction and flight schedules, noise can be noticeable. Buyers with noise sensitivity should visit any property at different times of day and consult the Tampa International Airport flight path maps before committing.

Town N Country Real Estate for Investors

Town N Country is a solid market for real estate investors, supported by strong and consistent rental demand. The community's location next to Tampa International Airport and the Westshore employment cluster means there is a steady pool of renters: airline and airport workers, corporate tenants in the Westshore area, young professionals who want metro access without South Tampa prices, and families priced out of tighter markets. That demand foundation has supported rental rates and occupancy through various market cycles.

Single-family homes are the most common investment vehicle in Town N Country, with long-term residential rentals providing stable cash flow. Townhome communities are also active for investors, particularly newer developments without CDD fees that keep carrying costs manageable. Some investors have targeted older single-family homes for renovation and resale, capitalizing on the community's older housing stock and the value uplift from updating properties to current buyer standards.

The airport adjacency also creates a potential market for medium-term or extended-stay rentals serving airline crews, corporate travelers, and relocating employees, though this strategy requires understanding Hillsborough County's short-term rental regulations before pursuing it. Our investment real estate section covers broader Tampa Bay investment strategy. Commercial real estate near the Westshore corridor is also an option worth exploring for investors looking beyond residential.

For investors considering Town N Country, the current market conditions, with more inventory and longer days on market, provide an entry point with more negotiating room than the market offered in 2021 or 2022. Investors who can acquire well-located properties at reasonable prices and hold through a market normalization cycle are generally well-positioned in this location. A conversation with Barrett about current investment opportunities is the right starting point. Sellers with investment properties to exit are also welcome to connect.

Frequently Asked Questions About Town N Country

Is Town N Country a city or unincorporated?
Town N Country is an unincorporated community in Hillsborough County. It is not a municipality, meaning it operates under Hillsborough County government and services rather than a city administration. This has implications for zoning, code enforcement, and some service levels that buyers should understand before purchasing.

What is the population of Town N Country?
The community has a population of approximately 80,000 to 90,000, making it one of the larger unincorporated communities in Hillsborough County. It has a diverse population reflecting the broader west Tampa area.

How close is Town N Country to Tampa International Airport?
Very close. Depending on the specific neighborhood within Town N Country, the airport can be reached in as little as 5 to 10 minutes by car. It is one of the community's defining location advantages and a primary reason real estate prices here are higher than comparable suburban markets farther from the airport.

What are the best neighborhoods in Town N Country?
Dana Shores is widely regarded as the premium neighborhood within Town N Country for waterfront living and proximity to the airport. Sweetwater Creek and Timberlane Woodlake are popular for families. The core single-family subdivisions offer solid value for buyers seeking established neighborhoods with character. The best fit depends on budget, lifestyle, and priorities.

Is Town N Country safe?
Like any community of 80,000 to 90,000 people, safety varies by specific street and neighborhood. Parts of Town N Country have lower crime rates consistent with suburban Hillsborough County norms. Other areas have higher rates. Buyers should research crime data for any specific neighborhood or street using Hillsborough County Sheriff's Office resources. General suburban vigilance applies.

How are the schools in Town N Country?
School quality in Town N Country is mixed within the Hillsborough County Public School district. Some zones have stronger-performing schools, particularly in the northern sections closer to Westchase and Countryway. Families should verify current school zoning for any specific property before purchasing, as boundaries change and performance varies by campus. Private school alternatives in the Westshore and South Tampa corridors are within a manageable drive.

What is the Veterans Expressway and does it help Town N Country residents?
The Veterans Expressway (SR-589) is a north-south toll road that runs directly through Town N Country, connecting it to Carrollwood, Northdale, and Lutz to the north and to I-275 and the downtown Tampa area to the south. It is one of the most significant commute advantages the community offers, providing fast access to major employment centers with less congestion than parallel surface roads. Regular users should invest in a SunPass for discounted toll rates.

Are there waterfront homes in Town N Country?
Yes. Dana Shores has genuine waterfront properties on deep water canals leading to Old Tampa Bay, with some homes featuring private boat docks and direct bay access. These are among the most premium residential addresses in the community and are priced accordingly. Rocky Point, adjacent to Dana Shores, also offers waterfront-proximate properties.

What is the typical commute time from Town N Country to downtown Tampa?
In normal traffic, 20 to 25 minutes via I-275 or Westshore Boulevard to downtown Tampa. Morning rush hour can extend this, particularly near the airport interchange. The Westshore District is closer, roughly 10 to 15 minutes. Overall, Town N Country's commute profile to major Tampa employment centers is one of the best in the western suburbs.

Is there public transportation in Town N Country?
Limited. HART (Hillsborough Area Regional Transit) operates bus routes that serve parts of Town N Country, and the HARTFlex on-demand van service provides additional coverage. However, the area is primarily car-dependent, and most residents rely on personal vehicles for daily errands and commuting. Rideshare services are available throughout the community.

How does Town N Country compare to South Tampa?
Town N Country offers comparable metro access at a lower price point. South Tampa has more walkability, a denser urban character, and higher-rated schools in many zones, but home prices are significantly higher. Town N Country is the better choice for buyers who prioritize highway access, airport proximity, and value. South Tampa is the better choice for buyers who want walkability, nightlife, and waterfront exclusivity.

Is Town N Country a good market for real estate investors?
Yes, particularly for long-term residential rentals. Strong and stable rental demand from airport and Westshore workers, young professionals, and families supports occupancy rates. The current market provides better entry points than the 2021-2022 peak. Investors should understand HOA rules for any community and local short-term rental regulations before purchasing.

What are nearby communities to explore alongside Town N Country?
Westchase and Countryway to the north offer newer planned communities with generally stronger school ratings. Clearwater to the northwest offers beach access and a vibrant downtown. South Tampa to the east offers urban walkability. Brandon and Riverview to the east offer more affordable suburban options with expanding amenities.

Are there new homes available in Town N Country?
New construction in Town N Country is primarily townhome infill development rather than large master-planned communities. Several new townhome communities have delivered in recent years with modern finishes and no CDD fees. For more variety in new construction, the north Hillsborough corridor toward Land O Lakes and Wesley Chapel has more active new home builder communities.

What resources should I read before buying in Town N Country?
Start with our buyer's guide, our Florida closing costs guide, our flood zones guide, and if you are considering a community with an HOA, our Florida HOA rules guide. For first-time buyers, the first-time buyer section of this site is a great starting point. A home valuation is a useful early step as well.

title: Town n Country 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ homes in Town 'n' Country typically range from $230,000-$400,000. Top active adult communities in the area include Nearby Sun Bay South and nearby Aston Gardens in Tampa, offering resort-style amenities, low-maintenance living, and an active social calendar.

Why Active Adults Choose Town 'n' Country

Town 'n' Country has become an increasingly popular destination for active adults and retirees seeking the Florida lifestyle without sacrificing access to quality healthcare, cultural amenities, and everyday convenience. Town 'n' Country is a large, centrally located community in unincorporated Hillsborough County, west of Tampa. It offers exceptional convenience to Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, and the Veterans Expressway, making it a commuter favorite.

The appeal of 55+ living in Town 'n' Country extends far beyond the weather. Active adult communities in this area provide a turnkey lifestyle that includes exterior home maintenance, landscaping, and community amenities - freeing residents to focus on the activities, travel, and social connections that make retirement fulfilling. With no state income tax, Florida remains one of the most tax-friendly states for retirees, and Town 'n' Country's cost of living compares favorably to many other retirement destinations along the Gulf Coast.

Whether you are planning a full-time relocation, seeking a seasonal winter residence, or downsizing from a larger home in the area, Town 'n' Country's 55+ market offers a range of options from maintenance-free villas to single-family homes with full resort amenities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping active adult buyers find the right community and home to match their lifestyle and budget.

Top 55+ Communities in and Near Town 'n' Country

The following communities represent the best options for 55+ buyers in the Town 'n' Country area. Each offers a distinct lifestyle, amenity package, and price point.

Nearby Sun Bay South

Nearby Sun Bay South is among the most established and well-regarded active adult communities serving Town 'n' Country residents. This community offers a comprehensive lifestyle package that includes maintained exteriors, community pools, fitness facilities, and an extensive calendar of social events, clubs, and organized activities. Homes range from attached villas with two bedrooms and two bathrooms to larger single-family residences with three bedrooms, dens, and two-car garages. Floor plans are designed specifically for active adult living, with single-story layouts, wide doorways, step-free entries, and owners suites positioned for privacy. The community atmosphere is welcoming and social, with residents forming lasting friendships through shared activities that range from golf and tennis to card games, art classes, and group travel.

nearby Aston Gardens in Tampa

nearby Aston Gardens in Tampa provides another excellent option for 55+ buyers in the Town 'n' Country area. This community appeals to active adults who want a maintenance-free lifestyle without sacrificing home quality or community amenities. Properties here feature modern finishes, energy-efficient construction, and thoughtful floor plans that accommodate both daily living and entertaining. The amenity package typically includes a community clubhouse, pool, walking trails, and organized social programming. Residents appreciate the sense of community that develops naturally when neighbors share similar life stages and interests. The location provides convenient access to healthcare facilities, shopping, dining, and the cultural attractions that make Town 'n' Country such an appealing retirement destination.

Price & Monthly Cost Overview for Town 'n' Country 55+ Homes

Understanding the full cost of 55+ living - including purchase price, HOA fees, and additional community charges - is essential for retirement planning. The table below outlines typical costs for active adult properties in the Town 'n' Country area.

3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Premium$230,000-$400,000$300-$600Full maintenance, lawn, amenities, cable

Monthly HOA fees in 55+ communities cover a wide range of services. Some communities include exterior painting, roof maintenance, lawn care, pest control, cable TV, and community amenities in a single monthly fee. Others charge separately for certain services. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a complete cost breakdown for any community you are considering. Contact Barrett for current pricing and availability.

Amenities & Lifestyle in Town 'n' Country 55+ Communities

The amenity package is what truly sets 55+ communities apart from traditional neighborhoods. Active adult communities in the Town 'n' Country area offer lifestyle amenities that rival upscale resorts.

Fitness and Wellness

Most 55+ communities in Town 'n' Country include fitness centers equipped with cardio machines, strength training equipment, and stretching areas designed for active adults. Many offer group fitness classes such as water aerobics, yoga, tai chi, and low-impact cardio that cater specifically to the 55+ demographic. Walking trails, swimming pools, and spa facilities provide additional wellness options that encourage daily physical activity in a comfortable, age-appropriate setting.

Social Clubs and Activities

The social calendar in a well-run 55+ community is remarkably full. Residents in Town 'n' Country area communities can typically choose from dozens of clubs and interest groups covering everything from bridge and mahjong to woodworking, photography, gardening, and performing arts. Organized activities such as day trips, dinner outings, holiday celebrations, and educational seminars keep the community engaged and connected. For many residents, this built-in social network is the single greatest benefit of 55+ living.

Golf, Tennis, and Recreation

Golf remains a cornerstone of the 55+ lifestyle in Hillsborough County, and many active adult communities near Town 'n' Country offer on-site or nearby golf courses. Tennis and pickleball courts have become increasingly popular, with organized leagues and social play available most days. Bocce ball, shuffleboard, and horseshoes are additional recreational options that provide both exercise and social interaction in a relaxed, friendly setting.

Pools and Outdoor Living

Community pools in Town 'n' Country 55+ neighborhoods are designed for both exercise and relaxation. Heated pools extend the swimming season year-round, while separate spa and soaking pools provide therapeutic benefits. Many communities feature poolside pavilions, outdoor grills, and covered seating areas where residents gather for impromptu socializing and organized pool parties throughout the year.

Healthcare Access Near Town 'n' Country

Access to quality healthcare is a top priority for 55+ buyers, and Town 'n' Country delivers excellent options. The greater Tampa Bay area is home to some of Florida's finest medical facilities, ensuring that active adult residents are never far from the care they need.

Major healthcare providers serving the Town 'n' Country area include BayCare Health System, AdventHealth (formerly Florida Hospital), HCA Healthcare facilities, and Tampa General Hospital - consistently ranked among the top hospitals in Florida. Specialty care, including cardiology, orthopedics, oncology, and rehabilitation, is readily available at multiple facilities within a short drive of most Town 'n' Country neighborhoods.

Many 55+ communities in the area also provide on-site or nearby primary care offices, pharmacy services, and wellness programs that make routine healthcare convenient and accessible. The combination of world-class medical facilities and community-level wellness resources gives Town 'n' Country 55+ residents confidence that their healthcare needs will be met at every stage of retirement.

What 55+ Buyers Should Know

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations beyond a traditional home purchase. Barrett Henry advises every active adult buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Age verification requirements: Under the Housing for Older Persons Act, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one resident who is 55 or older. Communities enforce this through age verification at purchase. Some communities also restrict the age of permanent residents under 55, though policies vary.
  • Deed restrictions: 55+ communities typically have deed restrictions that govern modifications, rentals, pets, and use of common areas. Read these documents carefully to ensure they align with your lifestyle. Some communities restrict pet sizes, limit the number of overnight guests, or require owner-occupancy for a minimum period before renting.
  • HOA governance: Understand how the HOA is structured, who serves on the board, and how decisions are made. Attend an HOA meeting before purchasing if possible. A well-governed HOA with transparent finances and responsive management is essential to a positive 55+ living experience.
  • Reserve fund health: Review the reserve study and financial statements to ensure the community has adequate funds for future repairs and replacements. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments that create unexpected financial burdens for residents on fixed incomes.
  • Resale considerations: Consider the community's historical resale performance and current market dynamics. Some 55+ communities experience higher inventory levels due to natural turnover, which can affect resale timing and pricing. Barrett Henry can provide comparable sales data to help you evaluate resale potential.
  • Insurance requirements: Verify what insurance is covered by the HOA and what you need to carry individually. Some communities include master insurance policies that cover exterior structures and common areas, while individual unit owners are responsible for interior coverage and personal property.

Why Town 'n' Country?

Central location minutes from Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, International Mall, and Citrus Park Mall with Veterans Expressway access.

With a population of approximately 82,000 and a median home price around $340,000, Town 'n' Country provides an accessible entry point to the Tampa Bay lifestyle. The local economy is supported by Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, Raymond James, USAA, nearby MacDill AFB, and the broader region offers cultural attractions including performing arts, museums, professional sports, and waterfront dining that keep active adults engaged and entertained.

For 55+ buyers exploring Town 'n' Country real estate, the combination of Florida's tax advantages, the area's healthcare infrastructure, and the quality of available active adult communities makes Town 'n' Country a compelling retirement destination. Whether you are relocating from out of state or downsizing from a larger home in Hillsborough County, Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can guide you through every step of the process. Frequently Asked Questions About Town 'n' Country 55+ Homes

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community?

Federal law requires that at least 80 percent of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Most communities in the Town 'n' Country area allow younger spouses or partners to reside with a qualifying 55+ owner. However, policies regarding other household members under 55 vary by community. Some restrict younger residents entirely, while others allow exceptions with board approval. Barrett Henry can clarify the age policies for any community you are considering.

What do HOA fees cover in Town 'n' Country 55+ communities?

HOA fees in Town 'n' Country 55+ communities typically cover exterior home maintenance, roof reserves, lawn care, common area landscaping, community amenity operations, security, and sometimes cable TV, internet, and pest control. The scope of coverage varies significantly between communities, so it is important to get a detailed breakdown before comparing fees between different neighborhoods. Higher fees are not necessarily a negative - they often reflect a more comprehensive maintenance and amenity package.

Are 55+ homes a good investment?

55+ homes in the Town 'n' Country area have generally appreciated in line with or slightly below the broader market, depending on the specific community and its management quality. The primary value proposition of 55+ homes is lifestyle rather than investment return - the maintenance-free living, social amenities, and community atmosphere provide a quality of life that is difficult to quantify financially. That said, well-managed communities with strong HOAs and desirable locations have shown solid appreciation over time.

Can I rent out my 55+ home in Town 'n' Country?

Rental policies vary by community. Some 55+ communities in the Town 'n' Country area permit rentals with restrictions such as minimum lease terms (often 6-12 months), annual rental limits, and tenant age requirements. Others prohibit rentals entirely or restrict them to hardship cases with board approval. If future rental flexibility is important to you, verify the community's rental policy before purchasing.

What is the social atmosphere like in Town 'n' Country 55+ communities?

Most 55+ communities near Town 'n' Country foster a warm, welcoming social atmosphere with organized activities, clubs, and events that make it easy for newcomers to connect with neighbors. From card groups and book clubs to organized outings and holiday celebrations, the social calendar provides ample opportunities to build friendships and stay engaged. Many residents describe the social aspect of 55+ living as the most unexpected and rewarding benefit of their purchase decision.

title: Town n Country Condos & Townhomes
content:
Quick Answer
