Why Condos & Townhomes Are Popular in Town 'n' Country

Condos and townhomes represent one of the fastest-growing segments of the Town 'n' Country real estate market. Buyers are drawn to the lower price points, reduced maintenance responsibilities, and community amenities that attached and multi-family housing provides. Town 'n' Country is a large, centrally located community in unincorporated Hillsborough County, west of Tampa. It offers exceptional convenience to Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, and the Veterans Expressway, making it a commuter favorite.

For first-time buyers, condos and townhomes in Town 'n' Country offer an affordable entry point into homeownership. For downsizers, they provide a lock-and-leave lifestyle that eliminates the burden of yard maintenance, exterior upkeep, and roof repairs. And for investors, the strong rental demand in the Town 'n' Country area makes condos and townhomes an attractive addition to a real estate portfolio - provided the association allows rentals.

The Town 'n' Country market offers a wide range of condo and townhome options, from garden-style condos with ground-floor access to multi-story townhomes with private garages and rooftop terraces. Whether you prioritize walkability, commute convenience, or community amenities, there is a condo or townhome community in Town 'n' Country that fits your needs. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping buyers navigate the unique considerations of condo and townhome purchases.

Popular Condo & Townhome Communities in Town 'n' Country

The following communities represent some of the best options for condo and townhome buyers in the Town 'n' Country area.

Town 'n' Country condos

Town 'n' Country condos is one of the most sought-after condo and townhome communities in Town 'n' Country. The community offers a range of floor plans from compact two-bedroom units to spacious three-bedroom residences with modern finishes. Residents enjoy community amenities including a pool, fitness area, and well-maintained common spaces. The location provides convenient access to major employers, shopping centers, and transportation corridors, making Town 'n' Country condos particularly popular with working professionals and young families who want an affordable home in a desirable location.

Westgate townhomes

Westgate townhomes appeals to buyers who value a well-managed community with consistent standards and solid finances. Units here feature updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and open floor plans that maximize living space. The community amenity package includes pool access, covered parking, and professionally maintained grounds. Westgate townhomes has maintained a strong resale track record, with properties typically selling within a reasonable timeframe and at competitive prices relative to the broader Town 'n' Country market.

Bay Crest Park villas

Bay Crest Park villas offers another excellent option for condo and townhome buyers in Town 'n' Country. This community provides a mix of unit types that accommodate different household sizes and budgets. Common amenities include a pool, playground or recreation area, and visitor parking. The HOA is well-managed with adequate reserves, and the community has a track record of stable fees and minimal special assessments. For buyers prioritizing value and long-term stability, Bay Crest Park villas deserves serious consideration.

Price & HOA Overview for Town 'n' Country Condos & Townhomes

HOA fees for condos are generally higher than for townhomes because condo associations typically cover more services including exterior insurance, roof maintenance, painting, and sometimes water, sewer, and trash. Condo vs. Townhome: Understanding the Differences

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they have important legal and practical differences that affect ownership, financing, and daily life.

Ownership Structure

In a condo, you own the interior space of your unit and share ownership of common areas (building exterior, roof, grounds, amenities) with other unit owners through the association. In a townhome, you typically own the structure and the land beneath it, with shared ownership limited to common areas like pools, parks, and private roads. This distinction affects insurance requirements, maintenance responsibilities, and how future improvements are funded.

Maintenance Responsibility

Condo associations in Town 'n' Country generally handle all exterior maintenance, including the roof, building envelope, painting, landscaping, and common areas. Townhome owners often retain responsibility for their own roof, driveway, and limited exterior maintenance, though the HOA may handle landscaping and common area upkeep. This difference is reflected in HOA fees - condo fees tend to be higher because they cover more services.

Privacy and Space

Townhomes typically offer more interior space, multiple floors, a private garage, and sometimes a small yard or pation. Condos tend to be single-level units that may share walls on multiple sides. For buyers who prioritize privacy and the feel of a traditional home, townhomes are often the better choice. For buyers who prefer single-level living and minimal maintenance, condos may be more appropriate.

What Condo & Townhome Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome in Town 'n' Country requires due diligence beyond what a traditional single-family home purchase demands. Barrett Henry advises every buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Association financial health: Request the most recent financial statements, budget, and reserve study. Look for adequate reserves (ideally 20 percent or more of the annual budget), stable fee history, and no pending special assessments. Florida law now requires reserve studies and adequate funding for structural components following legislative changes in recent years.
  • Reserve fund compliance: Florida statutes now require condo associations to maintain funded reserves for structural components, including the roof, foundation, and load-bearing walls. Verify that the association is in compliance, as underfunded reserves can trigger special assessments and affect property values.
  • Insurance coverage: Understand the difference between the association's master policy and your individual HO-6 policy. The master policy typically covers the building exterior and common areas, while your HO-6 covers your interior, personal property, and liability. Verify coverage limits and deductibles for both policies.
  • Rules and restrictions: Review the association's governing documents, including CC&Rs, bylaws, and rules and regulations. Common restrictions cover pets, rentals, parking, noise, renovations, and use of common areas. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the unit in the future, verify the association's rental policy. Many Town 'n' Country associations limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously, impose minimum lease terms, or require tenant approval by the board. Some associations prohibit rentals entirely.
  • Pending litigation and violations: Ask whether the association is involved in any lawsuits and whether the building has any outstanding code violations. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Financing Condos: Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable

Financing a condo purchase in Town 'n' Country requires understanding the distinction between warrantable and non-warrantable condominiums, as this classification directly affects your mortgage options.

A warrantable condo meets the guidelines set by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which means it qualifies for conventional financing with competitive interest rates and standard down payment requirements. To be warrantable, a condo association generally must have adequate reserves, no more than 15 percent of units delinquent on fees, no single entity owning more than 20 percent of units, and at least 50 percent of units owner-occupied.

A non-warrantable condo fails to meet one or more of these guidelines, which limits financing options to portfolio loans, credit unions, or cash purchases. Non-warrantable condos often carry higher interest rates, larger down payment requirements, and fewer lender options. Common reasons a Town 'n' Country condo might be non-warrantable include high investor concentration, pending litigation, inadequate reserves, or a single entity owning too many units.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can help you determine the warrantability status of any condo you are considering and connect you with lenders who specialize in both warrantable and non-warrantable financing. Contact Barrett to discuss your financing options.

Lifestyle Benefits of Condo & Townhome Living

Beyond the financial considerations, condos and townhomes in Town 'n' Country offer lifestyle advantages that appeal to a wide range of buyers.

  • Low maintenance: Say goodbye to weekend yard work, exterior painting, and roof repairs. Condo and townhome living frees up time for the activities you actually enjoy.
  • Community amenities: Many Town 'n' Country communities include pools, fitness centers, and social spaces that would cost thousands to replicate in a single-family home setting.
  • Affordability: Condos and townhomes typically offer a lower entry price than comparable single-family homes, making homeownership accessible to first-time buyers and those on a budget.
  • Location: Attached housing communities are often situated in prime locations near employment centers, shopping, dining, and entertainment - areas where single-family homes may be priced significantly higher.
  • Security: Many condo communities in Town 'n' Country feature controlled access, security cameras, and well-lit common areas that provide an added layer of safety.
  • Lock and leave: For frequent travelers, seasonal residents, and busy professionals, the ability to lock the door and leave without worrying about yard maintenance or home security is invaluable.

Why Town 'n' Country?

Central location minutes from Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, International Mall, and Citrus Park Mall with Veterans Expressway access.

Town 'n' Country has a population of approximately 82,000 and a median home price of $340,000. The local economy benefits from Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, Raymond James, USAA, nearby MacDill AFB, creating consistent demand for housing at all price points. For buyers exploring Town 'n' Country real estate, condos and townhomes offer an affordable, low-maintenance path to homeownership in one of Florida's most dynamic markets.

Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an affordable entry point, a downsizer seeking a simpler lifestyle, or an investor building a rental portfolio, Town 'n' Country's condo and townhome market has options to match your goals. Frequently Asked Questions About Town 'n' Country Condos & Townhomes

How much are HOA fees for condos in Town 'n' Country?

Monthly HOA fees for condos in Town 'n' Country typically range from $200 to $500, depending on the community's amenity package, age, and services included. Fees that cover exterior insurance, roof reserves, water, sewer, and trash tend to be higher but reduce the owner's out-of-pocket costs for those items. Barrett Henry can provide exact fee information and a breakdown of included services for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my condo or townhome in Town 'n' Country?

Rental policies vary by association. Some Town 'n' Country communities allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on total rental units. Others prohibit rentals or require board approval for each tenant. If rental flexibility is important to you, verify the association's policy before purchasing and confirm that the current rental cap has not been reached.

What is a special assessment and should I be worried?

A special assessment is a one-time charge levied by the association to cover unexpected expenses or projects that exceed reserve fund capacity. Common triggers include roof replacement, elevator modernization, structural repairs, and insurance premium increases. While special assessments are a normal part of condo ownership, frequent or large assessments may indicate poor financial planning. Reviewing the reserve study and financial statements before purchasing helps assess this risk.

Do I need separate insurance for my condo?

Yes. While the association's master policy covers the building exterior and common areas, individual condo owners in Town 'n' Country need an HO-6 policy that covers interior finishes, personal property, liability, and loss assessment coverage. Loss assessment coverage is particularly important, as it protects you if the association levies a special assessment for a covered loss that exceeds the master policy's coverage.

What is the difference between a condo and a townhome for financing purposes?

Condos face additional financing scrutiny because lenders evaluate the entire association - not just the individual unit. Townhomes, which typically convey land with the structure, are often financed more like single-family homes with fewer association-level requirements. However, some townhome communities are structured as condominiums from a legal standpoint, which triggers condo financing requirements. Town 'n' Country is a large, centrally located community in unincorporated Hillsborough County, west of Tampa. Country Place

Security Features in Town 'n' Country Gated Communities

Security is often the primary motivation for buying in a gated community, and Town 'n' Country communities offer various levels of access control and monitoring.

  • Guard-gated entry: The highest level of security, with a staffed gatehouse that verifies every visitor. Guard-gated communities such as Country Place typically have higher HOA fees but provide the strongest access control and residents report the greatest peace of mind.
  • Automated gate entry: Electronic gates with keypad, key fob, or remote access are the most common type in Town 'n' Country. These systems control vehicle access effectively while keeping HOA costs lower than guard-gated alternatives.
  • Perimeter fencing and walls: Most gated communities in Town 'n' Country feature continuous perimeter fencing or walls that define the community boundary and deter unauthorized access.
  • Security cameras and monitoring: Many communities supplement gate access with camera systems at entries, common areas, and perimeter points. Some HOAs contract with private security firms for regular patrols.
  • Guest management systems: Modern gated communities increasingly use smartphone-based guest management apps that allow residents to pre-authorize visitors, receive entry notifications, and manage access remotely.

Community Amenities That Define Gated Living

The amenity package is what transforms a gated neighborhood from a collection of homes into a true community. In Town 'n' Country, buyers can expect the following amenities in most gated communities.

Pool and Fitness Facilities

Nearly every gated community in Town 'n' Country includes at least one community pool, and many feature resort-style aquatic centers with lap lanes, children's splash areas, and poolside cabanas. Fitness centers range from basic equipment rooms to full-service gyms with cardio machines, free weights, and group fitness studios. These amenities eliminate the need for gym memberships and provide convenient, steps-from-home fitness options.

Tennis, Pickleball, and Recreation

Tennis and pickleball courts have become standard amenities in Town 'n' Country gated communities, reflecting the explosive growth of racket sports in Florida. Many communities also include basketball courts, playgrounds, dog parks, and multi-use athletic fields that serve residents of all ages.

Clubhouse and Social Spaces

Community clubhouses serve as gathering spots for HOA meetings, holiday parties, book clubs, and private events. Larger gated communities in Town 'n' Country may include event rooms with catering kitchens, covered outdoor pavilions, and dedicated meeting spaces that foster social connection among residents.

What to Ask Before Buying in a Town 'n' Country Gated Community

Barrett Henry advises every buyer considering a gated community in Town 'n' Country to evaluate the following factors before making an offer.

  • HOA financial health: Request the most recent budget, financial statements, and reserve study. A well-funded reserve (typically 30 percent or more of the annual budget) indicates the community can handle major repairs and replacements without special assessments.
  • Special assessments history: Ask whether the community has levied any special assessments in the past five years and what projects prompted them. Frequent special assessments may signal underfunded reserves or aging infrastructure.
  • Rules and restrictions: Read the CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions) thoroughly. Common restrictions cover exterior paint colors, landscaping, parking, rentals, pets, and home-based businesses. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the property in the future, verify the community's rental policies. Many gated communities in Town 'n' Country limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously or impose minimum lease terms.
  • Insurance requirements: Some gated communities require specific insurance coverage levels or types. Verify insurance requirements and obtain quotes before closing to avoid surprises.
  • Pending litigation: Ask the HOA whether any lawsuits are pending against the association. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Why Town 'n' Country?

Central location minutes from Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, International Mall, and Citrus Park Mall with Veterans Expressway access.

Town 'n' Country has a population of approximately 82,000 and a median home price of $340,000. The local economy is supported by Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, Raymond James, USAA, nearby MacDill AFB, providing a stable employment base that drives consistent housing demand. For buyers exploring Town 'n' Country real estate, gated communities offer a compelling combination of security, amenities, and property value protection.

The broader Tampa Bay region continues to attract new residents from across the country, and gated communities in Town 'n' Country are among the first neighborhoods to feel the benefit of that growth. Whether you are relocating for work, retiring to Florida, or upgrading to a more amenity-rich lifestyle, Town 'n' Country's gated communities deliver a standard of living that is difficult to match. Explore homes for sale in Town 'n' Country with Barrett Henry, REALTOR® or learn about selling your home in a gated community.

Frequently Asked Questions About Town 'n' Country Gated Communities

How much are HOA fees in Town 'n' Country gated communities?

HOA fees in Town 'n' Country gated communities typically range from $150 to $500 per month, depending on the amenity package, security level, and maintenance scope. Guard-gated communities with extensive amenities tend to be at the higher end, while communities with automated gates and fewer amenities are more affordable. Barrett Henry can provide exact HOA fee information for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my home in a Town 'n' Country gated community?

Rental policies vary by community. Some gated neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on the total number of rental units. Others prohibit rentals entirely or require HOA board approval for each tenant. Always review the CC&Rs before purchasing if you anticipate renting the property.

Are gated communities safer than non-gated neighborhoods?

Gated communities in Town 'n' Country generally experience lower rates of property crime compared to non-gated areas, though no security system is impervious. The controlled access, reduced through-traffic, and community awareness that gated living provides create an environment where residents feel more secure. Guard-gated communities with active patrol and camera systems offer the highest level of security.

Do gated community homes hold their value better?

Historically, homes in well-managed gated communities in Town 'n' Country have shown strong value retention and appreciation. The consistent maintenance standards, controlled development, and desirable amenities help protect property values even in softer markets. The key factor is HOA management quality - communities with strong financial reserves and proactive maintenance outperform those with deferred maintenance and underfunded reserves.

What happens if the HOA raises fees significantly?

HOA fee increases in Town 'n' Country gated communities typically require board approval and are communicated to homeowners in advance. Most communities limit annual increases to a set percentage unless a special vote authorizes a larger increase. Reviewing the HOA's budget trajectory and reserve study will give you insight into whether significant fee increases are likely in the near future.

Homes for Sale in Town 'n' Country, FL

Town 'n' Country is one of western Hillsborough County's most accessible and affordable communities, offering a wide range of housing options for buyers at every stage. Town 'n' Country is an unincorporated community located between Tampa and Westchase. Its housing stock includes single-family homes from the 1970s through the 2020s, townhomes, and condominiums. You will find everything from modest ranch-style homes in established neighborhoods to larger, newer builds in the Countryway area. This variety is one reason the community appeals to such a broad range of buyers.

The area benefits from direct access to the Veterans Expressway and close proximity to Tampa International Airport, making it a practical choice for commuters and frequent travelers. Shopping, dining, and essential services are plentiful along Hillsborough Avenue and the Citrus Park corridor.

title: Town n Country Homes with Pool
content:
Quick Answer

Town 'n' Country pool homes typically range from $290,000-$550,000, with screened enclosures being standard across Hillsborough County. Buyers should budget for pool inspection, resurfacing timelines, and updated equipment when evaluating resale pool properties.

Schedule a ShowingSearch Homes

Why Pool Homes Are So Popular in Town 'n' Country

In Town 'n' Country, a swimming pool is not a luxury - it is a way of life. With average temperatures above 70 degrees for nine months of the year and summer highs regularly reaching the mid-90s, residents rely on their backyard pools for daily relief, weekend entertaining, and year-round outdoor living. Town 'n' Country is a large, centrally located community in unincorporated Hillsborough County, west of Tampa. It offers exceptional convenience to Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, and the Veterans Expressway, making it a commuter favorite.

Pool homes in Town 'n' Country consistently command higher resale values than comparable non-pool properties. According to recent market data, homes with pools sell for approximately 5-8 percent more than similar homes without one. For families, retirees, and remote workers who spend significant time at home, a pool transforms the backyard into a private retreat that rivals any resort.

The popularity of pool homes has only increased since 2020, when more buyers began prioritizing outdoor living space, home offices with views, and personal recreation areas. In Town 'n' Country, that trend shows no signs of slowing, with pool-equipped listings often receiving multiple offers within days of hitting the market.

Best Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Town 'n' Country

Choosing the right neighborhood is just as important as finding the right pool. Here are the top areas in Town 'n' Country where pool homes are most prevalent and desirable.

Country Place

Country Place is widely regarded as one of the premier neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country for pool homes. Properties here tend to feature larger lots, established landscaping, and pools that have been well-maintained over the years. Many homes in Country Place include screened pool enclosures with extended lanais, outdoor kitchens, and tropical plantings that create a true backyard oasis. The neighborhood offers convenient access to shopping, dining, and major roadways, making it ideal for families and professionals alike.

Bay Crest Park

Bay Crest Park attracts buyers who want pool homes with a community feel. Many properties in this neighborhood include pools with newer equipment, updated decking, and spacious screen enclosures. The area is known for its well-kept streetscapes, neighborhood parks, and family-friendly atmosphere. Pool homes in Bay Crest Park tend to offer excellent value, with price points that appeal to first-time pool home buyers and move-up buyers.

Westgate

For buyers seeking pool homes with larger lots and more privacy, Westgate delivers. This area features properties with expansive backyards, mature trees, and pools that serve as the centerpiece of outdoor entertainment areas. Many pool homes in Westgate include covered patios, summer kitchens, and fire pit areas that extend the usable outdoor space well beyond the pool deck itself.

Town 'n' Country Park

Town 'n' Country Park rounds out the top pool home neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country with a mix of newer construction and updated resale homes. Pools here range from classic rectangular designs to freeform tropical layouts with water features. The neighborhood benefits from newer infrastructure, well-maintained HOA standards, and proximity to parks and recreation areas that complement the backyard pool lifestyle.

Pool Home Price Overview in Town 'n' Country

The following table provides a general overview of pool home pricing across Town 'n' Country by property type and size. Prices vary by neighborhood, pool condition, lot size, and home features.

Property TypePool Home Price RangeTypical Lot Size
3-Bedroom / 2-Bath$290,000-$550,0000.15-0.25 acres

The median home price in Town 'n' Country is approximately $340,000, with pool homes generally commanding a premium above that figure. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed market analysis for your specific neighborhood and price range. Contact Barrett for current pool home inventory.

Types of Pools You Will Find in Town 'n' Country

Not all pools are created equal, and understanding the types available in Town 'n' Country will help you narrow your search and budget accordingly.

Screened Pool Enclosures

The vast majority of residential pools in Town 'n' Country - and across Florida - feature aluminum-framed screen enclosures, commonly called pool cages. These enclosures keep out insects, reduce debris, and provide a measure of safety for children and pets. A standard pool cage in good condition adds significant value to a home and is considered essential by most buyers in Hillsborough County. Replacement costs for a full pool cage can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on size, so cage condition is a key inspection item.

Saltwater Pools

Saltwater pool systems have surged in popularity across Town 'n' Country due to lower maintenance costs and a more comfortable swimming experience. Saltwater generators produce chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, reducing the need for chemical handling and producing water that is gentler on skin, hair, and swimwear. Many resale homes have been converted from traditional chlorine to saltwater systems, and most new construction pools include saltwater as standard.

Heated Pools

While Town 'n' Country enjoys a warm climate, winter mornings can bring pool water temperatures down into the 60s. Gas heaters, heat pumps, and solar heating systems extend the swimming season to a full twelve months. Gas heaters provide the fastest heat-up time, while heat pumps offer better energy efficiency for day-to-day use. Solar heating is the most economical long-term option and works well with the abundant Florida sunshine.

Freeform and Custom Pools

Many homes in Town 'n' Country feature custom-designed freeform pools with rock waterfalls, grottos, tanning ledges, and infinity edges. These resort-style pools are most common in upscale neighborhoods and estate properties, where the pool and outdoor living area serve as the architectural focal point of the home. Buyers should note that custom pools may cost more to maintain and insure than standard designs.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist

Purchasing a pool home requires additional due diligence beyond a standard home inspection. Barrett Henry recommends every pool home buyer evaluate the following items before making an offer.

  • Pool inspection: Hire a certified pool inspector separate from the general home inspector. They will evaluate the shell, plumbing, equipment, deck, and screen enclosure for defects, leaks, and code compliance.
  • Resurfacing timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or quartz) typically last 8-15 years. Determine when the pool was last resurfaced and budget accordingly if resurfacing is due within the next few years. Costs range from $5,000 to $12,000.
  • Equipment age: Pool pumps, filters, heaters, and salt systems have a lifespan of 5-10 years. Aging equipment may work today but represent a near-term replacement cost. Ask the seller for maintenance records and equipment installation dates.
  • Screen enclosure condition: Inspect the cage for corrosion, torn screens, sagging frames, and signs of storm damage. A full cage replacement can cost $8,000-$15,000, so factor this into your offer if damage is present.
  • Insurance impact: Pool ownership affects homeowners insurance premiums and liability coverage. Discuss pool-specific coverage with your insurance agent before closing. A pool fence or cage is typically required for compliance with local safety codes.
  • Deck and drainage: Pool decks should be level, free of large cracks, and properly graded to direct water away from the home. Settling, trip hazards, and poor drainage are common issues in older pool homes.

Outdoor Living Features Beyond the Pool

In Town 'n' Country, the pool is often just one element of a comprehensive outdoor living area. The best pool homes pair the swimming pool with features that extend the home's livable square footage into the backyard.

Lanais and Covered Patios

A screened lanai adjacent to the pool provides shaded seating, outdoor dining, and protection from afternoon rain showers. Many Town 'n' Country homes feature extended lanais with ceiling fans, recessed lighting, and tile or travertine flooring that create a seamless indoor-outdoor transition.

Summer Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens - called summer kitchens in Florida - have become a must-have amenity in Town 'n' Country pool homes. A typical summer kitchen includes a built-in grill, countertop space, a mini-refrigerator, and a sink. Upscale versions add pizza ovens, smokers, kegerators, and bar seating that turn the pool area into an entertainment destination.

Landscape and Lighting

Tropical landscaping, LED pool lighting, and landscape lighting create a resort atmosphere that enhances both daytime and evening enjoyment. Mature palms, birds of paradise, and jasmine hedges are popular plantings that thrive in Town 'n' Country's climate and complement the pool setting.

Why Town 'n' Country?

Central location minutes from Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, International Mall, and Citrus Park Mall with Veterans Expressway access.

With a population of approximately 82,000, Town 'n' Country offers a strong and diverse economy anchored by Tampa International Airport, Westshore business district, Raymond James, USAA, nearby MacDill AFB. The combination of employment opportunities, lifestyle amenities, and a growing real estate market makes Town 'n' Country one of the most compelling places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region.

For buyers exploring Town 'n' Country real estate, pool homes represent an outstanding investment in both quality of life and long-term property value. Whether you are relocating from out of state, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for your retirement oasis, Town 'n' Country delivers the Florida lifestyle at a price point that competes favorably with other Gulf Coast markets.

Frequently Asked Questions About Town 'n' Country Pool Homes

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Town 'n' Country?

Monthly pool maintenance in Town 'n' Country typically runs between $100 and $200 for weekly professional service, which includes chemical balancing, skimming, brushing, and equipment checks. Homeowners who maintain their own pools can reduce costs to $40-$80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual costs for electricity to run the pump average $600-$1,200 depending on the pump type and run time.

Do pool homes cost more to insure in Town 'n' Country?

Yes, pool homes generally carry higher homeowners insurance premiums due to increased liability exposure. The additional cost is typically $100-$300 per year, though rates vary by insurer, pool type, and whether the pool has a safety fence or enclosure. Screen enclosures can help reduce premiums by meeting safety barrier requirements.

What is the best time to buy a pool home in Town 'n' Country?

The best time to buy a pool home in Town 'n' Country is typically during the late fall and winter months (November through February), when buyer competition decreases and sellers may be more willing to negotiate. However, inventory for pool homes tends to be limited year-round, so working with an experienced agent like Barrett Henry ensures you see new listings the moment they hit the market.

Should I buy a home with an existing pool or build one?

Both options have merits. Buying an existing pool home avoids the 3-6 month construction timeline and the hassle of managing a pool build project. However, building a new pool lets you customize the design, equipment, and features to your exact specifications. New pool construction in Town 'n' Country typically costs $35,000-$80,000 depending on size, features, and site conditions. Barrett Henry can help you evaluate both options based on available inventory and your budget.

Are there HOA restrictions on pools in Town 'n' Country?

Many neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country have HOA guidelines that govern pool construction, including setback requirements, fence or enclosure standards, and equipment placement. Some HOAs require architectural review board approval before a pool can be built. Barrett Henry can review HOA documents and identify any restrictions before you make an offer on a property where you plan to add a pool.

Why Buy New Construction in Town 'n' Country?

Buying new construction in Town 'n' Country means moving into a home designed with today's lifestyle in mind. Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Town 'n' Country also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Town 'n' Country area, including Mostly resale with some infill. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Town 'n' Country typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Town 'n' Country
Entry-Level / Starter$300K-$370K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s
Premium / Luxury$450K+

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Town 'n' Country?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

Town 'n' Country is a large, centrally located community in unincorporated Hillsborough County, west of Tampa. It offers exceptional convenience to Tampa International Airport, the Westshore business district, and the Veterans Expressway, making it a commuter favorite.

Population growth in the greater Tampa Bay area has accelerated in recent years, fueled by remote work flexibility, corporate relocations, and the appeal of Florida's tax-friendly environment. Town 'n' Country, with a population of approximately 82,000, benefits directly from this growth as buyers discover the quality of life, value, and convenience the community offers. What Is Coming on the Market in Town 'n' Country

The Town 'n' Country market sees a regular flow of new listings across all property types, with seasonal patterns that savvy buyers can use to their advantage. Here is what you can expect in the current market.

Spring and early summer (March through June) represent the peak listing season in Town 'n' Country, when inventory expands as sellers prepare their homes for the busiest buying months. This is when you will find the widest selection, including move-up homes, new construction completions, and relocation listings from families timing their moves with the school calendar.

Late summer and fall (July through October) bring a moderate slowdown in new listings, though serious sellers continue to list and motivated buyers face less competition. This period can offer negotiating advantages that are difficult to achieve during the spring rush.

Winter (November through February) sees reduced local listing activity but an influx of out-of-state buyers making relocation decisions. Properties that list during the winter months in Town 'n' Country often face less competition and benefit from buyers who are actively relocating rather than casually browsing.

Properties here attract strong buyer interest due to the neighborhood's established character, convenient location, and competitive pricing relative to newer communities. Homes in Country Place range from updated single-family residences with pools and modern finishes to value-opportunity properties that reward buyers willing to invest in cosmetic updates. The neighborhood benefits from mature trees, established infrastructure, and a strong sense of community identity that newer subdivisions cannot easily replicate. New listings in Country Place move quickly, making it essential to have an agent who monitors this area daily.

Properties in Westgate benefit from proximity to parks, shopping, and employment centers, and the neighborhood's ongoing development signals continued investment and appreciation potential. Whether you are looking for a starter home, a family residence, or an investment property, Westgate warrants a prominent spot on your watch list.

The neighborhood's location provides practical daily convenience, and its steady listing activity means new opportunities appear regularly for patient, prepared buyers.

Bay Crest Park

Bay Crest Park is another neighborhood where new listings in Town 'n' Country consistently generate buyer interest. The area combines attractive pricing with neighborhood character and convenient access to the amenities and employment centers that make Town 'n' Country such a compelling place to live. Understanding the Town 'n' Country Market

Making a smart purchase in Town 'n' Country requires understanding the broader market dynamics that influence pricing, inventory, and negotiating leverage.

The Town 'n' Country market is currently characterized by moderate inventory levels, steady buyer demand, and gradual price appreciation. While the frenetic bidding wars of 2021 and 2022 have largely subsided, well-priced homes in desirable neighborhoods continue to sell quickly and often above asking price. Overpriced listings, on the other hand, tend to sit longer and eventually sell at or below market value after price reductions.

Interest rates remain a significant factor in the Town 'n' Country market. Rate fluctuations directly affect buyer purchasing power and, consequently, the pace of sales. Barrett Henry monitors rate trends and helps buyers evaluate their options whether rates are rising, falling, or holding steady. In many cases, buying at a slightly higher rate and refinancing later proves more advantageous than waiting for rates to drop while home prices continue to appreciate.

New construction in Town 'n' Country represents a growing share of available inventory, with national builders and regional developers delivering homes across multiple price points. New construction offers the advantage of modern floor plans, energy efficiency, builder warranties, and the ability to select finishes - but it also requires navigating builder contracts, timelines, and the potential for cost overruns. title: Town n Country Waterfront Homes
content:
Quick Answer

Waterfront homes in Town 'n' Country include properties on Old Tampa Bay shoreline, Rocky Point area. Pricing varies widely based on water type, lot size, and direct access. Flood insurance and seawall condition are key considerations.

Browse Town n Country Waterfront Homes Homes for Sale

Updated daily from the MLS. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to schedule a showing.

Types of Waterfront in Town 'n' Country

Town 'n' Country offers several types of waterfront living, each with its own character, pricing, and lifestyle:

  • Old Tampa Bay shoreline, Rocky Point area - the primary waterfront options in Town 'n' Country range from open-water properties with panoramic views to canal-front homes with private dock access and lake-front properties with peaceful settings.

The type of waterfront determines not just the lifestyle but also insurance costs, maintenance requirements, and resale value. Open-water properties with direct bay or Gulf access typically command the highest premiums.

Popular Waterfront Areas

The most sought-after waterfront neighborhoods in Town 'n' Country include areas within Town 'n' Country Park, Westchase border, Rocky Point area. These neighborhoods offer a mix of water types, lot sizes, and price points.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Town 'n' Country require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Town 'n' Country?

Flood insurance costs in Town 'n' Country vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Town 'n' Country?

Most waterfront properties in Town 'n' Country allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Town 'n' Country generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.

title: Treasure Island FL Real Estate | Homes for Sale
content:
Browse Treasure Island Real Estate Homes for Sale

Updated daily from the MLS. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to schedule a showing.

Treasure Island is a barrier island city of approximately 6,500 residents on the Gulf of Mexico, positioned between St. Pete Beach to the south and Madeira Beach to the north along the central Pinellas County coast. The city encompasses three distinct barrier islands connected by bridges: Treasure Island proper, Paradise Island to the north, and Isle of Capri, each with its own residential character and price profile within the broader Treasure Island municipal framework. The median listing price runs approximately $792,000 as of January 2026 (with sold prices averaging closer to $697,000, down approximately 10% year over year), placing it in the mid-tier of the Pinellas County barrier island market and reflecting the broader normalization from pandemic-era peaks that has affected coastal Florida real estate throughout the region.

Treasure Island is known among Tampa Bay residents primarily for its live music culture and its Gulf beach, two characteristics that feed each other: the consistent foot traffic from a beach community that operates year-round rather than seasonally supports the multiple venues with daily live music that have become a defining feature of the island's commercial character. Ricky T's, Middle Grounds Grill, Caddy's, and the other waterfront bars and restaurants that anchor the Gulf Boulevard commercial strip give Treasure Island an energy that is less formal than the Don CeSar atmosphere to the south and more accessible than the tourist-density of Clearwater Beach to the north.

For buyers, Treasure Island offers barrier island Gulf beach living at price points that reflect both the genuine appeal of the location and the market's current adjustment from the pandemic era. The combination of a 10% year-over-year price decline in sold prices and a 78-day-or-longer average time on market for many listings creates genuine negotiating opportunities for buyers who are patient and willing to do thorough due diligence on condominium financials and flood zone status, which are the two primary complexity factors in any Treasure Island purchase.

Interested in buying or selling in Treasure Island? Barrett Henry with REMAX Collective covers every Treasure Island neighborhood, from Sunset Beach single-family homes to Isle of Capri condominiums to Gulf-front properties along the main island. Let's talk about what fits your priorities and what the current market looks like for buyers.

Schedule a Conversation

Schedule a Free ConsultationSee What Your Home Is Worth

Treasure Island Neighborhood Guide

Treasure Island's three connected islands each have a distinct residential character. Understanding the differences is essential for buyers who are evaluating the market from outside the area and may not realize how meaningfully the experience varies from one part of the city to another.

Sunset Beach

Sunset Beach occupies the southern portion of Treasure Island proper, the area nearest to the Blind Pass connection to St. Pete Beach. The neighborhood is the most residential of Treasure Island's districts, with a concentration of single-family homes, smaller condominiums, and duplex properties that have a local-occupant character that distinguishes it from the hotel-heavy stretches of the northern barrier island. Sunset Beach is named for its western orientation and the sunset viewing it enables, and the small boardwalk area at the southern tip of the neighborhood provides a community gathering point that draws residents for evening walks and informal socializing throughout the year.

Homes in the Sunset Beach area range from approximately $550,000 for a smaller older property with limited water access to over $1.5 million for fully renovated single-family homes with Gulf or bay frontage. The residential scale of the neighborhood, combined with its proximity to both the Gulf beach and the commercial activity of the Treasure Island main strip to the north, makes Sunset Beach one of the most appealing addresses for buyers who want barrier island living without the hotel-adjacent atmosphere that some Gulf Boulevard addresses carry during peak season.

Treasure Island Main Strip and Gulf Boulevard

The main stretch of Treasure Island along Gulf Boulevard encompasses the city's primary hotel and resort properties, including the Bilmar Beach Resort and the Postcard Inn, alongside condominium buildings of varying vintage and quality, retail shops, and the restaurants and bars that anchor the island's live music culture. Condominiums along this corridor range from $350,000 for units in older buildings (subject to the full Florida post-Champlain condominium due diligence process) to over $1.5 million for premium Gulf-front units in newer or fully renovated towers.

The Gulf Boulevard corridor is the most tourist-facing part of Treasure Island, and buyers who purchase here should understand that the neighborhood's ambient character changes significantly between peak season and the quieter shoulder months. For buyers who want the investment income potential of a vacation rental in a high-traffic tourist corridor, this area provides the strongest short-term rental demand in the city, subject to the applicable regulatory requirements. For buyers who want a primary or second home with a quiet residential atmosphere, the corridor's seasonal tourist intensity is worth experiencing firsthand during a peak weekend before committing to a purchase.

Isle of Capri

Isle of Capri is the northernmost of the three Treasure Island barrier islands, connected to the main island by a short bridge and providing a more sheltered residential environment with Intracoastal Waterway access on the bay side and bay views rather than direct Gulf frontage for most properties. Roselli Park on Isle of Capri provides a waterfront park area with picnic facilities and a boat ramp that serves as the community gathering point for the island's residential population. Homes on Isle of Capri range from approximately $450,000 for mid-century ranches on interior lots to over $900,000 for updated bay-front properties with dock access.

Isle of Capri attracts buyers who want the Treasure Island address and barrier island lifestyle at a more accessible price point than the Gulf-front properties, with the bay-side character and Intracoastal access compensating for the lack of direct Gulf frontage. The island's more residential and less tourist-oriented atmosphere relative to the Gulf Boulevard main strip makes it a practical option for buyers who want year-round primary residence living rather than the seasonal tourist rhythm of the beachfront properties.

Sunshine Beach and the Northern Island

Sunshine Beach and the northern section of Treasure Island approaching the Johns Pass Bridge provide a transitional zone between the city and the adjacent Madeira Beach community, with a mix of single-family homes, condominiums, and rental properties in the $500,000 to $1.2 million range. The proximity to Johns Pass Village, technically in Madeira Beach but functionally accessible as a walkable dining and activity destination for northern Treasure Island residents, adds to the lifestyle appeal of this part of the city. Johns Pass is one of the most active commercial fishing areas in Pinellas County, with charter boat operators, seafood restaurants, and a village commercial atmosphere that provides a practical day destination for Treasure Island residents in the northern part of the city.

Dining and Live Music in Treasure Island

Treasure Island's food and entertainment scene is anchored by a cluster of waterfront restaurants and bars that have developed daily live music programming as a defining community feature. The concentration of live music venues, seafood restaurants, and beach bars along the Gulf Boulevard commercial strip gives Treasure Island a social energy that draws visitors from the broader Pinellas County area on weekends and serves the island's own residential base throughout the week.

Local Dining Favorites

Caddy's on the Beach is one of the most beloved casual waterfront venues in the Pinellas barrier island market, with a direct beach setting, live music, and the kind of relaxed atmosphere that exemplifies what Gulf Coast beach bar culture can be when it is executed with genuine care for the experience rather than pure commercial efficiency. Middle Grounds Grill has earned recognition in the Florida Trend magazine's Top 500 Restaurants list, giving it a credibility that distinguishes it from the purely tourist-facing establishments in the corridor. Shrimpy's has developed a following for its New Orleans-inspired approach to Gulf seafood, bringing a different regional tradition to the barrier island market that is well-received in a city with a diverse resident base. Gigi's Italian, a family-run restaurant that has operated for more than five decades on Treasure Island, represents the kind of multi-generational neighborhood dining institution that barrier island communities rarely sustain through the turnover pressures of the Florida coastal market. Ricky T's provides daily live music alongside beach bar food and drink in a casual outdoor setting that draws both residents and visitors in equal measure throughout the year.

Sanding Ovations Festival

The Sanding Ovations master sand sculpting competition is held annually on Treasure Island Beach, drawing professional sand sculptors from around the world to create large-scale sand sculptures in a competitive format that draws tens of thousands of visitors over a multi-day event. The festival has established Treasure Island as an arts-and-culture destination beyond the standard beach resort category, and it provides an annual event anchor that residents point to as evidence of the city's investment in community programming beyond the standard beach activities. For buyers evaluating the community's character, the Sanding Ovations festival reflects the combination of beach accessibility and community investment in cultural programming that distinguishes Treasure Island from purely generic barrier island resort communities.

Short-Term Rentals and Investment in Treasure Island

Treasure Island's short-term rental regulatory environment is distinct from the adjacent St. Pete Beach market and should be researched specifically for any property a buyer is considering. The regulatory framework in Treasure Island has evolved over time and involves zone-specific rules that affect what rental activity is permissible for any given property. Buyers targeting vacation rental income should verify the current applicable regulations for the specific property address and zone before building investment projections based on short-term rental income, and should consider consulting with a local attorney or the city planning department to confirm current requirements before proceeding.

Text Barrett

The Gulf Boulevard main strip and the beachfront condominiums in permissive zones represent the strongest short-term rental demand in the city, with visitor occupancy driven by the beach access, the live music venues, and the Treasure Island name recognition that has been established through decades of tourism marketing. For investors who have verified that a specific property is in a permissive short-term rental zone, the demand fundamentals for well-located Treasure Island beachfront properties remain reasonable despite the price softening that has occurred across the market in the current normalization period.

Treasure Island Real Estate Market Overview

The Treasure Island real estate market in early 2026 is experiencing a meaningful normalization from the pandemic-era peak, with the approximately 10% year-over-year decline in sold prices and the widening gap between list prices and sale prices indicating that buyers have regained meaningful negotiating power relative to where the market stood in 2021 and 2022. The median listing price of $792,000 and the average days on market that has extended significantly for most property types signal that sellers who anchor to prior-peak pricing are finding the current market unresponsive to aspirational numbers.

Price Ranges by Area and Property Type

Gulf-front condominiums along the main strip: $350,000 for smaller units in older buildings needing potential assessment reserves to over $1.5 million for premium Gulf-front units in renovated or newer towers. Single-family homes in Sunset Beach: $550,000 to over $1.5 million depending on water access and condition. Isle of Capri residential: $450,000 to $900,000. Sunshine Beach and northern island: $500,000 to $1.2 million. Bay-side non-waterfront single-family on interior lots: $500,000 to $800,000. The full range of the Treasure Island market reflects the island's mix of mid-century modesty and Gulf-front luxury rather than a single-price-point community.

Condominium Due Diligence

Condominium buyers in Treasure Island face the same post-Champlain regulatory due diligence requirements that apply throughout coastal Florida. Buildings three stories or taller must complete milestone structural inspections and fund reserves adequately, and the resulting special assessments have been substantial in some older Treasure Island buildings. Before making an offer on any condo unit, buyers should request the most recent reserve study, the current reserve fund balance, any pending or anticipated special assessments, and the milestone inspection status. The older beachfront condo inventory on Treasure Island has a higher concentration of these compliance-related financial risks than newer construction, and buyers in this segment who skip the financial due diligence step expose themselves to potentially significant unexpected costs after closing.

Flood and Insurance Considerations

Treasure Island is a barrier island with full Gulf and bay exposure, and flood and wind insurance costs are substantial and should be factored into the true cost of ownership for every property on the island. Most of the island falls within FEMA Special Flood Hazard Areas requiring flood insurance for federally backed mortgages. Under the FEMA Risk Rating 2.0 methodology, premiums are calculated per property based on individual risk factors, and buyers should obtain specific flood insurance quotes using the actual property address rather than general area estimates. Wind insurance costs have risen significantly across coastal Pinellas County and are a material ownership cost for all island properties regardless of flood zone.

Who Buys in Treasure Island

Treasure Island draws a buyer pool that is oriented toward active beach lifestyle buyers and vacation rental investors more than the history-conscious and preservation-focused buyers who drive demand in St. Pete Beach's Pass-a-Grille area. The island's live music culture, the beach bar atmosphere, and the more accessible price points relative to some comparable Florida Gulf Coast markets attract buyers who want a barrier island lifestyle with social energy rather than the more sedate spa resort or historic village character available in adjacent communities.

Second-home buyers from the Northeast and Midwest who discovered the island through vacation visits are a consistent segment, drawn by the beach access and the live music culture's year-round energy that keeps the island feeling alive rather than seasonally dormant. The vacation rental investor segment, buying in zones where short-term rentals are permissible and building projections around beach visitor demand, remains active in the Gulf Boulevard corridor despite the broader price softening. Year-round residents who want barrier island living at price points somewhat more accessible than Clearwater Beach's premium zone choose Treasure Island for the combination of Gulf beach access, practical residential services, and the social atmosphere that the daily live music programming creates.

Treasure Island FL Real Estate FAQ

What is the median home price in Treasure Island, FL?

The median listing price in Treasure Island runs approximately $792,000 as of January 2026, with the median sold price closer to $697,000, down approximately 10% year over year. The price softening reflects the broader normalization from pandemic-era peaks and creates genuine negotiating opportunities for buyers who conduct thorough due diligence on condominium financials and flood zone status.

What is Sunset Beach in Treasure Island?

Sunset Beach is the southern portion of Treasure Island proper, the most residential district of the city, with a concentration of single-family homes, smaller condominiums, and duplex properties that have a local-occupant character. The small boardwalk area at the southern tip provides a community gathering point. Homes range from approximately $550,000 for smaller older properties to over $1.5 million for renovated Gulf or bay-front homes.

What restaurants and entertainment are in Treasure Island?

Caddy's on the Beach (casual waterfront, live music), Middle Grounds Grill (FL Trend Top 500), Shrimpy's (New Orleans-inspired Gulf seafood), Gigi's Italian (family-run since 1967), and Ricky T's (daily live music, beach bar) are the most recognized local establishments. The live music culture across multiple venues is a defining feature of the island's commercial character, drawing visitors from throughout Pinellas County.

How does Treasure Island compare to St. Pete Beach?

Treasure Island has a higher median listing price ($792K vs $699K for St. Pete Beach) but a similar sold median after negotiations. St. Pete Beach has the Don CeSar Hotel and Pass-a-Grille's historic district as its primary anchors. Treasure Island has the live music bar culture and Caddy's beach atmosphere as its defining character. St. Pete Beach has more restrictive STR regulations; Treasure Island's framework differs. Many buyers visit both before deciding based on preferred community character.

What is the Sanding Ovations festival?

The Sanding Ovations master sand sculpting competition is an annual event on Treasure Island Beach drawing professional sand sculptors from around the world to create large-scale competitive sand sculptures over a multi-day event. It draws tens of thousands of visitors and has established Treasure Island as an arts-and-culture destination beyond the standard beach resort category.

What should I know about buying a condo in Treasure Island?

Buyers must conduct full Florida post-Champlain regulatory due diligence: reserve study, current reserve fund balance, pending assessments, and milestone inspection status for buildings three stories or taller. Older beachfront condo inventory from the 1960s-1980s has higher concentration of compliance-related financial risks. This due diligence is essential and must occur before making an offer rather than after going under contract.

Is Treasure Island good for short-term rentals?

Treasure Island's STR regulatory framework involves zone-specific rules that must be verified for any specific property. The Gulf Boulevard main strip and beachfront condominiums in permissive zones have the strongest vacation rental demand, driven by beach access and the island's live music entertainment culture. Buyers targeting STR income must verify the specific property's zoning and current city ordinances before building income projections, as the regulatory environment has evolved and regulations vary by property location.

What is Isle of Capri in Treasure Island?

Isle of Capri is the northernmost of Treasure Island's three connected barrier islands, with a more sheltered residential environment featuring Intracoastal Waterway access and bay views rather than direct Gulf frontage for most properties. Roselli Park provides a waterfront community gathering point with a boat ramp. Homes range from $450,000 for mid-century ranches to over $900,000 for updated bay-front properties with dock access. Isle of Capri offers the Treasure Island address at more accessible price points with a quieter residential atmosphere.
