title: Treasure Island 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ communities in Treasure Island offer active adult living starting in the $319Ks and reaching $1,160K+ for premium homes. These age-restricted communities provide low-maintenance living, social activities, and resort-style amenities designed for adults 55 and older.

Why Treasure Island Is a Top Choice for 55+ Living

Treasure Island is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast. With a population of 7K and a median home price of $580K, this Pinellas County community offers an exceptional lifestyle for active adults seeking their next chapter. The combination of warm year-round weather, proximity to Gulf beaches, excellent healthcare facilities, and a vibrant social scene makes Treasure Island one of the most desirable 55+ destinations in the Tampa Bay region.

Florida has long been the top state for retirees, and Treasure Island exemplifies why. No state income tax means your retirement income stretches further. The cost of living in Pinellas County is moderate compared to South Florida, and the cultural amenities rival much larger metropolitan areas. From world-class museums and performing arts to fishing, golfing, and boating, Treasure Island offers the active retirement lifestyle that many buyers envision.

Top 55+ Communities in Treasure Island

Several 55+ communities have established strong reputations in the Treasure Island area. Each offers its own character, amenities, and price point.

Sunset Beach

Sunset Beach is one of the most popular 55+ communities in the Treasure Island area. Residents enjoy a low-maintenance lifestyle with HOA-covered exterior maintenance, landscaping, and access to community amenities including a clubhouse, pool, fitness facilities, and organized social activities. Homes in Sunset Beach range from $319,000 to $754,000 depending on size, updates, and location within the community. The neighborhood fosters a welcoming atmosphere where new residents quickly connect with neighbors through clubs, game nights, and community events.

Gulf Boulevard corridor

Gulf Boulevard corridor offers another compelling option for active adults in Treasure Island. This community features well-maintained grounds, a heated community pool, and a calendar full of social activities. Homes are typically single-story with open floor plans, updated kitchens, and screened lanais perfect for morning coffee or evening relaxation. Pricing in Gulf Boulevard corridor ranges from $319,000 to $493,000, making it an attractive option for buyers seeking value without sacrificing quality or community engagement.

Central Treasure Island

Central Treasure Island provides a third strong option for 55+ buyers in the Treasure Island market. Known for its peaceful setting and active resident community, Central Treasure Island features a mix of single-family homes and villa-style residences. Amenities often include shuffleboard, bocce ball, walking paths, and a community center. Homes here range from $493,000 to $1,160,000 for larger, updated units with premium views or locations within the community.

55+ Home Prices and Monthly Costs in Treasure Island

Understanding the full picture of 55+ living costs helps you budget accurately and choose the right community for your financial situation.

CategoryPrice RangeMonthly HOA/FeesWhat Is Included
Entry-Level 55+$319,000 to $493,000$2,320 to $4,060Lawn care, exterior maintenance, community pool, clubhouse
Mid-Range 55+$493,000 to $754,000$4,060 to $6,380All above plus fitness center, organized activities, cable TV
Premium 55+$754,000 to $1,160,000+$6,380+All above plus golf, spa, concierge, gated access, resort pool

Amenities and Lifestyle in Treasure Island 55+ Communities

The amenities in 55+ communities are designed to support an active, social, and comfortable lifestyle. Most communities in Treasure Island offer a central clubhouse that serves as the social hub of the neighborhood, hosting everything from card games and potlucks to holiday parties and educational seminars.

Common amenities across Treasure Island 55+ communities include:

  • Heated Swimming Pools: Most communities feature at least one heated pool for year-round swimming. Some offer separate lap pools and leisure pools with spa features.
  • Fitness Centers: On-site fitness rooms with cardio equipment, weight machines, and sometimes group fitness classes keep residents active without a gym membership.
  • Courts and Games: Tennis, pickleball, bocce ball, and shuffleboard courts are staples of Florida 55+ living. Many communities host regular tournaments and leagues.
  • Walking and Biking Trails: Paved trails winding through landscaped grounds encourage daily exercise and provide a pleasant way to socialize with neighbors.
  • Libraries and Computer Labs: Quiet spaces for reading, research, and staying connected are common in larger communities.
  • Social Calendars: Active communities maintain packed social calendars with day trips, guest speakers, craft groups, book clubs, and themed dinner events.

Healthcare Access Near Treasure Island

Access to quality healthcare is a critical factor for 55+ buyers, and Treasure Island delivers exceptional medical infrastructure. Pinellas County is served by several major hospital systems including BayCare Health System, HCA Florida, and Orlando Health. Facilities like Morton Plant Hospital in Clearwater, St. Anthony's Hospital in St. Petersburg, and Mease Countryside Hospital in Safety Harbor provide comprehensive care including emergency services, cardiac care, orthopedics, and oncology.

Beyond hospitals, Treasure Island offers convenient access to a wide network of primary care physicians, specialists, urgent care centers, and outpatient surgical facilities. Many 55+ communities are strategically located near medical corridors, ensuring that routine appointments and emergency care are just minutes away. This proximity to quality healthcare gives residents and their families peace of mind and is a significant advantage of choosing Treasure Island for retirement.

Social Life and Community Engagement in Treasure Island

One of the greatest benefits of 55+ living in Treasure Island is the built-in social network. Moving to a new community can feel isolating, but age-restricted neighborhoods are specifically designed to facilitate connections between residents. From the moment you move in, you have access to organized activities, clubs, and casual gathering spaces that make meeting your neighbors natural and enjoyable.

Many Treasure Island 55+ communities feature active social committees that organize weekly and monthly events. These might include morning walking groups, bridge and mahjong clubs, wine tasting evenings, cooking classes, and group outings to local attractions. The Pinellas Trail, which runs through much of the county, provides an excellent venue for cycling and walking groups. Gulf beaches are typically a short drive away, and community-organized beach days are popular throughout the warmer months.

Volunteering opportunities also abound. Treasure Island residents contribute to local nonprofits, schools, and community organizations. Many 55+ communities partner with local charities for fundraising events, creating a sense of purpose and giving back that enriches the retirement experience.

What to Know Before Buying a 55+ Home in Treasure Island

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations that differ from a standard home purchase. Here are the essential factors to evaluate:

  1. Age Requirements: Federal Housing for Older Persons Act (HOPA) requires that at least 80% of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Some communities are stricter, requiring all residents to be 55+. Understand the specific age policy before making an offer.
  2. Resale Restrictions: Some 55+ communities have first right of refusal clauses or approval processes for new buyers. These can add time to the closing process but help maintain community standards.
  3. Pet Policies: While many 55+ communities in Treasure Island allow pets, breed restrictions, weight limits, and pet number caps are common. If you have pets, verify the policy in writing before committing.
  4. Guest and Visitor Rules: Some communities limit how long guests can stay (often 14 to 30 consecutive days) and may require guest registration. If you expect frequent extended visits from family, make sure the community's guest policy accommodates that.
  5. Reserve Fund Health: Review the community's reserve fund and recent financial statements. A well-funded reserve protects against special assessments for major repairs like roof replacements, road repaving, or clubhouse renovations.
  6. Land Lease vs. Fee Simple: Some 55+ communities in Florida operate on land lease arrangements where you own the home but lease the land. Others are fee simple, meaning you own both. This distinction significantly impacts financing options and long-term costs.

Why Treasure Island Stands Out for 55+ Buyers

Treasure Island offers a retirement lifestyle that balances activity with relaxation, community with privacy, and value with quality. The city is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast, creating an environment where active adults can thrive. The combination of Florida's tax-friendly policies, Pinellas County's natural beauty, and Treasure Island's specific community character makes this an outstanding choice for your next chapter.

With a median home price of $580K and 55+ options starting well below that, Treasure Island provides attainable entry points for buyers coming from higher-cost markets. The strong resale market for 55+ homes, combined with the area's continued population growth, means your investment is well-positioned for the future.

For expert guidance on finding the right 55+ community in Treasure Island, contact Barrett Henry today. If you are selling a home to fund your move, visit the home selling page for resources and assistance.

Frequently Asked Questions About 55+ Homes in Treasure Island

What is the cheapest 55+ community in Treasure Island?

Entry-level 55+ homes in Treasure Island start around $319,000, typically offering two-bedroom floor plans with updated interiors and community amenities. These properties provide excellent value for buyers seeking affordable, maintenance-free living in a social environment. Monthly fees at entry-level communities generally range from $2,320 to $4,060.

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community in Treasure Island?

Under federal law, 55+ communities must have at least one resident aged 55 or older in 80% of occupied units. This means that a spouse or partner under 55 can typically live in the community. However, all residents usually must be at least 18 years old, and some communities have stricter age requirements. Children under 18 are generally not permitted as permanent residents in 55+ communities.

Do 55+ communities in Treasure Island appreciate in value?

Yes, 55+ communities in Treasure Island have shown steady appreciation, particularly those with strong amenities, well-funded reserves, and desirable locations. Demand for age-restricted housing continues to grow as baby boomers and early Gen Xers enter retirement. Properties in well-maintained communities with active social programs tend to appreciate at or near the broader market rate.

What financing options are available for 55+ homes?

Most fee-simple 55+ homes qualify for conventional mortgages, FHA loans, and VA loans. However, some lenders have restrictions on communities with high investor-ownership ratios or pending litigation. If the 55+ property is a condo, the community may need to be approved by FHA or VA for those loan types. Cash purchases are also very common in 55+ transactions. Your lender can advise on the specific options available for your target community.

What is the difference between 55+ and independent living?

A 55+ community is a residential neighborhood with an age restriction where residents own or rent their homes and live independently. Independent living facilities, on the other hand, are typically rental-based communities that may offer meals, housekeeping, and some level of personal assistance. 55+ communities in Treasure Island are designed for active, self-sufficient adults who want community and amenities without the structured services of an independent living facility.

title: Treasure Island Condos & Townhomes
content:
Quick Answer

Condos and townhomes in Treasure Island range from $290K for entry-level condos to $1,334K+ for luxury waterfront or downtown units. These properties offer low-maintenance living, community amenities, and prime locations throughout Treasure Island.

Why Condos and Townhomes Are Popular in Treasure Island

Treasure Island is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast. With a population of 7K and a median home price of $580K, the city attracts a wide range of buyers, from first-time purchasers and young professionals to downsizing retirees and seasonal residents. Condos and townhomes in Treasure Island address multiple buyer needs: lower entry prices compared to single-family homes, reduced maintenance responsibilities, and access to community amenities like pools, fitness centers, and secured entry.

The condo and townhome market in Treasure Island has evolved significantly, with new developments adding modern units alongside established communities that offer proven value. Whether you are seeking a walkable downtown lifestyle, waterfront views, or a quiet residential setting, Treasure Island has condo and townhome options to match your vision. The variety of architectural styles, price points, and locations makes this one of the most diverse segments of the Treasure Island real estate market.

Popular Areas for Condos and Townhomes in Treasure Island

Location is paramount when shopping for condos and townhomes. Each area within Treasure Island offers a distinct lifestyle and price point.

Gulf Blvd beachfront

Gulf Blvd beachfront is the premier destination for condo and townhome buyers in Treasure Island. This area offers walkability, dining, entertainment, and in many cases water views. Condos here range from $493,000 to $1,334,000 depending on the building, floor, view, and finishes. High-rise buildings offer panoramic views and full-service amenities including concierge, valet parking, rooftop pools, and fitness centers. Mid-rise and boutique buildings provide a more intimate setting with lower HOA fees while still benefiting from the prime location.

Sunset Beach

Sunset Beach provides excellent condo and townhome options for buyers seeking a balance of convenience and value. This area features a mix of updated older buildings and newer construction, with prices ranging from $290,000 to $812,000. Many units offer generous floor plans, assigned parking, community pools, and well-maintained grounds. The area's central location provides easy access to shopping, dining, and major transportation routes throughout Pinellas County.

Paradise Island

Condos and townhomes in the Paradise Island area cater to buyers who appreciate a quieter residential setting while still enjoying community amenities. This area features a variety of options from affordable two-bedroom condos starting around $290,000 to spacious townhomes priced up to $812,000. Many properties here offer attached garages, private patios or balconies, and updated interiors. The area is popular with both full-time residents and snowbirds who appreciate the low-maintenance lifestyle.

Isle of Palms

Isle of Palms rounds out the top condo and townhome areas in Treasure Island. Buyers here find a variety of options at competitive prices, from one-bedroom starter condos to three-bedroom townhomes with all the space of a small single-family home. Prices typically range from $290,000 to $493,000. The area offers good access to parks, grocery stores, and local restaurants, making it a practical choice for everyday living.

Condo and Townhome Pricing in Treasure Island

The following table provides an overview of pricing and typical HOA fees across different categories of condos and townhomes in Treasure Island.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOATypical Features
Entry-Level Condo$290,000 to $493,000$2,900 to $5,2201-2 bedrooms, community pool, assigned parking
Mid-Range Condo/Townhome$493,000 to $812,000$5,220 to $8,7002-3 bedrooms, updated finishes, garage, fitness center
Luxury Condo$812,000 to $1,334,000+$8,700+Premium views, concierge, valet, rooftop amenities, high-end finishes

Condo vs. Townhome: Which Is Right for You?

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they offer fundamentally different living experiences. Understanding these differences helps you make a better decision for your specific needs and lifestyle.

FeatureCondoTownhome
OwnershipYou own the interior; association owns exterior and common areasYou own the structure and land beneath it in most cases
MaintenanceHOA covers exterior, roof, landscaping, and often insuranceYou are responsible for more exterior maintenance in many communities
PrivacyShared walls on multiple sides, hallway access commonShared walls on one or two sides, private entrance
Outdoor SpaceBalcony or pation, sometimes screened lanaiPrivate yard or pation, sometimes a small fenced yard
ParkingAssigned spaces or garage, sometimes valet in high-risesAttached or detached garage is standard
HOA FeesGenerally higher due to more covered servicesGenerally lower but with more owner responsibility

In Treasure Island, condos are ideal for buyers who want a lock-and-leave lifestyle with minimal maintenance, while townhomes appeal to those who want more space, a private entrance, and a home that feels more like a single-family residence. Both options provide community amenities and shared maintenance of common areas.

What Condo and Townhome Buyers Should Know in Treasure Island

Purchasing a condo or townhome involves specific considerations that differ from buying a single-family home. Here are the key factors to evaluate:

  • Review the HOA Documents: Request and thoroughly review the declaration of condominium (or covenants for townhomes), bylaws, rules and regulations, recent meeting minutes, and financial statements. These documents reveal the community's financial health, any pending litigation, special assessments, and the rules you will be expected to follow.
  • Understand Insurance Requirements: Condo insurance (HO-6 policy) covers your personal belongings, interior improvements, and liability within your unit. The association's master policy covers the building structure and common areas. Verify exactly where the association's coverage ends and yours begins, often referred to as "walls-in" versus "walls-out" coverage.
  • Check the Reserve Fund: A well-funded reserve is critical for condos and townhomes. Florida's updated reserve requirements (following the Surfside tragedy) now mandate structural inspections and fully funded reserves for buildings three stories or higher and 30+ years old. Ask for the most recent reserve study and ensure the community is on track to meet these requirements.
  • Assess Rental and Lease Restrictions: If you plan to rent the unit at any point, verify the community's rental policies. Some Treasure Island condo communities limit rentals to once per year with a 12-month minimum lease, while others are more flexible. Short-term rental restrictions are increasingly common.
  • Evaluate the Location Within the Complex: Not all units in a building are equal. Corner units offer more windows and natural light, upper floors provide better views and less foot traffic noise, and units away from elevators and trash chutes tend to be quieter. These factors can also impact resale value.

Financing a Condo or Townhome in Treasure Island

Financing a condo purchase comes with unique requirements that buyers should understand early in the process. Not all lenders treat condos the same way they treat single-family homes, and the community's financial health and legal status can directly impact your loan approval.

Conventional loans through Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac have specific requirements for condo communities, including owner-occupancy ratios, reserve fund adequacy, and insurance coverage. FHA loans require the community to be on the FHA-approved condo list, which not all Treasure Island communities maintain. VA loans have their own approval process that can take additional time.

Townhomes generally face fewer financing restrictions because they are often classified as single-family attached homes rather than condominiums. However, if the townhome is part of a condo association, the same condo financing rules may apply. Work with a lender experienced in Pinellas County condo and townhome transactions to navigate these requirements smoothly.

Cash purchases are common in the Treasure Island condo market, particularly among snowbird buyers and investors. If you are competing against cash offers, having a pre-approval letter and demonstrating financial readiness can help level the playing field.

The Condo and Townhome Lifestyle in Treasure Island

Living in a condo or townhome in Treasure Island offers a distinctive lifestyle that appeals to a variety of buyers. The reduced maintenance allows more time for enjoying what Treasure Island has to offer: Gulf beaches, waterfront parks, dining, cultural events, and outdoor recreation. Many condo communities feature resort-style pools, fitness centers, social rooms, and grilling areas that create a vacation-like atmosphere without leaving home.

For seasonal residents, the lock-and-leave convenience of condo living is particularly valuable. When you head north for the summer, your unit is secure, your landscaping is maintained, and your community amenities are ready when you return. Many Treasure Island condo communities have strong seasonal populations that create vibrant social calendars from November through April.

Full-time residents benefit from the sense of community that condo and townhome living provides. Shared amenities create natural opportunities for socializing, and the proximity of neighbors means you always have someone nearby. Whether you are a young professional seeking a low-maintenance first home, a couple downsizing from a larger property, or a retiree looking for waterfront living, the condo and townhome market in Treasure Island has options to fit your lifestyle.

Why Treasure Island for Condos and Townhomes

Treasure Island offers condo and townhome buyers a compelling combination of location, value, and lifestyle. The city is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast, with a population of 7K that supports a diverse economy and vibrant community life. The median home price of $580K provides context for the condo and townhome market, where entry points are often significantly below the single-family median.

The variety of condo and townhome options in Treasure Island is impressive. From affordable one-bedroom condos perfect for first-time buyers to luxury waterfront units with panoramic views, the market accommodates virtually every budget and preference. New construction continues to add modern inventory, while established communities offer proven value and stable associations.

Frequently Asked Questions About Treasure Island Condos and Townhomes

What is the average HOA fee for condos in Treasure Island?

HOA fees for condos in Treasure Island typically range from $2,900 to $8,700 per month, depending on the building's age, amenities, and services covered. Higher fees usually reflect more comprehensive coverage including building insurance, reserves, water, sewer, cable, and sometimes even electricity. Always evaluate what the fee covers rather than focusing solely on the dollar amount.

Are condos in Treasure Island a good investment?

Condos in well-managed buildings in desirable Treasure Island locations have shown steady appreciation over time. Key factors for investment potential include the building's financial health, location quality, rental flexibility, and physical condition. Waterfront and downtown condos tend to appreciate most consistently. As with any investment, thorough due diligence on the specific building and association is essential.

Can I get an FHA loan for a condo in Treasure Island?

FHA loans are available for condos in communities that appear on the FHA-approved condo list. Not all Treasure Island condo communities maintain this approval, as it requires the association to submit documentation and meet specific financial and operational standards. Check the HUD condo lookup tool or work with an FHA-experienced lender to verify whether your target community qualifies.

What is the difference between a condo fee and a townhome HOA fee?

Condo fees typically cover a broader range of services including building insurance, exterior maintenance, roof repairs, and sometimes utilities. Townhome HOA fees generally cover common area maintenance, landscaping of shared spaces, and community amenities, but the homeowner is responsible for more of the individual property maintenance. As a result, townhome HOA fees tend to be lower, but out-of-pocket maintenance costs may be higher.

How do Florida's new condo laws affect buyers in Treasure Island?

Florida's updated condominium safety laws, enacted after the Surfside building collapse, require milestone structural inspections for buildings three stories or higher that are 30 years old (or 25 years old if within three miles of the coast). Communities must also maintain fully funded reserves for structural components. These requirements are designed to protect buyers and residents by ensuring buildings are properly maintained. When evaluating a condo in Treasure Island, ask for the most recent inspection report and reserve study to confirm the building is compliant.

title: Treasure Island Gated Communities
content:
Quick Answer

Gated community homes in Treasure Island range from $493K to over $1,450K, with HOA fees covering security, amenities, and community maintenance. These private communities offer controlled access, maintained grounds, and resort-style living.

Why Gated Communities Appeal to Treasure Island Home Buyers

Gated communities in Treasure Island offer a lifestyle that goes far beyond a security gate. These neighborhoods provide controlled access, professionally maintained common areas, and a curated living experience that appeals to families, retirees, and professionals alike. In a market where Treasure Island is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast, the appeal of a gated community is clear: you get privacy, safety, and community in one package.

With a population of 7K and a median home price of $580K, Treasure Island offers gated community options at various price points. Whether you want a guard-gated entrance with 24/7 staffing or a well-maintained community with electronic gate access, there are options to fit different budgets and lifestyles. Gated homes in Treasure Island typically sell at a premium of 15 to 30 percent above comparable non-gated properties due to the added amenities, privacy, and perceived safety.

Top Gated Communities in Treasure Island

Several gated communities have established themselves as premier addresses in Treasure Island. Here are the standout options:

Isle of Palms

Isle of Palms is one of the most recognized gated communities in Treasure Island. Residents enjoy controlled access, manicured landscapes, and a strong homeowners association that maintains property standards throughout the community. Homes in Isle of Palms range from $667,000 to $1,450,000 depending on size, lot, and updates. The community features well-maintained roads, streetlights, and common areas that contribute to a polished, well-kept atmosphere. Many homes here include pools, updated owners suites, and open floor plans designed for Florida living.

Paradise Island

Paradise Island offers another excellent gated option in the Treasure Island area. Known for its community amenities and well-planned layout, Paradise Island attracts buyers who value convenience and quality. Homes typically range from $493,000 to $986,000, with a variety of floor plans from three-bedroom single-story homes to larger four and five-bedroom properties. The community maintains a strong sense of neighborhood with organized events, walking trails, and shared recreational facilities.

Isle of Palms

Isle of Palms rounds out the top gated community options near Treasure Island. This community is particularly popular among buyers seeking a balance of privacy and access to the broader Treasure Island area. Homes range from $667,000 to $1,450,000 and often feature upgraded finishes, spacious layouts, and outdoor living areas. The HOA maintains high standards for landscaping and exterior maintenance, which helps protect property values across the community.

Pricing and HOA Fees for Treasure Island Gated Communities

Understanding the full cost of gated community living means looking beyond the purchase price. HOA fees in Treasure Island gated communities cover a range of services including gate maintenance, security, landscaping, and amenity upkeep.

Community TypePrice RangeMonthly HOAAmenities Included
Standard Gated$493,000 to $667,000$2,900 to $4,640Gate access, landscaping, basic maintenance
Amenity-Rich Gated$667,000 to $986,000$4,640 to $6,960Pool, clubhouse, fitness center, walking trails
Luxury Guard-Gated$986,000 to $1,450,000+$6,960+24/7 guard, golf, tennis, spa, concierge services

Security Features in Treasure Island Gated Communities

Security is often the primary motivation for choosing a gated community, and Treasure Island communities offer varying levels of access control and monitoring. Understanding these differences helps you choose the right level of security for your needs.

  • Electronic Gate Access: The most common type, using key cards, key fobs, or coded entry. Visitors are granted access via a call box or visitor code. This system provides a solid barrier to casual traffic while remaining convenient for residents. Most gated communities in Treasure Island at the entry and mid-level price points use this approach.
  • Guard-Gated Entry: Premium communities feature a staffed guardhouse at the entrance, providing real-time verification of every visitor. Guards log all guests and delivery vehicles. This level of security is found in higher-end communities and adds significant peace of mind, especially for residents who travel frequently.
  • Camera and Surveillance Systems: Many communities supplement gate access with perimeter cameras, license plate recognition technology, and motion-activated lighting. These systems record activity around the clock and provide an additional layer of deterrence.
  • Perimeter Fencing and Walls: Gated communities in Treasure Island typically feature continuous perimeter fencing, ranging from decorative iron fences to solid masonry walls. The height and material of the perimeter barrier varies by community and contributes to both security and aesthetic appeal.
  • Community Patrol: Some larger communities employ roving security patrols, particularly during evening and overnight hours. These patrols check common areas, report suspicious activity, and provide a visible security presence that deters unauthorized access.

Community Amenities in Treasure Island Gated Neighborhoods

Beyond security, gated communities in Treasure Island differentiate themselves through the amenities they offer residents. The quality and variety of these amenities directly impact HOA fees but also enhance daily living and property values.

Typical amenities include community pools with cabanas, fitness centers, tennis and pickleball courts, walking and biking trails, playgrounds, dog parks, and clubhouses available for private events. Higher-end communities may offer golf courses, marina access, spa facilities, and dedicated social coordinators who organize resident events throughout the year.

When evaluating a gated community, consider which amenities you will actually use regularly. A community with a golf course commands higher HOA fees, and if you do not golf, that premium may not make sense for your lifestyle. Conversely, a community with a well-maintained pool, walking trails, and a clubhouse may offer the perfect balance of amenities at a more moderate monthly cost.

What to Ask Before Buying in a Treasure Island Gated Community

Purchasing in a gated community involves additional due diligence beyond a standard home purchase. Here are the essential questions every buyer should ask:

  1. What does the HOA fee cover? Get a detailed breakdown of what is included in the monthly or quarterly assessment. Some HOAs cover exterior maintenance, roof insurance, and cable TV, while others only cover gate access and common area landscaping. Understanding this prevents surprises after closing.
  2. Are there special assessments pending? Review the HOA's financial statements and reserve fund. A well-funded reserve means the community can handle major repairs (like gate replacement or road repaving) without levying special assessments on homeowners.
  3. What are the rental restrictions? Many gated communities limit rental activity to preserve the owner-occupied character. If you plan to rent the property in the future, verify the community's rental policies, including minimum lease terms and approval processes.
  4. What are the architectural guidelines? Gated communities typically enforce standards for exterior modifications, paint colors, landscaping, and even holiday decorations. Review the covenants, conditions, and restrictions (CC&Rs) before making an offer to ensure you can live comfortably within the rules.
  5. How is the HOA managed? Ask whether the HOA is self-managed by residents or professionally managed by a management company. Professional management generally provides more consistent enforcement and maintenance, but comes at a higher cost. Review recent meeting minutes to gauge the board's priorities and any ongoing disputes.
  6. What is the community's insurance master policy? Some gated communities carry a master insurance policy that covers building exteriors and common areas. Understanding what is covered under the master policy versus what you need to insure individually helps you budget accurately.

Why Treasure Island Is Ideal for Gated Community Living

Treasure Island offers a combination of factors that make it an excellent location for gated community living. The city is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast, with a strong sense of community and convenient access to Gulf beaches, Tampa, and regional amenities. The population of 7K supports a robust local economy with diverse dining, shopping, and entertainment options.

For buyers considering gated communities in Treasure Island, the market offers options at multiple price points. From starter homes in well-maintained communities to luxury estates in guard-gated enclaves, there is a gated community in Treasure Island to match virtually every buyer profile. Florida's lack of state income tax and the area's favorable insurance rates compared to South Florida make Treasure Island an even more attractive destination for buyers relocating from other states.

Ready to explore gated communities in Treasure Island? Contact Barrett Henry for a personalized consultation. If you are also selling a home, explore the home selling resources to coordinate your move.

Frequently Asked Questions About Treasure Island Gated Communities

How much are HOA fees in Treasure Island gated communities?

HOA fees in Treasure Island gated communities range from $2,900 to $6,960 or more per month, depending on the amenities and services provided. Communities with golf courses, guard-gated entries, and resort-style pools typically have higher fees. Always review the HOA budget and reserve fund before purchasing.

Are gated community homes a good investment in Treasure Island?

Yes, gated community homes in Treasure Island have historically maintained strong property values. The combination of controlled access, maintained common areas, and community standards helps protect property values even during market fluctuations. Gated homes also tend to sell faster than comparable non-gated properties due to consistent buyer demand.

Can I rent out my home in a Treasure Island gated community?

Rental policies vary significantly between communities. Some gated neighborhoods in Treasure Island allow rentals with minimum lease terms of six months to one year, while others restrict rentals entirely or limit the number of times a property can be rented. Always review the community's CC&Rs and consult with the HOA before purchasing if rental income is part of your plan.

What is the difference between a gated community and a guard-gated community?

A standard gated community uses electronic access (key cards, codes, or remotes) to control entry, while a guard-gated community has a staffed guardhouse that verifies every visitor. Guard-gated communities offer a higher level of security but typically have higher HOA fees. Both types are available in Treasure Island.

Do gated communities in Treasure Island allow pets?

Most gated communities in Treasure Island allow pets, though breed restrictions, size limits, and leash requirements are common. Some communities designate dog parks or pet-friendly areas within the grounds. Always verify the specific pet policy with the HOA, as some communities limit the number of pets per household or require registration.

title: Treasure Island Homes with Pool
content:
Quick Answer

Treasure Island pool homes start in the mid-$435Ks and range above $1,276K+ for luxury properties with resort-style outdoor spaces. With over 300 days of sunshine each year, a pool is one of the most popular features for buyers in Treasure Island.

Why Pool Homes Are in High Demand in Treasure Island

Treasure Island is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast. With a population of 7K and a median home price around $580K, the city offers a compelling blend of lifestyle and value. Pool homes here are especially popular because Florida's warm subtropical climate allows for year-round outdoor living. Whether you are a family looking for weekend fun, a retiree wanting a private oasis, or a buyer seeking strong resale value, a pool home in Treasure Island is an excellent investment.

Homes with pools in Treasure Island tend to command a premium of 10 to 20 percent compared to similar homes without pools. Buyers consistently rank a private pool as one of their top must-have features, and in a market like Treasure Island, where sunshine is abundant and outdoor entertaining is a way of life, that demand only grows. The neighborhood you choose, the pool type you prefer, and your budget all play important roles in finding the right property.

Popular Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Treasure Island

Several neighborhoods in Treasure Island stand out for their concentration of pool homes and desirable living conditions. Here are the top areas to explore:

Sunset Beach

Sunset Beach is one of the most sought-after neighborhoods in Treasure Island for pool homes. Properties here often feature spacious lots with mature landscaping, screened-in pool enclosures, and updated outdoor kitchens. Many homes back up to canals or offer water views, making a pool the perfect complement to the setting. Prices in Sunset Beach typically range from $435,000 to $870,000 depending on size and updates.

Paradise Island

Paradise Island offers a blend of established charm and modern upgrades. Pool homes in this neighborhood often sit on generous lots with room for expanded patios, fire pits, and tropical landscaping. The area is well-connected to shopping, dining, and major roadways, making it convenient for commuters. Expect pool homes in Paradise Island to start around $435,000 and reach $870,000 or more for renovated properties.

Gulf Boulevard

Gulf Boulevard is known for its family-friendly atmosphere and well-maintained homes. Pool properties here tend to feature newer construction or recently updated interiors with open floor plans that flow seamlessly to a screened lanai and pool area. The neighborhood benefits from proximity to parks, schools, and community amenities. Homes with pools in Gulf Boulevard are typically priced between $580,000 and $1,276,000.

Isle of Palms

Isle of Palms rounds out the top areas for pool home buyers. This neighborhood features a mix of ranch-style and two-story homes, many with updated pools and outdoor living spaces. The tree-lined streets and quiet cul-de-sacs make it a favorite among families. Pool homes in Isle of Palms are generally priced between $435,000 and $870,000.

Pool Home Price Ranges in Treasure Island

Understanding the price landscape helps you set realistic expectations and identify the best opportunities in the Treasure Island pool home market.

CategoryPrice RangeWhat to Expect
Entry-Level Pool Homes$435,000 to $580,000Smaller pools, older construction, standard screened enclosures
Mid-Range Pool Homes$580,000 to $870,000Updated kitchens, heated pools, expanded lanais, 3-4 bedrooms
Luxury Pool Homes$870,000 to $1,276,000+Resort-style pools, outdoor kitchens, saltwater systems, water views

Types of Pools You Will Find in Treasure Island

Not all pools are created equal, and the type of pool a home features can significantly impact maintenance costs, enjoyment, and resale value. Here are the most common pool types in Treasure Island:

  • Screened Pools: The most common type in Florida, screened pools feature an aluminum and mesh enclosure that keeps out insects, debris, and provides UV protection. Nearly every pool home in Treasure Island has some form of screen enclosure, known locally as a "cage." Rescreening typically costs $3,000 to $8,000 depending on size.
  • Saltwater Pools: Growing in popularity, saltwater systems use a chlorine generator that creates a gentler, less chemically harsh swimming experience. Many buyers in Treasure Island specifically seek saltwater pools for their lower ongoing chemical costs and softer feel. Conversion from traditional chlorine runs $1,500 to $3,500.
  • Heated Pools: While Florida is warm most of the year, winter mornings can cool pool water into the 60s. Electric heat pumps are the most common heating option in Treasure Island and extend comfortable swimming from roughly 8 months to a full 12 months. A quality heat pump costs $3,000 to $6,000 installed.
  • Spa and Pool Combos: Many mid-range and luxury pool homes include an attached spa or hot tub. These combined systems offer versatility and are especially popular among buyers who entertain frequently. Expect a premium of $10,000 to $20,000 for homes with spa combos versus standard pools.
  • Infinity and Custom Pools: Found primarily in luxury properties priced above $1,276,000, infinity-edge and custom-designed pools with waterfalls, grottos, or swim-up bars represent the top tier of outdoor living in Treasure Island. These homes are rare and tend to sell quickly.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist for Treasure Island

Purchasing a pool home involves additional considerations beyond a standard home purchase. Use this checklist to ensure you are making a well-informed decision:

  1. Pool Inspection: Always hire a certified pool inspector in addition to your general home inspector. They will check the pump, filter, heater, plumbing lines, pool surface, and screen enclosure. Budget $150 to $300 for a standalone pool inspection.
  2. Age of Equipment: Ask about the age of the pool pump, filter, heater, and salt cell if applicable. Most pool pumps last 8 to 12 years. Replacing a pump and motor runs $800 to $2,000 depending on the model.
  3. Resurfacing Timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or tile) typically last 10 to 15 years before needing resurfacing. A full resurface costs $5,000 to $15,000 depending on material and pool size. Ask when the pool was last resurfaced.
  4. Insurance Considerations: Pools can increase your homeowner's insurance premium by $50 to $150 per year. A screened enclosure can help mitigate liability concerns. Discuss pool coverage with your insurance agent before closing.
  5. Monthly Maintenance Costs: Budget $100 to $250 per month for professional pool maintenance if you prefer not to handle it yourself. This includes chemical balancing, cleaning, and equipment checks. Many Treasure Island homeowners find a pool service essential for keeping their pool swim-ready year-round.
  6. Fence and Safety Requirements: Florida law requires a barrier around residential pools. A screened enclosure satisfies this requirement in most cases, but verify with Pinellas County building codes if the screen is damaged or the pool is unenclosed.

Outdoor Living and Entertainment in Treasure Island

A pool home in Treasure Island is more than just a house with a pool. It represents an entire outdoor lifestyle. The best pool properties feature thoughtfully designed outdoor living spaces that extend usable square footage and create a resort-like atmosphere right at home.

Look for homes with covered lanais that provide shade during the hottest months, outdoor kitchens equipped with grills and bar seating, and tropical landscaping that creates privacy and ambiance. Many pool homes in Sunset Beach and Paradise Island feature upgraded pavers around the pool deck, LED pool lighting for evening swims, and automated pool controls that let you manage temperature and cleaning from your phone.

The outdoor living trend continues to grow in Treasure Island, with buyers increasingly prioritizing usable outdoor space. Homes with well-designed pool areas and lanais consistently sell faster and at higher prices than comparable homes without these features. If you are planning to sell in the future, investing in your outdoor space is one of the best returns you can get in the Treasure Island market.

Why Treasure Island Is a Great Place to Own a Pool Home

Treasure Island stands out among Pinellas County communities for several reasons that make pool home ownership especially rewarding. The city offers a strong sense of community, convenient access to Gulf beaches, quality schools, and a diverse dining and entertainment scene. With a population of 7K, Treasure Island strikes the right balance between having enough amenities for daily convenience and maintaining the neighborhood character that residents love.

The real estate market in Treasure Island has shown steady appreciation over the past decade, with pool homes leading the way in value retention. Buyers from across the country are drawn to the combination of affordable pricing (compared to South Florida), no state income tax, and the ability to enjoy outdoor living 12 months a year. Whether you are relocating from the Northeast, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for a vacation property, Treasure Island delivers outstanding value.

For personalized guidance on finding the perfect pool home, contact Barrett Henry for a consultation. You can also explore the home selling resources if you need to sell before buying.

Frequently Asked Questions About Treasure Island Pool Homes

How much does a pool home cost in Treasure Island?

Pool homes in Treasure Island generally range from $435,000 for entry-level properties up to $1,276,000 or more for luxury homes with resort-style pools. The median price for a pool home typically runs 10 to 20 percent above the overall market median of $580K. Pricing depends on neighborhood, lot size, pool condition, and overall home features.

Are pool homes a good investment in Treasure Island?

Yes. Pool homes in Treasure Island consistently hold their value well and tend to appreciate at or above the overall market rate. A well-maintained pool adds measurable value to a property in Florida, where outdoor living is a key selling point. Buyers relocating from colder climates specifically seek pool homes, which supports demand and pricing stability year-round.

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Treasure Island?

Monthly pool maintenance in Treasure Island typically costs $100 to $250 if you hire a professional service. This covers chemical balancing, skimming, filter cleaning, and equipment monitoring. DIY maintenance can reduce costs to $50 to $80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual expenses for electricity to run the pump average $600 to $1,200 depending on pump efficiency.

What should I look for during a pool inspection?

A thorough pool inspection should cover the pool surface condition (cracks, staining, delamination), pump and filter function, heater operation, plumbing integrity, screen enclosure condition, and deck or paver levelness. The inspector should also test water chemistry and check for any code violations. Always schedule a pool-specific inspection in addition to the standard home inspection.

Do I need a separate pool fence if the pool has a screen enclosure?

In most cases, a screened pool enclosure satisfies Florida's pool barrier requirements as long as the enclosure is in good condition with a self-closing and self-latching door. However, if the screen is torn or the door mechanism is not functioning, additional safety measures may be required. Always verify current Pinellas County requirements before closing on a pool home purchase.

Why Buy New Construction in Treasure Island?

Buying new construction in Treasure Island means moving into a home designed with today's lifestyle in mind. Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Treasure Island also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Treasure Island area, including Custom builders. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Treasure Island typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Treasure Island
Entry-Level / Starter$500K-$700K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s
Premium / Luxury$800K+

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Treasure Island?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

The neighborhood sees consistent turnover, meaning new opportunities arise regularly for attentive buyers.

Paradise Island

The neighborhood features well-maintained homes, good access to parks and shopping, and a strong sense of community. Prices in Paradise Island typically range from $377,000 to $580,000, making it accessible to a broad range of buyers. First-time buyers in particular find Paradise Island an attractive starting point in the Treasure Island market.

Treasure Bay and Isle of Palms

These areas offer distinct advantages: Treasure Bay features mature trees, established character, and steady demand, while Isle of Palms attracts buyers with its growth trajectory and improving amenities. Together, they round out the neighborhoods where the most compelling new listings in Treasure Island tend to appear.   • Days on Market: Well-priced new listings in desirable Treasure Island neighborhoods typically go under contract within 10 to 21 days. Overpriced listings or those in less desirable locations may sit longer. Monitoring days on market helps you identify properties where sellers may be open to negotiation.
  • Inventory Levels: The Pinellas County market has seen fluctuating inventory levels. Low inventory creates competition and can drive prices up, while increasing inventory gives buyers more options and negotiating leverage. Barrett Henry tracks these trends weekly to provide clients with current market intelligence.
  • Seasonal Patterns: The Treasure Island market follows seasonal patterns, with the highest activity typically from January through April when snowbird buyers are active. Summer and fall tend to see slightly less competition, which can benefit buyers willing to search during the off-peak season.
  • Price Per Square Foot: Evaluating properties on a price-per-square-foot basis helps compare new listings objectively. In Treasure Island, price per square foot varies significantly by neighborhood, condition, and features. Your agent can provide neighborhood-specific metrics to help you identify fair pricing.

The most successful buyers in competitive markets are those who see properties first. In Treasure Island, there are several ways to gain an advantage over other buyers when it comes to new listing access:

Coming Soon Listings: Some sellers opt for a "coming soon" period before their home is officially active on the MLS. During this window, the property is marketed privately, giving connected buyers a chance to view and make offers before the broader market sees the listing. Pocket Listings: Occasionally, sellers prefer to market their property off-MLS through their agent's network. These pocket listings never appear on public portals but are shared among trusted agents. Automated MLS Alerts: Once you define your search criteria, automated alerts deliver new listings to your inbox or phone within minutes of going live on the MLS. Agent Network Intelligence: Real estate agents talk. They share information about upcoming listings, seller motivations, and market conditions. An agent who is well-connected in the Treasure Island market can provide intelligence that no algorithm or portal can match. This human network advantage is one of the most valuable tools a buyer can have.

Treasure Island continues to be one of the most dynamic real estate markets in Pinellas County. The city is a quiet barrier island with wide sandy beaches, stunning sunsets, and a relaxed community atmosphere along the Gulf coast, and its combination of lifestyle, location, and value draws buyers from across the country. With a population of 7K and strong community infrastructure, Treasure Island supports steady demand for housing across all price points.

Whether you are a first-time buyer, a growing family upgrading to a larger home, a retiree seeking the Florida lifestyle, or an investor adding to your portfolio, Treasure Island offers opportunities worth pursuing. How often do new listings appear in Treasure Island?

New listings in Treasure Island appear throughout the week, with the highest volume typically posted on Thursdays and Fridays as sellers prepare for weekend showings. During peak season (January through April), new listing volume increases significantly. Working with an agent who monitors the MLS daily ensures you see every new opportunity as it becomes available.

How long do new listings stay on the market in Treasure Island?

Well-priced listings in desirable Treasure Island neighborhoods often go under contract within 10 to 21 days. Homes priced below the area median or in high-demand neighborhoods may receive offers within the first weekend. Properties that remain on the market beyond 30 days may be overpriced or have condition issues, and sellers may be more open to negotiation at that point.

Should I make an offer the same day I see a new listing?

In a competitive market, same-day or next-day offers are common for properties that meet your criteria and are priced correctly. Having your pre-approval, offer terms, and strategy prepared in advance allows you to move quickly without feeling rushed. Your agent will advise you on the urgency level based on current market conditions and the specific property's expected demand.

Yes, through coming soon listings and pocket listings, some properties are available for showing before they appear on public portals. If a property goes under contract before you can view it, do not lose hope. Roughly 10 to 15 percent of contracts fall through due to inspection issues, financing problems, or buyer changes of mind. Your agent can position you as a backup offer, which means you would have the next opportunity if the initial contract fails. title: Treasure Island Waterfront Homes
content:
Quick Answer

Waterfront homes in Treasure Island include properties on Gulf of Mexico, Boca Ciega Bay, Intracoastal Waterway. Pricing varies widely based on water type, lot size, and direct access. Flood insurance and seawall condition are key considerations.

Browse Treasure Island Waterfront Homes Homes for Sale

Updated daily from the MLS. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to schedule a showing.

Types of Waterfront in Treasure Island

Treasure Island offers several types of waterfront living, each with its own character, pricing, and lifestyle:

  • Gulf of Mexico, Boca Ciega Bay, Intracoastal Waterway - the primary waterfront options in Treasure Island range from open-water properties with panoramic views to canal-front homes with private dock access and lake-front properties with peaceful settings.

The type of waterfront determines not just the lifestyle but also insurance costs, maintenance requirements, and resale value. Open-water properties with direct bay or Gulf access typically command the highest premiums.

Popular Waterfront Areas

The most sought-after waterfront neighborhoods in Treasure Island include areas within Sunset Beach, Paradise Island, Treasure Island proper. These neighborhoods offer a mix of water types, lot sizes, and price points.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Treasure Island require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Treasure Island?

Flood insurance costs in Treasure Island vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Treasure Island?

Most waterfront properties in Treasure Island allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Treasure Island generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.
