Why Westchase is One of Northwest Tampa's Most Sought-After Master-Planned Communities

Westchase is the kind of community that people specifically move to Tampa for. It is not a coincidence that families who start their home search in northwest Hillsborough County often end up at Westchase after exploring their options. The combination of a well-executed master plan, two resort-style swim and tennis centers, an 18-hole golf course, West Park Village Town Center, A-rated elementary school, and a community culture built around connection and programming is difficult to replicate at any price point in the Tampa metro.

Schedule a Free ConsultationSearch Westchase Homes

Westchase is a large community, approximately 3,478 homes across more than 30 distinct neighborhoods, with a total population near 25,000. Despite its size, it manages to feel organized and cohesive, largely because of the significant preserved land integrated throughout and the two swim and tennis centers that anchor the community's social life. The Westchase Community Association (WCA) is an active governing body that coordinates programming ranging from USTA tennis leagues and youth swim teams to holiday events and after-school care.

What makes Westchase feel different from other master-planned communities in the Tampa Bay area is the quality of execution that has held up over decades. Homes were built from the 1990s through the early 2000s, giving the community a mature character that newer developments cannot match. The tree canopy is established, the golf course is in a beautiful natural setting winding through wetlands, and the West Park Village Town Center has developed into a genuine neighborhood commercial hub with restaurants, services, and daily conveniences accessible by foot or bicycle for many residents.

Barrett Henry has helped buyers navigate the Westchase market across multiple market cycles and understands which neighborhoods within the community offer the best value, how the HOA structure works, and what to look for when evaluating Westchase homes that have been on the market for varying lengths of time.

Where is Westchase? Location, Geography, and Getting Around

Westchase is located in northwest Hillsborough County, bordered roughly by Linebaugh Avenue to the north, the Veterans Expressway to the east, Countryway Boulevard to the south, and Sheldon Road to the west. The community's central access point from the Veterans Expressway puts most of Tampa Bay within practical reach without the congestion of more centrally located neighborhoods.

Tampa International Airport is approximately 15 to 20 minutes from Westchase via the Veterans Expressway, one of the most convenient airport commutes in the Tampa Bay area. International Plaza and Bay Street is about 20 minutes south on the Veterans Expressway. Downtown Tampa is 20 to 30 minutes depending on time of day and routing. The University of South Florida is 25 to 30 minutes east via Linebaugh or Fletcher Avenue. St. Petersburg and Clearwater are accessible in 40 to 50 minutes via the Veterans Expressway connecting to the Bayside Bridge or Howard Frankland Bridge.

The Veterans Expressway is Westchase's main commuting artery and it works well for reaching Tampa's Westshore business district (15-20 minutes south), the airport (15-20 minutes), and downtown (20-30 minutes). The community is also adjacent to Citrus Park and the International Mall corridor, giving residents easy access to retail and dining without being in the middle of commercial development. This balance of accessibility without congestion is one of Westchase's most valued qualities.

Westchase Real Estate Market Overview

Westchase carries a premium over the broader northwest Tampa market, reflecting the community's quality, schools, and amenity infrastructure. As of early 2026, the median home price in Westchase is in the range of $475,000 to $525,000. Single-family homes range from the high $400,000s for smaller ranch-style homes to over $1 million for large lakefront properties in the community's most desirable sections. Townhomes and condos within the Westchase area start around $350,000, providing an accessible entry point into this highly sought community.

In the $500,000 to $700,000 range, Westchase buyers find well-maintained 3 to 5 bedroom homes with updated kitchens and baths, two-car garages, and access to the community's amenity centers. Above $700,000, the Westchase market offers more premium homes in neighborhoods close to the golf course or on pond and conservation views, with higher-end finishes and more square footage. Lakefront properties in Westchase are the most coveted, with limited supply and prices that regularly exceed $800,000 to $1.2 million.

Westchase is a mature, largely built-out community. The limited inventory and consistent demand from buyers who specifically seek this community keep the market competitive. Well-priced homes in Westchase tend to move faster than the broader Tampa market average. Compared to newer master-planned communities further east or south, Westchase's established character and northwest Tampa location command a premium that buyers consistently find justified by the lifestyle and school quality.

Westchase Neighborhoods

Westchase is organized into more than 30 distinct neighborhoods, each with its own character, price range, and proximity to community amenities. Some of the established neighborhoods include:

Glencliff

Glencliff is one of Westchase's established neighborhoods, offering single-family homes with the community's mature character. Homes in Glencliff are well-maintained with the established landscaping that comes from 23+ years of growth within the master plan.

The Bridges and Stonebridge

These neighborhoods within Westchase offer a range of floor plans and positions within the community, with some homes backing to conservation areas or ponds that create private, green rear views that enhance the feel of the entire community.

Harbor Links

Harbor Links is a neighborhood in the Westchase community with proximity to the golf course, making it attractive to golf enthusiasts who want to walk or bike to the club. The golf course setting creates scenic views and a resort feel for surrounding properties.

West Park Village

West Park Village is Westchase's Town Center neighborhood, built around a walkable commercial core with shops, restaurants, professional services, daycare, and more accessible on foot. Homes in West Park Village have a distinctive architectural character compared to the broader community, with a village-style streetscape and porches designed for neighborly interaction. The Town Center is the social hub of the community and residents of West Park Village have the most direct access to its restaurants and services.

Westchase Amenities

Westchase's amenity infrastructure is what keeps demand consistently high for this community. The WCA manages two resort-style swim and tennis centers, hundreds of acres of preserved land, parks, playgrounds, picnic pavilions, nature trails, a soccer field, and the community's relationship with the Westchase Golf Club.

Village Swim and Tennis Center

The Village Swim and Tennis Center features two community pools with lap lanes, a shallow play area, a pool slide, a toddler pool, covered shade areas, and restrooms. Four lit hard tennis and pickleball courts host recreational play, USTA league competition, private lessons, clinics, and seasonal programs. Pool hours run 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily. This center serves as a social anchor for the community, particularly during Tampa's long pool season.

Countryway Swim and Tennis Center

The Countryway location mirrors the Village center with two pools, lap lanes, shallow play areas, and toddler pool. It also features four lit hard tennis courts and six permanent pickleball courts. The Countryway center extends pool access hours from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Monday through Sunday. The availability of six pickleball courts at one location is a meaningful draw as the sport's popularity has surged across the Tampa Bay area.

Westchase Golf Club

Westchase Golf Club is a daily-fee public course designed by Lloyd Clifton, measuring 6,699 yards at a par 72. The course winds through natural wetlands and wooden bridges, creating a scenic and ecologically interesting layout that is unusual for a community course. The club serves both Westchase residents and the broader public and adds a visual and recreational dimension to the community that goes beyond what most HOA amenity centers provide. Homes adjacent to the golf course often command a premium for the preserved views and resort feel they provide year-round.

WCA Programming

The Westchase Community Association operates programming for every age group: toddler swim lessons, youth tennis camps, after-school care, adult USTA leagues, senior walking clubs, arts and crafts classes, fitness programming, and seasonal community events. The WCA's depth of programming is one of the reasons Westchase residents cite the community identity as a primary reason for staying. The community is known for its trick-or-treat event, holiday celebrations, and the kind of neighborhood activities that create genuine connection rather than just geographic proximity.

Schools in Westchase

Westchase's school quality is one of its most important draws for family buyers. The feeder pattern runs through three schools with strong academic track records.

Westchase Elementary School is one of the strongest elementary schools in northwest Tampa. Ranked in the top 10% of all Florida elementary schools as of 2024-2025, Westchase Elementary earned an A- on Niche and a 9 out of 10 on GreatSchools. Academic performance is notable: 86% of third graders tested proficient or better in math (vs. 58% for Hillsborough County and 63% for Florida), and 82% tested proficient or better in English Language Arts (vs. 53% county, 57% state). These are genuinely exceptional results that place Westchase Elementary among the elite elementary schools in Hillsborough County.

Davidsen Middle School serves grades 6 through 8 with 942 students. In 2024-2025, 74% of Davidsen students were proficient in Algebra 1 (vs. 59% county and 60% state), and 100% of students testing in Geometry were proficient. Davidsen holds a B rating on Niche, reflecting solid overall performance with particular strength in mathematics. The school also earned a ranking in the top 50% of Florida schools overall.

Alonso High School is the primary feeder high school for Westchase, serving 2,930 students in grades 9 through 12. Alonso holds an A- rating on Niche and is ranked 162nd of Florida's high schools. In 2024-2025, Alonso outperformed both the district and state averages in Algebra 1, Geometry, Biology 1, and US History. Graduation rates have been strong, consistently ranging from 86% to 96% over recent years. Alonso offers a wide range of academic and extracurricular programming appropriate for a large suburban high school.

For families who want private school options, the northwest Tampa area has several faith-based and independent private schools within a reasonable drive. Carrollwood Day School (top-ranked private school in Tampa) is accessible from Westchase in about 15 to 20 minutes.

Things to Do in Westchase

Westchase's two swim and tennis centers, golf course, park system, preserved land network, and West Park Village Town Center create a rich ecosystem of activities within the community itself. But the broader northwest Tampa location adds regional options as well.

Within the community, the swim and tennis facilities host year-round programming. The USTA tennis leagues draw competitive recreational players from across the community and from outside it. The swim team and summer camps keep the pools busy from spring through fall. Westchase Park and Recreation Center, operated by Hillsborough County, adds further programming options adjacent to the community.

The community's hundreds of acres of preserved land include nature trails that wind through oak canopy and Florida wetland landscapes. These trails are genuinely beautiful and well-used by walkers, joggers, and cyclists. Several neighborhood parks and picnic pavilions are distributed throughout the community, giving residents outdoor gathering options close to home.

Nearby Citrus Park Town Center provides retail and dining at a major mall format approximately 10 minutes from Westchase. International Plaza and Bay Street, one of Tampa's premier shopping and dining destinations, is about 20 minutes south via the Veterans Expressway. Westchase's northwest Tampa location also provides reasonably easy access to Clearwater Beach (40-50 minutes via the Veterans Expressway and the Courtney Campbell Causeway).

Best Restaurants and Dining in Westchase

Westchase has developed a genuine dining scene beyond the chain restaurants that often dominate suburban corridors. The West Park Village Town Center concentrates much of the local dining character, with restaurants, cafes, and bars accessible on foot from surrounding neighborhoods.

Local Favorites

Tampa Bay Brewing Company's Westchase location offers 24 rotating craft beer taps featuring IPAs, sours, and Florida-Weisse beers brewed on-site, alongside a menu of pizzas, burgers, and classic staples. The outdoor patio with fire pits and bottomless mimosa brunch service make it a weekend community gathering point. Grand Hacienda brings authentic Mexican cuisine with standout dishes including nachos, birria tacos, and the seafood-forward 7 Mare soup. Rice and Spice offers a dynamic fusion of Laotian, Thai, and Chinese cuisines with innovative house-made sauces and a sushi lineup that makes it a local favorite for a full-service Asian dining experience. The Hungry Greek serves generous portions of authentic Greek food cooked on a wood-burning grill, drawing regulars who appreciate both the food quality and the straightforward approach to Greek cooking.

West Park Village's Town Center also has café options, breakfast spots, and the kind of everyday casual dining that makes a walkable neighborhood commercial center work for daily life. The WCA hosts community events at the Town Center and at the park areas that bring residents together regularly around food and local business.

Commute and Transportation from Westchase

Westchase has one of the strongest commute profiles of any northwest Tampa community. The Veterans Expressway provides efficient access north and south without requiring navigation of local surface road congestion. The airport commute in particular stands out as a competitive advantage for Westchase buyers.

Tampa International Airport: 15 to 20 minutes via Veterans Expressway. Westshore business district: 15 to 20 minutes south. Downtown Tampa: 20 to 30 minutes. MacDill Air Force Base: 30 to 40 minutes via Veterans Expressway and Dale Mabry south. USF: 25 to 30 minutes east. International Mall: 20 minutes south on the Veterans Expressway. St. Petersburg: 40 to 50 minutes west via Veterans Expressway and Courtney Campbell or Howard Frankland Bridge. Clearwater Beach: 40 to 50 minutes west.

Public transit is limited in the Westchase area. Hillsborough Area Regional Transit (HART) does not provide meaningful commuter service to this neighborhood. Westchase residents commute by personal vehicle. The expressway access does make the commuting experience more predictable than surface-road-dependent suburbs.

Cost of Living in Westchase

Westchase's true monthly cost includes the mortgage or rent, property taxes, and HOA fees. There are no CDD fees in Westchase, which is a meaningful advantage over newer Hillsborough County communities where CDD assessments add $1,500 to $3,500 or more per year to the tax bill.

HOA fees in Westchase cover community maintenance, the swim and tennis centers, park maintenance, and WCA programming. Monthly HOA fees in Westchase typically range from approximately $100 to $200 depending on the specific neighborhood section. This fee structure delivers genuine value given the amenity infrastructure it supports. Some individual neighborhoods within Westchase may have additional neighborhood-level HOA fees on top of the community-wide fee. Request full HOA documentation for any property before making an offer. Our HOA rules guide covers what to look for in the disclosure package.

Property taxes in Hillsborough County run approximately 1.0% to 1.5% of assessed value annually. On a $500,000 Westchase home, expect roughly $5,000 to $7,500 per year before the homestead exemption. Florida's homestead exemption reduces assessed value by $50,000 for primary residence owners, with increases capped at 3% annually under Save Our Homes. Standard homeowners insurance for Westchase properties reflects the broader Tampa Bay market's elevated insurance environment but is generally more predictable than coastal properties in communities like Apollo Beach. Most of Westchase is not in a high-risk flood zone, which keeps flood insurance costs out of the equation for most buyers here.

New Construction in Westchase

Westchase is a largely built-out community and has minimal new construction activity within its established boundaries. Most of the development that defined Westchase occurred from the 1990s through the early 2000s, and infill new construction is rare. Buyers who want new construction in northwest Tampa with a similar master-planned community feel should look at communities in the Lutz or Land O' Lakes areas in Pasco County, where national builders including Lennar, DR Horton, and Taylor Morrison are active. Our Tampa Bay Home Builders Guide covers all active builders across the region.

Pros and Cons of Living in Westchase

Pros

Westchase Elementary School. Top 10% in Florida, 86% math proficiency, 9/10 on GreatSchools. One of the strongest elementary schools in northwest Tampa. For families with young children, this is a primary draw.

Two full-service swim and tennis centers. Two resort-style pool complexes with lap lanes, slides, pickleball, and tennis serve a community of 3,400+ homes, ensuring the facilities are accessible rather than overcrowded.

No CDD fees. Unlike many newer Hillsborough communities, Westchase has no Community Development District fee overlay. The HOA covers community amenities without the additional CDD tax burden.

Veterans Expressway access. Airport in 15-20 minutes. Westshore in 15-20 minutes. Downtown in 20-30 minutes. The highway access here is genuinely superior to most northwest Tampa communities.

Established community identity. Westchase has a community culture, built over 30 years, that new developments simply cannot recreate. The WCA programming, the trick-or-treat events, the tennis leagues, the swim teams: these create the social fabric that keeps residents here for decades.

West Park Village Town Center. A walkable commercial center within a suburban community is rare and genuinely valuable for daily quality of life.

Cons

Limited inventory. Westchase is largely built out. When you find a home you like, competition can be meaningful. Buyers should be prepared to act quickly and have financing ready.

Older housing stock. Most Westchase homes were built 20 to 30 years ago. Some have been fully updated; others carry deferred maintenance. Budget for updates when evaluating older homes in the community.

Price premium. Westchase commands a premium over comparable square footage in non-HOA northwest Tampa communities. The premium is justified by the amenities and schools, but it is real and should be accounted for in your budget.

Westchase Real Estate for Investors

Westchase has strong rental fundamentals driven by the school quality and location. Families who want the Westchase Elementary feeder zone but are not ready to purchase, or who are relocating and want to rent before buying, create consistent rental demand. Single-family rentals in Westchase command $2,500 to $3,500 per month depending on size, condition, and proximity to amenities. HOA rules govern rental activity, and some neighborhoods within Westchase may have restrictions on lease terms or rental frequency. Verify HOA rental policies before purchasing with investment intent. Short-term rentals are generally restricted within Westchase's HOA guidelines. Is Westchase a good place to live?

Westchase is consistently rated one of the best master-planned communities in northwest Tampa. The combination of Westchase Elementary (top 10% in Florida), two resort-style swim and tennis centers, the Westchase Golf Club, West Park Village Town Center, and established community character makes it highly attractive to families and professionals. What schools serve Westchase?

Westchase Elementary (top 10% in Florida, 86% math proficiency), Davidsen Middle School (B rating on Niche, strong math performance), and Alonso High School (A- on Niche, 162nd in Florida, 86-96% graduation rate). What are home prices in Westchase?

Single-family homes range from the high $400,000s to over $1 million for lakefront properties. The market moves relatively quickly due to consistent demand and limited inventory.

Does Westchase have HOA fees?

Yes, Westchase has HOA fees typically in the range of $100 to $200 per month depending on the neighborhood section. Importantly, Westchase has no CDD (Community Development District) fees, which is an advantage over many newer Hillsborough communities where CDD assessments add significantly to the annual tax bill.

What amenities does Westchase have?

Westchase offers two full-service swim and tennis centers (both with multiple pools, lap lanes, toddler pools, and lit tennis and pickleball courts), the Westchase Golf Club (18-hole public course), West Park Village Town Center (walkable shopping and dining), hundreds of acres of preserved land with nature trails, parks, playgrounds, picnic pavilions, and a soccer field. Approximately 15 to 20 minutes via the Veterans Expressway. This is one of the closest airport commutes of any major northwest Tampa residential community, making Westchase particularly attractive to frequent travelers.

Is Westchase in a flood zone?

Most of Westchase is not in a high-risk FEMA flood zone, which keeps flood insurance out of the required expense category for most properties here. The community's significant preserved land and retention systems help manage stormwater effectively. Individual parcels should be verified, but Westchase does not carry the flood zone complexity of coastal Hillsborough communities.

title: Westchase 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ homes in Westchase typically range from $380,000-$650,000. Top active adult communities in the area include Nearby Pebble Creek in Lutz and nearby Carrollwood 55+ sections, offering resort-style amenities, low-maintenance living, and an active social calendar.

Why Active Adults Choose Westchase

Westchase has become an increasingly popular destination for active adults and retirees seeking the Florida lifestyle without sacrificing access to quality healthcare, cultural amenities, and everyday convenience. Westchase is one of Tampa Bay's most prestigious master-planned communities, located in northwest Hillsborough County. With beautifully maintained streetscapes, top-rated schools, village-style neighborhoods, and resort-level amenities, Westchase attracts families and professionals seeking an elevated suburban lifestyle.

The appeal of 55+ living in Westchase extends far beyond the weather. Active adult communities in this area provide a turnkey lifestyle that includes exterior home maintenance, landscaping, and community amenities - freeing residents to focus on the activities, travel, and social connections that make retirement fulfilling. With no state income tax, Florida remains one of the most tax-friendly states for retirees, and Westchase's cost of living compares favorably to many other retirement destinations along the Gulf Coast.

Whether you are planning a full-time relocation, seeking a seasonal winter residence, or downsizing from a larger home in the area, Westchase's 55+ market offers a range of options from maintenance-free villas to single-family homes with full resort amenities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping active adult buyers find the right community and home to match their lifestyle and budget.

Top 55+ Communities in and Near Westchase

The following communities represent the best options for 55+ buyers in the Westchase area. Each offers a distinct lifestyle, amenity package, and price point.

Nearby Pebble Creek in Lutz

Nearby Pebble Creek in Lutz is among the most established and well-regarded active adult communities serving Westchase residents. This community offers a comprehensive lifestyle package that includes maintained exteriors, community pools, fitness facilities, and an extensive calendar of social events, clubs, and organized activities. Homes range from attached villas with two bedrooms and two bathrooms to larger single-family residences with three bedrooms, dens, and two-car garages. Floor plans are designed specifically for active adult living, with single-story layouts, wide doorways, step-free entries, and owners suites positioned for privacy. The community atmosphere is welcoming and social, with residents forming lasting friendships through shared activities that range from golf and tennis to card games, art classes, and group travel.

nearby Carrollwood 55+ sections

nearby Carrollwood 55+ sections provides another excellent option for 55+ buyers in the Westchase area. This community appeals to active adults who want a maintenance-free lifestyle without sacrificing home quality or community amenities. Properties here feature modern finishes, energy-efficient construction, and thoughtful floor plans that accommodate both daily living and entertaining. The amenity package typically includes a community clubhouse, pool, walking trails, and organized social programming. Residents appreciate the sense of community that develops naturally when neighbors share similar life stages and interests. The location provides convenient access to healthcare facilities, shopping, dining, and the cultural attractions that make Westchase such an appealing retirement destination.

Price & Monthly Cost Overview for Westchase 55+ Homes

Understanding the full cost of 55+ living - including purchase price, HOA fees, and additional community charges - is essential for retirement planning. The table below outlines typical costs for active adult properties in the Westchase area.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Includes
2-Bed / 2-Bath Villa$380,000-$650,000$200-$500Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities

Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a complete cost breakdown for any community you are considering. Contact Barrett for current pricing and availability.

Amenities & Lifestyle in Westchase 55+ Communities

The amenity package is what truly sets 55+ communities apart from traditional neighborhoods. Active adult communities in the Westchase area offer lifestyle amenities that rival upscale resorts.

Fitness and Wellness

Most 55+ communities in Westchase include fitness centers equipped with cardio machines, strength training equipment, and stretching areas designed for active adults. Many offer group fitness classes such as water aerobics, yoga, tai chi, and low-impact cardio that cater specifically to the 55+ demographic. Walking trails, swimming pools, and spa facilities provide additional wellness options that encourage daily physical activity in a comfortable, age-appropriate setting.

Social Clubs and Activities

The social calendar in a well-run 55+ community is remarkably full. Residents in Westchase area communities can typically choose from dozens of clubs and interest groups covering everything from bridge and mahjong to woodworking, photography, gardening, and performing arts. Organized activities such as day trips, dinner outings, holiday celebrations, and educational seminars keep the community engaged and connected. For many residents, this built-in social network is the single greatest benefit of 55+ living.

Golf, Tennis, and Recreation

Golf remains a cornerstone of the 55+ lifestyle in Hillsborough County, and many active adult communities near Westchase offer on-site or nearby golf courses. Tennis and pickleball courts have become increasingly popular, with organized leagues and social play available most days. Bocce ball, shuffleboard, and horseshoes are additional recreational options that provide both exercise and social interaction in a relaxed, friendly setting.

Pools and Outdoor Living

Community pools in Westchase 55+ neighborhoods are designed for both exercise and relaxation. Heated pools extend the swimming season year-round, while separate spa and soaking pools provide therapeutic benefits. Many communities feature poolside pavilions, outdoor grills, and covered seating areas where residents gather for impromptu socializing and organized pool parties throughout the year.

Healthcare Access Near Westchase

Access to quality healthcare is a top priority for 55+ buyers, and Westchase delivers excellent options. The greater Tampa Bay area is home to some of Florida's finest medical facilities, ensuring that active adult residents are never far from the care they need.

Major healthcare providers serving the Westchase area include BayCare Health System, AdventHealth (formerly Florida Hospital), HCA Healthcare facilities, and Tampa General Hospital - consistently ranked among the top hospitals in Florida. Specialty care, including cardiology, orthopedics, oncology, and rehabilitation, is readily available at multiple facilities within a short drive of most Westchase neighborhoods.

Many 55+ communities in the area also provide on-site or nearby primary care offices, pharmacy services, and wellness programs that make routine healthcare convenient and accessible. The combination of world-class medical facilities and community-level wellness resources gives Westchase 55+ residents confidence that their healthcare needs will be met at every stage of retirement.

What 55+ Buyers Should Know

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations beyond a traditional home purchase. Barrett Henry advises every active adult buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Age verification requirements: Under the Housing for Older Persons Act, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one resident who is 55 or older. Communities enforce this through age verification at purchase. Some communities also restrict the age of permanent residents under 55, though policies vary.
  • Deed restrictions: 55+ communities typically have deed restrictions that govern modifications, rentals, pets, and use of common areas. Read these documents carefully to ensure they align with your lifestyle. Some communities restrict pet sizes, limit the number of overnight guests, or require owner-occupancy for a minimum period before renting.
  • HOA governance: Understand how the HOA is structured, who serves on the board, and how decisions are made. Attend an HOA meeting before purchasing if possible. A well-governed HOA with transparent finances and responsive management is essential to a positive 55+ living experience.
  • Reserve fund health: Review the reserve study and financial statements to ensure the community has adequate funds for future repairs and replacements. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments that create unexpected financial burdens for residents on fixed incomes.
  • Resale considerations: Consider the community's historical resale performance and current market dynamics. Some 55+ communities experience higher inventory levels due to natural turnover, which can affect resale timing and pricing. Barrett Henry can provide comparable sales data to help you evaluate resale potential.
  • Insurance requirements: Verify what insurance is covered by the HOA and what you need to carry individually. Some communities include master insurance policies that cover exterior structures and common areas, while individual unit owners are responsible for interior coverage and personal property.

Why Westchase?

Prestigious master-planned living with top-rated schools, swim and tennis centers, walkable West Park Village, and a 15-minute commute to the Westshore business district.

With a population of approximately 25,000 and a median home price around $550,000, Westchase provides an accessible entry point to the Tampa Bay lifestyle. The local economy is supported by Westshore business district, Tampa International Airport, Raymond James, Citigroup, nearby USF, and the broader region offers cultural attractions including performing arts, museums, professional sports, and waterfront dining that keep active adults engaged and entertained.

For 55+ buyers exploring Westchase real estate, the combination of Florida's tax advantages, the area's healthcare infrastructure, and the quality of available active adult communities makes Westchase a compelling retirement destination. Whether you are relocating from out of state or downsizing from a larger home in Hillsborough County, Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can guide you through every step of the process. Frequently Asked Questions About Westchase 55+ Homes

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community?

Federal law requires that at least 80 percent of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Most communities in the Westchase area allow younger spouses or partners to reside with a qualifying 55+ owner. However, policies regarding other household members under 55 vary by community. Some restrict younger residents entirely, while others allow exceptions with board approval. Barrett Henry can clarify the age policies for any community you are considering.

What do HOA fees cover in Westchase 55+ communities?

HOA fees in Westchase 55+ communities typically cover exterior home maintenance, roof reserves, lawn care, common area landscaping, community amenity operations, security, and sometimes cable TV, internet, and pest control. The scope of coverage varies significantly between communities, so it is important to get a detailed breakdown before comparing fees between different neighborhoods. Higher fees are not necessarily a negative - they often reflect a more comprehensive maintenance and amenity package.

Are 55+ homes a good investment?

55+ homes in the Westchase area have generally appreciated in line with or slightly below the broader market, depending on the specific community and its management quality. The primary value proposition of 55+ homes is lifestyle rather than investment return - the maintenance-free living, social amenities, and community atmosphere provide a quality of life that is difficult to quantify financially. That said, well-managed communities with strong HOAs and desirable locations have shown solid appreciation over time.

Can I rent out my 55+ home in Westchase?

Rental policies vary by community. Some 55+ communities in the Westchase area permit rentals with restrictions such as minimum lease terms (often 6-12 months), annual rental limits, and tenant age requirements. Others prohibit rentals entirely or restrict them to hardship cases with board approval. If future rental flexibility is important to you, verify the community's rental policy before purchasing.

What is the social atmosphere like in Westchase 55+ communities?

Most 55+ communities near Westchase foster a warm, welcoming social atmosphere with organized activities, clubs, and events that make it easy for newcomers to connect with neighbors. From card groups and book clubs to organized outings and holiday celebrations, the social calendar provides ample opportunities to build friendships and stay engaged. Many residents describe the social aspect of 55+ living as the most unexpected and rewarding benefit of their purchase decision.

For first-time buyers, condos and townhomes in Westchase offer an affordable entry point into homeownership. For downsizers, they provide a lock-and-leave lifestyle that eliminates the burden of yard maintenance, exterior upkeep, and roof repairs. And for investors, the strong rental demand in the Westchase area makes condos and townhomes an attractive addition to a real estate portfolio - provided the association allows rentals.

The Westchase market offers a wide range of condo and townhome options, from garden-style condos with ground-floor access to multi-story townhomes with private garages and rooftop terraces. Whether you prioritize walkability, commute convenience, or community amenities, there is a condo or townhome community in Westchase that fits your needs. Popular Condo & Townhome Communities in Westchase

The following communities represent some of the best options for condo and townhome buyers in the Westchase area.

The community offers a range of floor plans from compact two-bedroom units to spacious three-bedroom residences with modern finishes. Residents enjoy community amenities including a pool, fitness area, and well-maintained common spaces. The location provides convenient access to major employers, shopping centers, and transportation corridors, making West Park Village townhomes particularly popular with working professionals and young families who want an affordable home in a desirable location.

Harbor Links condos appeals to buyers who value a well-managed community with consistent standards and solid finances. Units here feature updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and open floor plans that maximize living space. The community amenity package includes pool access, covered parking, and professionally maintained grounds. Harbor Links condos has maintained a strong resale track record, with properties typically selling within a reasonable timeframe and at competitive prices relative to the broader Westchase market.

Westchase villas

Westchase villas offers another excellent option for condo and townhome buyers in Westchase. This community provides a mix of unit types that accommodate different household sizes and budgets. Common amenities include a pool, playground or recreation area, and visitor parking. The HOA is well-managed with adequate reserves, and the community has a track record of stable fees and minimal special assessments. For buyers prioritizing value and long-term stability, Westchase villas deserves serious consideration.

Westchase villas

Westchase villas rounds out the top condo and townhome options in Westchase with units that balance affordability and quality. This community attracts a diverse mix of first-time buyers, downsizers, and investors who appreciate the combination of reasonable pricing, solid HOA management, and a convenient location. Depending on the specific unit, buyers may find updated interiors with granite countertops, stainless appliances, and luxury vinyl flooring that give the home a fresh, modern feel.

Condo vs. Townhome: Understanding the Differences

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they have important legal and practical differences that affect ownership, financing, and daily life.

Ownership Structure

In a condo, you own the interior space of your unit and share ownership of common areas (building exterior, roof, grounds, amenities) with other unit owners through the association. In a townhome, you typically own the structure and the land beneath it, with shared ownership limited to common areas like pools, parks, and private roads. This distinction affects insurance requirements, maintenance responsibilities, and how future improvements are funded.

Maintenance Responsibility

Condo associations in Westchase generally handle all exterior maintenance, including the roof, building envelope, painting, landscaping, and common areas. Townhome owners often retain responsibility for their own roof, driveway, and limited exterior maintenance, though the HOA may handle landscaping and common area upkeep. This difference is reflected in HOA fees - condo fees tend to be higher because they cover more services.

Privacy and Space

Townhomes typically offer more interior space, multiple floors, a private garage, and sometimes a small yard or pation. Condos tend to be single-level units that may share walls on multiple sides. For buyers who prioritize privacy and the feel of a traditional home, townhomes are often the better choice. For buyers who prefer single-level living and minimal maintenance, condos may be more appropriate.

What Condo & Townhome Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome in Westchase requires due diligence beyond what a traditional single-family home purchase demands. Barrett Henry advises every buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Association financial health: Request the most recent financial statements, budget, and reserve study. Look for adequate reserves (ideally 20 percent or more of the annual budget), stable fee history, and no pending special assessments. Florida law now requires reserve studies and adequate funding for structural components following legislative changes in recent years.
  • Reserve fund compliance: Florida statutes now require condo associations to maintain funded reserves for structural components, including the roof, foundation, and load-bearing walls. Verify that the association is in compliance, as underfunded reserves can trigger special assessments and affect property values.
  • Insurance coverage: Understand the difference between the association's master policy and your individual HO-6 policy. The master policy typically covers the building exterior and common areas, while your HO-6 covers your interior, personal property, and liability. Verify coverage limits and deductibles for both policies.
  • Rules and restrictions: Review the association's governing documents, including CC&Rs, bylaws, and rules and regulations. Common restrictions cover pets, rentals, parking, noise, renovations, and use of common areas. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the unit in the future, verify the association's rental policy. Many Westchase associations limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously, impose minimum lease terms, or require tenant approval by the board. Some associations prohibit rentals entirely.
  • Pending litigation and violations: Ask whether the association is involved in any lawsuits and whether the building has any outstanding code violations. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Financing Condos: Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable

Financing a condo purchase in Westchase requires understanding the distinction between warrantable and non-warrantable condominiums, as this classification directly affects your mortgage options.

A warrantable condo meets the guidelines set by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which means it qualifies for conventional financing with competitive interest rates and standard down payment requirements. To be warrantable, a condo association generally must have adequate reserves, no more than 15 percent of units delinquent on fees, no single entity owning more than 20 percent of units, and at least 50 percent of units owner-occupied.

A non-warrantable condo fails to meet one or more of these guidelines, which limits financing options to portfolio loans, credit unions, or cash purchases. Non-warrantable condos often carry higher interest rates, larger down payment requirements, and fewer lender options. Common reasons a Westchase condo might be non-warrantable include high investor concentration, pending litigation, inadequate reserves, or a single entity owning too many units.

Lifestyle Benefits of Condo & Townhome Living

Beyond the financial considerations, condos and townhomes in Westchase offer lifestyle advantages that appeal to a wide range of buyers.

  • Low maintenance: Say goodbye to weekend yard work, exterior painting, and roof repairs. Condo and townhome living frees up time for the activities you actually enjoy.
  • Community amenities: Many Westchase communities include pools, fitness centers, and social spaces that would cost thousands to replicate in a single-family home setting.
  • Affordability: Condos and townhomes typically offer a lower entry price than comparable single-family homes, making homeownership accessible to first-time buyers and those on a budget.
  • Location: Attached housing communities are often situated in prime locations near employment centers, shopping, dining, and entertainment - areas where single-family homes may be priced significantly higher.
  • Security: Many condo communities in Westchase feature controlled access, security cameras, and well-lit common areas that provide an added layer of safety.
  • Lock and leave: For frequent travelers, seasonal residents, and busy professionals, the ability to lock the door and leave without worrying about yard maintenance or home security is invaluable.

Why Westchase?

Prestigious master-planned living with top-rated schools, swim and tennis centers, walkable West Park Village, and a 15-minute commute to the Westshore business district.

Westchase has a population of approximately 25,000 and a median home price of $550,000. The local economy benefits from Westshore business district, Tampa International Airport, Raymond James, Citigroup, nearby USF, creating consistent demand for housing at all price points. For buyers exploring Westchase real estate, condos and townhomes offer an affordable, low-maintenance path to homeownership in one of Florida's most dynamic markets.

Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an affordable entry point, a downsizer seeking a simpler lifestyle, or an investor building a rental portfolio, Westchase's condo and townhome market has options to match your goals. Frequently Asked Questions About Westchase Condos & Townhomes

How much are HOA fees for condos in Westchase?

Monthly HOA fees for condos in Westchase typically range from $200 to $500, depending on the community's amenity package, age, and services included. Fees that cover exterior insurance, roof reserves, water, sewer, and trash tend to be higher but reduce the owner's out-of-pocket costs for those items. Barrett Henry can provide exact fee information and a breakdown of included services for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my condo or townhome in Westchase?

Rental policies vary by association. Some Westchase communities allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on total rental units. Others prohibit rentals or require board approval for each tenant. If rental flexibility is important to you, verify the association's policy before purchasing and confirm that the current rental cap has not been reached.

What is a special assessment and should I be worried?

A special assessment is a one-time charge levied by the association to cover unexpected expenses or projects that exceed reserve fund capacity. Common triggers include roof replacement, elevator modernization, structural repairs, and insurance premium increases. While special assessments are a normal part of condo ownership, frequent or large assessments may indicate poor financial planning. Reviewing the reserve study and financial statements before purchasing helps assess this risk.

Do I need separate insurance for my condo?

Yes. While the association's master policy covers the building exterior and common areas, individual condo owners in Westchase need an HO-6 policy that covers interior finishes, personal property, liability, and loss assessment coverage. Loss assessment coverage is particularly important, as it protects you if the association levies a special assessment for a covered loss that exceeds the master policy's coverage.

What is the difference between a condo and a townhome for financing purposes?

Condos face additional financing scrutiny because lenders evaluate the entire association - not just the individual unit. Townhomes, which typically convey land with the structure, are often financed more like single-family homes with fewer association-level requirements. However, some townhome communities are structured as condominiums from a legal standpoint, which triggers condo financing requirements.   • Rules and restrictions: Read the CC&Rs (Covenants, Conditions & Restrictions) thoroughly. Common restrictions cover exterior paint colors, landscaping, parking, rentals, pets, and home-based businesses. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the property in the future, verify the community's rental policies. Many gated communities in Westchase limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously or impose minimum lease terms.
  • Insurance requirements: Some gated communities require specific insurance coverage levels or types. Verify insurance requirements and obtain quotes before closing to avoid surprises.
  • Pending litigation: Ask the HOA whether any lawsuits are pending against the association. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

title: Westchase Homes with Pool
content:
Quick Answer

Westchase pool homes typically range from $450,000-$1,200,000+, with screened enclosures being standard across Hillsborough County. Buyers should budget for pool inspection, resurfacing timelines, and updated equipment when evaluating resale pool properties.

Why Pool Homes Are So Popular in Westchase

In Westchase, a swimming pool is not a luxury - it is a way of life. With average temperatures above 70 degrees for nine months of the year and summer highs regularly reaching the mid-90s, residents rely on their backyard pools for daily relief, weekend entertaining, and year-round outdoor living. Westchase is one of Tampa Bay's most prestigious master-planned communities, located in northwest Hillsborough County. With beautifully maintained streetscapes, top-rated schools, village-style neighborhoods, and resort-level amenities, Westchase attracts families and professionals seeking an elevated suburban lifestyle.

Pool homes in Westchase consistently command higher resale values than comparable non-pool properties. According to recent market data, homes with pools sell for approximately 5-8 percent more than similar homes without one. For families, retirees, and remote workers who spend significant time at home, a pool transforms the backyard into a private retreat that rivals any resort.

The popularity of pool homes has only increased since 2020, when more buyers began prioritizing outdoor living space, home offices with views, and personal recreation areas. In Westchase, that trend shows no signs of slowing, with pool-equipped listings often receiving multiple offers within days of hitting the market.

Best Neighborhoods for Pool Homes in Westchase

Choosing the right neighborhood is just as important as finding the right pool. Here are the top areas in Westchase where pool homes are most prevalent and desirable.

Glencliff

Glencliff is widely regarded as one of the premier neighborhoods in Westchase for pool homes. Properties here tend to feature larger lots, established landscaping, and pools that have been well-maintained over the years. Many homes in Glencliff include screened pool enclosures with extended lanais, outdoor kitchens, and tropical plantings that create a true backyard oasis. The neighborhood offers convenient access to shopping, dining, and major roadways, making it ideal for families and professionals alike.

Stonebridge

Stonebridge attracts buyers who want pool homes with a community feel. Many properties in this neighborhood include pools with newer equipment, updated decking, and spacious screen enclosures. The area is known for its well-kept streetscapes, neighborhood parks, and family-friendly atmosphere. Pool homes in Stonebridge tend to offer excellent value, with price points that appeal to first-time pool home buyers and move-up buyers.

Harbor Links

For buyers seeking pool homes with larger lots and more privacy, Harbor Links delivers. This area features properties with expansive backyards, mature trees, and pools that serve as the centerpiece of outdoor entertainment areas. Many pool homes in Harbor Links include covered patios, summer kitchens, and fire pit areas that extend the usable outdoor space well beyond the pool deck itself.

The Greens

The Greens rounds out the top pool home neighborhoods in Westchase with a mix of newer construction and updated resale homes. Pools here range from classic rectangular designs to freeform tropical layouts with water features. The neighborhood benefits from newer infrastructure, well-maintained HOA standards, and proximity to parks and recreation areas that complement the backyard pool lifestyle.

Pool Home Price Overview in Westchase

The following table provides a general overview of pool home pricing across Westchase by property type and size. Prices vary by neighborhood, pool condition, lot size, and home features.

The median home price in Westchase is approximately $550,000, with pool homes generally commanding a premium above that figure. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed market analysis for your specific neighborhood and price range. Contact Barrett for current pool home inventory.

Types of Pools You Will Find in Westchase

Not all pools are created equal, and understanding the types available in Westchase will help you narrow your search and budget accordingly.

Screened Pool Enclosures

The vast majority of residential pools in Westchase - and across Florida - feature aluminum-framed screen enclosures, commonly called pool cages. These enclosures keep out insects, reduce debris, and provide a measure of safety for children and pets. A standard pool cage in good condition adds significant value to a home and is considered essential by most buyers in Hillsborough County. Replacement costs for a full pool cage can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on size, so cage condition is a key inspection item.

Saltwater Pools

Saltwater pool systems have surged in popularity across Westchase due to lower maintenance costs and a more comfortable swimming experience. Saltwater generators produce chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, reducing the need for chemical handling and producing water that is gentler on skin, hair, and swimwear. Many resale homes have been converted from traditional chlorine to saltwater systems, and most new construction pools include saltwater as standard.

Heated Pools

While Westchase enjoys a warm climate, winter mornings can bring pool water temperatures down into the 60s. Gas heaters, heat pumps, and solar heating systems extend the swimming season to a full twelve months. Gas heaters provide the fastest heat-up time, while heat pumps offer better energy efficiency for day-to-day use. Solar heating is the most economical long-term option and works well with the abundant Florida sunshine.

Freeform and Custom Pools

Many homes in Westchase feature custom-designed freeform pools with rock waterfalls, grottos, tanning ledges, and infinity edges. These resort-style pools are most common in upscale neighborhoods and estate properties, where the pool and outdoor living area serve as the architectural focal point of the home. Buyers should note that custom pools may cost more to maintain and insure than standard designs.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist

Purchasing a pool home requires additional due diligence beyond a standard home inspection. Barrett Henry recommends every pool home buyer evaluate the following items before making an offer.

  • Pool inspection: Hire a certified pool inspector separate from the general home inspector. They will evaluate the shell, plumbing, equipment, deck, and screen enclosure for defects, leaks, and code compliance.
  • Resurfacing timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or quartz) typically last 8-15 years. Determine when the pool was last resurfaced and budget accordingly if resurfacing is due within the next few years. Costs range from $5,000 to $12,000.
  • Equipment age: Pool pumps, filters, heaters, and salt systems have a lifespan of 5-10 years. Aging equipment may work today but represent a near-term replacement cost. Ask the seller for maintenance records and equipment installation dates.
  • Screen enclosure condition: Inspect the cage for corrosion, torn screens, sagging frames, and signs of storm damage. A full cage replacement can cost $8,000-$15,000, so factor this into your offer if damage is present.
  • Insurance impact: Pool ownership affects homeowners insurance premiums and liability coverage. Discuss pool-specific coverage with your insurance agent before closing. A pool fence or cage is typically required for compliance with local safety codes.
  • Deck and drainage: Pool decks should be level, free of large cracks, and properly graded to direct water away from the home. Settling, trip hazards, and poor drainage are common issues in older pool homes.

Outdoor Living Features Beyond the Pool

In Westchase, the pool is often just one element of a comprehensive outdoor living area. The best pool homes pair the swimming pool with features that extend the home's livable square footage into the backyard.

Lanais and Covered Patios

A screened lanai adjacent to the pool provides shaded seating, outdoor dining, and protection from afternoon rain showers. Many Westchase homes feature extended lanais with ceiling fans, recessed lighting, and tile or travertine flooring that create a seamless indoor-outdoor transition.

Summer Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens - called summer kitchens in Florida - have become a must-have amenity in Westchase pool homes. A typical summer kitchen includes a built-in grill, countertop space, a mini-refrigerator, and a sink. Upscale versions add pizza ovens, smokers, kegerators, and bar seating that turn the pool area into an entertainment destination.

Landscape and Lighting

Tropical landscaping, LED pool lighting, and landscape lighting create a resort atmosphere that enhances both daytime and evening enjoyment. Mature palms, birds of paradise, and jasmine hedges are popular plantings that thrive in Westchase's climate and complement the pool setting.

Why Westchase?

Prestigious master-planned living with top-rated schools, swim and tennis centers, walkable West Park Village, and a 15-minute commute to the Westshore business district.

With a population of approximately 25,000, Westchase offers a strong and diverse economy anchored by Westshore business district, Tampa International Airport, Raymond James, Citigroup, nearby USF. The combination of employment opportunities, lifestyle amenities, and a growing real estate market makes Westchase one of the most compelling places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region.

For buyers exploring Westchase real estate, pool homes represent an outstanding investment in both quality of life and long-term property value. Whether you are relocating from out of state, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for your retirement oasis, Westchase delivers the Florida lifestyle at a price point that competes favorably with other Gulf Coast markets.

Frequently Asked Questions About Westchase Pool Homes

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Westchase?

Monthly pool maintenance in Westchase typically runs between $100 and $200 for weekly professional service, which includes chemical balancing, skimming, brushing, and equipment checks. Homeowners who maintain their own pools can reduce costs to $40-$80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual costs for electricity to run the pump average $600-$1,200 depending on the pump type and run time.

Do pool homes cost more to insure in Westchase?

Yes, pool homes generally carry higher homeowners insurance premiums due to increased liability exposure. The additional cost is typically $100-$300 per year, though rates vary by insurer, pool type, and whether the pool has a safety fence or enclosure. Screen enclosures can help reduce premiums by meeting safety barrier requirements.

What is the best time to buy a pool home in Westchase?

The best time to buy a pool home in Westchase is typically during the late fall and winter months (November through February), when buyer competition decreases and sellers may be more willing to negotiate. However, inventory for pool homes tends to be limited year-round, so working with an experienced agent like Barrett Henry ensures you see new listings the moment they hit the market.

Should I buy a home with an existing pool or build one?

Both options have merits. Buying an existing pool home avoids the 3-6 month construction timeline and the hassle of managing a pool build project. However, building a new pool lets you customize the design, equipment, and features to your exact specifications. New pool construction in Westchase typically costs $35,000-$80,000 depending on size, features, and site conditions. Barrett Henry can help you evaluate both options based on available inventory and your budget.

Are there HOA restrictions on pools in Westchase?

Many neighborhoods in Westchase have HOA guidelines that govern pool construction, including setback requirements, fence or enclosure standards, and equipment placement. Some HOAs require architectural review board approval before a pool can be built. Barrett Henry can review HOA documents and identify any restrictions before you make an offer on a property where you plan to add a pool.

Why Buy New Construction in Westchase?

Buying new construction in Westchase means moving into a home designed with today's lifestyle in mind. Modern floor plans emphasize open-concept living, large kitchen islands, flexible bonus rooms, and indoor-outdoor flow with covered lanais. You also get the peace of mind that comes with a builder warranty, brand-new mechanical systems, and current building codes designed for Florida's climate.

New homes in Westchase also offer energy efficiency advantages - impact-rated windows, modern insulation, high-efficiency HVAC systems, and ENERGY STAR appliances can significantly reduce your monthly utility and insurance costs compared to older homes.

Active Builders and Communities

Several reputable builders are active in the Westchase area, including Mostly resale; select new construction. These builders offer a range of floor plans, lot sizes, and customization options to fit different budgets and preferences.

New construction communities in Westchase typically include amenities such as community pools, playgrounds, walking trails, and clubhouses. Some larger developments offer fitness centers, tennis courts, and resort-style recreation.

What to Know Before Buying

  • Builder warranties: Most new homes come with a 1-year comprehensive warranty, 2-year systems warranty, and 10-year structural warranty. Understand what is covered and for how long.
  • Customization timeline: If you are buying pre-construction, expect a build timeline of 6-12 months depending on the builder and level of customization. Quick-move-in homes may be available sooner.
  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

New Construction Price Ranges

CategoryTypical Range in Westchase
Entry-Level / Starter$500K-$650K range
Move-Up / FamilyMid $400s - $500s
Premium / Luxury$700K+

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Westchase?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

title: Westchase Waterfront Homes
content:
Quick Answer

Waterfront homes in Westchase include properties on Community lakes, Brooker Creek. Pricing varies widely based on water type, lot size, and direct access. Flood insurance and seawall condition are key considerations.

Browse Westchase Waterfront Homes Homes for Sale

Updated daily from the MLS. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to schedule a showing.

Types of Waterfront in Westchase

Westchase offers several types of waterfront living, each with its own character, pricing, and lifestyle:

  • Community lakes, Brooker Creek - the primary waterfront options in Westchase range from open-water properties with panoramic views to canal-front homes with private dock access and lake-front properties with peaceful settings.

The type of waterfront determines not just the lifestyle but also insurance costs, maintenance requirements, and resale value. Open-water properties with direct bay or Gulf access typically command the highest premiums.

Popular Waterfront Areas

The most sought-after waterfront neighborhoods in Westchase include areas within The Bridges, Westchase Estates, West Park Village, Glencliff, Stonebridge. These neighborhoods offer a mix of water types, lot sizes, and price points.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Westchase require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Westchase?

Flood insurance costs in Westchase vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Westchase?

Most waterfront properties in Westchase allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Westchase generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.
