title: Wimauma Real Estate | Barrett Henry
content:
Browse Wimauma Real Estate Homes for Sale

Updated daily from the MLS. Contact Barrett Henry at (813) 733-7907 to schedule a showing.

Wimauma is one of south Hillsborough County's fastest-changing zip codes. What was once a quiet agricultural community along US-301 is now home to master-planned subdivisions, an active adult resort community, a crystal-clear lagoon, and a brand-new high school built for thousands of students. If you are searching for affordable new construction close to Tampa with room to grow, Wimauma deserves a serious look.

This guide covers everything you need to know about Wimauma real estate: neighborhoods, schools, commutes, new construction builders, investment potential, and honest pros and cons. Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has helped buyers and sellers navigate the Tampa Bay market for over two decades. Call (813) 733-7907 to talk through whether Wimauma fits your goals.

Talk to a Tampa Bay ExpertSearch All Homes

Why Wimauma is One of Tampa Bay's Best Kept Secrets

Wimauma has flown under the radar for years while neighboring communities like Riverview, Brandon, and Ruskin absorbed most of the south Hillsborough growth. That is changing fast. Builders including D.R. Horton, Pulte, Highland Homes, Ryan Homes, and Lennar have planted significant flags here, and the Southshore Bay lagoon community has put Wimauma on the map for buyers who want resort-style amenities at a price below what they would pay closer to Tampa.

The median sale price in Wimauma is meaningfully lower than in Riverview or Apollo Beach, yet buyers are still within a reasonable commute of downtown Tampa, MacDill Air Force Base, and the employment corridors along I-75. For first-time buyers and move-up buyers alike, that value equation is hard to ignore. First-time buyers in particular find that Wimauma stretches their budget further than almost anywhere else in the county.

The community also has a distinctive character rooted in its agricultural and Latino heritage. That cultural richness, combined with waves of newer residents from across the country, gives Wimauma an energy that more established suburbs sometimes lack.

Where is Wimauma? Location, Geography, and Getting Around

Wimauma sits in the southern portion of Hillsborough County, roughly 25 to 30 miles south of downtown Tampa. It is bounded to the west by Sun City Center and to the north by Riverview. Ruskin is just northwest along US-301, and the city of Apollo Beach sits on Tampa Bay to the northwest. To the south, Wimauma borders Manatee County farmland and begins to transition toward the Bradenton metro area.

The backbone of Wimauma's road network is US-301, which runs north into Tampa and south toward Sarasota. Interstate 75 is accessible roughly six miles west via Sun City Center Boulevard, giving residents a direct highway connection to St. Petersburg, Bradenton, and Fort Myers in one direction, and Tampa, Wesley Chapel, and Gainesville in the other.

The terrain is classic south Florida: flat, with pockets of wetlands, agricultural land, and the Little Manatee River threading through the eastern portion of the community. The river corridor provides natural beauty and has anchored one of the area's most popular outdoor destinations, Little Manatee River State Park.

Wimauma carries the zip code 33598 and falls under Hillsborough County jurisdiction. It is an unincorporated community, meaning municipal services are provided by the county rather than a city government.

Wimauma Real Estate Market Overview

As of early 2026, there are over 400 homes listed for sale in Wimauma, with median prices hovering around $360,000 to $375,000 depending on the source and timing. That figure is notably below the broader Tampa metro median, making Wimauma one of the more accessible entry points into Hillsborough County homeownership.

The market has shifted toward buyers compared to the frenzied pace of 2021 and 2022. Average days on market climbed in 2026, and sellers have increasingly needed to price competitively or offer concessions to attract offers. For buyers, this represents a window of opportunity that did not exist a few years ago.

Over the long term, Wimauma has been a strong appreciator. According to market data, the area has seen roughly 169% appreciation over the past decade, placing it in the top tier nationally for home value growth. That track record reflects the structural shift from rural to suburban and the continued arrival of major builders investing real capital in the community.

The overwhelming majority of homes, roughly 83%, are single-family detached houses, and about 78% of the housing stock has been built since 2000. This means buyers are generally purchasing newer homes with modern layouts, energy-efficient construction, and contemporary finishes at prices that would feel like bargains in Brandon or Tampa. If you are tracking the closing costs and total purchase picture, Wimauma's lower price points can make a meaningful difference.

Investors should note that the rental market has held up reasonably well. Approximately 20% of households in Wimauma are renter-occupied, and average rents have been reported in the $2,000 to $2,500 range for single-family homes. See the investor section below for more detail.

Ready to see what is available right now? Browse current Wimauma listings or call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to discuss what is active and under contract in specific neighborhoods.

Neighborhoods and Subdivisions in Wimauma

Wimauma's growth has produced a diverse collection of communities ranging from gated resort-style neighborhoods to smaller legacy subdivisions. Here is an overview of the major areas buyers should know.

Southshore Bay

Southshore Bay is anchored by a five-acre MetroLagoon, a man-made crystal-clear lagoon with a sandy beach, swim-up bars, kayaking, and paddleboarding. The development includes both family-focused sections and the Medley at Southshore Bay, a 55+ active adult component with maintenance-free living. Builders including Lennar have been active here. The lagoon amenity has made Southshore Bay one of the most searched communities in south Hillsborough, drawing buyers who want a resort feel at a non-resort price.

Valencia Lakes

Valencia Lakes is a premier 55+ active adult community developed by GL Homes, situated about 25 miles south of Tampa. The community features a large clubhouse, resort-style pools, tennis and pickleball courts, bocce, and a robust calendar of clubs and social activities. Valencia Lakes is strictly for buyers aged 55 and older and is one of the most established active adult communities in the south Hillsborough area. If you are exploring retirement communities in the region, our Tampa Bay 55+ Communities Guide covers Valencia Lakes alongside other options in detail. Do not confuse Valencia Lakes with the family-oriented sections of Wimauma: these are separate markets with different HOA rules and lifestyle expectations. Our HOA Rules Florida Guide can help you understand what to review before buying in any age-restricted or HOA-governed community.

Berry Bay

Berry Bay is a community along US-301 featuring new construction homes primarily by D.R. Horton. It sits just minutes from I-75 and has attracted buyers looking for newer homes with builder warranties and modern floor plans. Berry Bay is a family-friendly community with pools and playgrounds and has been one of the more active new construction addresses in Wimauma over the past few years.

Sereno

Sereno is a gated community in Wimauma featuring resort-style amenities and larger homesites. It has attracted buyers who want more privacy and larger lots than are typically available in tightly packed new construction subdivisions. The gated entry and community amenities set Sereno apart for buyers willing to pay a modest premium for the security and lifestyle.

Cypress Ridge Ranch

Cypress Ridge Ranch is a newer neighborhood by Highland Homes near Little Manatee River State Park and the Southshore Bay lagoon. The community offers resort amenities, proximity to outdoor recreation, and quick access to US-301 and I-75. Model homes are open and move-in ready inventory is available. Highland Homes is a Florida-based builder known for customizable options at accessible price points.

Creek Preserve

Creek Preserve is an established community in Wimauma with single-family homes in a more attainable price range. It appeals to buyers who want a neighborhood with existing trees and infrastructure rather than a brand-new development still under construction around them.

Legacy, Lake Toscana, and Smaller Subdivisions

Wimauma also includes a number of smaller subdivisions and scattered single-family homes on larger lots, some with agricultural or equestrian zoning. Buyers interested in land, hobby farms, or rural-adjacent lifestyle will find opportunities here that are increasingly rare in more urbanized parts of Hillsborough County.

Use the search tool below to see active listings across Wimauma communities:

Want help comparing communities side by side? Our Buyer's Guide walks through the full purchase process, and Barrett can help you understand which neighborhoods fit your priorities and price range. Call (813) 733-7907 anytime.

Schools in Wimauma: Ratings, Zoning, and Options

Schools are one of the most important factors for families considering Wimauma, and the picture here is evolving. The honest answer is that the traditional public school options in Wimauma have historically scored below state averages, but the situation is actively changing as the community grows and Hillsborough County invests in new facilities.

Aquilla J. Morgan High School

The biggest school news in Wimauma's recent history is the opening of Aquilla J. Morgan High School, which opened in fall 2025. Named after the first African American teacher at Wimauma Elementary in the 1960s, Morgan High is the largest school construction project in Hillsborough County history, designed to serve up to 3,500 students. The school opened to grades 9 through 11, with a senior class added in 2026. Morgan High was built to relieve overcrowding at both Lennard High and Sumner High, and many Wimauma-area students now fall within its boundaries. Always verify zoning for your specific address through the Hillsborough County Public Schools website, as boundaries shift as new schools open.

Lennard High School

Lennard High School in Ruskin has historically served much of the Wimauma area and continues to serve portions of the community. Check current zoning to confirm which high school applies to your specific address, as the opening of Morgan High has shifted some attendance zones.

Elementary and Middle Schools

Wimauma Elementary School serves grades PK through 5 and has received lower state accountability grades in recent years, receiving a D grade in the 2024-2025 school year. The school serves a population with a high percentage of economically disadvantaged students. RCMA Wimauma Community Academy, a charter school serving K through 8, has performed better and received a B grade. Families with school-age children should research elementary and middle school options carefully and consider charter options alongside traditional zoning.

Private and Charter Options

Several private and charter schools in the broader SouthShore and Riverview area are within a reasonable drive of Wimauma. Families willing to commute slightly for school access have more options than the local public school footprint alone suggests. Barrett can connect you with current residents who can speak to their own school experience in the community.

Bottom line: school quality in Wimauma is in transition, and the opening of Morgan High is a meaningful investment in the community's educational future. Families should visit campuses, speak with current parents, and verify current zoning before making a final decision.

Things to Do in Wimauma

Wimauma's identity as a place to live is increasingly defined by its access to outdoor recreation and the amenities within its master-planned communities, rather than a dense urban entertainment core. That trade-off suits a specific lifestyle, and buyers who understand it tend to love the area.

Little Manatee River State Park

Little Manatee River State Park is Wimauma's anchor outdoor attraction. The park features 12 miles of equestrian trails, hiking through rare sand pine scrub and oak ecosystems, canoeing and kayaking on the river, primitive camping, and picnicking. The Canoe Outpost on the Little Manatee River, located just over a mile from the park, offers canoe and kayak rentals for those who want a guided paddle experience. The park is consistently well-reviewed and draws visitors from across the Tampa Bay region.

Southshore Bay Lagoon

The five-acre MetroLagoon at Southshore Bay has become one of the most talked-about amenities in south Hillsborough. Even if you do not live in Southshore Bay, the lagoon has put Wimauma on the map as a destination. Residents of the community enjoy beach access, kayaking, paddleboarding, a swim-up bar, and a resort atmosphere without the resort price tag.

Nearby Attractions

Wimauma's location gives residents quick access to a broad range of regional attractions. Apollo Beach Nature Preserve and the Tampa Electric Manatee Viewing Center are roughly 9 miles northwest. E.G. Simmons Regional Park in Ruskin offers waterfront access to Tampa Bay. The Florida Railroad Museum and Ruskin Family Drive-In are short drives away and popular with families. Camp Bayou Outdoor Learning Center provides environmental education and nature experiences.

For major entertainment, Busch Gardens Tampa Bay, the Florida Aquarium, and Amalie Arena are all accessible within 35 to 45 minutes via I-75. Tampa Bay's beaches are roughly an hour west in St. Petersburg or Clearwater. Wimauma residents accept a trade-off: you get more home for your money, and you drive a bit further for urban amenities.

Community Amenities Within Neighborhoods

Many of Wimauma's master-planned communities have invested heavily in on-site amenities. Community pools, fitness centers, playgrounds, dog parks, and walking trails are common features in Berry Bay, Southshore Bay, Sereno, and newer subdivisions. This is partly by design: builders know that buyers in more remote locations need strong amenity packages to say yes. The result is that Wimauma residents often have resort-quality recreation within their own neighborhood without leaving home.

Best Restaurants and Dining in Wimauma

Wimauma's dining scene is small but authentic. The community's deep agricultural and Latino roots mean that some of the best food in the area is not at chain restaurants. Wimauma proper has a limited number of sit-down restaurants, and residents frequently supplement local options with dining in nearby Ruskin, Sun City Center, and along the US-301 corridor.

Local and Nearby Dining

Garcia's Bakery is a local favorite offering authentic Mexican and South American baked goods, large cookies, pastries, and traditional treats. It represents the kind of community-rooted business that gives Wimauma its distinctive character. The Country Cuban and Waves Crab House are among the area's better-reviewed dining options, with Waves attracting seafood lovers from across the SouthShore corridor. SOL Mexican Cocina rounds out the Mexican dining options in the broader area.

For everyday convenience, Wimauma and the surrounding US-301 corridor offer the typical mix of pizza chains, fast food, and casual dining. Ruskin, just a few miles northwest, has a more developed restaurant scene and has seen new dining options arrive alongside the broader SouthShore population growth.

The honest assessment: Wimauma is not a dining destination yet, and buyers who prioritize walkable restaurant access should weigh that against the area's housing value advantages. The dining landscape is improving as the population grows, but it is not comparable to Brandon or Riverview at this point.

Thinking About Wimauma? Let's Talk.

Barrett Henry has helped buyers and sellers across the Tampa Bay area navigate real estate decisions with confidence. Whether you're exploring Wimauma for the first time or ready to make a move, a quick conversation can save you time and money.

Call or text: (813) 733-7907 | Email: barrett@nowtb.com

Commute and Transportation from Wimauma

Wimauma is a car-dependent community. Public transportation is essentially unavailable for commuters: data consistently shows near-zero transit ridership from Wimauma, and there is no meaningful bus or rail service that connects the area to Tampa's employment centers. If you do not drive, Wimauma is not a practical place to live.

For drivers, the commute picture is workable but real. Downtown Tampa is approximately 30 to 35 miles away, and drive times during off-peak hours run 35 to 45 minutes via US-301 north or via I-75 north from Sun City Center Boulevard. During peak rush hour, that commute can stretch to 50 to 70 minutes depending on conditions along I-75 and the Selmon Expressway interchange. Buyers who are commuting to Tampa five days a week should factor fuel costs, vehicle wear, and time into their overall cost calculation.

MacDill Air Force Base is approximately 30 miles northwest. St. Petersburg is accessible via I-75 south to I-275 or via the Selmon Expressway, typically a 45 to 60 minute drive. Bradenton is roughly 25 miles south on US-301 or I-75, making Wimauma an interesting option for buyers whose employers are in the Bradenton or Sarasota corridor.

Lakeland is accessible to the northeast via I-4, though it requires connecting through Tampa, adding time to that commute. Overall, Wimauma is best suited for buyers commuting within a 30- to 45-minute radius and who are comfortable with a driving-only lifestyle.

Cost of Living in Wimauma

Wimauma's cost of living sits slightly above the national average when all categories are included, but housing is where it outperforms most of the Tampa metro. The median home value in Wimauma has been reported in the $360,000 to $425,000 range depending on the data source and time period, and that figure represents meaningfully better value per square foot than comparable new construction in Riverview, Brandon, or Apollo Beach.

Florida's lack of a state income tax is a significant advantage for residents from higher-tax states. Property taxes in Hillsborough County are moderate by Florida standards. Many Wimauma communities have HOA fees ranging from modest to more substantial depending on the amenity package, and some have Community Development District (CDD) assessments layered on top of property taxes. Our CDD Fee Florida Guide explains exactly how these work and what to look for before buying in any master-planned community.

Healthcare costs in the Wimauma area are reported to be slightly below the national average. Grocery and everyday retail options are limited locally, which can mean driving to larger retailers in Ruskin, Sun City Center, or along the Gibsonton/Riverview corridor. Fuel costs for commuters should be treated as a meaningful monthly expense when evaluating affordability.

For buyers financing their purchase, current mortgage rates and the lower purchase prices in Wimauma can combine to produce monthly payments that are competitive with rental costs in the broader Tampa metro. Talk to Barrett about a realistic total cost picture before you start comparing communities. Use our home valuation tool to understand what your current home is worth if you are considering a move.

Flood zone status is worth checking carefully in Wimauma given the Little Manatee River and low-lying terrain in some areas. Our Florida Flood Zones Guide explains how to read FEMA maps and what flood insurance may cost. Some neighborhoods in Wimauma fall outside high-risk flood zones, but this varies by location.

New Construction in Wimauma

New construction is the engine of Wimauma's growth, and buyers have more builder options here than almost anywhere else in Hillsborough County at these price points. The breadth of builders active in Wimauma As of 2026 and 2026 is notable.

D.R. Horton

D.R. Horton is active in Berry Bay and other Wimauma communities, offering entry-level to mid-range single-family homes with competitive pricing and express move-in inventory. D.R. Horton is the nation's largest homebuilder and is known for functional layouts and builder-grade finishes at accessible price points.

Highland Homes

Highland Homes, a Florida-based builder, is active in Cypress Ridge Ranch near Little Manatee River State Park. Highland Homes is known for customizable floor plans, Florida-specific design features, and a strong local reputation. Model homes are open and quick move-in options are available.

Ryan Homes

Ryan Homes has multiple communities in Wimauma and is one of the more prolific builders in the area. Ryan offers a range of floor plans and has been active across several Wimauma communities simultaneously, giving buyers flexibility in terms of community type and lot options.

Lennar

Lennar is building in the Southshore Bay community, including the Medley at Southshore Bay 55+ section. Lennar's "Everything's Included" model means most upgrades are standard, which simplifies the buying process and can reduce the final price surprise that sometimes accompanies new construction with extensive options.

Pulte and Other Builders

Pulte Homes has also been active in Wimauma, and additional builders including M/I Homes and others have had communities in the area. The pipeline of new inventory means buyers can typically find something in construction or move-in ready within a short window.

Working with a Buyer's Agent on New Construction

One of the most common misconceptions in new construction is that buyers do not need their own agent because the builder has sales staff on site. Builder sales agents represent the builder. Period. Having Barrett in your corner costs you nothing as a buyer (builders pay the commission), and it provides representation, negotiation support, and an independent review of the contract before you sign. See our full buyer's guide for more on how new construction purchases work in Florida.

Interested in browsing new construction listings in Wimauma? Call Barrett at (813) 733-7907 to get a current builder inventory update, discuss which communities have the best incentives, and understand the full cost picture before you visit a model home.

Pros and Cons of Living in Wimauma

Every market has trade-offs. Here is an honest look at what Wimauma gets right and where it falls short, so you can make a clear-eyed decision.

Pros

Affordability. Wimauma offers some of the lowest new construction price points in Hillsborough County. Buyers regularly find homes that would cost 15% to 25% more in Riverview or Brandon for similar square footage and age.

New housing stock. About 78% of Wimauma's homes were built after 2000. Buyers are generally getting newer construction with modern layouts, better energy efficiency, and lower near-term maintenance needs compared to older housing stock in established Tampa neighborhoods.

Nature access. Little Manatee River State Park, the Canoe Outpost, Camp Bayou, and the broader rural landscape give Wimauma a connection to nature that is genuinely rare at this price point and this close to a major metro.

Resort-style community amenities. The Southshore Bay lagoon and the amenity packages in Sereno, Berry Bay, and other communities are genuinely impressive for the price. Buyers get swimming pools, fitness centers, and walking trails that feel aspirational.

Active adult options. Valencia Lakes is one of the best 55+ communities in the Tampa Bay region, and Medley at Southshore Bay adds a second strong option. Wimauma has become a legitimate destination for active adult buyers who want value and lifestyle.

Long-term appreciation track record. The structural shift from rural to suburban has driven significant appreciation over the past decade. The investment thesis for Wimauma real estate has been validated by the market.

Authentic community character. Wimauma's Latino heritage and working-class roots give the community a genuineness that more polished suburbs sometimes lack. Cultural events, local food businesses, and a young, diverse population create a distinct sense of place.

Cons

Schools need improvement. Traditional public elementary and middle school options in Wimauma have historically underperformed state averages. Morgan High School is a genuine investment in the community's future, but elementary and middle school families need to do careful research on their specific options.

Car dependency is total. There is no public transit in Wimauma. Every errand, every commute, every school pickup happens by car. Fuel costs and vehicle expenses are a real budget line item for residents.

Commute length is real. A 30- to 45-minute average commute to Tampa is manageable for many buyers, but it becomes a 50- to 70-minute drive during rush hour. Over a five-day work week, that adds up in time and cost.

Limited local dining and retail. Wimauma does not have a town center, a major grocery anchor, or a dense retail corridor. Residents drive to Ruskin, Sun City Center, or further north for most shopping. This is improving as the population grows, but it remains a gap compared to more established suburbs.

Construction disruption. If you buy in or near an active new construction community, expect construction traffic, noise, and dust for an extended period as the neighborhood builds out. This is the nature of early-stage suburban growth and can last years.

CDD and HOA fees. Many Wimauma communities have CDD assessments in addition to HOA fees. These can add several hundred dollars per year (or more) to the effective cost of ownership. Always review the full fee structure before making an offer. Our CDD Fee Guide and HOA Rules Guide explain what to look for.

Wimauma Real Estate for Investors

Wimauma has been on investor radar for several years, driven by strong long-term appreciation, new construction activity, and an expanding rental demand base. Here is how the investment landscape looks heading into 2026.

Rental Market Fundamentals

Approximately 20% of Wimauma households are renter-occupied. Average rents for single-family homes have been reported in the $2,000 to $2,500 range, with three-bedroom homes trending toward the higher end of that range. The renter population is supported by Wimauma's working-class employment base, agricultural sector workers, and families who have not yet been able to purchase in the current market.

Appreciation and Long-Term Value

Wimauma's ten-year appreciation rate of approximately 169% places it in the top 10% of U.S. markets nationally according to market tracking data. The structural driver of that appreciation, the conversion of rural and agricultural land to suburban residential use, has further room to run as builders continue to develop the corridor south of Riverview along US-301.

New Construction as an Investment Play

Some investors have used new construction contracts in Wimauma as an equity-building strategy, purchasing early in a community's development cycle and selling as the neighborhood matures and builder prices rise. This approach carries risk in a buyer's market and requires careful timing, but it has rewarded investors who got in ahead of the major development wave.

Cautions for Investors

The 2026 market showed increased inventory and longer days on market, which has pressured resale values. Investors purchasing for short-term appreciation or quick flip strategies face more headwinds than they did in 2021 and 2022. Long-term buy-and-hold rental strategies are better suited to the current environment. Many new construction communities also have HOA rules restricting short-term rentals, so Airbnb or VRBO strategies are often not viable. Verify HOA rules before purchasing for any rental purpose.

Barrett has worked with investors across the Tampa Bay investment market and can help you run realistic numbers on any Wimauma property before you commit. Call (813) 733-7907 or visit our investment resources page. If you are evaluating commercial or multi-family opportunities in the area, those conversations are worth having as well.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wimauma

Is Wimauma a good place to live?

Wimauma is a good fit for buyers who prioritize affordability, newer homes, outdoor recreation access, and community amenities, and who are comfortable with a car-dependent lifestyle and a commute to Tampa. It is not the right fit for buyers who need walkable neighborhoods, strong local dining, or top-rated public elementary schools. The community is genuinely improving, and buyers getting in now are positioned ahead of further growth.

How far is Wimauma from Tampa?

Wimauma is approximately 25 to 30 miles south of downtown Tampa. The drive takes roughly 35 to 45 minutes during off-peak hours via I-75 or US-301. Rush hour commutes can run 50 to 70 minutes depending on traffic conditions.

What is the median home price in Wimauma?

As of early 2026, median home prices in Wimauma are reported in the $360,000 to $375,000 range depending on the data source. This places Wimauma meaningfully below the broader Tampa metro median and makes it one of the more affordable new construction markets in Hillsborough County. Prices vary significantly by community, with entry-level new construction starting below $300,000 in some communities and move-up homes in gated communities reaching well above $450,000.

What neighborhoods are in Wimauma, FL?

Major communities in Wimauma include Southshore Bay (including the lagoon and Medley 55+ section), Valencia Lakes (55+ only), Berry Bay, Sereno, Cypress Ridge Ranch, Creek Preserve, and Lake Toscana, among smaller subdivisions and rural residential properties. The community landscape is expanding as new builders continue to develop available land along the US-301 corridor.

Is Wimauma FL a safe area?

Safety perceptions in Wimauma vary depending on which part of the community you are in. Newer master-planned communities with HOAs and gated entries tend to have lower crime rates. The older, more established parts of Wimauma have more mixed profiles. As with any community, research crime data for the specific neighborhood and street, not just the zip code. Niche, NeighborhoodScout, and local Hillsborough County Sheriff data are good starting points.

What schools serve Wimauma, FL?

As of 2026-2026, Wimauma-area students attend Wimauma Elementary (PK-5), RCMA Wimauma Community Academy (K-8 charter), and either Lennard High School or the newly opened Aquilla J. Morgan High School for high school. Attendance zones have shifted with Morgan High's opening. Always verify your specific address zoning through Hillsborough County Public Schools before purchasing.

Is Valencia Lakes in Wimauma for all ages?

No. Valencia Lakes is a 55+ active adult community restricted to residents 55 and older. It is not appropriate for families with minor children as primary residents. If you are a younger buyer, Valencia Lakes is not an option. Southshore Bay, Berry Bay, Sereno, and most other Wimauma communities welcome all ages. Our Tampa Bay 55+ Guide covers Valencia Lakes and similar communities in detail.

What builders are building new homes in Wimauma?

Active builders in Wimauma As of 2026-2026 include D.R. Horton, Highland Homes, Ryan Homes, Lennar, Pulte Homes, and M/I Homes, among others. The breadth of builder activity gives buyers meaningful choices in terms of community type, floor plan, price point, and delivery timeline. New builders may enter or exit the market as community buildouts progress, so it is worth getting a current builder inventory update from an agent who tracks this closely.

Does Wimauma have CDD fees?

Many Wimauma master-planned communities have Community Development District assessments in addition to HOA fees. CDDs fund infrastructure like roads, utilities, and community amenities and are repaid over time through annual assessments on property owners. These fees can add meaningfully to annual ownership costs and should be reviewed carefully before any purchase. Our CDD Fee Florida Guide explains how these work and what questions to ask.

What is the Southshore Bay lagoon?

The Southshore Bay lagoon is a five-acre man-made crystal-clear lagoon developed by Metro Development Group within the Southshore Bay master-planned community in Wimauma. Residents access a sandy beach, swimming areas, kayaking, paddleboarding, and a swim-up bar. The lagoon has become one of the most distinctive amenities in south Hillsborough County and has significantly raised the profile of Wimauma as a lifestyle destination.

How does Wimauma compare to Riverview?

Wimauma is generally more affordable than Riverview and has more active new construction at lower price points. Riverview has a more developed commercial and retail infrastructure, stronger school ratings in some zones, and shorter commutes to Tampa. Wimauma offers more nature access and resort-style community amenities at a lower entry price. Which is right for you depends on your priorities around commute, budget, schools, and lifestyle.

Is Wimauma good for first-time buyers?

Wimauma can be an excellent entry point for first-time buyers in the Tampa Bay market. The lower median prices compared to more established suburbs, the availability of new construction with builder incentives, and the opportunity to build equity in an appreciating market all work in a first-time buyer's favor. The trade-offs, primarily commute length and limited local amenities, are manageable for buyers whose top priority is building equity rather than walkability. Our first-time buyer resources can help you understand the full purchase process.

What is the population of Wimauma, FL?

Wimauma's population has been reported at approximately 9,000 to 10,000 residents, with a notably young median age of around 29, which is significantly younger than both Florida and the broader Tampa metro. The community is growing rapidly and the true population is likely higher as new construction communities continue to fill in.

Should I use a buyer's agent in Wimauma?

Yes, and it costs you nothing as a buyer. Whether you are buying resale or new construction, having a buyer's agent provides representation, negotiation support, and local market knowledge. Builder sales agents represent the builder. title: Wimauma 55+ Homes
content:
Quick Answer

55+ homes in Wimauma typically range from $220,000-$380,000. Top active adult communities in the area include Nearby Sun City Center and nearby Kings Point, offering resort-style amenities, low-maintenance living, and an active social calendar.

Why Active Adults Choose Wimauma

Wimauma has become an increasingly popular destination for active adults and retirees seeking the Florida lifestyle without sacrificing access to quality healthcare, cultural amenities, and everyday convenience. Wimauma is a small, rapidly developing community in southern Hillsborough County that offers some of the most affordable new construction in the Tampa Bay area. Major builders are creating master-planned neighborhoods that attract first-time buyers and young families.

The appeal of 55+ living in Wimauma extends far beyond the weather. Active adult communities in this area provide a turnkey lifestyle that includes exterior home maintenance, landscaping, and community amenities - freeing residents to focus on the activities, travel, and social connections that make retirement fulfilling. With no state income tax, Florida remains one of the most tax-friendly states for retirees, and Wimauma's cost of living compares favorably to many other retirement destinations along the Gulf Coast.

Whether you are planning a full-time relocation, seeking a seasonal winter residence, or downsizing from a larger home in the area, Wimauma's 55+ market offers a range of options from maintenance-free villas to single-family homes with full resort amenities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping active adult buyers find the right community and home to match their lifestyle and budget.

Top 55+ Communities in and Near Wimauma

The following communities represent the best options for 55+ buyers in the Wimauma area. Each offers a distinct lifestyle, amenity package, and price point.

Nearby Sun City Center

Nearby Sun City Center is among the most established and well-regarded active adult communities serving Wimauma residents. This community offers a comprehensive lifestyle package that includes maintained exteriors, community pools, fitness facilities, and an extensive calendar of social events, clubs, and organized activities. Homes range from attached villas with two bedrooms and two bathrooms to larger single-family residences with three bedrooms, dens, and two-car garages. Floor plans are designed specifically for active adult living, with single-story layouts, wide doorways, step-free entries, and owners suites positioned for privacy. The community atmosphere is welcoming and social, with residents forming lasting friendships through shared activities that range from golf and tennis to card games, art classes, and group travel.

nearby Kings Point

nearby Kings Point provides another excellent option for 55+ buyers in the Wimauma area. This community appeals to active adults who want a maintenance-free lifestyle without sacrificing home quality or community amenities. Properties here feature modern finishes, energy-efficient construction, and thoughtful floor plans that accommodate both daily living and entertaining. The amenity package typically includes a community clubhouse, pool, walking trails, and organized social programming. Residents appreciate the sense of community that develops naturally when neighbors share similar life stages and interests. The location provides convenient access to healthcare facilities, shopping, dining, and the cultural attractions that make Wimauma such an appealing retirement destination.

Price & Monthly Cost Overview for Wimauma 55+ Homes

Understanding the full cost of 55+ living - including purchase price, HOA fees, and additional community charges - is essential for retirement planning. The table below outlines typical costs for active adult properties in the Wimauma area.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Includes
2-Bed / 2-Bath Villa$220,000-$380,000$200-$500Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2-Bath Single Family$220,000-$380,000$250-$550Exterior maintenance, lawn, amenities
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Premium$220,000-$380,000$300-$600Full maintenance, lawn, amenities, cable
Condo / Attached Villa$220,000-$380,000$350-$700Exterior, roof, insurance, amenities

Monthly HOA fees in 55+ communities cover a wide range of services. Some communities include exterior painting, roof maintenance, lawn care, pest control, cable TV, and community amenities in a single monthly fee. Others charge separately for certain services. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a complete cost breakdown for any community you are considering. Contact Barrett for current pricing and availability.

Amenities & Lifestyle in Wimauma 55+ Communities

The amenity package is what truly sets 55+ communities apart from traditional neighborhoods. Active adult communities in the Wimauma area offer lifestyle amenities that rival upscale resorts.

Fitness and Wellness

Most 55+ communities in Wimauma include fitness centers equipped with cardio machines, strength training equipment, and stretching areas designed for active adults. Many offer group fitness classes such as water aerobics, yoga, tai chi, and low-impact cardio that cater specifically to the 55+ demographic. Walking trails, swimming pools, and spa facilities provide additional wellness options that encourage daily physical activity in a comfortable, age-appropriate setting.

Social Clubs and Activities

The social calendar in a well-run 55+ community is remarkably full. Residents in Wimauma area communities can typically choose from dozens of clubs and interest groups covering everything from bridge and mahjong to woodworking, photography, gardening, and performing arts. Organized activities such as day trips, dinner outings, holiday celebrations, and educational seminars keep the community engaged and connected. For many residents, this built-in social network is the single greatest benefit of 55+ living.

Golf, Tennis, and Recreation

Golf remains a cornerstone of the 55+ lifestyle in Hillsborough County, and many active adult communities near Wimauma offer on-site or nearby golf courses. Tennis and pickleball courts have become increasingly popular, with organized leagues and social play available most days. Bocce ball, shuffleboard, and horseshoes are additional recreational options that provide both exercise and social interaction in a relaxed, friendly setting.

Pools and Outdoor Living

Community pools in Wimauma 55+ neighborhoods are designed for both exercise and relaxation. Heated pools extend the swimming season year-round, while separate spa and soaking pools provide therapeutic benefits. Many communities feature poolside pavilions, outdoor grills, and covered seating areas where residents gather for impromptu socializing and organized pool parties throughout the year.

Healthcare Access Near Wimauma

Access to quality healthcare is a top priority for 55+ buyers, and Wimauma delivers excellent options. The greater Tampa Bay area is home to some of Florida's finest medical facilities, ensuring that active adult residents are never far from the care they need.

Major healthcare providers serving the Wimauma area include BayCare Health System, AdventHealth (formerly Florida Hospital), HCA Healthcare facilities, and Tampa General Hospital - consistently ranked among the top hospitals in Florida. Specialty care, including cardiology, orthopedics, oncology, and rehabilitation, is readily available at multiple facilities within a short drive of most Wimauma neighborhoods.

Many 55+ communities in the area also provide on-site or nearby primary care offices, pharmacy services, and wellness programs that make routine healthcare convenient and accessible. The combination of world-class medical facilities and community-level wellness resources gives Wimauma 55+ residents confidence that their healthcare needs will be met at every stage of retirement.

What 55+ Buyers Should Know

Purchasing in a 55+ community involves unique considerations beyond a traditional home purchase. Barrett Henry advises every active adult buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Age verification requirements: Under the Housing for Older Persons Act, at least 80 percent of occupied units must have at least one resident who is 55 or older. Communities enforce this through age verification at purchase. Some communities also restrict the age of permanent residents under 55, though policies vary.
  • Deed restrictions: 55+ communities typically have deed restrictions that govern modifications, rentals, pets, and use of common areas. Read these documents carefully to ensure they align with your lifestyle. Some communities restrict pet sizes, limit the number of overnight guests, or require owner-occupancy for a minimum period before renting.
  • HOA governance: Understand how the HOA is structured, who serves on the board, and how decisions are made. Attend an HOA meeting before purchasing if possible. A well-governed HOA with transparent finances and responsive management is essential to a positive 55+ living experience.
  • Reserve fund health: Review the reserve study and financial statements to ensure the community has adequate funds for future repairs and replacements. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments that create unexpected financial burdens for residents on fixed incomes.
  • Resale considerations: Consider the community's historical resale performance and current market dynamics. Some 55+ communities experience higher inventory levels due to natural turnover, which can affect resale timing and pricing. Barrett Henry can provide comparable sales data to help you evaluate resale potential.
  • Insurance requirements: Verify what insurance is covered by the HOA and what you need to carry individually. Some communities include master insurance policies that cover exterior structures and common areas, while individual unit owners are responsible for interior coverage and personal property.

Why Wimauma?

Affordable new construction with large lots, a rural feel, and proximity to Sun City Center, Apollo Beach, and the growing SouthShore corridor.

With a population of approximately 10,000 and a median home price around $320,000, Wimauma provides an accessible entry point to the Tampa Bay lifestyle. The local economy is supported by Agriculture, nearby Amazon in Riverview, growing logistics and distribution centers, and the broader region offers cultural attractions including performing arts, museums, professional sports, and waterfront dining that keep active adults engaged and entertained.

For 55+ buyers exploring Wimauma real estate, the combination of Florida's tax advantages, the area's healthcare infrastructure, and the quality of available active adult communities makes Wimauma a compelling retirement destination. Whether you are relocating from out of state or downsizing from a larger home in Hillsborough County, Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can guide you through every step of the process. Learn more about selling your current home or contact Barrett to begin your search.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wimauma 55+ Homes

Can someone under 55 live in a 55+ community?

Federal law requires that at least 80 percent of occupied units have at least one resident aged 55 or older. Most communities in the Wimauma area allow younger spouses or partners to reside with a qualifying 55+ owner. However, policies regarding other household members under 55 vary by community. Some restrict younger residents entirely, while others allow exceptions with board approval. Barrett Henry can clarify the age policies for any community you are considering.

What do HOA fees cover in Wimauma 55+ communities?

HOA fees in Wimauma 55+ communities typically cover exterior home maintenance, roof reserves, lawn care, common area landscaping, community amenity operations, security, and sometimes cable TV, internet, and pest control. The scope of coverage varies significantly between communities, so it is important to get a detailed breakdown before comparing fees between different neighborhoods. Higher fees are not necessarily a negative - they often reflect a more comprehensive maintenance and amenity package.

Are 55+ homes a good investment?

55+ homes in the Wimauma area have generally appreciated in line with or slightly below the broader market, depending on the specific community and its management quality. The primary value proposition of 55+ homes is lifestyle rather than investment return - the maintenance-free living, social amenities, and community atmosphere provide a quality of life that is difficult to quantify financially. That said, well-managed communities with strong HOAs and desirable locations have shown solid appreciation over time.

Can I rent out my 55+ home in Wimauma?

Rental policies vary by community. Some 55+ communities in the Wimauma area permit rentals with restrictions such as minimum lease terms (often 6-12 months), annual rental limits, and tenant age requirements. Others prohibit rentals entirely or restrict them to hardship cases with board approval. If future rental flexibility is important to you, verify the community's rental policy before purchasing.

What is the social atmosphere like in Wimauma 55+ communities?

Most 55+ communities near Wimauma foster a warm, welcoming social atmosphere with organized activities, clubs, and events that make it easy for newcomers to connect with neighbors. From card groups and book clubs to organized outings and holiday celebrations, the social calendar provides ample opportunities to build friendships and stay engaged. Many residents describe the social aspect of 55+ living as the most unexpected and rewarding benefit of their purchase decision.

title: Wimauma Condos & Townhomes
content:
Quick Answer

Condos and townhomes in Wimauma range from $170,000-$310,000, offering low-maintenance living with community amenities. Popular options include Sereno townhomes and Ayersworth Glen townhomes. Buyers should carefully review association finances, insurance, and warrantability before purchasing.

Why Condos & Townhomes Are Popular in Wimauma

Condos and townhomes represent one of the fastest-growing segments of the Wimauma real estate market. Buyers are drawn to the lower price points, reduced maintenance responsibilities, and community amenities that attached and multi-family housing provides. Wimauma is a small, rapidly developing community in southern Hillsborough County that offers some of the most affordable new construction in the Tampa Bay area. Major builders are creating master-planned neighborhoods that attract first-time buyers and young families.

For first-time buyers, condos and townhomes in Wimauma offer an affordable entry point into homeownership. For downsizers, they provide a lock-and-leave lifestyle that eliminates the burden of yard maintenance, exterior upkeep, and roof repairs. And for investors, the strong rental demand in the Wimauma area makes condos and townhomes an attractive addition to a real estate portfolio - provided the association allows rentals.

The Wimauma market offers a wide range of condo and townhome options, from garden-style condos with ground-floor access to multi-story townhomes with private garages and rooftop terraces. Whether you prioritize walkability, commute convenience, or community amenities, there is a condo or townhome community in Wimauma that fits your needs. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® specializes in helping buyers navigate the unique considerations of condo and townhome purchases.

Popular Condo & Townhome Communities in Wimauma

The following communities represent some of the best options for condo and townhome buyers in the Wimauma area.

Sereno townhomes

Sereno townhomes is one of the most sought-after condo and townhome communities in Wimauma. The community offers a range of floor plans from compact two-bedroom units to spacious three-bedroom residences with modern finishes. Residents enjoy community amenities including a pool, fitness area, and well-maintained common spaces. The location provides convenient access to major employers, shopping centers, and transportation corridors, making Sereno townhomes particularly popular with working professionals and young families who want an affordable home in a desirable location.

Ayersworth Glen townhomes

Ayersworth Glen townhomes appeals to buyers who value a well-managed community with consistent standards and solid finances. Units here feature updated kitchens, modern bathrooms, and open floor plans that maximize living space. The community amenity package includes pool access, covered parking, and professionally maintained grounds. Ayersworth Glen townhomes has maintained a strong resale track record, with properties typically selling within a reasonable timeframe and at competitive prices relative to the broader Wimauma market.

South Fork villas

South Fork villas offers another excellent option for condo and townhome buyers in Wimauma. This community provides a mix of unit types that accommodate different household sizes and budgets. Common amenities include a pool, playground or recreation area, and visitor parking. The HOA is well-managed with adequate reserves, and the community has a track record of stable fees and minimal special assessments. For buyers prioritizing value and long-term stability, South Fork villas deserves serious consideration.

South Fork villas

South Fork villas rounds out the top condo and townhome options in Wimauma with units that balance affordability and quality. This community attracts a diverse mix of first-time buyers, downsizers, and investors who appreciate the combination of reasonable pricing, solid HOA management, and a convenient location. Depending on the specific unit, buyers may find updated interiors with granite countertops, stainless appliances, and luxury vinyl flooring that give the home a fresh, modern feel.

Price & HOA Overview for Wimauma Condos & Townhomes

The following table provides general pricing guidance for condos and townhomes in the Wimauma market. HOA fees vary by community and the services included.

Property TypePrice RangeMonthly HOA (Est.)Typical Features
1-Bed / 1-Bath Condo$170,000-$310,000$200-$400Pool, basic maintenance
2-Bed / 2-Bath Condo$170,000-$310,000$250-$500Pool, fitness, parking
2-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$170,000-$310,000$150-$350Garage, exterior maintenance
3-Bed / 2.5-Bath Townhome$170,000-$310,000$175-$400Garage, pool, exterior maintenance

HOA fees for condos are generally higher than for townhomes because condo associations typically cover more services including exterior insurance, roof maintenance, painting, and sometimes water, sewer, and trash. Townhome HOAs tend to cover less, with owners responsible for their own exterior maintenance and insurance in some communities. Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can provide a detailed HOA fee breakdown and financial review for any community. Contact Barrett for current listings and pricing.

Condo vs. Townhome: Understanding the Differences

While condos and townhomes are often grouped together, they have important legal and practical differences that affect ownership, financing, and daily life.

Ownership Structure

In a condo, you own the interior space of your unit and share ownership of common areas (building exterior, roof, grounds, amenities) with other unit owners through the association. In a townhome, you typically own the structure and the land beneath it, with shared ownership limited to common areas like pools, parks, and private roads. This distinction affects insurance requirements, maintenance responsibilities, and how future improvements are funded.

Maintenance Responsibility

Condo associations in Wimauma generally handle all exterior maintenance, including the roof, building envelope, painting, landscaping, and common areas. Townhome owners often retain responsibility for their own roof, driveway, and limited exterior maintenance, though the HOA may handle landscaping and common area upkeep. This difference is reflected in HOA fees - condo fees tend to be higher because they cover more services.

Privacy and Space

Townhomes typically offer more interior space, multiple floors, a private garage, and sometimes a small yard or pation. Condos tend to be single-level units that may share walls on multiple sides. For buyers who prioritize privacy and the feel of a traditional home, townhomes are often the better choice. For buyers who prefer single-level living and minimal maintenance, condos may be more appropriate.

What Condo & Townhome Buyers Should Know

Purchasing a condo or townhome in Wimauma requires due diligence beyond what a traditional single-family home purchase demands. Barrett Henry advises every buyer to evaluate the following factors.

  • Association financial health: Request the most recent financial statements, budget, and reserve study. Look for adequate reserves (ideally 20 percent or more of the annual budget), stable fee history, and no pending special assessments. Florida law now requires reserve studies and adequate funding for structural components following legislative changes in recent years.
  • Reserve fund compliance: Florida statutes now require condo associations to maintain funded reserves for structural components, including the roof, foundation, and load-bearing walls. Verify that the association is in compliance, as underfunded reserves can trigger special assessments and affect property values.
  • Insurance coverage: Understand the difference between the association's master policy and your individual HO-6 policy. The master policy typically covers the building exterior and common areas, while your HO-6 covers your interior, personal property, and liability. Verify coverage limits and deductibles for both policies.
  • Rules and restrictions: Review the association's governing documents, including CC&Rs, bylaws, and rules and regulations. Common restrictions cover pets, rentals, parking, noise, renovations, and use of common areas. Ensure the rules align with your lifestyle before committing.
  • Rental restrictions: If you may want to rent the unit in the future, verify the association's rental policy. Many Wimauma associations limit the number of units that can be rented simultaneously, impose minimum lease terms, or require tenant approval by the board. Some associations prohibit rentals entirely.
  • Pending litigation and violations: Ask whether the association is involved in any lawsuits and whether the building has any outstanding code violations. Litigation can affect insurance costs, property values, and the overall financial health of the community.

Financing Condos: Warrantable vs. Non-Warrantable

Financing a condo purchase in Wimauma requires understanding the distinction between warrantable and non-warrantable condominiums, as this classification directly affects your mortgage options.

A warrantable condo meets the guidelines set by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, which means it qualifies for conventional financing with competitive interest rates and standard down payment requirements. To be warrantable, a condo association generally must have adequate reserves, no more than 15 percent of units delinquent on fees, no single entity owning more than 20 percent of units, and at least 50 percent of units owner-occupied.

A non-warrantable condo fails to meet one or more of these guidelines, which limits financing options to portfolio loans, credit unions, or cash purchases. Non-warrantable condos often carry higher interest rates, larger down payment requirements, and fewer lender options. Common reasons a Wimauma condo might be non-warrantable include high investor concentration, pending litigation, inadequate reserves, or a single entity owning too many units.

Barrett Henry, REALTOR® can help you determine the warrantability status of any condo you are considering and connect you with lenders who specialize in both warrantable and non-warrantable financing. Contact Barrett to discuss your financing options.

Lifestyle Benefits of Condo & Townhome Living

Beyond the financial considerations, condos and townhomes in Wimauma offer lifestyle advantages that appeal to a wide range of buyers.

  • Low maintenance: Say goodbye to weekend yard work, exterior painting, and roof repairs. Condo and townhome living frees up time for the activities you actually enjoy.
  • Community amenities: Many Wimauma communities include pools, fitness centers, and social spaces that would cost thousands to replicate in a single-family home setting.
  • Affordability: Condos and townhomes typically offer a lower entry price than comparable single-family homes, making homeownership accessible to first-time buyers and those on a budget.
  • Location: Attached housing communities are often situated in prime locations near employment centers, shopping, dining, and entertainment - areas where single-family homes may be priced significantly higher.
  • Security: Many condo communities in Wimauma feature controlled access, security cameras, and well-lit common areas that provide an added layer of safety.
  • Lock and leave: For frequent travelers, seasonal residents, and busy professionals, the ability to lock the door and leave without worrying about yard maintenance or home security is invaluable.

Why Wimauma?

Affordable new construction with large lots, a rural feel, and proximity to Sun City Center, Apollo Beach, and the growing SouthShore corridor.

Wimauma has a population of approximately 10,000 and a median home price of $320,000. The local economy benefits from Agriculture, nearby Amazon in Riverview, growing logistics and distribution centers, creating consistent demand for housing at all price points. For buyers exploring Wimauma real estate, condos and townhomes offer an affordable, low-maintenance path to homeownership in one of Florida's most dynamic markets.

Whether you are a first-time buyer looking for an affordable entry point, a downsizer seeking a simpler lifestyle, or an investor building a rental portfolio, Wimauma's condo and townhome market has options to match your goals. Frequently Asked Questions About Wimauma Condos & Townhomes

How much are HOA fees for condos in Wimauma?

Monthly HOA fees for condos in Wimauma typically range from $200 to $500, depending on the community's amenity package, age, and services included. Fees that cover exterior insurance, roof reserves, water, sewer, and trash tend to be higher but reduce the owner's out-of-pocket costs for those items. Barrett Henry can provide exact fee information and a breakdown of included services for any community you are considering.

Can I rent out my condo or townhome in Wimauma?

Rental policies vary by association. Some Wimauma communities allow rentals with restrictions such as minimum 12-month lease terms and a cap on total rental units. Others prohibit rentals or require board approval for each tenant. If rental flexibility is important to you, verify the association's policy before purchasing and confirm that the current rental cap has not been reached.

What is a special assessment and should I be worried?

A special assessment is a one-time charge levied by the association to cover unexpected expenses or projects that exceed reserve fund capacity. Common triggers include roof replacement, elevator modernization, structural repairs, and insurance premium increases. While special assessments are a normal part of condo ownership, frequent or large assessments may indicate poor financial planning. Reviewing the reserve study and financial statements before purchasing helps assess this risk.

Do I need separate insurance for my condo?

Yes. While the association's master policy covers the building exterior and common areas, individual condo owners in Wimauma need an HO-6 policy that covers interior finishes, personal property, liability, and loss assessment coverage. Loss assessment coverage is particularly important, as it protects you if the association levies a special assessment for a covered loss that exceeds the master policy's coverage.

What is the difference between a condo and a townhome for financing purposes?

Condos face additional financing scrutiny because lenders evaluate the entire association - not just the individual unit. Townhomes, which typically convey land with the structure, are often financed more like single-family homes with fewer association-level requirements. However, some townhome communities are structured as condominiums from a legal standpoint, which triggers condo financing requirements. Types of Pools You Will Find in Wimauma

Not all pools are created equal, and understanding the types available in Wimauma will help you narrow your search and budget accordingly.

Screened Pool Enclosures

The vast majority of residential pools in Wimauma - and across Florida - feature aluminum-framed screen enclosures, commonly called pool cages. These enclosures keep out insects, reduce debris, and provide a measure of safety for children and pets. A standard pool cage in good condition adds significant value to a home and is considered essential by most buyers in Hillsborough County. Replacement costs for a full pool cage can range from $5,000 to $15,000 depending on size, so cage condition is a key inspection item.

Saltwater Pools

Saltwater pool systems have surged in popularity across Wimauma due to lower maintenance costs and a more comfortable swimming experience. Saltwater generators produce chlorine naturally from dissolved salt, reducing the need for chemical handling and producing water that is gentler on skin, hair, and swimwear. Many resale homes have been converted from traditional chlorine to saltwater systems, and most new construction pools include saltwater as standard.

Heated Pools

While Wimauma enjoys a warm climate, winter mornings can bring pool water temperatures down into the 60s. Gas heaters, heat pumps, and solar heating systems extend the swimming season to a full twelve months. Gas heaters provide the fastest heat-up time, while heat pumps offer better energy efficiency for day-to-day use. Solar heating is the most economical long-term option and works well with the abundant Florida sunshine.

Freeform and Custom Pools

Many homes in Wimauma feature custom-designed freeform pools with rock waterfalls, grottos, tanning ledges, and infinity edges. These resort-style pools are most common in upscale neighborhoods and estate properties, where the pool and outdoor living area serve as the architectural focal point of the home. Buyers should note that custom pools may cost more to maintain and insure than standard designs.

Pool Home Buyer Checklist

Purchasing a pool home requires additional due diligence beyond a standard home inspection. Barrett Henry recommends every pool home buyer evaluate the following items before making an offer.

  • Pool inspection: Hire a certified pool inspector separate from the general home inspector. They will evaluate the shell, plumbing, equipment, deck, and screen enclosure for defects, leaks, and code compliance.
  • Resurfacing timeline: Pool surfaces (plaster, pebble, or quartz) typically last 8-15 years. Determine when the pool was last resurfaced and budget accordingly if resurfacing is due within the next few years. Costs range from $5,000 to $12,000.
  • Equipment age: Pool pumps, filters, heaters, and salt systems have a lifespan of 5-10 years. Aging equipment may work today but represent a near-term replacement cost. Ask the seller for maintenance records and equipment installation dates.
  • Screen enclosure condition: Inspect the cage for corrosion, torn screens, sagging frames, and signs of storm damage. A full cage replacement can cost $8,000-$15,000, so factor this into your offer if damage is present.
  • Insurance impact: Pool ownership affects homeowners insurance premiums and liability coverage. Discuss pool-specific coverage with your insurance agent before closing. A pool fence or cage is typically required for compliance with local safety codes.
  • Deck and drainage: Pool decks should be level, free of large cracks, and properly graded to direct water away from the home. Settling, trip hazards, and poor drainage are common issues in older pool homes.

Outdoor Living Features Beyond the Pool

In Wimauma, the pool is often just one element of a comprehensive outdoor living area. The best pool homes pair the swimming pool with features that extend the home's livable square footage into the backyard.

Lanais and Covered Patios

A screened lanai adjacent to the pool provides shaded seating, outdoor dining, and protection from afternoon rain showers. Many Wimauma homes feature extended lanais with ceiling fans, recessed lighting, and tile or travertine flooring that create a seamless indoor-outdoor transition.

Summer Kitchens

Outdoor kitchens - called summer kitchens in Florida - have become a must-have amenity in Wimauma pool homes. A typical summer kitchen includes a built-in grill, countertop space, a mini-refrigerator, and a sink. Upscale versions add pizza ovens, smokers, kegerators, and bar seating that turn the pool area into an entertainment destination.

Landscape and Lighting

Tropical landscaping, LED pool lighting, and landscape lighting create a resort atmosphere that enhances both daytime and evening enjoyment. Mature palms, birds of paradise, and jasmine hedges are popular plantings that thrive in Wimauma's climate and complement the pool setting.

Why Wimauma?

Affordable new construction with large lots, a rural feel, and proximity to Sun City Center, Apollo Beach, and the growing SouthShore corridor.

With a population of approximately 10,000, Wimauma offers a strong and diverse economy anchored by Agriculture, nearby Amazon in Riverview, growing logistics and distribution centers. The combination of employment opportunities, lifestyle amenities, and a growing real estate market makes Wimauma one of the most compelling places to buy a pool home in the Tampa Bay region.

For buyers exploring Wimauma real estate, pool homes represent an outstanding investment in both quality of life and long-term property value. Whether you are relocating from out of state, upgrading from a non-pool home, or searching for your retirement oasis, Wimauma delivers the Florida lifestyle at a price point that competes favorably with other Gulf Coast markets.

Frequently Asked Questions About Wimauma Pool Homes

How much does it cost to maintain a pool in Wimauma?

Monthly pool maintenance in Wimauma typically runs between $100 and $200 for weekly professional service, which includes chemical balancing, skimming, brushing, and equipment checks. Homeowners who maintain their own pools can reduce costs to $40-$80 per month for chemicals and supplies. Annual costs for electricity to run the pump average $600-$1,200 depending on the pump type and run time.

Do pool homes cost more to insure in Wimauma?

Yes, pool homes generally carry higher homeowners insurance premiums due to increased liability exposure. The additional cost is typically $100-$300 per year, though rates vary by insurer, pool type, and whether the pool has a safety fence or enclosure. Screen enclosures can help reduce premiums by meeting safety barrier requirements.

What is the best time to buy a pool home in Wimauma?

The best time to buy a pool home in Wimauma is typically during the late fall and winter months (November through February), when buyer competition decreases and sellers may be more willing to negotiate. However, inventory for pool homes tends to be limited year-round, so working with an experienced agent like Barrett Henry ensures you see new listings the moment they hit the market.

Should I buy a home with an existing pool or build one?

Both options have merits. Buying an existing pool home avoids the 3-6 month construction timeline and the hassle of managing a pool build project. However, building a new pool lets you customize the design, equipment, and features to your exact specifications. New pool construction in Wimauma typically costs $35,000-$80,000 depending on size, features, and site conditions. Barrett Henry can help you evaluate both options based on available inventory and your budget.

Are there HOA restrictions on pools in Wimauma?

Many neighborhoods in Wimauma have HOA guidelines that govern pool construction, including setback requirements, fence or enclosure standards, and equipment placement. Some HOAs require architectural review board approval before a pool can be built. Barrett Henry can review HOA documents and identify any restrictions before you make an offer on a property where you plan to add a pool.

  • Price escalation clauses: Some builders include clauses that allow price increases during the build process. Review your contract carefully.
  • Lot premiums: Corner lots, preserve lots, and water-view lots often carry premiums of $10K-$50K+ above the base price.
  • HOA fees: Most new construction communities have HOA fees that cover common area maintenance, amenities, and sometimes landscaping.
  • Get your own agent: The builder's sales office represents the builder, not you. Having your own Broker Associate like Barrett Henry ensures your interests are protected throughout the process.

Tips for Buying New Construction

  1. Visit multiple communities. Compare builders, floor plans, included features, and lot options before committing.
  2. Negotiate upgrades, not price. Builders often prefer to include upgrades (appliances, flooring, countertops) rather than reduce the base price.
  3. Get an independent inspection. Even new homes can have construction defects. Schedule an inspection before your final walkthrough.
  4. Review the CDD/HOA carefully. Some communities have Community Development District (CDD) fees in addition to HOA fees that add to your monthly costs.
  5. Bring your own agent. Barrett Henry can represent you at no cost - the builder pays the buyer's agent commission.

Common Questions

Do I need an agent to buy new construction?

You don't have to, but you should. The builder's sales agent works for the builder. Having your own Broker Associate protects your interests during negotiations, contract review, and the inspection process - at no extra cost to you.

How long does it take to build a new home in Wimauma?

Typical build times range from 6 to 12 months, depending on the builder, community, and level of customization. Quick-move-in inventory homes may be available in 30-90 days.

Can I negotiate with a builder?

Yes. While builders may not negotiate significantly on base price, they often offer closing cost contributions, upgrade packages, and rate buydowns - especially on inventory homes. An experienced agent knows what to ask for.

  • Little Manatee River, community lakes - the primary waterfront options in Wimauma range from open-water properties with panoramic views to canal-front homes with private dock access and lake-front properties with peaceful settings.

The type of waterfront determines not just the lifestyle but also insurance costs, maintenance requirements, and resale value. Open-water properties with direct bay or Gulf access typically command the highest premiums.

Popular Waterfront Areas

The most sought-after waterfront neighborhoods in Wimauma include areas within Waterset, Mirada nearby, South Fork area. These neighborhoods offer a mix of water types, lot sizes, and price points.

When evaluating waterfront properties, consider the water depth, seawall condition, dock permits, and whether the property offers direct open-water access or requires navigating through canals or no-wake zones.

Insurance and Flood Zone Considerations

Waterfront properties in Wimauma require careful attention to insurance costs:

  • Flood insurance: Most waterfront homes are in FEMA-designated flood zones (AE, VE, or X). Properties in AE and VE zones require flood insurance if you have a mortgage. Even X-zone properties may benefit from flood coverage.
  • Windstorm insurance: Florida's coastal areas may require separate windstorm coverage, which can add significantly to your annual costs.
  • Elevation certificates: An elevation certificate determines your flood risk and insurance premium. Properties built above the Base Flood Elevation (BFE) enjoy lower premiums.
  • Seawall assessment: If the property has a seawall, get it inspected. Seawall replacement can cost $500-$1,500 per linear foot.

Pro tip: Get insurance quotes before making an offer on any waterfront property. Insurance costs can vary by thousands of dollars between properties just blocks apart.

What Waterfront Buyers Should Know

  1. Water access matters. Not all waterfront is equal. A canal-front home with a fixed bridge may limit boat size. Open-water properties with deep-water docks offer the most flexibility.
  2. Check the seawall. A failing seawall is expensive to replace. Include a seawall inspection in your due diligence.
  3. Understand the flood zone. Your flood zone designation affects insurance costs, building requirements, and future renovation options. Request the FEMA flood zone map for any property you consider.
  4. Factor in maintenance. Waterfront properties require more maintenance - salt air corrosion, dock upkeep, seawall maintenance, and landscaping in wet conditions all add to ongoing costs.
  5. Work with a waterfront specialist. An agent who understands waterfront properties can identify issues, negotiate effectively, and connect you with marine surveyors and waterfront-specific inspectors.

Common Questions

How much does flood insurance cost in Wimauma?

Flood insurance costs in Wimauma vary widely - from $500 to $5,000+ per year depending on the flood zone, elevation, home value, and coverage limits. Properties elevated above the Base Flood Elevation typically qualify for lower premiums.

Can I put a dock on a waterfront property in Wimauma?

Most waterfront properties in Wimauma allow docks, but permits are required. The permitting process depends on the water body, dock size, and local regulations. Your agent can help you verify dock eligibility before purchase.

Are waterfront homes a good investment?

Waterfront homes in Wimauma generally appreciate well over time, as waterfront land is a finite resource. However, factor in higher insurance, maintenance, and potential storm exposure when calculating your total cost of ownership.
