title: 55+ Communities in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
Looking for 55+ communities in Tampa Bay? Tampa Bay is home to some of Florida’s largest and most established active adult communities, from Sun City Center and Kings Point in Hillsborough County to Del Webb neighborhoods in Pasco and Polk counties. With no state income tax, mild winters, and hundreds of amenities designed for adults 55 and older, Tampa Bay is one of the top retirement destinations in the country.

50+Active Adult Communities
0%State Income Tax
240+Sunny Days Per Year
8Counties Served

What Are the Best 55+ Communities in Tampa Bay?

Tampa Bay offers dozens of active adult communities across eight counties. The options range from large, self-contained retirement cities with their own shopping centers and medical offices to smaller villa developments with a clubhouse and pool. The best fit depends on your budget, lifestyle preferences, and how close you want to be to the coast, hospitals, and airports.

Sun City Center

Sun City Center is the largest and most well-known 55+ community in the Tampa Bay region. Located in unincorporated Hillsborough County between Brandon and Ruskin, Sun City Center is essentially a self-contained town. Residents have access to multiple golf courses, over 200 clubs and organizations, a performing arts center, fitness facilities, and on-site medical offices. Home prices range from the low $200s for older condos and villas to $500K+ for newer single-family homes with updated finishes.

Kings Point

Kings Point is a large gated 55+ community within the Sun City Center footprint. It operates under a separate HOA with its own clubhouse, pools, fitness center, and activities calendar. Homes in Kings Point tend to be more affordable than standalone Sun City Center properties, with condos starting in the $100s and villas in the $200s. The gated entry and maintained landscaping appeal to buyers looking for a low-maintenance, secure environment.

Del Webb Communities

Del Webb is one of the most recognized names in active adult living. In Tampa Bay, Del Webb operates communities including Del Webb Bexley in Land O’ Lakes (Pasco County) and Del Webb Lakewood Ranch near Bradenton (Manatee County). These neighborhoods feature resort-style amenities, large clubhouses, pools, pickleball courts, walking trails, and organized social events. Home prices typically range from the mid-$300s to the low $600s depending on floor plan and lot size.

Valencia Lakes

Located in Wimauma (Hillsborough County), Valencia Lakes is a GL Homes 55+ community known for its resort-style clubhouse, multiple pools, tennis and pickleball courts, and a full-time activities director. Homes range from the high $300s to the mid-$500s.

Other Notable Communities

  • Cresswind at Lake Bee, Riverview: Kolter Homes community with homes from the mid-$300s
  • Mirabella, Bradenton: Smith Douglas Homes, starting in the $300s
  • Lake Ashton, Lake Wales: Golf and lake community in Polk County
  • Summerset at Fern Hill, Riverview: 55+ section within a larger master-planned community

Find Your Ideal 55+ Community in Tampa Bay

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience and specializes in helping buyers find the right active adult community. Call (813) 733-7907 or request a consultation to discuss your goals, budget, and timeline.

What Should You Look for in a 55+ Community?

Not all active adult communities are created equal. Before committing, evaluate these factors:

  • HOA fees: Monthly fees vary from $150 to $600+. Understand exactly what is covered, lawn care, exterior maintenance, cable, insurance, amenities access.
  • Age restrictions: Most communities require at least one resident to be 55 or older. Some allow younger residents with restrictions. Review the community’s CC&Rs carefully.
  • Healthcare proximity: How close is the nearest hospital or urgent care? Sun City Center has on-site medical facilities. More remote communities may require a 20-30 minute drive.
  • Resale value: Established communities like Sun City Center have a long resale track record. Newer developments may appreciate differently.
  • Pet policies: Some communities restrict pet size or number. Confirm before you buy.

How Does Buying in a 55+ Community Differ from a Standard Purchase?

The home buying process is largely the same, inspections, appraisals, title work, and closing, but there are additional layers. You will need to review and agree to the community’s CC&Rs, which govern everything from exterior modifications to guest parking. Many communities also require buyer interviews or applications through the HOA. Your REALTOR should be familiar with these additional steps to avoid delays.

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has guided hundreds of buyers through these transitions. With 23+ years of real estate experience, Barrett understands the nuances of 55+ community purchases, from navigating HOA approval processes to comparing amenity packages across communities. Call (813) 733-7907 to get started.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can someone under 55 buy in a 55+ community?

In most 55+ communities, at least one resident in the household must be 55 or older. Some communities allow younger residents (typically 40+) as long as the primary resident meets the age requirement. Each community sets its own rules, so review the CC&Rs before making an offer.

What do HOA fees cover in 55+ communities?

HOA fees typically cover lawn and exterior maintenance, community amenity access (pools, clubhouses, fitness centers), common area upkeep, and sometimes cable, internet, or basic home insurance. Fees range from $150 to $600+ per month depending on the community and what is included.

Are 55+ communities a good investment?

Established 55+ communities in Tampa Bay have historically maintained strong resale values due to consistent demand from retirees relocating to Florida. Communities in desirable locations near healthcare, shopping, and major roads tend to appreciate steadily. However, like any real estate purchase, market conditions and community management quality affect long-term value.

What is the cheapest 55+ community in Tampa Bay?

Kings Point in Sun City Center typically offers the lowest entry point, with condos starting in the low $100s. These are older units that may need updating, but the community amenities and gated security are included. For newer construction, Cresswind at Lake Bee in Riverview and some sections of Valencia Lakes offer homes starting in the mid-$300s.

title: Best Neighborhoods for Families in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
Where should families live in Tampa Bay? The best neighborhoods for families combine top-rated schools, low crime rates, parks and recreation, and reasonable home prices. Areas like Westchase, FishHawk Ranch, Valrico, and Wesley Chapel consistently rank among the top choices for families relocating to Tampa Bay.

A-RatedSchool Districts Available
8Counties to Choose From
$350K to $550KFamily Home Price Range
240+Sunny Days Per Year

What Makes a Tampa Bay Neighborhood Great for Families?

Choosing where to raise your family comes down to schools, safety, community feel, and access to the things your family uses daily, parks, grocery stores, pediatricians, and commute routes. Tampa Bay has dozens of family-friendly neighborhoods across its eight counties, but not all areas are equal.

School quality varies significantly by district and individual school. Hillsborough, Pasco, and Pinellas counties each operate their own school systems with different rating profiles. Many families also consider proximity to private and charter schools. Crime data, HOA community standards, and neighborhood age all factor into the decision.

Top Family Neighborhoods in Hillsborough County

FishHawk Ranch, Lithia

FishHawk Ranch is one of the most sought-after master-planned communities for families in Tampa Bay. Located in Lithia, it features top-rated schools within walking distance, miles of trails, multiple community pools, sports fields, and a vibrant town center. Homes range from the mid-$300s to over $700K. The community is zoned for highly rated Hillsborough County schools including Bevis Elementary and Newsome High School.

Westchase

Westchase is a master-planned community in northwest Hillsborough County known for its excellent schools, well-maintained common areas, and family-oriented events. The community has its own swim and tennis center, multiple parks, and a commercial village with restaurants and shops. Homes range from the $400s to $800K+. Westchase is zoned for some of the highest-rated schools in Hillsborough County.

Valrico and Brandon

Valrico and Brandon offer a balance of affordability, school quality, and convenience. Located east of Tampa with direct access to I-75 and the Crosstown Expressway, these communities provide shorter commutes than many suburban alternatives. Home prices range from the $300s to $500s in most neighborhoods. Families here have access to Bloomingdale and Durant high school zones, both well-regarded in the county.

Top Family Neighborhoods in Pasco County

Wesley Chapel

Wesley Chapel has seen explosive growth over the past decade and is now one of the most popular family destinations in Tampa Bay. The Wiregrass and Epperson communities offer new construction from major builders, resort-style amenity centers, and A-rated schools. The Tampa Premium Outlets, AdventHealth medical center, and a growing retail corridor make daily life convenient. Homes range from the $300s to $600s.

Land O’ Lakes

Land O’ Lakes provides a more rural feel while still being within commuting distance of Tampa. Communities like Bexley and Connerton offer new construction with modern amenities. School ratings are strong, and the area has easy access to the Suncoast Parkway for commuters heading south to Tampa or north to Hernando County. Homes range from the low $300s to $500K+.

Top Family Neighborhoods in Pinellas County

Safety Harbor and Oldsmar

Safety Harbor and Oldsmar offer small-town charm with access to excellent Pinellas County schools. Safety Harbor’s walkable downtown, waterfront parks, and tight-knit community feel attract families who want a less suburban environment. Oldsmar provides slightly more affordable housing with newer subdivisions. Homes in both areas range from the $350s to $600K.

Find the Right Neighborhood for Your Family

Barrett Henry has 23+ years of real estate experience helping families find the right community in Tampa Bay. Whether you need top-rated schools, a short commute, or a specific price range, Barrett can narrow your search. Call (813) 733-7907 or schedule a consultation.

How Do Tampa Bay School Districts Compare?

Hillsborough County is the eighth-largest school district in the nation with over 200,000 students. Pasco County has grown rapidly and has invested heavily in new school construction. Pinellas County offers magnet and choice programs that allow families to apply to schools outside their zone. All three counties have a mix of A, B, and C-rated schools, the key is knowing which neighborhoods feed into the top-performing campuses.

Beyond public schools, Tampa Bay has a strong network of private and charter school options including Academy at the Lakes, Berkeley Preparatory School, and Corbett Preparatory School. Your REALTOR should understand school zoning and help you verify current assignments, which can change year to year.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the safest neighborhood for families in Tampa Bay?

Master-planned communities with HOA oversight tend to have the lowest crime rates. FishHawk Ranch, Westchase, and Bexley in Land O’ Lakes consistently rank among the safest. Gated communities provide additional security. Always check current crime data from the county sheriff’s office for specific addresses.

Where are the best schools in Tampa Bay?

Top-rated elementary and middle schools are concentrated in FishHawk Ranch, Westchase, Valrico, and Wesley Chapel. High school ratings vary, Newsome, Steinbrenner, and Wiregrass Ranch are among the highest-rated public high schools. Always verify current school assignments with the county school district before purchasing.

How much does a family home cost in Tampa Bay?

A typical 3-4 bedroom single-family home in a family-friendly neighborhood ranges from $350,000 to $550,000 depending on location, age, and community amenities. Newer construction in Wesley Chapel and FishHawk tends to be at the higher end, while Brandon and parts of Riverview offer more affordable options in the $300s.

Is Tampa Bay a good place to raise kids?

Yes. Tampa Bay offers a combination of outdoor recreation year-round, strong school options, affordable housing compared to other major Florida metros, and a growing job market. The region has theme parks, beaches, professional sports teams, museums, and nature preserves, all within a short drive. The main considerations are hurricane preparedness and choosing the right school zone for your children.

title: Cost of Living in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
How much does it cost to live in Tampa Bay? Tampa Bay’s cost of living is approximately 3-5% above the national average, driven primarily by housing and insurance costs. However, Florida has no state income tax, which offsets those costs significantly for many households. Median home prices range from $295,000 to $448,000 depending on the county, and property taxes average 0.86% of assessed value.

0%State Income Tax
$350KMedian Home Price
0.86%Avg Property Tax Rate
$2,800Avg Annual Home Insurance

How Does Tampa Bay Compare to Other Major Cities?

Tampa Bay is more affordable than Miami, Orlando’s coastal areas, and most Northeastern and West Coast metros. A household earning $100,000 in Tampa Bay keeps more of that income than the same household in New York, California, or Illinois because Florida has no state income tax. That single factor can represent $4,000 to $8,000 in annual savings depending on income level and the state you are leaving.

Compared to the national average, Tampa Bay’s housing costs are slightly above average, groceries are roughly at the national average, and healthcare costs are close to the national median. The area where Tampa Bay is notably more expensive is property insurance, Florida’s homeowners insurance market has seen significant rate increases since 2020.

What Does Housing Cost in Tampa Bay?

Housing is the largest cost category for most households. Median home prices across Tampa Bay’s eight counties vary significantly:

CountyMedian Home PriceTypical Range
Hillsborough$385,000$280K to $600K
Pinellas$375,000$260K to $550K
Pasco$340,000$250K to $480K
Manatee$420,000$300K to $650K
Sarasota$448,000$320K to $700K
Hernando$312,000$220K to $420K
Polk$315,000$230K to $440K
Citrus$295,000$200K to $400K

Renters can expect to pay $1,600 to $2,200 per month for a two-bedroom apartment in Hillsborough or Pinellas counties. Pasco, Hernando, and Polk counties tend to run $200 to $400 less per month for comparable units.

What About Property Taxes in Florida?

Florida’s property tax system includes a homestead exemption that reduces your taxable value by $50,000 for primary residences. Beyond that, the Save Our Homes cap limits annual assessed value increases to 3% or the Consumer Price Index, whichever is lower. This means long-term homeowners often pay significantly less in property taxes than their home’s current market value would suggest.

Effective property tax rates in Tampa Bay counties range from approximately 0.75% to 1.1% of assessed value. Hillsborough County tends to be on the higher end, while Pasco and Hernando counties are typically lower.

How Much Is Homeowners Insurance in Tampa Bay?

This is the cost category that surprises most newcomers. Florida’s homeowners insurance market has experienced major disruption, with several carriers leaving the state and premiums rising sharply. The average annual premium in Tampa Bay ranges from $2,400 to $3,500 depending on the home’s age, roof condition, location relative to the coast, and coverage limits. Flood insurance is separate and required for homes in FEMA-designated flood zones, that adds $500 to $2,000+ annually.

Buyers should get insurance quotes before finalizing a purchase. Your REALTOR and lender can help you understand the full cost picture before you commit.

Get a Complete Cost Breakdown for Your Tampa Bay Move

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, helps buyers understand the true cost of living in Tampa Bay, not just the purchase price. With 23+ years of real estate experience, Barrett provides detailed neighborhood comparisons. Call (813) 733-7907 or reach out online.

What About Utilities and Daily Expenses?

Monthly utilities for a typical 1,500-square-foot home average $200 to $300, with electricity being the largest component. Tampa Electric (TECO) serves Hillsborough County, while Duke Energy covers Pinellas and Pasco. Summer electric bills can spike due to air conditioning, expect $250+ during June through September.

Groceries are roughly at the national average. Gas prices tend to run slightly below the national average. Healthcare costs are in line with national medians, though Florida’s insurance marketplace premiums vary by county and age.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tampa Bay cheaper than Miami?

Yes. Tampa Bay’s housing costs are approximately 25-35% lower than Miami-Dade County. Insurance costs are comparable, but the overall cost of living, including groceries, dining, and transportation, is lower in Tampa Bay. Both areas benefit from Florida’s zero state income tax.

What salary do you need to live comfortably in Tampa Bay?

A household income of $75,000 to $90,000 provides a comfortable lifestyle for a single person or couple in most Tampa Bay communities. Families with children should target $100,000+ to comfortably afford a home in a top-rated school zone, insurance, childcare, and daily expenses.

Does Florida have any state taxes?

Florida has no state income tax. However, the state does collect a 6% sales tax (with county surtaxes adding 0.5% to 2.5%), property taxes, and documentary stamp taxes on real estate transactions. There is no estate or inheritance tax at the state level.

How much is car insurance in Tampa Bay?

Florida has some of the highest auto insurance rates in the nation. Tampa Bay drivers typically pay $1,800 to $2,800 annually for full coverage, depending on driving record, vehicle, and coverage limits. This is higher than the national average and should be factored into your cost-of-living calculations.

title: Gated Communities in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
Searching for gated communities in Tampa Bay? Tampa Bay has hundreds of gated neighborhoods ranging from luxury estate communities to affordable townhome developments. Gated communities offer controlled access, lower traffic, and often include amenities like pools, clubhouses, and fitness centers. Popular options include FishHawk Ranch, Waterchase, MiraBay, and Tampa Palms.

200+Gated Communities
$250K to $2M+Price Range
8Counties Served
24/7Controlled Access

Why Choose a Gated Community in Tampa Bay?

Gated communities provide a layer of security and privacy that open neighborhoods do not. Controlled access points, whether staffed guard gates, key fob systems, or coded entries, limit who enters the community. This reduces through traffic, solicitors, and opportunistic crime. Beyond security, gated communities often maintain higher property values because of consistent HOA enforcement, landscaped common areas, and community amenities.

The trade-off is HOA fees. Monthly dues in gated communities typically range from $150 to $500+ depending on the amenities and services included. Guard-gated communities with staffed entrances cost more than those with electronic access only. Buyers should review HOA financials, reserves, and rules before purchasing.

Top Gated Communities in Hillsborough County

MiraBay, Apollo Beach

MiraBay in Apollo Beach is a guard-gated waterfront community with a private beach club, resort-style pool, marina, fitness center, and tennis courts. Homes range from the $400s to over $1.5 million. The community sits on Tampa Bay with direct boating access and is zoned for well-rated Hillsborough County schools.

Waterchase, Tampa

Waterchase is a gated community in the Westchase area of northwest Tampa. The neighborhood features a community pool, playground, and walking trails within a secure gated perimeter. Homes range from the $400s to $700K. The location provides easy access to Veterans Expressway, Tampa International Airport, and the Westchase commercial district.

Tampa Palms

Tampa Palms is one of Tampa’s oldest and most established master-planned communities, with multiple gated sections including Tampa Palms Country Club. Homes range from the $300s to $800K+. The community is close to the University of South Florida, AdventHealth, and I-75 access.

Top Gated Communities in Pasco County

Bexley, Land O’ Lakes

Bexley in Land O’ Lakes is a newer master-planned community with both gated and non-gated sections. The community features a unique adventure-themed amenity center with a treehouse, zip line, kayak launch, and resort pool. Homes range from the $300s to $600K from builders including Pulte and Taylor Morrison.

Epperson, Wesley Chapel

Epperson in Wesley Chapel features Florida’s first Crystal Lagoon, a swimmable, turquoise lagoon in the center of the community. Gated sections offer new construction from multiple builders with homes starting in the mid-$300s.

Tour Gated Communities in Tampa Bay

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has 23+ years of real estate experience and can help you compare gated communities based on your priorities, security level, amenities, school zones, and budget. Call (813) 733-7907 or schedule a tour.

What to Know Before Buying in a Gated Community

  • HOA fees and what they cover: Ask for a complete breakdown. Some HOAs cover landscaping, exterior maintenance, and insurance; others cover only gate maintenance and common areas.
  • HOA financial health: Request the most recent financial statements and reserve study. Underfunded reserves can lead to special assessments.
  • Rules and restrictions: Some communities restrict rental periods, vehicle types (boats, RVs), exterior colors, and landscaping changes. Read the CC&Rs before you buy.
  • Guest access: How do visitors enter? Some communities require advance registration; others have a call-in system at the gate.
  • Gate type: Staffed guard gates provide the highest level of access control. Unmanned gates with key fobs or codes offer convenience but less security.

Frequently Asked Questions

Are gated communities safer than non-gated neighborhoods?

Studies generally show that gated communities experience lower rates of property crime than comparable non-gated neighborhoods. The controlled access reduces opportunistic crime by limiting entry to residents and authorized guests. However, gates are not a guarantee of safety, they are one layer of a broader security approach.

Do gated communities hold their value better?

In most Tampa Bay markets, gated communities maintain and appreciate property values at rates equal to or slightly above comparable non-gated neighborhoods. The combination of controlled access, HOA-maintained common areas, and consistent architectural standards supports long-term value retention.

What is the cheapest gated community in Tampa Bay?

Affordable gated options include townhome and condo communities in Riverview, Brandon, and parts of Pasco County, with prices starting in the $200s. Single-family gated communities in Hillsborough County typically start in the $300s.

Can I rent out my home in a gated community?

Many gated communities allow rentals, but most have restrictions. Common rules include minimum lease terms (typically 6-12 months), a maximum number of rental permits per year, and HOA approval of tenants. Some communities prohibit short-term or vacation rentals entirely. Always verify rental policies in the CC&Rs before purchasing if you plan to rent the property.

title: Moving to Tampa Bay Guide | Barrett Henry
content:
Thinking about moving to Tampa Bay? Tampa Bay is one of the fastest-growing metropolitan areas in the United States, drawing new residents with no state income tax, 240+ sunny days per year, a growing job market, and home prices that remain more affordable than Miami and most Northeastern metros.

3.2M+Metro Population
0%State Income Tax
240+Sunny Days Per Year
$350KMedian Home Price

Why Are So Many People Moving to Tampa Bay?

Florida’s zero state income tax saves most households $3,000 to $8,000 per year compared to states like New York, California, Illinois, and New Jersey. The climate delivers mild winters and year-round outdoor access. The job market has diversified beyond tourism into healthcare, finance, technology, and defense.

Housing costs remain significantly lower than comparable metros. A 2,000-square-foot home in a good school zone that would cost $700K+ in the Northeast sells for $350,000 to $500,000 in Tampa Bay communities like Valrico, Riverview, and Wesley Chapel.

Where Should You Live in Tampa Bay?

Tampa Bay spans eight counties with dramatically different personalities:

  • Urban living: Downtown Tampa, South Tampa, St. Petersburg, walkable, restaurants and nightlife, higher price points
  • Suburban families: Brandon, Valrico, FishHawk Ranch, Westchase, Wesley Chapel top schools, $350K-$600K
  • Beach access: Clearwater, St. Pete Beach coastal lifestyle, higher insurance
  • Affordable growth: Riverview, Zephyrhills, Plant City new construction, lower entry points
  • Retirement: Sun City Center, Del Webb, see 55+ guide

What Is the Job Market Like?

Major employers include BayCare, AdventHealth, Tampa General Hospital (healthcare), USAA, JPMorgan Chase, Citi (finance), MacDill Air Force Base (defense), and a growing tech sector. Remote workers keep higher salaries while benefiting from Florida’s lower cost of living and zero income tax.

What Should You Know About Weather?

Summers are hot and humid, daily highs in the low-to-mid 90s with afternoon thunderstorms. Winters bring daytime highs in the 70s with low humidity. Hurricane season runs June 1 through November 30. Every homeowner should carry proper insurance and understand their evacuation zone.

Planning Your Move to Tampa Bay?

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has 23+ years of real estate experience and has helped hundreds of families relocate. Call (813) 733-7907 or start a conversation online.

What Surprises Newcomers?

  • Insurance costs: Homeowners insurance is significantly higher than national average. See the cost of living guide.
  • Traffic: I-275 and I-4 are among the most congested corridors in Florida.
  • Summer humidity: Air conditioning is not optional.

For a step-by-step plan, see the Moving to Tampa Bay Checklist.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Tampa Bay a good place to live?

Tampa Bay consistently ranks among the top metro areas for quality of life, job growth, and affordability. No state income tax, year-round outdoor recreation, professional sports, beaches, and a growing economy make it one of the most popular relocation destinations.

How long does it take to buy a home?

From initial search to closing, most buyers take 60-90 days. Cash buyers can close in 14-21 days. Conventional and FHA loans require 30-45 days from contract to close.

Should I rent or buy when moving?

Renting for 6-12 months helps learn neighborhoods, but a two-bedroom apartment runs $1,600 to $2,200 per month. Many buyers with clear needs buy immediately with an experienced REALTOR.

What is the best time of year to move?

October through March offers mild weather but higher competition. Summer months have more inventory and less competition, but intense heat makes moving harder.

  • Register your vehicle within 30 days. Get Florida plates and insurance.

  • Register to vote at RegisterToVoteFlorida.gov.
  • Find healthcare: BayCare, AdventHealth, Tampa General are major systems.

Let Barrett Henry Simplify Your Move

Do Not Forget: Homestead Exemption

The homestead exemption reduces your taxable value by up to $50,000 and caps annual assessment increases at 3%. File by March 1 of the year following your purchase. Hillsborough: HCPAFL.org. Pasco: PascoPA.com. Missing the deadline costs you the full benefit for that tax year.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does closing take in Florida?

30-45 days financed, 14-21 days cash. New construction: 30 days (completed) to 6-12 months (build-to-order).

What do I need for a Florida driver’s license?

One primary ID, proof of Social Security number, and two proofs of residential address. Fee is approximately $48.

When should I file for homestead exemption?

Between January 1 and March 1 of the year following your purchase. Filing is free and available online through your county Property Appraiser.

How much does an interstate move cost?

title: Pre-Foreclosure Homes in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
What is a pre-foreclosure? A pre-foreclosure is a property where the homeowner has fallen behind on mortgage payments and the lender has filed a lis pendens, but the foreclosure sale has not yet occurred. Buyers can sometimes purchase these properties at below-market prices, but the process requires patience, negotiation skill, and understanding of Florida foreclosure law.

Lis PendensLegal Filing Starts Process
6 to 18 MoTypical FL Timeline
JudicialFL Foreclosure Type
Court OrderRequired for Sale

How Does Pre-Foreclosure Work in Florida?

Florida uses a judicial foreclosure process, every foreclosure must go through the court system. The pre-foreclosure stage begins when the lender files a lis pendens and ends when the property is sold at auction, purchased by a third party, or the homeowner resolves the default. During this period, the homeowner still owns the property and has the right to sell it.

How Can You Find Pre-Foreclosure Properties?

  • County Clerk of Court websites: Hillsborough, Pinellas, Pasco clerks maintain searchable lis pendens databases.
  • MLS listings: Some are listed as short sales or bank-approved sales.
  • Direct outreach: Some agents contact homeowners in pre-foreclosure to discuss options.

What Are the Risks?

  • Title issues: Multiple liens, second mortgages, tax liens, HOA liens, judgment liens.
  • Property condition: Deferred maintenance is common. Inspections are critical.
  • Uncertain timelines: If it involves a short sale, the process can take 3-12 months.
  • Emotional complexity: The homeowner is in a difficult situation. Negotiations require sensitivity.

Navigate Pre-Foreclosure Purchases with Expert Guidance

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has 23+ years of real estate experience including distressed property transactions. Call (813) 733-7907 or get in touch.

Pre-Foreclosure vs. Foreclosure: What Is the Difference?

StageWho Owns ItHow to Buy
Pre-ForeclosureHomeownerNegotiate with homeowner (and lender if short sale)
Foreclosure AuctionTransitioningBid at courthouse, cash only, no inspection
REO (Bank-Owned)LenderPurchase through MLS listing

Should Homeowners in Pre-Foreclosure Consider Selling?

Selling before the foreclosure sale can protect your credit and give you more control. In many cases, the home has enough equity for a standard sale. If underwater, a short sale may be an option. Call (813) 733-7907 for a confidential conversation.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you buy a pre-foreclosure with a mortgage?

Yes, if the homeowner agrees to a standard sale or lender-approved short sale. Conventional, FHA, and VA financing all work. Cash offers are stronger but not required.

How much can you save?

Savings vary widely. Some sell at market value; others (particularly short sales) may sell 5-20% below market depending on condition, motivation, and lender willingness.

How long does pre-foreclosure last in Florida?

Typically 6-18 months from lis pendens to sale, though contested cases can extend beyond two years. The homeowner retains ownership throughout.

Is buying pre-foreclosure ethical?

Yes, when done properly. A fair-market purchase helps homeowners avoid foreclosure and protect their credit. Work with a licensed REALTOR who conducts these transactions professionally.

title: Short Sales in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
What is a short sale? A short sale occurs when a homeowner sells for less than the mortgage balance, with lender approval. The lender accepts less than full payoff to avoid foreclosure costs. Short sales can offer buyers below-market prices, but the process is slower and more complex than standard transactions.

3 to 6 MoAverage Approval Time
LenderMust Approve Price
5 to 20%Potential Savings
As-IsTypical Condition

How Does a Short Sale Work?

  1. Listing and offer (Week 1-4): Home listed below market value. Buyers submit offers.
  2. Seller submits to lender (Week 2-6): Short sale package including financials, hardship letter, and contract.
  3. Lender review (Month 2-4): BPO or appraisal ordered, offer evaluated against loan balance.
  4. Lender response (Month 3-6): May approve, counter, or deny. Multiple lien holders each approve separately.
  5. Closing (30-45 days after approval): Standard closing with inspections and title work.

What Should Buyers Know?

  • Timeline uncertainty: Wait 3-6 months for approval. The lender can reject your offer at any time.
  • As-is condition: Budget for repairs and deferred maintenance.
  • Multiple offers: Lenders sometimes solicit additional offers during review.
  • Title issues: Additional liens (HOA, tax, judgment) must be resolved.

Need Help Navigating a Short Sale?

Barrett Henry, Broker Associate at REMAX Collective, has 23+ years of real estate experience including short sale transactions. Call (813) 733-7907 or contact Barrett.

How Does a Short Sale Affect the Seller?

  • Credit impact: Less severe than foreclosure. Generally 50-150 point drop recovering over 2-4 years.
  • Deficiency judgment: In Florida, lenders can pursue the difference. Many waive this in the approval letter.
  • Tax implications: Forgiven debt may be taxable. Consult a tax professional.
  • Future purchase: Eligible for conventional mortgage after 4 years (2 with extenuating circumstances), FHA after 3 years.

Short Sale vs. Pre-Foreclosure vs. Foreclosure

FactorShort SalePre-ForeclosureForeclosure
SellerHomeowner (with lender approval)HomeownerCourt/Bank
Timeline3-6 months for approvalVariesCourt-set auction date
InspectionsYes (typically as-is)YesNo (auction)
FinancingAvailableAvailableCash only (auction)

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you negotiate a short sale price?

The initial offer is negotiated with the homeowner, but the lender has final say. The lender orders an independent valuation and typically will not approve significantly below that value. Price competitively, lowball offers waste months.

Can you inspect a short sale?

Yes. You have the right to inspect, though most are sold as-is. The inspection helps budget for repairs. You can withdraw before lender approval if major issues are found.

Why do short sales take so long?

The lender’s loss mitigation department handles high volume. Each requires financial analysis, property valuation, and internal approval. Multiple lien holders double the timeline.

Is a short sale a good deal?

Potentially, prices are typically 5-20% below market. The trade-offs are timeline uncertainty, as-is condition, and possible deal failure. Best for buyers with patience and flexibility.

title: VA Home Loans in Tampa Bay | Barrett Henry
content:
Are you a veteran or active-duty service member? VA home loans offer zero down payment, no PMI, competitive interest rates, and limited closing costs. Tampa Bay’s proximity to MacDill Air Force Base makes it one of Florida’s top destinations for military families and veterans.

$0Down Payment
No PMINo Mortgage Insurance
LowerInterest Rates
ReusableBenefit

What Are the Benefits?

  • Zero down payment: Finance 100% of the purchase price.
  • No PMI: Saves $100-$300+ per month vs. conventional with less than 20% down.
  • Competitive rates: Typically 0.25-0.50% lower than conventional.
  • Limited closing costs: Sellers can contribute up to 4% toward closing.
  • No prepayment penalty.
  • Reusable benefit: Use it multiple times throughout your life.

Who Is Eligible?

  • 90 consecutive days active service during wartime
  • 181 days active service during peacetime
  • 6 years National Guard or Reserves
  • Surviving spouse of service member who died in line of duty

Verify eligibility with a Certificate of Eligibility (COE) through your lender or the VA’s eBenefits portal.

Why Is Tampa Bay Ideal for VA Buyers?

  • MacDill Air Force Base: CENTCOM and SOCOM headquarters
  • James A. Haley VA Hospital: One of the largest VA medical centers nationally
  • Bay Pines VA Healthcare: Comprehensive services in Pinellas County
  • Military-friendly communities: Brandon, Riverview, Valrico are popular with military families
  • Florida veterans’ benefits: Property tax exemptions for disabled veterans, no state income tax on military retirement

Work with a Military Relocation Professional

Barrett Henry holds the Military Relocation Professional (MRP) designation and has 23+ years of real estate experience. Barrett understands VA loan requirements and military PCS timelines. Call (813) 733-7907 or connect online.

What Should VA Buyers Know About This Market?

  • VA appraisal requirements: Properties must meet Minimum Property Requirements (MPRs). Older homes may need repairs to pass.
  • Seller perception: Some sellers view VA offers as weaker. An experienced REALTOR addresses their concerns.
  • VA funding fee: 1.25% to 3.3% of loan amount (can be financed). Disabled veterans exempt.
  • Closing timeline: 30-45 days, similar to conventional loans.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I use a VA loan for a condo?

Yes, but the condo project must be VA-approved. Check the VA’s approved condo list before making an offer.

Can I use my VA benefit more than once?

Yes. Your benefit can be restored after paying off a previous VA loan. You can also have two VA loans simultaneously with remaining entitlement.

What credit score do I need?

The VA sets no minimum, but lenders typically require 580-620+. Higher scores get better rates. Shop multiple VA-approved lenders.

What is the VA funding fee?

A one-time fee: 2.15% first use with zero down, 3.3% subsequent use. Reduced with larger down payments. Waived entirely for veterans with service-connected disabilities.

title: Mainlands: Pinellas Park, FL
content:
Quick Answer: Mainlands is one of the largest and most established residential communities in Pinellas Park, FL. Built primarily in the 1960s and 1970s, the neighborhood spans several sections (Mainlands 1-6) and offers affordable single-family homes, many with Florida rooms, carports, and mature landscaping. Median home prices in Mainlands range from $225,000 to $325,000, making it one of the most affordable entry points in Pinellas County.

What Makes Mainlands a Good Place to Live?

Mainlands is a sprawling residential community in Pinellas Park that has been a staple of Pinellas County living for over 50 years. The neighborhood is divided into several sections, commonly referred to as Mainlands 1 through 6, each with its own civic association and community character. The sections share a common identity as affordable, well-established neighborhoods with easy access to the beaches, downtown St. Petersburg, and the broader Tampa Bay metro.

The community is popular with first-time buyers, retirees, and investors due to its competitive pricing relative to the rest of Pinellas County. Many homes in Mainlands offer 2-3 bedrooms, Florida rooms or enclosed patios, single-car carports, and larger lots than you would find in newer construction. Updated homes with modern kitchens, new roofs, and impact windows command premiums but still remain well below the Pinellas County median.

What Are Homes Like in Mainlands?

Most homes in Mainlands are concrete block construction, the standard for Florida homes built in the 1960s and 1970s. Typical floor plans range from 900 to 1,400 square feet with 2-3 bedrooms and 1-2 bathrooms. Many homes have been updated over the years with new kitchens, bathrooms, flooring, and roofs. Screened-in Florida rooms and enclosed porches are common additions that add usable living space.

Lot sizes in Mainlands are generally generous by Pinellas County standards, with many properties offering fenced backyards, mature fruit trees, and room for pools. The neighborhood has a mix of owner-occupied homes and rental properties, with strong rental demand from the area's proximity to beaches and employment centers.

Where Is Mainlands Located?

Mainlands is located in Pinellas Park, centrally positioned in Pinellas County. The community sits south of Park Boulevard and west of US-19, providing quick access to:

  • St. Petersburg 10 minutes south
  • Clearwater and Clearwater Beach, 15 minutes north
  • Seminole and Largo 5-10 minutes west
  • Madeira Beach and the Gulf beaches, 15-20 minutes west
  • Tampa, 30-40 minutes east via I-275

What About HOA and Community Fees?

Each section of Mainlands has its own civic association with modest annual dues, typically $50-$150 per year, far less than the HOA fees in newer communities. The civic associations maintain common areas, organize community events, and represent residents on local issues. There are no CDDs (Community Development Districts) in Mainlands.

Is Mainlands a Good Investment?

Mainlands offers strong investment potential for several reasons. The low entry price point combined with Pinellas County's high rental demand creates favorable cash-on-cash returns. Properties that have been updated with new roofs, kitchens, and impact windows can command $1,400-$1,800/month in rent, delivering cap rates in the 5-7% range depending on purchase price and condition.

The area's central Pinellas location, beach proximity, and affordability ensure consistent tenant demand from both long-term renters and seasonal residents.

Frequently Asked Questions About Mainlands

What is the average home price in Mainlands?

Homes in Mainlands typically range from $225,000 to $325,000 depending on size, condition, and updates. Fully renovated homes with new roofs and impact windows can reach $350,000+.

Is Mainlands in a flood zone?

Some sections of Mainlands are in FEMA flood zones, which requires flood insurance for financed purchases. Check the specific property's flood zone designation before making an offer. Barrett can help you verify this during the buying process.

Are there age restrictions in Mainlands?

No, Mainlands is NOT an age-restricted community. It is open to buyers and renters of all ages, including families with children.

What school zone is Mainlands in?

Mainlands is served by Pinellas County Schools. Specific school assignments depend on the section and should be verified through the Pinellas County Schools website.

title: Bayshore Beautiful, South Tampa FL
content:
Bayshore Beautiful, South Tampa's Waterfront Gem

Perched along Tampa Bay's southern shore, Bayshore Beautiful is one of the most coveted residential enclaves in all of South Tampa. The neighborhood has earned recognition from Forbes, HGTV, and multiple national publications as one of Tampa's premier luxury communities, and for good reason. It delivers something rare: genuine waterfront tranquility just minutes from everything urban Tampa has to offer.

Architecture and Character

Bayshore Beautiful blends mid-century charm with modern luxury. Some of the neighborhood's finest homes date to the 1960s, well-built concrete block construction with the kind of architectural detail that doesn't get replicated in modern subdivisions. Alongside these originals, you'll find newer custom builds and thoughtful renovations that respect the neighborhood's established character. The result is a streetscape with real variety and personality, where no two homes look alike.

The lots here are generous by South Tampa standards, with mature landscaping providing privacy and shade. Many properties feature detached garages, circular driveways, and the kind of setbacks that give homes room to breathe, a luxury in a market where teardowns are increasingly replaced by lot-line-to-lot-line new construction.

The Bayshore Boulevard Lifestyle

What truly sets Bayshore Beautiful apart is its position along the tail end of Bayshore Boulevard, the world's longest continuous sidewalk at 4.5 miles. Residents step out their doors to stunning bay views, runners, cyclists, and some of the most photographed sunsets in Florida. The daily ritual of walking, jogging, or cycling along Bayshore isn't just exercise, it's the neighborhood's social fabric.

From Bayshore Beautiful, you're a short drive or bike ride to Hyde Park Village for shopping and dining, Downtown Tampa's Riverwalk and cultural district, and the SoHo corridor's restaurants and nightlife. MacDill Air Force Base is also nearby, making this a popular choice for senior military officers and defense contractors.

Home Values in 2026

  • Single-family homes: $600K to $7 million+ for Bayshore Boulevard-fronting estates
  • Average single-family sale price: just under $1.7 million
  • Waterfront estates: $3M to $7M+ with direct bay views and private docks
  • Interior lots: $600K to $1.5M, still luxury, with more approachable entry points

Most purchases here require a jumbo loan. Barrett works with portfolio lenders experienced in South Tampa waterfront transactions. Use the mortgage calculator for payment estimates.

Flood Insurance and Waterfront Considerations

Properties along Bayshore Boulevard may fall in FEMA flood zones AE or VE, requiring flood insurance ($1,500 to $5,000+/year depending on elevation and coverage). Barrett helps buyers evaluate flood risk, insurance costs, and elevation certificates before making an offer. Seawall condition is another critical factor for bayfront properties, replacement costs $300 to $800 per linear foot.

Schools and Families

Despite its luxury price point, Bayshore Beautiful is a genuinely family-friendly community. The neighborhood is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools with zoning for some of South Tampa's most sought-after campuses, including Plant High School. Private school options nearby include Berkeley Preparatory, Tampa Preparatory, and Academy of the Holy Names.

Culbreath Isles, Deep-Water Canal Living in South Tampa

Culbreath Isles is South Tampa's boating community, a neighborhood of waterfront homes along deep-water canals with direct access to Hillsborough Bay and the Gulf of Mexico. If you want to keep your boat in your backyard, fish from your dock, and cruise to the Bahamas on a long weekend, Culbreath Isles is where you do it. The neighborhood sits along the western shore of the Interbay peninsula, offering some of the most functional waterfront in all of Tampa.

Waterfront and Homes

The canal system in Culbreath Isles provides deep-water access, no bridges to duck under, no shallow drafts to navigate. Homes along the canals feature private docks, boat lifts, and direct sailboat-depth water access to Tampa Bay. The housing stock ranges from well-maintained 1960s, 1980s waterfront homes to fully renovated and custom-built modern estates. Even non-waterfront homes in the neighborhood benefit from the boating lifestyle and the premium location.

Home Values in 2026

  • Waterfront canal homes: $1.2M to $4 million+
  • Average single-family sale price: approximately $1.5 million
  • Non-waterfront interior lots: $800K to $1.3M
  • Key value drivers: dock condition, seawall age, water depth, lot width

Jumbo financing is standard. Waterfront purchases require additional due diligence on seawalls ($300 to $800/linear ft replacement), dock permits, and flood insurance. Barrett coordinates marine surveys and seawall inspections as part of every waterfront transaction.

Boating Access

  • Deep-water canals no fixed bridges, sailboat accessible
  • Tampa Bay minutes to open water
  • Gulf of Mexico through the Egmont Channel
  • Bahamas/Keys weekend cruising distance for serious boaters

Location

Culbreath Isles is minutes from MacDill Air Force Base (popular with military officers), Dale Mabry Highway shopping and dining, and Gandy Bridge to St. Petersburg. The neighborhood is zoned for Plant High School, one of Tampa's most sought-after public high schools.

title: Davis Islands, Tampa FL
content:
Davis Islands, Tampa's Premier Island Community

Davis Islands is a pair of man-made islands in Hillsborough Bay, connected to Downtown Tampa by a short bridge. The community offers something almost impossible to find elsewhere in Tampa: genuine island living with a 5-minute drive to the business district. With its own airport (Peter O. Knight), yacht club, public beach, pool complex, tennis courts, and dog park, Davis Islands operates as a self-contained village, except with a major metro skyline as the backdrop.

Architecture and Homes

The island's architectural diversity is remarkable. Mediterranean Revival homes from the 1920s and '30s sit alongside mid-century ranches, contemporary waterfront estates, and tasteful new construction. The mix creates streetscapes with real character, no cookie-cutter subdivisions here. Waterfront properties along the seawall command the highest premiums, with unobstructed views of Hillsborough Bay and the downtown Tampa skyline.

Home Values in 2026

Schools

title: Hyde Park, South Tampa FL
content:
Why Hyde Park Is One of Tampa's Most Desired Neighborhoods

Hyde Park is truly one of Tampa's most highly desired neighborhoods for a plethora of reasons. It is known for its rich architecture and abundance of incredible things to do, all within walking distance. From Hyde Park Village, which is an outdoor shopping and dining experience, to being located in close proximity to Downtown Tampa and just steps from Bayshore Boulevard, Hyde Park offers a lifestyle that few Tampa neighborhoods can match.

Historic Charm and Architecture

Hyde Park is considered a historic neighborhood, and the charm of the old architecture truly gives the community a feeling of its own. Known for its beautiful tree-lined streets, canopied with mature live oaks, the neighborhood blends early 1900s Mediterranean Revival, Colonial Revival, and Craftsman-style homes with thoughtfully designed modern construction. Many homes have been meticulously restored, preserving the original character while incorporating modern amenities.

Living Options in Hyde Park

Hyde Park offers a range of living options, from luxury condos and townhomes to gorgeous historic single-family homes. The variety makes Hyde Park accessible to professionals, couples, and families at different price points, though this is firmly a premium market:

  • Single-family homes: $800K to $5 million+ for Bayshore estate properties
  • Average single-family sale price: $1.6 to $1.7 million
  • Condos and townhomes: $300K to $1.2 million depending on size and building
  • Lot sizes: Vary from compact village lots to sprawling Bayshore Boulevard estates

Hyde Park Village, Shopping, Dining, and Community

Hyde Park Village is the neighborhood's centerpiece, a walkable outdoor shopping and dining destination featuring restaurants, boutiques, Sur La Table, Anthropologie, and a central fountain plaza where families gather on weekends. The village hosts regular events, farmers markets, and outdoor dining under the oaks. It is the social hub of South Tampa.

Location and Lifestyle

What makes Hyde Park exceptional beyond the homes themselves is the location. Residents are walking or biking distance to:

  • Bayshore Boulevard the world's longest continuous sidewalk, perfect for running, biking, and sunset views of Tampa Bay
  • Downtown Tampa 5-minute drive to the business district, Amalie Arena, Tampa Riverwalk
  • University of Tampa across the river, adding energy and culture to the area
  • SoHo (South Howard Avenue) Tampa's premier dining and nightlife corridor

Schools and Families

Hyde Park is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools. Gorrie Elementary is the neighborhood school and consistently rated among the top elementary schools in Tampa. Families also have access to several well-regarded private schools in the South Tampa area, including The Academy of the Holy Names, Tampa Preparatory, and Berkeley Preparatory School.

title: Palma Ceia, Tampa FL
content:
Palma Ceia, Tampa's Country Club Community

Palma Ceia is one of South Tampa's most established and prestigious residential neighborhoods, anchored by the historic Palma Ceia Golf & Country Club. The neighborhood attracts families drawn to its mature tree canopy, wide streets, and proximity to some of Tampa's best public and private schools. Palma Ceia has a quieter, more residential feel than the busier Hyde Park and SoHo corridors nearby, perfect for families who want luxury without the nightlife energy at their doorstep.

Homes and Architecture

Palma Ceia's housing stock spans from beautifully maintained 1930s, 1950s Mediterranean and Colonial Revival homes to modern custom builds. The older homes are prized for their craftsmanship, solid masonry construction, hardwood floors, original fireplaces, and the kind of architectural detail that new construction rarely replicates. Newer homes tend toward transitional and contemporary styles on lots where original structures have been replaced.

Home Values in 2026

  • Single-family homes: $900K to $3 million+
  • Average single-family sale price: approximately $1.1 million
  • Golf course-fronting properties: premium pricing for fairway views
  • Palma Ceia West: slightly more affordable adjacent neighborhood, $700K to $1.5M

Jumbo loan financing is typical at this price point. Calculate your payment.

The Country Club Lifestyle

Palma Ceia Golf & Country Club is a private club with an 18-hole golf course designed by Donald Ross, tennis facilities, a pool, fitness center, and active social calendar. Membership is separate from homeownership, not all residents are members, and not all members live in the neighborhood. The club adds a lifestyle dimension that attracts buyers looking for built-in community and recreation.

Schools

The school zone is a major draw. Palma Ceia feeds into some of Hillsborough County's top-rated public schools, including Grady Elementary, Coleman Middle, and the acclaimed Plant High School. The South Tampa area also offers Berkeley Prep, Tampa Prep, and Academy of the Holy Names for private school families.

title: Parkland Estates, South Tampa FL
content:
Parkland Estates, South Tampa's Best Kept Secret

Parkland Estates is located just west of South Howard Avenue, the corridor known locally as SoHo, making it one of the most walkable luxury neighborhoods in all of Tampa. Every restaurant, bar, and boutique along SoHo is literally steps from Parkland Estates' tree-lined streets, while Hyde Park and Bayshore Boulevard are a stone's throw in the other direction. You get the best of both worlds without ever needing to get in your car.

A Family-Friendly Community With Serious Character

Known as a very family-friendly community, Parkland Estates features stunning streets lined with well-planned and thoughtfully designed homes, a mix of beautifully maintained older properties and tasteful new construction that respects the neighborhood's character. The streets are canopied with large Grand Oak trees that create a feeling of security and comfort while giving the neighborhood an almost fairyland-type atmosphere.

Parkland Estates is also defined by its large lot sizes and the beautiful character of its homes. Much like the city around it, this community has a strong sense of community pride, residents do an exceptional job maintaining the quality and charm that makes this neighborhood what it is.

Home Values in Parkland Estates

  • Single-family homes: $900K to $2.5 million
  • Average single-family sale price: roughly $1.8 million
  • Lot sizes: Generous by South Tampa standards, many well over a quarter acre
  • Home styles: Mix of restored historic, renovated, and new construction

At this price point, most Parkland Estates purchases require a jumbo loan (above the $806,500 conforming limit). Barrett works with portfolio lenders who offer competitive rates for South Tampa luxury transactions. Use the mortgage calculator to estimate payments.

SoHo, Tampa's Premier Dining and Nightlife

Living in Parkland Estates means you're walking distance to SoHo's legendary dining scene, from Bern's Steak House (a Tampa institution since 1956) to the latest craft cocktail bars and farm-to-table restaurants. South Howard Avenue is Tampa's most vibrant street, and Parkland Estates residents can enjoy it all without worrying about parking or rideshares.

Location Advantages

  • SoHo (South Howard Ave) steps away, Tampa's best dining and nightlife
  • Hyde Park Village short walk to shopping, dining, and the fountain plaza
  • Bayshore Boulevard minutes to the world's longest continuous sidewalk
  • Downtown Tampa 5-minute drive to the business district and Riverwalk
  • MacDill Air Force Base convenient access via Bayshore or Gandy

Schools

Parkland Estates is served by Hillsborough County Public Schools. Wilson Middle School and Plant High School, one of Tampa's most acclaimed public high schools, are both nearby. The South Tampa area also has several top private schools including Tampa Preparatory, Berkeley Preparatory, and Academy of the Holy Names.
